Modify the Research Manager to output adoption rationale and unresolved disagreements; leave main-graph changes to C.\n217: \n218: ### Deliverables\n219: - review.py, context_builder.py; bull/bear/Research Manager adaptation; approved schema changes.\n220: - review/context offline tests, review_cases, and fixed-set tests with real candidate Prompts.\n221: - Prompt.md, the actual versioned runtime Prompt, ADR-003, the review-context contract.\n222: - One's own plan, test approvals, complete session, report section, and reflection.\n223: \n224: ### Acceptance\n225: Initial views do not read the other party's arguments; the response target exists; evidence IDs are valid; error structures are boundedly repaired; compression does not drop hard constraints.\n226: Demonstration: specified rebuttal and disagreement updates; key constraints remain before and after compression.\n227: \n228: ## 6.             "output": "<path>/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/.github/workflows/release-assets.yml</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: name: Release assets\n2: \n3: # Builds the source archive and wheel from the release tag and attaches them to\n4: # the GitHub release, so a version can be installed without cloning:\n5: #   pip install https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents/releases/download/<tag>/<wheel>\n6: # Run it by hand with a tag to attach builds to an earlier release.\n7: \n8: on:\n9:   release:\n10:     types: [published]\n11:   workflow_dispatch:\n12:     inputs:\n13:       tag:\n14:         description: \"Release tag to build and attach, for example v0.6.0\"\n15:         required: true\n16: \n17: permissions: {}\n18: \n19: concurrency:\n20:   group: release-assets-${{ inputs.tag || github.event.release.tag_name }}\n21:   cancel-in-progress: false\n22: \n23: jobs:\n24:   build:\n25:     name: build and attach\n26:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n27:     permissions:\n28:       contents: write\n29:     env:\n30:       TAG: ${{ inputs.tag || github.event.release.tag_name }}\n31:       GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}\n32:     steps:\n33:       - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n34:         with:\n35:           # Release branches share their tag's name, so name the tag explicitly.\n36:           ref: refs/tags/${{ env.TAG }}\n37:       - uses: actions/setup-python@v7\n38:         with:\n39:           python-version: \"3.13\"\n40:       - name: Check the package version matches the tag\n41:         run: |\n42:           version=$(python -c \"import re, pathlib; print(re.search(r'__version__ = \\\"([^\\\"]+)\\\"', pathlib.Path('tradingagents/__init__.py').read_text()).group(1))\")\n43:           if [ \"v$version\" != \"$TAG\" ]; then\n44:             echo \"tradingagents/__init__.py says $version, but the tag is $TAG\"\n45:             exit 1\n46:           fi\n47:       - name: Build the source archive and wheel\n48:         run: |\n49:           python -m pip install --upgrade build\n50:           python -m build\n51:       - name: Install the wheel in a clean environment\n52:         run: |\n53:           python -m venv /tmp/smoke\n54:           /tmp/smoke/bin/pip install dist/*.whl\n55:           # From another directory, so the imports come from the wheel, not the checkout.\n56:           cd /tmp\n57:           /tmp/smoke/bin/python -c \"import importlib.resources as r, tradingagents, cli.main;               "file": "tests/test_layering.py",
              "patch": "Index: tests/test_layering.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/test_layering.py\t\n+++ tests/test_layering.py\t\n@@ -1,35 +1,37 @@\n \"\"\"Only the data layer imports vendor libraries.\n \n Vendor calls belong in dataflows, where failures are raised as VendorError\n subclasses; a call made elsewhere can report an outage as a fact about the market.\n \"\"\"\n \n import ast\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import pytest\n \n-ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n+import tradingagents\n+\n+ROOT = Path(tradingagents.__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n VENDOR_LIBRARIES = {\"yfinance\"}\n \n \n def _imports(path: Path) -> set[str]:\n     names = set()\n     for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))):\n         if isinstance(node, ast.Import):\n             names |= {a.name.split(\".\")[0] for a in node.names}\n         elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module and not node.level:\n             names.add(node.module.split(\".\")[0])\n     return names\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_vendor_libraries_are_imported_only_by_the_data_layer():\n     data_layer = ROOT / \"tradingagents\" / \"dataflows\"\n     offenders = sorted(\n         str(path.relative_to(ROOT))\n         for package in (\"tradingagents\", \"cli\")\n         for path in (ROOT / package).rglob(\"*.py\")\n         if data_layer not in path.parents and _imports(path) & VENDOR_LIBRARIES\n     )\n     assert offenders == []\n",

          "text": "<path>/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/.agent/rules.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Project Covenant (.agent/rules.md)\n2: \n3: Binding rules for how the team and the coding agent work on this repository.\n4: Changes to this file require human approval.\n5: \n6: ## Abstraction limits\n7: \n8: - Prefer small, single-responsibility modules over deep inheritance.\n9: - No new abstraction unless it removes real duplication or enforces an invariant.\n10: \n11: ## Dependency constraints\n12: \n13: - Only the data layer may import vendor libraries (INV-001).\n14: - New third-party dependencies require justification in `docs/debt-register.md`\n15:   and must pass the dependency-check gate.\n16: \n17: ## Test independence\n18: \n19: - Tests must not depend on ordering or on each other.\n20: - At least **one negative test per feature** (a test that fails when the\n21:   feature/invariant is violated).\n22: \n23: ## Safety-critical changes\n24: \n25: - Changing safety-critical code (`dataflows/**`, `agents/structured.py`,\n26:   `agents/rating.py`, `default_config.py` env overrides, permission files,\n27:   requirements registry, CI workflow) requires an **architecture decision** and\n28:   **human approval** before merge.\n29: \n30: ## Context freshness\n31: \n32: - These rules and the architecture artifacts are updated within **one sprint**\n33:   of a requirements change; stale context is a defect.\n\n(End of file - total 33 lines)\n</content>",

Primary ownership agreement\n7: \n8: | Member | Fixed Module Responsibility | Main Results | Cross Reviewer |\n9: |---|---|---|---|\n10: | A | evidence, requirements, and traceability | conclusions have queryable bases, and evidence time status is clear | E |\n11: | B | Collaboration protocol and context | Independent arguments, targeted responses, constraints preserved after context compression | A |\n12: | C | Workflow, budget, and recovery | Scheduling based on questions and budget, all loops bounded | D |\n13: | D | Deterministic safety and final adjudication | AI cannot bypass hard rules, failures have specific handling | B |\n14: | E | Run records, experiments, CI and delivery | Comparable, reproducible, gates truly block | C |\n15: \n16: The primary owner is responsible for content correctness, interfaces, self-testing, OpenCode supervision, and on-time delivery; reviewers do not do the work for them. E integrates the report and does not write other members' experiments and reflections.\n17: Each person uses an independent branch/working copy; multiple people must not edit in the same directory simultaneously.\n18: \n19: ## 2. Final Functional Boundaries\n20: \n21: Run: Analyst → Shared evidence → Independent bull/bear arguments → Unresolved questions → Targeted response/Budget stop → Research Manager and Trader → Deterministic check → Final Manager → Re-validation → Report and run records.\n22: \n23: - Retain the original path for baseline comparison; prefer extending over replacing the original architecture.\n24: - This week, independent arguments may be generated sequentially, but they are mutually invisible in the first round; subsequent rounds respond according to explicit responds_to.\n25: - For duplicate detection, first implement normalized text deduplication/fingerprinting; do not claim to fully identify semantic duplicates.\n26: - Report-level evidence is not the same as news-level source tracing; only a reliable source time can prove historical availability, and unknown times are explicitly marked.\n27: - The budget is about quota reservation and stage control; the provider's actual billing, hidden retries, and estimation errors are recorded as-is.\n28: - The original three risk roles are retained by default; a streamlined risk path is an optional experimental switch, and the baseline cannot be removed without validation.\n29: - Do not implement live order placement, complex portfolio ledgers, new data platforms, or new frontends.\n30: \n31: ## 3. Permission files and CI scripts must be implemented according to the actual tool version; the above filenames do not mean the tools will automatically read them.\n188: \n189: ## 4. A's detailed tasks and personal deliverables\n190: \n191: ### What to Do\n192: 1. Compile the full set of requirements from the course and source code, with links to sources; distinguish existing capabilities from this group's additions.\n193: 2. Define Evidence: ID, source tier, ticker, analysis_time, available_at or unknown, content_hash, run_id.\n194: 3. Implement registration, deduplication, querying, reference validity, snapshot saving and recovery.\n195: 4. Provide B/D with a valid evidence list and error reasons, do not directly manipulate the main graph.\n196: 5. Maintain the trace-matrix; collect the test and monitoring mappings of the other four members.\n197: \n198: ### Deliverables\n199: - evidence.py、test_evidence.py、evidence_cases.json。\n200: - prd.yaml、requirements.yaml、req-schema.json、check_requirements.py。\n201: - evidence contract, ADR-002, memory-design, trace-matrix.\n202: - One's own plan, test approvals, full sessions, experiment/bug entries, report sections, and reflections.\n203: \n204: ### Acceptance\n205: Invalid references are rejected; future times cannot enter strict historical judgment; unknown time does not masquerade as verified; snapshots read back identically; different runs are not mixed.\n206: Demonstration: trace from a conclusion's evidence ID to the original report text, then demonstrate invalid references and future metadata.\n207: \n208: ## 5. B Detailed Tasks and Individual Deliverables\n209: \n210: ### What to do\n211: 1. Define Claim/ReviewResult: claim_id, speaker, statement, evidence_ids, responds_to, unresolved_questions.\n212: 2. Modify the bull/bear researchers: in the first round they independently propose views; in the next round they only respond to designated questions.\n213: 3. Validate output structure and reference relationships; format repair at most once, then enter explicit fallback if it still fails.\n214: 4. Implement layered context: identity/hard constraints/evidence/current task/necessary history/recovery state.\n215: 5. Define token limits, compression thresholds, deduplication, priority, and re-injection of constraints after compression.\n216: 6. Modify the Research Manager to output adoption rationale and unresolved disagreements; leave main-graph changes to C.\n217: \n218: ### Deliverables\n219: - review.py, context_builder.py; bull/bear/Research Manager adaptation; approved schema changes.\n220: - review/context offline tests, review_cases, and fixed-set tests with real candidate Prompts.\n221: - Prompt.md, the actual versioned runtime Prompt, ADR-003, the review-context contract.\n222: - One's own plan, test approvals, complete session, report section, and reflection.\n223: \n224: ### Acceptance\n225: Initial views do not read the other party's arguments; the response target exists; evidence IDs are valid; error structures are boundedly repaired; compression does not drop hard constraints.\n226: Demonstration: specified rebuttal and disagreement updates; key constraints remain before and after compression.\n227: \n228: ## 6. C Detailed Tasks and Personal Deliverables\n229: \n230: ### What to do\n231: 1. Compare three candidates: original, simple reduction, adaptive collaboration, and record the selection rationale.\n232: 2. Unify AgentState fields and interfaces, integrate A/B/D/E; only the main graph and shared state are modified.\n233: 3. Select target roles based on unresolved questions, no longer only fixed round alternation.\n234: 4. Implement quota reservation, pre-call checks, actual-usage updates, final review budget and hard loop limits.\n235: 5. Output explicit stop reasons for no progress, budget exhaustion, format failure, etc.; do not retry blindly.\n236: 6. The checkpoint signature considers policy/protocol/Prompt/evidence snapshot versions; refuse silent resume when incompatible.\n237: \n238: ### Delivery\n239: - execution_policy.py, graph files, state/config adaptation.\n240: - policy/resume tests and samples; complete routing table.\n241: - Blueprint, ADR-001/004, evaluation-table, runtime-policy-catalog, execution-budget contract.\n242: - One's own plan, test approval, complete session, experiments, report section, and reflection.\n243: \n244: ### Acceptance\n245: All paths are bounded; no invalid routing targets; insufficient budget does not initiate calls not permitted by policy; resume does not mix versions; baseline is runnable.\n246: Demo: paths and reasons for high vs. low budget with the same input; repeated discussion stops.\n247: \n248: ## 7. D's detailed tasks and personal deliverables\n249: \n250: ### What to Do\n251: 1. Define hard invariants, PASS/BLOCK/REVIEW, and the specific actions for each violation.\n252: 2. Check for negative/non-finite prices, missing key fields, invalid evidence, time limits, unknown holdings.\n253: 3. Validate the Trader's post-check recommendations, and verify again after the final manager is generated, to prevent reintroducing violations.\n254: 4. The final conclusion explains adopted views, evidence, and unresolved disagreements; BLOCK cannot be changed to PASS by the LLM.\n255: 5. Draft governance and permissions; human-only rules are maintained by students; safety changes require an ADR and human approval first.\n256: 6. Review the security boundary of every PR; collect real bug/debt records.\n257: \n258: ### Delivery\n259: - constraints.py and portfolio_manager adaptation; field requirements submitted to B, main-graph requirements submitted to C.\n260: - constraints/safety_boundary tests, safety_cases.\n261: - AGENTS.md, .agent/rules.md, the permissions policy source, CODEOWNERS recommendations.\n262: - invariants, permission-model, structural/verification constraints, MCP checklist, ADR-005, validation contract.\n263: - Own plans, approvals and complete sessions; review/debt/bug summaries; report sections and reflections.\n264: \n265: ### Acceptance\n266: Violations cannot cross the final boundary; unknown positions do not equal empty positions; insufficient information outputs REVIEW; all negative tests hit.\n267: Demonstration: the model proposes a violating recommendation, deterministic rules block it; regenerating by the model still cannot bypass.\n268: \n269: ## 8. E Detailed Tasks and Individual Deliverables\n270: \n271: ### What to Do\n272: 1. Freeze the baseline and environment; organize a separate PR for the src migration, branch strategy, and installation verification.\n273: 2. Define RunEvent and the run manifest, recording version, configuration, Prompt hash, snapshot, usage, duration, failures and stop reasons.\n274: 3. Compare V0 original/V1 simple reduction/V2 adaptive; fix inputs, model and memory starting point and repeat runs.\n275: 4. Semantic evaluation runs candidate Prompts/models; saved response replays are only for process verification.\n276: 5. The six gates and required checks are actually implemented; security paths require human review and an ADR.\n277: 6. Check test discovery: original tests suite + test/offline+requiredlive; do not write \"passed\" if not run.\n278: 7. Compile the report, contributions, session list, and demo; reproduce in a clean environment, check keys, and package.\n279: \n280: ### Delivery\n281: - run_recorder, stats_handler, compare_runs, evaluation/installation/CI scripts and configuration.\n282: - recorder/gate/integration tests, fixed_eval_cases and live evaluation entry points.\n283: - run-event contract, evaluation/protocol, results, README, Report summary, contribution table, gate evidence.\n284: - Own plans, test approvals, complete sessions, report sections and reflections; final ZIP and video compiled by E.\n285: \n286: ### Acceptance\n287: Results bound to version and input; no fabricated passes; missing evaluation evidence does not silently allow Prompt changes; gate failures can block merges; reproducible in a clean environment.\n288: Demonstration: the comparison results table, and a change that does not update the AI log being rejected by CI.\n289: \n290: ## 9. Shared Files and Approval Ownership\n291: \n292: | File/Area | Modification method |\n293: |---|---|\n294: | state.py, setup.py, conditional_logic.py, trading_graph.py | C sole integrator; other members submit field/node requests |\n295: | schemas.py | solely owned by B; D proposes field requirements; C checks compatibility |\n296: | requirements.yaml, trace-matrix.md | everyone provides entries, A merges and checks ID/source/mapping |\n297: | ai-use-log.yaml | Each PR author submits their own real entries; E resolves merge conflicts |\n298: | review-memo.md | The reviewer writes the conclusion, compiled by D; an author cannot sign APPROVE for themselves |\n299: | bug/debt | The finder records it first, the module owner handles it, and D tracks it |\n300: | .opencode/rules.md | Maintained by humans, no write permission granted to the coding agent |\n301: | approvals/, branch protection | Independent human approval; agents cannot sign on behalf of others or self-authorize |\n302: | Report.md | A—D each submit their own section, E integrates; section content is confirmed by its author |\n303: \n304: Everyone must keep their own original session. A reference to \"approved\" must be able to locate the plan/test version, the approver, and the approval time; it cannot rely only on YAML text that the author can modify.\n305: \n306: ## 10. Common Personal Submission Checklist for Each Member\n307: \n308: - [ ] Requirements package: functions, quality, invariants, provenance, MoSCoW and machine-checkable acceptance.\n309: - [ ] Module code and interfaces, not beyond approved paths; relevant ADR/INV references.\n310: - [ ] Positive and negative tests; tests are approved independently before implementation.\n311: - [ ] Real verification output, explicitly stating not-run/skipped/failed.\n312: - [ ] Comparison data or quality evidence for this module, not just screenshots of a successful page.\n313: - [ ] Versioned plan and human approval evidence.\n314: - [ ] transcripts/<student-id>-<name>.md: complete original session + clearly separated intervention notes; do not substitute a summary for the original text.\n315: - [ ] Real bugs/debts/reviews I found or handled, and traceability updates.\n316: - [ ] Report sections, names and student IDs, about 300—500 words of personal reflection, verifiable contributions.\n317: - [ ] A roughly 1-minute feature demo clip and explanation.\n318: \n319: No requirement to fabricate that everyone found the same number of defects; do not invent events that did not happen. If credentials are accidentally leaked, revoke them first and desensitize properly; do not commit usable Keys.\n320: \n321: ## 11. What to do each day\n322: \n323: | Day | A | B | C | D | E | Common Deliverable |\n324: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n325: | D1 | Requirements/schema/evidence contract | Collaboration/context contract | Architecture candidates/state interfaces | Invariants/permissions | baseline/environment/migration plan | First batch of plan and test independent approval |\n326: | D2 | Evidence implementation | Single-round protocol and context | Budget and graph | Rules and manager | Records and CI | Modules independently testable |\n327: | D3 | Evidence integration testing | Discuss integration testing | Main graph integration | Final validation | End-to-end/regression | Minimal closed loop working |\n328: | D4 | snapshot/time boundary | targeted response/compression | stop/resume | security escape verification | six gates/branch protection | second-round architecture revision and verification |\n329: | D5 | Evidence scoring | Collaboration scoring | Budget experiment | Security/risk experiment | Unified three-version comparison | Measured tables and failure cases |\n330: | D6 | Documentation/fixes/recording | Same as left | Same as left | Same as left | Compilation/candidate package | Submit candidate |\n331: | D7 | Cross-review | Cross-review | Cross-review | Cross-review | Clean reproduction/packaging | Complete submission |\n332: \n333: Process rotation: First round D1—D3: E chairs, A reviews requirements, B coordinates validation, D reviews security, C audits the process; second round D4—D6: C chairs, B reviews requirements, D coordinates validation, A reviews security, E audits the process. Fixed module ownership remains unchanged; reviews must be independent of the implementer of the same change.\n334: \n335: ## 12. Final Submission Check for the Whole Group\n336: \n337: 1. D1–D9 are all locatable; the root Blueprint is unique, no two drifting copies.\n338: 2. The requirements YAML and schema are valid; each fit/INV maps to tests/run monitoring.\n339: 3. Source code, original suite and new tests complete; offline/online boundary clear.\n340: 4. Six types of gates: test-first approval, static, schema, semantic, regression, AI logs; GitHub required checks and human safety review actually configured.\n341: 5. The permission source matches the actual OpenCode config and passes allow/deny tests; do not assume permissions.jsonc takes effect automatically.\n342: 6. The five members' sessions, plans, approvals, reviews, defects/debts, and contributions are authentic and complete.\n343: 7. Single Report markdown: ≤10,000 words (excluding figures), exceeding 15 pages at 12pt single line spacing; five-member reflections and contributions.\n344: 8. The README provides the GitHub address, architecture, directory, offline/online/full test commands; reproducible in a clean environment.\n345: 9. The ZIP does not contain videos, usable keys, or unnecessary caches; the 10-minute video is submitted separately.\n346: 10. Metrics such as a 20%—25% token reduction are preset targets; actual results follow the experiment report, no promises or fabricated results.\n347: \n348: ## 13. Basis and Related Materials\n349: \n350: - Full course specification: D:/Download/Chrome/CS5351-2026-2027-project.pdf, D1—D9 and blocking gates.\n351: - Introductory slides: D:/Homework/cs5351/group project/original/cs5351-introduction.pdf, project/video/development tool requirements.\n352: - Previous local execution manual: CS5351-execution-manual.md; startup constraint templates are in startup-templates/.\n353: - This directory is a task assignment based on reviewed local code and the final design; it does not indicate that the latest commits in the remote repository as of 2026-11-19 were re-fetched or verified.\n354: \n355: The current delivery consists only of planning documents; the original project was not modified, OpenCode was not run, and the team's GitHub configuration was not completed on their behalf.\n\n(End of file - total 355 lines)\n</content>",

Project Overview\n10: - 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n11: - 3. Deliverables\n12: - 4. Submission Format\n13: - 5. Required Repository Structure\n14: - 6. Blocking-Gate Requirements\n15: \n16: > **Submission model:** One repository plus five annotated agent-session transcripts and one process report. The AI-use log is mandatory and must be up to date at submission.\n17: \n18: ---\n19: \n20: ## 1. Project Overview\n21: \n22: Your team will design, build, and maintain a software application that contains an AI component, using an AI coding agent under human supervision. The project applies the full software engineering lifecycle taught in this course: you will specify requirements in machine-readable form, produce architecture artifacts that constrain what the coding agent may and may not do, govern the agent's code generation and verification, and demonstrate that you can review, debug, and maintain AI-generated code.\n23: \n24: Your application is your own choice — it must contain at least one genuine AI component (an LLM-powered feature, a retrieval/augmentation pipeline, an AI-assisted decision path, etc.) and at least one safety-relevant boundary where the AI's output must be constrained by deterministic code. The reference implementation shown in lectures (VHIS) is a pattern to follow, not a project to extend.\n25: \n26: ---\n27: \n28: ## 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n29: \n30: Your team should rotate roles so that students can experience different responsibilities in producing software using an AI coding agent, project management, or software engineering processes.\n31: \n32: ### Free Runner and Strong Contributor\n33: \n34: - Some students may be less motivated or less committed, while some other students may be much more engaged.\n35: - Your report should include a section of relative contributions. The average contribution is 1.0; students with less contribution can be assigned a lower weight, and students with stronger contributions will be assigned a higher weight.\n36: \n37: ---\n38: \n39: ## 3. Deliverables\n40: \n41: ### D1 — Requirements (machine-readable)\n42: \n43: Produce a machine-readable product requirements document and a consolidated requirements registry, both in YAML, under `./docs/req/` where `.` is the project root.\n44: \n45: - `docs/req/requirements.yaml` — every requirement as an entry with an ID, type, statement, and a machine-checkable fit criterion, plus priority. Types cover functional behavior, invariants (non-negotiable rules with zero-tolerance fit criteria), quality attributes, performance, cost, governance, and security. Non-functional requirements are expressed as metric + threshold + verification. Prioritization uses MoSCoW, and states the tradeoff explicitly. Requirements discovered through analysis of any existing system or repository are included and linked to their sources.\n46: - `docs/req/req-schema.json` — the schema used by CI in GitHub to validate the registry as a date.\n47: \n48: ### D2 — Architecture Artifacts (all as markdown `.md` files)\n49: \n50: Produce the architecture documentation as a single artifact per file in `./docs/architecture/`, with `.` as the project root.\n51: \n52: 1. **Architecture blueprint** — the master constraint document that the Plan agent reads: scope, architectural drivers, system boundaries, components, authority boundaries (what is advisory vs. authoritative), agent workflow, permissions, verification strategy, observability, and change policy.\n53: 2. **Architecture Decision Record** — the chosen architecture, the alternatives considered, the rationale, consequences, and conditions that would reopen the decision. It should also present the architectural design process. In addition, for your AI component, present your designed layered context structure that the AI receives on every turn (e.g., identity, standing constraints, retrieved knowledge, conversation history, resumable state, and the current task), the assembly pipeline (e.g., deduplicate, prioritize, budget, compact, assemble), the token-budget cap with its compaction threshold, and the policy for re-injecting critical constraints after compaction.\n54: 3. **Invariant register** — every invariant with its statement, source requirement ID, enforcing component, verification method, and an operational fallback if it is ever violated (a concrete action, not \"fix the bug\").\n55: 4. **Trace matrix** — every requirement mapped to its enforcing component, its test/evidence, and its runtime monitor.\n56: 5. **Memory/state design** — what state survives across sessions, interruptions, and versions; write and retrieval policy; ownership; retention; privacy.\n57: 6. **Permission model** — file-level read/write rights for each AI coding agent's role; default is no read, no write; every path is explicitly whitelisted.\n58: 7. **Runtime policy catalog** — what the system does when each degraded or failure path is triggered.\n59: 8. **Candidate evaluation table** — the comparison that justifies the chosen architecture.\n60: 9. *[optional]* **Evaluation logbook** — the accumulated evidence behind the architecture choices.\n61: 10. *[optional]* **Risk list** — assumptions that could become defects, with review triggers.\n62: 11. *[optional]* **Option ledger** — rejected architectural options and when they should be reconsidered.\n63: \n64: ### D3 — Coding Governance\n65: \n66: Produce the governance files that control how the AI coding agent plans and builds the application:\n67: \n68: - `AGENTS.md` (at the project root directory) — the single entry point the coding agent reads. It declares the build target, the reading order for architecture artifacts, the code baseline, what is readable/modifiable/frozen, the module organization, the integration contracts between modules, and the verification requirements that the generated code must satisfy.\n69: - `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` — module organization rules: each architectural element maps to exactly one module; new work extends the existing baseline, never replaces it; every module and function references the architecture decision and invariant it implements; authority boundaries.\n70: - `docs/code-governance/mcp-tool-manifest.md` — the tools the coding agent may call, and which roles may call them.\n71: - `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` — the project-level permission model in machine-readable form, with guard rules and enforcement mechanisms.\n72: - `.opencode/rules.md` — the project-level always-on behavioral rules for the coding agent. Human-only file.\n73: - `.agent/rules.md` — the project covenant: abstraction limits, dependency constraints, test independence (at least one negative test per feature), the rule that changing safety-critical code requires an architecture decision and human approval, and context freshness (rules updated within one sprint of a requirements change).\n74: \n75: ### D4 — Verification Governance (as markdown `.md` files)\n76: \n77: Produce the verification rules that the verification agent applies, and the QA records the team maintains:\n78: \n79: - `docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md` — every fit criterion has at least one test; every invariant has at least one test that fails when the invariant is violated; every test references the requirement or invariant it verifies; every new round of work runs all previous rounds' test suites with zero regressions.\n80: - Verification is three-tiered: structural (imports, module boundaries, permissions, architectural fitness functions), regression (all prior suites pass), and behavioral (quality thresholds such as faithfulness/relevance scores, zero safety escapes).\n81: - `docs/review-memo.md` — a review memo per pull request, covering spec alignment, architecture alignment, code and test quality, and operational metadata, with security and efficiency checked throughout, ending in a verdict of APPROVE, CHANGES REQUIRED, or REJECT.\n82: - `docs/debt-register.md` — technical debt tracked across the AI-era categories: prompt rot, hallucinated dependencies, untouchable code, hidden dependencies, agent-induced bloat, evaluation debt, guardrail debt, and human/cognitive debt.\n83: - `docs/bug-diary.md` — a diary entry per significant bug: symptom, reproduction, classification, root cause, fix, and which invariant gap it exposed.\n84: \n85: ### D5 — Agent Session Transcripts\n86: \n87: One full, raw transcript of an AI coding agent session to build the system implementation from scratch. Each transcript is annotated with the student team members' marked interventions and a rationale for each, showing where the team interrupted, redirected, approved, or rejected the agent's work.\n88: \n89: Collectively, the transcripts must demonstrate the entire supervised pipeline: requirements classification, architecture candidate generation and evaluation, plan approval before code, build, verification compliance, and architecture revision based on test evidence.\n90: \n91: ### D6 — Report (as a single markdown `.md` file)\n92: \n93: This is the project summary report. The report should list all students' names and student numbers, as well as the whole team's relative contribution (see the following example). It should contain at most 10,000 words (excluding diagrams) and contain more than 15 pages in Point 12 with single-line spacing. It should present the team's software engineering process and how the team optimizes it. It should also include each member's self-reflection (one short (e.g., 300-500 words) paragraph per student, with name and student ID. Cover process quality evidence (requirement volatility, defect trends, ambiguity resolution), how the team kept artifacts co-evolving when anything changed, and what human oversight caught that the agent did not.\n94: \n95: #### Tips: Contributions of Team Members\n96: \n97: > Suggest using contributed efforts (e.g., pre-agreed manhours or story points) in determining the relative contributions of team members (as all of us are students).\n98: >\n99: > - Teams can decide their measures on contributions. The team should reward students who take up difficult tasks and project management.\n100: >\n101: > *Actual productive hours spent on the project (hrs) or story points*\n102: \n103: | Name | Sprint 1 | Sprint 2 | Sprint 3 | Sprint 4 | Sprint 5 | Total |\n104: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n105: | Zhou, A | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 60 |\n106: | Wang, B | 12 | 10 | 5 | 20 | 8 | 55 |\n107: | Chan, C | 5 | 10 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 35 |\n108: \n109: Mean contribution = (60 + 55 + 35) / 3 = 50\n110: \n111: - Zhou: 60 / Mean contribution = 60 / 50 = 1.2\n112: - Wang: 55 / Mean contribution = 55 / 50 = 1.1\n113: - Chan: 35 / Mean contribution = 35 / 50 = 0.7\n114: \n115: > If the project gets 69 (in the range of B+ [66.5, 69.5)), then Zhou gets 82.8 (A+), Wang gets 75.9 (A), and Chan gets 48.3 (C)\n116: \n117: - Marks will be pro-rated accordingly. [bounded for extreme, e.g., the presence of a free rider]\n118: - Present the contributions in the final report.\n119: - Respect your teammates, as not everyone wants A+.\n120: \n121: ### D7 — GitHub Repository (in GitHub)\n122: \n123: The team's repository contains the source code, test cases, a CI/CD pipeline with implemented blocking gates, branch protection, and a meaningful commit history. The repository README states the design of the blocking gates and\n124: \n125: ### D8 — Source and Tests\n126: \n127: `src/` and `test/` directories with the full application source code and test cases. Module names match architectural elements. Test layout separates deterministic offline tests from live tests that require API access.\n128: \n129: ### D9 — Prompt (static) (a markdown file in project root directory)\n130: \n131: A single static prompt file, `./Prompt.md`. Once the coding agent starts with `AGENTS.md`, this is the one prompt to read. It instructs the agent to begin by producing an execution plan (traceability, interface contract, scope boundaries, testing strategy, steps) and to stop for human approval before generating any code, then proceed through build and self-verification with human gates at each stage. The prompt is the launch instruction — it does not run the agent unattended to completion.\n132: \n133: ---\n134: \n135: ## 4. Submission Format\n136: \n137: Submit a zip containing the documents in the project directory structure as listed in Section 5 of this document.\n138: \n139: Repository README must include:\n140: \n141: - The project's purpose and architecture in a few paragraphs\n142: - The organization of the project files\n143: - How to run the offline tests, the live tests, and the full suite\n144: - GitHub repo that contains the real GitHub project\n145: \n146: ---\n147: \n148: ## 5. Required Repository Structure\n149: \n150: ```text\n151: <team-app>/\n152: ├── README.md                          ← project intro\n153: ├── AGENTS.md                          ← coding-agent governance     ← process report + reflections (D6)\n157: ├── docs/\n158: │   ├── req/\n159: │   │   ├── requirements.yaml          ← machine-readable PRD (D1)\n160: │   │   └── req-schema.json            ← CI  └── rules.md                       ← always-on behavioral rules (D3)\n183: ├── .agent/\n184: │   └── rules.md                       ← project covenant (D3)\n185: ├── .github/workflows/\n186: │   └──                 "text": "# CS5351 — Agentic Software Engineering Project\n\n**Project Requirement Sheet**\n\n> **Core expectation:** Design, build, verify, and maintain an AI-enabled software application using an AI coding agent under auditable human supervision.\n\n## Document Contents\n\n- 1. Project Overview\n- 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n- 3. Deliverables\n- 4. Submission Format\n- 5. Required Repository Structure\n- 6. Blocking-Gate Requirements\n\n> **Submission model:** One repository plus five annotated agent-session transcripts and one process report. The AI-use log is mandatory and must be up to date at submission.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Project Overview\n\nYour team will design, build, and maintain a software application that contains an AI component, using an AI coding agent under human supervision. The project applies the full software engineering lifecycle taught in this course: you will specify requirements in machine-readable form, produce architecture artifacts that constrain what the coding agent may and may not do, govern the agent's code generation and verification, and demonstrate that you can review, debug, and maintain AI-generated code.\n\nYour application is your own choice — it must contain at least one genuine AI component (an LLM-powered feature, a retrieval/augmentation pipeline, an AI-assisted decision path, etc.) and at least one safety-relevant boundary where the AI's output must be constrained by deterministic code. The reference implementation shown in lectures (VHIS) is a pattern to follow, not a project to extend.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n\nYour team should rotate roles so that students can experience different responsibilities in producing software using an AI coding agent, project management, or software engineering processes.\n\n### Free Runner and Strong Contributor\n\n- Some students may be less motivated or less committed, while some other students may be much more engaged.\n- Your report should include a section of relative contributions. The average contribution is 1.0; students with less contribution can be assigned a lower weight, and students with stronger contributions will be assigned a higher weight.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Deliverables\n\n### D1 — Requirements (machine-readable)\n\nProduce a machine-readable product requirements document and a consolidated requirements registry, both in YAML, under `./docs/req/` where `.` is the project root.\n\n- `docs/req/requirements.yaml` — every requirement as an entry with an ID, type, statement, and a machine-checkable fit criterion, plus priority. Types cover functional behavior, invariants (non-negotiable rules with zero-tolerance fit criteria), quality attributes, performance, cost, governance, and security. Non-functional requirements are expressed as metric + threshold + verification. Prioritization uses MoSCoW, and states the tradeoff explicitly. Requirements discovered through analysis of any existing system or repository are included and linked to their sources.\n- `docs/req/req-schema.json` — the schema used by CI in GitHub to validate the registry as a date.\n\n### D2 — Architecture Artifacts (all as markdown `.md` files)\n\nProduce the architecture documentation as a single artifact per file in `./docs/architecture/`, with `.` as the project root.\n\n1. **Architecture blueprint** — the master constraint document that the Plan agent reads: scope, architectural drivers, system boundaries, components, authority boundaries (what is advisory vs. authoritative), agent workflow, permissions, verification strategy, observability, and change policy.\n2. **Architecture Decision Record** — the chosen architecture, the alternatives considered, the rationale, consequences, and conditions that would reopen the decision. It should also present the architectural design process. In addition, for your AI component, present your designed layered context structure that the AI receives on every turn (e.g., identity, standing constraints, retrieved knowledge, conversation history, resumable state, and the current task), the assembly pipeline (e.g., deduplicate, prioritize, budget, compact, assemble), the token-budget cap with its compaction threshold, and the policy for re-injecting critical constraints after compaction.\n3. **Invariant register** — every invariant with its statement, source requirement ID, enforcing component, verification method, and an operational fallback if it is ever violated (a concrete action, not \"fix the bug\").\n4. **Trace matrix** — every requirement mapped to its enforcing component, its test/evidence, and its runtime monitor.\n5. **Memory/state design** — what state survives across sessions, interruptions, and versions; write and retrieval policy; ownership; retention; privacy.\n6. **Permission model** — file-level read/write rights for each AI coding agent's role; default is no read, no write; every path is explicitly whitelisted.\n7. **Runtime policy catalog** — what the system does when each degraded or failure path is triggered.\n8. **Candidate evaluation table** — the comparison that justifies the chosen architecture.\n9. *[optional]* **Evaluation logbook** — the accumulated evidence behind the architecture choices.\n10. *[optional]* **Risk list** — assumptions that could become defects, with review triggers.\n11. *[optional]* **Option ledger** — rejected architectural options and when they should be reconsidered.\n\n### D3 — Coding Governance\n\nProduce the governance files that control how the AI coding agent plans and builds the application:\n\n- `AGENTS.md` (at the project root directory) — the single entry point the coding agent reads. It declares the build target, the reading order for architecture artifacts, the code baseline, what is readable/modifiable/frozen, the module organization, the integration contracts between modules, and the verification requirements that the generated code must satisfy.\n- `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` — module organization rules: each architectural element maps to exactly one module; new work extends the existing baseline, never replaces it; every module and function references the architecture decision and invariant it implements; authority boundaries.\n- `docs/code-governance/mcp-tool-manifest.md` — the tools the coding agent may call, and which roles may call them.\n- `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` — the project-level permission model in machine-readable form, with guard rules and enforcement mechanisms.\n- `.opencode/rules.md` — the project-level always-on behavioral rules for the coding agent. Human-only file.\n- `.agent/rules.md` — the project covenant: abstraction limits, dependency constraints, test independence (at least one negative test per feature), the rule that changing safety-critical code requires an architecture decision and human approval, and context freshness (rules updated within one sprint of a requirements change).\n\n### D4 — Verification Governance (as markdown `.md` files)\n\nProduce the verification rules that the verification agent applies, and the QA records the team maintains:\n\n- `docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md` — every fit criterion has at least one test; every invariant has at least one test that fails when the invariant is violated; every test references the requirement or invariant it verifies; every new round of work runs all previous rounds' test suites with zero regressions.\n- Verification is three-tiered: structural (imports, module boundaries, permissions, architectural fitness functions), regression (all prior suites pass), and behavioral (quality thresholds such as faithfulness/relevance scores, zero safety escapes).\n- `docs/review-memo.md` — a review memo per pull request, covering spec alignment, architecture alignment, code and test quality, and operational metadata, with security and efficiency checked throughout, ending in a verdict of APPROVE, CHANGES REQUIRED, or REJECT.\n- `docs/debt-register.md` — technical debt tracked across the AI-era categories: prompt rot, hallucinated dependencies, untouchable code, hidden dependencies, agent-induced bloat, evaluation debt, guardrail debt, and human/cognitive debt.\n- `docs/bug-diary.md` — a diary entry per significant bug: symptom, reproduction, classification, root cause, fix, and which invariant gap it exposed.\n\n### D5 — Agent Session Transcripts\n\nOne full, raw transcript of an AI coding agent session to build the system implementation from scratch. Each transcript is annotated with the student team members' marked interventions and a rationale for each, showing where the team interrupted, redirected, approved, or rejected the agent's work.\n\nCollectively, the transcripts must demonstrate the entire supervised pipeline: requirements classification, architecture candidate generation and evaluation, plan approval before code, build, verification compliance, and architecture revision based on test evidence.\n\n### D6 — Report (as a single markdown `.md` file)\n\nThis is the project summary report. The report should list all students' names and student numbers, as well as the whole team's relative contribution (see the following example). It should contain at most 10,000 words (excluding diagrams) and contain more than 15 pages in Point 12 with single-line spacing. It should present the team's software engineering process and how the team optimizes it. It should also include each member's self-reflection (one short (e.g., 300-500 words) paragraph per student, with name and student ID. Cover process quality evidence (requirement volatility, defect trends, ambiguity resolution), how the team kept artifacts co-evolving when anything changed, and what human oversight caught that the agent did not.\n\n#### Tips: Contributions of Team Members\n\n> Suggest using contributed efforts (e.g., pre-agreed manhours or story points) in determining the relative contributions of team members (as all of us are students).\n>\n> - Teams can decide their measures on contributions. The team should reward students who take up difficult tasks and project management.\n>\n> *Actual productive hours spent on the project (hrs) or story points*\n\n| Name | Sprint 1 | Sprint 2 | Sprint 3 | Sprint 4 | Sprint 5 | Total |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Zhou, A | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 60 |\n| Wang, B | 12 | 10 | 5 | 20 | 8 | 55 |\n| Chan, C | 5 | 10 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 35 |\n\nMean contribution = (60 + 55 + 35) / 3 = 50\n\n- Zhou: 60 / Mean contribution = 60 / 50 = 1.2\n- Wang: 55 / Mean contribution = 55 / 50 = 1.1\n- Chan: 35 / Mean contribution = 35 / 50 = 0.7\n\n> If the project gets 69 (in the range of B+ [66.5, 69.5)), then Zhou gets 82.8 (A+), Wang gets 75.9 (A), and Chan gets 48.3 (C)\n\n- Marks will be pro-rated accordingly. [bounded for extreme, e.g., the presence of a free rider]\n- Present the contributions in the final report.\n- Respect your teammates, as not everyone wants A+.\n\n### D7 — GitHub Repository (in GitHub)\n\nThe team's repository contains the source code, test cases, a CI/CD pipeline with implemented blocking gates, branch protection, and a meaningful commit history. The repository README states the design of the blocking gates and\n\n### D8 — Source and Tests\n\n`src/` and `test/` directories with the full application source code and test cases. Module names match architectural elements. Test layout separates deterministic offline tests from live tests that require API access.\n\n### D9 — Prompt (static) (a markdown file in project root directory)\n\nA single static prompt file, `./Prompt.md`. Once the coding agent starts with `AGENTS.md`, this is the one prompt to read. It instructs the agent to begin by producing an execution plan (traceability, interface contract, scope boundaries, testing strategy, steps) and to stop for human approval before generating any code, then proceed through build and self-verification with human gates at each stage. The prompt is the launch instruction — it does not run the agent unattended to completion.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Submission Format\n\nSubmit a zip containing the documents in the project directory structure as listed in Section 5 of this document.\n\nRepository README must include:\n\n- The project's purpose and architecture in a few paragraphs\n- The organization of the project files\n- How to run the offline tests, the live tests, and the full suite\n- GitHub repo that contains the real GitHub project\n\n---\n\n## 5. Required Repository Structure\n\n```text\n<team-app>/\n├── README.md                          ← project intro\n├── AGENTS.md                          ← coding-agent governance (D3)\n├── reflections (D6)\n├── docs/\n│   ├── req/\n│   │   ├── requirements.yaml          ← machine-readable PRD (D1)\n│   │   └── req-schema.json            ← CI validation schema (D1)\n│   ├── architecture/                  ← 11 artifact types (D2)\n│   │   ├── adr/001-<choice>.md\n│   │   ├── invariants.md\n│   │   ├── trace-matrix.md\n│   │   ├── memory-design.md\n│   │   ├── option-ledger.md\n│   │   ├── permission-model.md\n│   │   ├── evaluation-logbook.md\n│   │   ├── risk-list.md\n│   │   ├── evaluation-table.md\n│   │   └── runtime-policy-catalog.md\n│   ├── code-governance/               ← (D3, D4)\n│   │   ├── structural-constraints.md\n│   │   ├── verification-constraints.md\n│   │   └── mcp-tool-manifest.md\n│   ├── ai-use-log.yaml                ← (D1)\n│   ├── review-memo.md                 ← review records (D4)\n│   ├── debt-register.md               ← (D4)\n│   └── bug-diary.md                   ← (D4)\n├── .opencode/\n│   ├── permissions.jsonc              ← machine-readable Blocking-Gate Requirements (D7)\n\nThe CI/CD pipeline must implement the following blocking gates.\n\n1. **Test approval gate** — no code change merges unless the tests for the change were approved before implementation began.\n2. **Static analysis gates** — lint, type-checking, and dependency checks run on every commit; contract, security, API-surface, and permission checks run on any pull request touching safety-relevant paths.\n3. **Schema gate** — the requirements registry validates against its JSON schema.\n4. **Semantic evaluation gate** — for any prompt or model change, the pipeline replays a fixed evaluation set against quality thresholds before the change can reach production; if a threshold fails, the change is blocked and reported.\n5. **Regression gate** — every change runs the full prior test suites; any regression blocks the merge.\n6. **AI-use log gate** — a pull request that changes code or prompts without updating the AI-use log is blocked.\n\n**Branch protection:** Branch protection must require passing CI, and changes to safety-critical paths must require human review with an accompanying architecture decision.\n\n---\n\n*Transcribed from `CS5351-2026-2027-project.pdf` (10 pages).                 "text": "import logging\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom typing import Any, TypedDict\n\nfrom langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage\nfrom langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph\nfrom langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents import (\n    create_aggressive_debator,\n    create_bear_researcher,\n    create_bull_researcher,\n    create_conservative_debator,\n    create_fundamentals_analyst,\n    create_market_analyst,\n    create_neutral_debator,\n    create_news_analyst,\n    create_portfolio_manager,\n    create_research_manager,\n    create_sentiment_analyst,\n    create_trader,\n)\nfrom tradingagents.agents.analysts.turn import WRAP_UP\nfrom tradingagents.agents.state import AgentState\n\nfrom .analyst_execution import build_analyst_execution_plan\nfrom .conditional_logic import ConditionalLogic\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n# Every target a shared conditional router can return. Each edge driven by the\n# router maps all of them, so a fall-through return (e.g. under prompt/i18n/\n# refactor drift in the speaker labels) can never hit a missing path_map entry\n# and crash LangGraph mid-run (#1088).\nDEBATE_PATH_MAP = {\n    \"Bull Researcher\": \"Bull Researcher\",\n    \"Bear Researcher\": \"Bear Researcher\",\n    \"Research Manager\": \"Research Manager\",\n}\nRISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP = {\n    \"Aggressive Analyst\": \"Aggressive Analyst\",\n    \"Conservative Analyst\": \"Conservative Analyst\",\n    \"Neutral Analyst\": \"Neutral Analyst\",\n    \"Portfolio Manager\": \"Portfolio Manager\",\n}\n\n\ndef _tools_or_done(state) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Route an analyst's turn: run its tool calls, or finish with its report.\"\"\"\n    return \"tools\" if state[\"messages\"][-1].tool_calls else END\n\n\ndef _analyst_graph(spec, agent, max_tool_rounds: int):\n    \"\"\"One analyst as a graph of its own: the model and its tools, on a private message history.\n\n    It returns only its report, so analysts running side by side never write the\n    same key, and its tool calls never reach the other analysts' messages. After\n    ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and\n    that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools\n    cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).\n    \"\"\"\n    output = TypedDict(f\"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report\", {spec.report_key: str})\n    graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)\n    graph.add_node(\"agent\", agent)\n    graph.add_edge(START, \"agent\")\n    if not spec.tools:\n        graph.add_edge(\"agent\", END)\n        return graph.compile()\n\n    def calls(messages):\n        return [call[\"name\"] for m in messages for call in (getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None) or [])]\n\n    def rounds(messages) -> int:\n        return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None))\n\n    def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:\n        return \"wrap_up\" if rounds(state[\"messages\"]) >= max_tool_rounds else \"agent\"\n\n    def wrap_up(state):\n        repeated = \", \".join(f\"{name} x{n}\" for name, n in Counter(calls(state[\"messages\"])).most_common())\n        logger.warning(\"%s used its %d tool rounds (%s); asking for its report\",\n                       spec.agent_node, max_tool_rounds, repeated)\n        return agent({**state, \"messages\": [*state[\"messages\"], HumanMessage(WRAP_UP)]})\n\n    graph.add_node(\"tools\", ToolNode(list(spec.tools)))\n    graph.add_node(\"wrap_up\", wrap_up)\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"agent\", _tools_or_done, [\"tools\", END])\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"tools\", more_or_wrap_up, [\"agent\", \"wrap_up\"])\n    graph.add_edge(\"wrap_up\", END)\n    return graph.compile()\n\n\nclass GraphSetup:\n    \"\"\"Handles the setup and configuration of the agent graph.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        quick_thinking_llm: Any,\n        deep_thinking_llm: Any,\n        conditional_logic: ConditionalLogic,\n        max_tool_rounds: int,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"Initialize with required components.\"\"\"\n        self.quick_thinking_llm = quick_thinking_llm\n        self.deep_thinking_llm = deep_thinking_llm\n        self.conditional_logic = conditional_logic\n        self.max_tool_rounds = max_tool_rounds\n\n    def setup_graph(\n        self, selected_analysts=(\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\"), memory_node=None\n    ):\n        \"\"\"Set up and compile the agent workflow graph.\n\n        Args:\n            selected_analysts (list): List of analyst types to include. Options are:\n                - \"market\": Market analyst\n                - \"social\": Sentiment analyst\n                - \"news\": News analyst\n                - \"fundamentals\": Fundamentals analyst\n            memory_node: Node that settles past decisions and returns the run's\n                ``past_context``. It runs alongside the analysts.\n        \"\"\"\n        plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analysts)\n\n        analyst_factories = {\n            \"market\": lambda: create_market_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"social\": lambda: create_sentiment_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"news\": lambda: create_news_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"fundamentals\": lambda: create_fundamentals_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n        }\n\n        bull_researcher_node = create_bull_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        bear_researcher_node = create_bear_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        research_manager_node = create_research_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n        trader_node = create_trader(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n\n        aggressive_analyst = create_aggressive_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        neutral_analyst = create_neutral_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        conservative_analyst = create_conservative_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        portfolio_manager_node = create_portfolio_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n\n        workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)\n\n        for spec in plan.specs:\n            workflow.add_node(spec.agent_node,\n                              _analyst_graph(spec, analyst_factories[spec.key](), self.max_tool_rounds))\n\n        workflow.add_node(\"Bull Researcher\", bull_researcher_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Bear Researcher\", bear_researcher_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Research Manager\", research_manager_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Trader\", trader_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Aggressive Analyst\", aggressive_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Neutral Analyst\", neutral_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Conservative Analyst\", conservative_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Portfolio Manager\", portfolio_manager_node)\n\n        # The analysts work at the same time; the research debate starts once\n        # every one of them has filed its report. The memory log settles past\n        # decisions alongside them: only the Portfolio Manager reads its lessons.\n        first_steps = [spec.agent_node for spec in plan.specs]\n        if memory_node is not None:\n            workflow.add_node(\"Memory Log\", memory_node)\n            first_steps.append(\"Memory Log\")\n        for node in first_steps:\n            workflow.add_edge(START, node)\n        workflow.add_edge(first_steps, \"Bull Researcher\")\n\n        # Both research-debate edges share the complete DEBATE_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n        for debate_node in (\"Bull Researcher\", \"Bear Researcher\"):\n            workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n                debate_node,\n                self.conditional_logic.should_continue_debate,\n                DEBATE_PATH_MAP,\n            )\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Research Manager\", \"Trader\")\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Trader\", \"Aggressive Analyst\")\n        # All three risk edges share the complete RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n        for risk_node in (\"Aggressive Analyst\", \"Conservative Analyst\", \"Neutral Analyst\"):\n            workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n                risk_node,\n                self.conditional_logic.should_continue_risk_analysis,\n                RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP,\n            )\n\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Portfolio Manager\", END)\n\n        return workflow",

            "output": "=== rouff / stats_handler ===\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\nfrom langchain_core.outputs import LLMResult\n\n\nclass StatsCallbackHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n    \"\"\"Callback handler that tracks LLM calls, tool calls, and token usage.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self.llm_calls = 0\n        self.tool_calls = 0\n        self.tokens_in = 0\n        self.tokens_out = 0\n\n    def on_llm_start(\n        self,\n        serialized: dict[str, Any],\n        prompts: list[str],\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment LLM call counter when an LLM starts.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.llm_calls += 1\n\n    def on_chat_model_start(\n        self,\n        serialized: dict[str, Any],\n        messages: list[list[Any]],\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment LLM call counter when a chat model starts.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.llm_calls += 1\n\n    def on_llm_end(self, response: LLMResult, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n=== llm_clients __init__ exports ===\nfrom .base_client import BaseLLMClient\nfrom .factory import build_llm_kwargs, create_llm_client, create_tier_client, tier_provider\n\n__all__ = [\"BaseLLMClient\", \"build_llm_kwargs\", \"create_llm_client\", \"create_tier_client\", \"tier_provider\"]\n=== reporting.py head ===\n\"\"\"Reusable report-tree writer shared by the CLI and the programmatic API.\n\nWrites a run's per-section markdown (analysts, research, trading, risk,\nportfolio) plus a consolidated ``complete_report.md`` under ``save_path``. The\nCLI and ``TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports`` both call this, so a headless / API\nrun produces the same on-disk report tree a CLI run does.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.rating import run_rating\n\n\ndef analyst_names(keys) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The analysts as users select them: the sentiment analyst's key is \"social\".\"\"\"\n    return [\"sentiment\" if key == \"social\" else key for key in keys or []]\n\n\ndef _header(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The report's title and what produced it: analysis date, version, models, analysts, vendors.\"\"\"\n    lines = [f\"# Trading Analysis Report: {ticker}\", \"\"]\n    if final_state.get(\"trade_date\"):\n        lines.append(f\"- Analysis date: {final_state['trade_date']}\")\n    if final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\"):\n        lines.append(f\"- Rating: {run_rating(final_state)}\")\n    lines.append(f\"- Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\")\n    if settings:\n        s = settings.get\n        deep_provider = s(\"deep_think_provider\") or s(\"llm_provider\", \"?\")\n",

              "patch": "Index: docs/ai-use-log.yaml\n===================================================================\n--- docs/ai-use-log.yaml\t\n+++ docs/ai-use-log.yaml\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@\n+# AI-use log. Every PR that changes code or prompts adds its own real entry here.\n+# E resolves merge conflicts; entries are authored by the PR author, not fabricated.\n+# Required fields per entry: pr, date, author, agent, summary, files, human_gates.\n+# (Schema is a team convention; the AI-use-log CI gate is a later E step.)\n+\n+entries:\n+  - pr: \"step-1-run-event-contract\"\n+    date: \"2026-11-21\"\n+    author: \"E\"\n+    agent: \"opencode\"\n+    summary: >-\n+      Added the RunEvent contract (docs/contracts/run-event.md), E's versioned plan\n+      (docs/plans/E-run-recorder.md), and initialised this AI-use log. Documentation\n+      only; no source or test files created.\n+    files:\n+      - docs/contracts/run-event.md\n+      - docs/plans/E-run-recorder.md\n+      - docs/ai-use-log.yaml\n+    human_gates:\n+      - \"Plan approved by human (APPROVED for step 1, documentation only).\"\n+      - \"Scope limited to docs; src/ and test/ deliberately untouched.\"\n",

              "file": "docs/contracts/run-event.md",
              "patch": "Index: docs/contracts/run-event.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/contracts/run-event.md\t\n+++ docs/contracts/run-event.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@\n+# RunEvent Contract\n+\n+Owner: E (runtime records, experiments, CI, delivery).\n+Status: **step 1 — documentation only.** No `run_recorder.py` and no tests exist yet.\n+Consumers: `src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py` (planned), `scripts/compare_runs.py`\n+(planned), evaluation results (`docs/evaluation/results/`, planned).\n+\n+This contract defines the on-disk JSON \"run manifest\" that records one analysis run\n+well enough to compare runs and to gate prompt/model changes. It is deliberately\n+minimal in this slice; fields owned by other members are marked and are **not**\n+validated here.\n+\n+## Design rules\n+\n+- **Deterministic by injection.** The recorder never reads the wall clock or a random\n+  source internally. `created_at`, `run_id`, and `version` are passed in explicitly;\n+  serialization uses `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`.\n+  Two calls with identical inputs produce identical bytes (\"byte-stable manifest\").\n+- **Schema is versioned.** Top-level `schema_version` is an `int`. The recorder writes\n+  `1` and rejects a manifest whose `schema_version` is not the supported value on read\n+  (explicit error, no silent coercion).\n+- **No secrets on disk.** Config keys whose name matches a secret pattern\n+  (`*_api_key`, `*_key`, `backend_url`, `*_token`, `*_password`) are excluded from\n+  `config_snapshot`; the manifest records only what is safe to compare.\n+- **Owned fields are not validated here.** `stop_reason` and the evidence/prompt\n+  snapshot shapes are contracts owned by C and A respectively. This slice stores them\n+  as opaque values and does **not** assert a value domain for them.\n+\n+## Field list (schema_version 1)\n+\n+| # | Field | Type | Req? | Inject./Caller-supplied | Owner | Notes |\n+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n+| 1 | `schema_version` | `int` (== 1) | required | recorder | E | Read rejects any other value. |\n+| 2 | `run_id` | `str` (non-empty) | required | caller | E | Opaque stable id; not `uuid4()` internally. |\n+| 3 | `created_at` | `str` (ISO-8601) | required | caller | E | Not `datetime.now()` internally. |\n+| 4 | `version` | `str` | required | caller (`tradingagents.__version__`) | E | Package version that produced the run. |\n+| 5 | `ticker` | `str` (non-empty) | required | caller | E | `company_of_interest` for the run. |\n+| 6 | `trade_date` | `str` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | required | caller | E | Analysis date. |\n+| 7 | `asset_type` | `str` | required | caller | E | e.g. `stock`, `crypto`. |\n+| 8 | `outcome` | `str` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | E | Final rating string, or `null` if the run produced none. |\n+| 9 | `config_snapshot` | `object` (str→scalar) | required | caller | E | Run settings minus secret-pattern keys (rule above). |\n+| 10 | `prompt_hashes` | `object` (str→str) | required (may be `{}`) | caller | B/A | Prompt name → hash. Shape/owner: B. Not validated here. |\n+| 11 | `evidence_snapshot` | `object` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | A | Evidence snapshot id/pointer. Shape/owner: A. Not validated here. |\n+| 12 | `usage` | `object` | required | caller | E | `{llm_calls:int, tool_calls:int, tokens_in:int, tokens_out:int}`. |\n+| 13 | `duration_seconds` | `number` (>= 0) or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | E | Wall time measured by the caller, passed in. |\n+| 14 | `failure` | `str` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | E | Failure summary if the run failed. |\n+| 15 | `stop_reason` | `str` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | **C** | Opaque here. Value domain owned by C's `execution_policy`; **not validated in this slice.** |\n+\n+All 15 keys are present on every manifest (nullable ones set to `null`). Required\n+`str` fields reject empty strings. Missing required keys, or an unsupported\n+`schema_version`, are rejected on write and on read.\n+\n+## What this contract deliberately does not define\n+\n+- No `stop_reason` enum (C owns it — see C §6.5 and `execution_policy.py`, planned).\n+- No prompt-hash algorithm (B owns prompt versioning, `prompts/prompt_v1.x.yaml`).\n+- No evidence snapshot schema (A owns `evidence.py` and `evidence.md`).\n+- No CLI/graph/stats integration (later steps depend on C's `AgentState` and stop enum).\n+- No CI gate. Gates (§6) are a later E step.\n+\n+## Negative cases the future recorder test must cover (slice 2)\n+\n+- Missing required field (e.g. `version`) → rejected with a specific error.\n+- Unsupported `schema_version` → rejected with a specific error.\n+- Secret-pattern config key (e.g. `openai_api_key`) → absent from `config_snapshot`.\n",
              "additions": 65,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },
            {
              "file": "docs/plans/E-run-recorder.md",
              "patch": "Index: docs/plans/E-run-recorder.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/plans/E-run-recorder.md\t\n+++ docs/plans/E-run-recorder.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@\n+# Plan — E: RunEvent contract + run recorder\n+\n+Owner: E. Version: v1 (2026-11-21). Status: step 1 (docs) approved; implementation pending.\n+\n+## Goal\n+\n+A deterministic, offline RunEvent/run-manifest recorder so runs can be compared and\n+prompt/model changes can be gated. Greenfield: depends on no other member for the\n+recorder's own contract.\n+\n+## Traceability\n+\n+- Course: D4 (verification records / runtime monitor foundation), D8 (offline tests),\n+  §6 gates 5–6 prerequisite (a manifest is what regression + AI-log gates diff).\n+- Team split §8.2 (RunEvent + manifest: version, config, prompt hash, snapshot, usage,\n+  duration, failure, stop reason).\n+- REQ/INV IDs: not yet assigned (A owns `requirements.yaml`); this plan references the\n+  requirement slot and marks IDs \"assigned by A\". No invented IDs.\n+\n+## Interface contract\n+\n+- Input: explicitly injected `created_at`, `run_id`, `version`, plus caller-supplied\n+  run fields (see `docs/contracts/run-event.md` field list).\n+- Output: a JSON manifest file with `schema_version: 1`, sorted keys, stable bytes for\n+  identical inputs.\n+- Errors: missing required key or unsupported `schema_version` → explicit error on\n+  write and read. Secret-pattern config keys excluded.\n+- Owned-but-not-validated: `stop_reason` (C), `prompt_hashes` (B), `evidence_snapshot` (A).\n+\n+## Scope boundaries\n+\n+In: `run_recorder.py` (serialize + read-back validation), offline tests, this contract.\n+Out: graph/CLI/stats wiring, `stop_reason` enum, prompt-hash algorithm, evidence\n+schema, any CI gate, `tests/`→`test/offline/` migration, `pyproject.toml` marker edits.\n+\n+## Steps + completion criteria\n+\n+1. **Docs (this step).** `docs/contracts/run-event.md`, this plan, `docs/ai-use-log.yaml`.\n+   Done when contract field list is fixed and reviewed.\n+2. **Recorder + tests.** `src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py`,\n+   `test/offline/__init__.py`, `test/offline/test_run_recorder.py`. No custom pytest\n+   marker (default `-m \"not integration\"` runs them). Done when positive + at least\n+   one negative test pass; `ruff check src tests` clean.\n+3. **Integration (depends on C).** Wire recorder into run completion once C's\n+   `AgentState`/stop enum and the graph integration point exist.\n+4. **compare_runs + gate (depends on B/C/D).** `scripts/compare_runs.py`, regression and\n+   AI-use-log gate wiring in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.\n+\n+## Testing strategy (slice 2)\n+\n+- Positive: round-trip write→read preserves all 15 fields.\n+- Positive: identical injected inputs → byte-identical output.\n+- Negative: missing required field → rejected.\n+- Negative: unsupported `schema_version` → rejected.\n+- Negative: secret-pattern config key excluded from `config_snapshot`.\n+\n+## Risks / human decisions\n+\n+- Field ownership overlaps C (stop reason) and A/B (snapshots); rework expected when\n+  their contracts land — tracked, not hidden.\n",
              "additions": 60,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            }
          ]
        },

failure=None,\n         stop_reason=\"completed\",\n     )\n     fields.update(overrides)\n     return fields\n \n \n def _make_event(**overrides) -> RunEvent:\n     return RunEvent(**_event_kwargs(**overrides))\n \n \n def _write_to(tmp_path, event, name=\"manifest.json\"):\n     path = tmp_path / name\n     write_manifest(event, path)\n     return path\n \n \n def               "file": "src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\t\n+++ src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@\n+\"\"\"Deterministic run manifest recorder (docs/contracts/run-event.md).\n+\n+Records one analysis run as a JSON manifest so runs can be compared and\n+prompt/model changes can be gated. The recorder never reads the wall clock or a\n+random source: ``created_at``, ``run_id`` and ``version`` are supplied by the\n+caller, so identical inputs produce byte-identical output (\"byte-stable\n+manifest\"). Fields owned by other members (``stop_reason`` for C,\n+``prompt_hashes`` for B, ``evidence_snapshot`` for A) are stored opaquely and are\n+not validated here.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import json\n+import re\n+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\n+from datetime import UTC, datetime\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+SCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n+\n+RUN_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n+\n+_STRING_FIELDS = (\"run_id\", \"created_at\", \"version\", \"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n+\n+# Keys that must never reach disk: their names carry credentials or endpoints.\n+_SECRET_SUFFIXES = (\"_api_key\", \"_key\", \"_token\", \"_password\")\n+_SECRET_EXACT = (\"backend_url\",)\n+\n+\n+def _is_secret_key(name: str) -> bool:\n+    return name in _SECRET_EXACT or name.endswith(_SECRET_SUFFIXES)\n+\n+\n+@dataclass(frozen=True)\n+class RunEvent:\n+    \"\"\"One run's record. Every field is required except ``schema_version``.\n+\n+    Omitting a required field raises ``TypeError`` at construction, so the\n+    manifest cannot be built half-formed. ``frozen`` keeps a recorded event\n+    immutable; adjust by constructing a new one.\n+    \"\"\"\n+\n+    run_id: str\n+    created_at: str\n+    version: str\n+    ticker: str\n+    trade_date: str\n+    asset_type: str\n+    outcome: str | None\n+    config_snapshot: dict\n+    prompt_hashes: dict\n+    evidence_snapshot: dict | None\n+    usage: dict\n+    duration_seconds: float | None\n+    failure: str | None\n+    stop_reason: str | None\n+    schema_version: int = SCHEMA_VERSION\n+\n+\n+def build_run_id(variant: str, ticker: str, trade_date: str, repeat: int, at: datetime) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"A stable, filename-safe run id: ``<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<n>-<stamp>``.\n+\n+    ``at`` is passed in; the clock is never read here. Inputs are **lowercased**\n+    (not rejected) so the id always satisfies ``RUN_ID_PATTERN`` regardless of\n+    how the caller spelled the variant or ticker. ``at`` is normalized to UTC and\n+    rendered ``YYYYMMDDtHHMM`` (e.g. ``20261121t1200``).\n+    \"\"\"\n+    if at.tzinfo is None:\n+        at = at.replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n+    stamp = at.astimezone(UTC).strftime(\"%Y%m%dt%H%M\")\n+    return f\"{variant.lower()}-{ticker.lower()}-{trade_date}-r{repeat}-{stamp}\"\n+\n+\n+def _validated_manifest(event: RunEvent) -> dict:\n+    \"\"\"Validate ``event`` and return the dict that is written to disk.\"\"\"\n+    if event.schema_version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n+        raise ValueError(\n+            f\"unsupported schema_version {event.schema_version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\"\n+        )\n+    if not RUN_ID_PATTERN.match(event.run_id):\n+        raise ValueError(f\"invalid run_id {event.run_id!r}; must match {RUN_ID_PATTERN.pattern}\")\n+    for name in _STRING_FIELDS:\n+        value = getattr(event, name)\n+        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n+            raise ValueError(f\"required field {name!r} must be a non-empty string\")\n+\n+    manifest = asdict(event)\n+    manifest[\"config_snapshot\"] = {\n+        key: value\n+        for key, value in event.config_snapshot.items()\n+        if not _is_secret_key(key)\n+    }\n+    return manifest\n+\n+\n+def write_manifest(event: RunEvent, path) -> Path:\n+    \"\"\"Write ``event`` as a JSON manifest to ``path``; never overwrite.\n+\n+    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported schema version, an invalid\n+    ``run_id``, or an empty required string, and ``FileExistsError`` if ``path``\n+    already exists.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    path = Path(path)\n+    manifest = _validated_manifest(event)\n+    payload = json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n+    # \"x\" refuses to overwrite an existing file atomically.\n+    with open(path, \"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n+        handle.write(payload)\n+    return path\n+\n+\n+def read_manifest(path) -> dict:\n+    \"\"\"Read a manifest, rejecting an unsupported ``schema_version``.\"\"\"\n+    with open(Path(path), encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n+        manifest = json.load(handle)\n+    version = manifest.get(\"schema_version\")\n+    if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n+        raise ValueError(f\"unsupported schema_version {version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\")\n+    return manifest\n",
              "additions": 120,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },
            {

event = _make_event()\n     path = _write_to(tmp_path, event)\n \n     manifest = read_manifest(path)\n \n     assert set(manifest) == set(REQUIRED_FIELDS)\n     assert manifest[\"schema_version\"] == manifest[\"ticker\"] == \"NVDA\"\n     assert manifest[\"trade_date\"] == \"2026-11-20\"\n     assert manifest[\"asset_type\"] == \"stock\"\n     assert manifest[\"outcome\"] == \"Buy\"\n     assert manifest[\"config_snapshot\"] == {\"llm_provider\": \"openai\", \"deep_think_llm\": \"gpt-5\"}\n     assert manifest[\"prompt_hashes\"] == {\"market\": \"sha256:aaa\"}\n     assert
