            "output": "\"\"\"Reusable report-tree writer shared by the CLI and the programmatic API.\n\nWrites a run's per-section markdown (analysts, research, trading, risk,\nportfolio) plus a consolidated ``complete_report.md`` under ``save_path``. The\nCLI and ``TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports`` both call this, so a headless / API\nrun produces the same on-disk report tree a CLI run does.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.rating import run_rating\n\n\ndef analyst_names(keys) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The analysts as users select them: the sentiment analyst's key is \"social\".\"\"\"\n    return [\"sentiment\" if key == \"social\" else key for key in keys or []]\n\n\ndef _header(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> str:\n---date_window---\n\"\"\"Point-in-time rules shared by every dated path: data is served as of the run's date.\n\n- ``as_of`` / ``as_of_window`` clamp a date or window the model asks for to the\n  trade date, so no tool reaches a vendor with a later one, and always hand it\n  over as ``YYYY-MM-DD``: vendors compare dates as text.\n- ``in_window`` trims dated items (news, StockTwits, Reddit) to the analysis\n  window: timestamps normalized to UTC, the upper bound exclusive at midnight\n  after ``end``, and an undated item kept only when the window reaches the\n  present, since a backtest cannot prove it is not from the future (#1126, #1220).\n- ``coverage_gap`` reports a window a feed cannot reach as unavailable, not empty.\n- ``withhold_live_profile`` withholds present-day snapshots from historical runs.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import UTC, date, datetime, timedelta\n\n\ndef to_utc(dt: datetime) -> datetime:\n    \"\"\"Normalize a datetime to UTC-aware; a naive value is assumed to be UTC.\"\"\"\n    return dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC) if dt.tzinfo is None else dt.astimezone(UTC)\n\n\ndef in_window(pub_dt: datetime | None, start_dt: datetime, end_dt: datetime) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether an item belongs in the half-open window ``[start, end + 1 day)``.\n\n    ``pub_dt`` None means undated: kept only when the window reaches the present.\n    \"\"\"\n    end = to_utc(end_dt)\n    if pub_dt is not None:\n        return to_utc(start_dt) <= to_utc(pub_dt) < end + timedelta(days=1)\n    return end >= datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1)\n\n\ndef get_current_date() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Today's date, YYYY-MM-DD.\"\"\"\n    return date.today().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n\n\ndef is_historical(run_date) -> bool:\n",

            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Deterministic run manifest recorder (docs/contracts/run-event.md).\n\nRecords one analysis run as a JSON manifest so runs can be compared and\nprompt/model changes can be gated. The recorder never reads the wall clock or a\nrandom source: ``created_at``, ``run_id`` and ``version`` are supplied by the\ncaller, so identical inputs produce byte-identical output (\"byte-stable\nmanifest\"). Fields owned by other members (``stop_reason`` for C,\n``prompt_hashes`` for B, ``evidence_snapshot`` for A) are stored opaquely and are\nnot validated here.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n\nRUN_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n\n_STRING_FIELDS = (\"run_id\", \"created_at\", \"version\", \"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n\n# Keys that must never reach disk: their names carry credentials or endpoints.\n_SECRET_SUFFIXES = (\"_api_key\", \"_key\", \"_token\", \"_password\")\n_SECRET_EXACT = (\"backend_url\",)\n\n\ndef _is_secret_key(name: str) -> bool:\n    return name in _SECRET_EXACT or name.endswith(_SECRET_SUFFIXES)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass RunEvent:\n    \"\"\"One run's record. Every field is required except ``schema_version``.\n\n    Omitting a required field raises ``TypeError`` at construction, so the\n    manifest cannot be built half-formed. ``frozen`` keeps a recorded event\n    immutable; adjust by constructing a new one.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    run_id: str\n    created_at: str\n    version: str\n    ticker: str\n    trade_date: str\n    asset_type: str\n    outcome: str | None\n    config_snapshot: dict\n    prompt_hashes: dict\n    evidence_snapshot: dict | None\n    usage: dict\n    duration_seconds: float | None\n    failure: str | None\n    stop_reason: str | None\n    schema_version: int = SCHEMA_VERSION\n\n\ndef build_run_id(variant: str, ticker: str, trade_date: str, repeat: int, at: datetime) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A stable, filename-safe run id: ``<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<n>-<stamp>``.\n\n    ``at`` is passed in; the clock is never read here. Inputs are **lowercased**\n    (not rejected) so the id always satisfies ``RUN_ID_PATTERN`` regardless of\n    how the caller spelled the variant or ticker. ``at`` is normalized to UTC and\n    rendered ``YYYYMMDDtHHMM`` (e.g. ``20261121t1200``).\n    \"\"\"\n    if at.tzinfo is None:\n        at = at.replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n    stamp = at.astimezone(UTC).strftime(\"%Y%m%dt%H%M\")\n    return f\"{variant.lower()}-{ticker.lower()}-{trade_date}-r{repeat}-{stamp}\"\n\n\ndef _validated_manifest(event: RunEvent) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Validate ``event`` and return the dict that is written to disk.\"\"\"\n    if event.schema_version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"unsupported schema_version {event.schema_version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\"\n        )\n    if not RUN_ID_PATTERN.match(event.run_id):\n        raise ValueError(f\"invalid run_id {event.run_id!r}; must match {RUN_ID_PATTERN.pattern}\")\n    for name in _STRING_FIELDS:\n        value = getattr(event, name)\n        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n            raise ValueError(f\"required field {name!r} must be a non-empty string\")\n\n    manifest = asdict(event)\n    manifest[\"config_snapshot\"] = {\n        key: value\n        for key, value in event.config_snapshot.items()\n        if not _is_secret_key(key)\n    }\n    return manifest\n\n\ndef write_manifest(event: RunEvent, path) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write ``event`` as a JSON manifest to ``path``; never overwrite.\n\n    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported schema version, an invalid\n    ``run_id``, or an empty required string, and ``FileExistsError`` if ``path``\n    already exists.\n    \"\"\"\n    path = Path(path)\n    manifest = _validated_manifest(event)\n    payload = json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n    # \"x\" refuses to overwrite an existing file atomically.\n    with open(path, \"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        handle.write(payload)\n    return path\n\n\ndef read_manifest(path) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Read a manifest, rejecting an unsupported ``schema_version``.\"\"\"\n    with open(Path(path), encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        manifest = json.load(handle)\n    version = manifest.get(\"schema_version\")\n    if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n        raise ValueError(f\"unsupported schema_version {version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\")\n    return manifest\n",

              "file": "src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\t\n+++ src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\t\n@@ -1,120 +1,144 @@\n \"\"\"Deterministic run manifest recorder (docs/contracts/run-event.md).\n \n Records one analysis run as a JSON manifest so runs can be compared and\n prompt/model changes can be gated. The recorder never reads the wall clock or a\n random source: ``created_at``, ``run_id`` and ``version`` are supplied by the\n caller, so identical inputs produce byte-identical output (\"byte-stable\n manifest\"). Fields owned by other members (``stop_reason`` for C,\n ``prompt_hashes`` for B, ``evidence_snapshot`` for A) are stored opaquely and are\n not validated here.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import json\n import re\n from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from pathlib import Path\n \n SCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n \n RUN_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n \n _STRING_FIELDS = (\"run_id\", \"created_at\", \"version\", \"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n \n+_REQUIRED_FIELDS = (\n+    \"schema_version\",\n+    \"run_id\",\n+    \"created_at\",\n+    \"version\",\n+    \"ticker\",\n+    \"trade_date\",\n+    \"asset_type\",\n+    \"outcome\",\n+    \"config_snapshot\",\n+    \"prompt_hashes\",\n+    \"evidence_snapshot\",\n+    \"usage\",\n+    \"duration_seconds\",\n+    \"failure\",\n+    \"stop_reason\",\n+)\n+\n # Keys that must never reach disk: their names carry credentials or endpoints.\n _SECRET_SUFFIXES = (\"_api_key\", \"_key\", \"_token\", \"_password\")\n _SECRET_EXACT = (\"backend_url\",)\n \n \n def _is_secret_key(name: str) -> bool:\n     return name in _SECRET_EXACT or name.endswith(_SECRET_SUFFIXES)\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class RunEvent:\n     \"\"\"One run's record. Every field is required except ``schema_version``.\n \n     Omitting a required field raises ``TypeError`` at construction, so the\n     manifest cannot be built half-formed. ``frozen`` keeps a recorded event\n     immutable; adjust by constructing a new one.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     run_id: str\n     created_at: str\n     version: str\n     ticker: str\n     trade_date: str\n     asset_type: str\n     outcome: str | None\n     config_snapshot: dict\n     prompt_hashes: dict\n     evidence_snapshot: dict | None\n     usage: dict\n     duration_seconds: float | None\n     failure: str | None\n     stop_reason: str | None\n     schema_version: int = SCHEMA_VERSION\n \n \n def build_run_id(variant: str, ticker: str, trade_date: str, repeat: int, at: datetime) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A stable, filename-safe run id: ``<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<n>-<stamp>``.\n \n     ``at`` is passed in; the clock is never read here. Inputs are **lowercased**\n     (not rejected) so the id always satisfies ``RUN_ID_PATTERN`` regardless of\n     how the caller spelled the variant or ticker. ``at`` is normalized to UTC and\n-    rendered ``YYYYMMDDtHHMM`` (e.g. ``20261121t1200``).\n+    rendered ``YYYYMMDDtHHMM`` (e.g. ``20261121t1200``). ``repeat`` is a 1-based\n+    index, so values below 1 are rejected.\n     \"\"\"\n+    if repeat < 1:\n+        raise ValueError(f\"repeat must be >= 1, got {repeat!r}\")\n     if at.tzinfo is None:\n         at = at.replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n     stamp = at.astimezone(UTC).strftime(\"%Y%m%dt%H%M\")\n     return f\"{variant.lower()}-{ticker.lower()}-{trade_date}-r{repeat}-{stamp}\"\n \n \n def _validated_manifest(event: RunEvent) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Validate ``event`` and return the dict that is written to disk.\"\"\"\n     if event.schema_version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"unsupported schema_version {event.schema_version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\"\n         )\n     if not RUN_ID_PATTERN.match(event.run_id):\n         raise ValueError(f\"invalid run_id {event.run_id!r}; must match {RUN_ID_PATTERN.pattern}\")\n     for name in _STRING_FIELDS:\n         value = getattr(event, name)\n         if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n             raise ValueError(f\"required field {name!r} must be a non-empty string\")\n \n     manifest = asdict(event)\n     manifest[\"config_snapshot\"] = {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in event.config_snapshot.items()\n         if not _is_secret_key(key)\n     }\n     return manifest\n \n \n def write_manifest(event: RunEvent, path) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write ``event`` as a JSON manifest to ``path``; never overwrite.\n \n     Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported schema version, an invalid\n     ``run_id``, or an empty required string, and ``FileExistsError`` if ``path``\n     already exists.\n     \"\"\"\n     path = Path(path)\n     manifest = _validated_manifest(event)\n     payload = json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n     # \"x\" refuses to overwrite an existing file atomically.\n     with open(path, \"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n         handle.write(payload)\n     return path\n \n \n def read_manifest(path) -> dict:\n-    \"\"\"Read a manifest, rejecting an unsupported ``schema_version``.\"\"\"\n+    \"\"\"Read a manifest, rejecting an unsupported ``schema_version`` or a missing key.\"\"\"\n     with open(Path(path), encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n         manifest = json.load(handle)\n     version = manifest.get(\"schema_version\")\n     if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n         raise ValueError(f\"unsupported schema_version {version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\")\n+    missing = [name for name in _REQUIRED_FIELDS if name not in manifest]\n+    if missing:\n+        raise ValueError(f\"manifest missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}\")\n     return manifest\n",
              "additions": 26,
              "deletions": 2,
              "status": "modified"
            },

return path\n \n \n def test_round_trip_preserves_all_fields(tmp_path):\n     event = _make_event()\n     path = _write_to(tmp_path, event)\n \n     manifest = read_manifest(path)\n \n     assert set(manifest) == set(REQUIRED_FIELDS)\n     assert manifest[\"schema_version\"] == SCHEMA_VERSION\n     assert manifest[\"run_id\"] == \"run-abc-001\"\n     assert manifest[\"created_at\"] == assert manifest[\"prompt_hashes\"] == {\"market\": \"sha256:aaa\"}\n     assert manifest[\"evidence_snapshot\"] == {\"snapshot_id\": \"snap-1\"}\n     assert manifest[\"usage\"] == {\"llm_calls\": 12, \"tool_calls\": 7, \"tokens_in\": 1000, \"tokens_out\": 500}\n     assert manifest[\"duration_seconds\"] == 42.5\n     assert manifest[\"failure\"] is None\n     assert manifest[\"stop_reason\"] == \"completed\"\n \n \n def test_identical_inputs_produce_byte_identical_output(tmp_path):\n     path_a = _write_to(tmp_path, _make_event(), \"a.json\")\n     path_b = _write_to(tmp_path, _make_event(), \"b.json\")\n \n     assert path_a.read_bytes() == path_b.read_bytes()\n \n \n def test_missing_required_field_is_rejected():\n     fields = _event_kwargs()\n     del fields[\"version\"]\n     with           "text": "<path>/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/.agent/rules.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Project Covenant (.agent/rules.md)\n2: \n3: Binding rules for how the team and the coding agent work on this repository.\n4: Changes to this file require human approval.\n5: \n6: ## Abstraction limits\n7: \n8: - Prefer small, single-responsibility modules over deep inheritance.\n9: - No new abstraction unless it removes real duplication or enforces an invariant.\n10: \n11: ## Dependency constraints\n12: \n13: - Only the data layer may import vendor libraries (INV-001).\n14: - New third-party dependencies require justification in `docs/debt-register.md`\n15:   and must pass the dependency-check gate.\n16: \n17: ## Test independence\n18: \n19: - Tests must not depend on ordering or on each other.\n20: - At least **one negative test per feature** (a test that fails when the\n21:   feature/invariant is violated).\n22: \n23: ## Safety-critical changes\n24: \n25: - Changing safety-critical code (`dataflows/**`, `agents/structured.py`,\n26:   `agents/rating.py`, `default_config.py` env overrides, permission files,\n27:   requirements registry, CI workflow) requires an **architecture decision** and\n28:   **human approval** before merge.\n29: \n30: ## Context freshness\n31: \n32: - These rules and the architecture artifacts are updated within **one sprint**\n33:   of a requirements change; stale context is a defect.\n\n(End of file - total 33 lines)\n</content>",

          "text": "<path>/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/not_delivered/CS5351-2026-2027-project.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # CS5351 — Agentic Software Engineering Project\n2: \n3: **Project Requirement Sheet**\n4: \n5: > **Core expectation:** Design, build, verify, and maintain an AI-enabled software application using an AI coding agent under auditable human supervision.\n6: \n7: ## Document Contents\n8: \n9: - 1. Project Overview\n10: - 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n11: - 3. Deliverables\n12: - 4. Submission Format\n13: - 5. Required Repository Structure\n14: - 6. Blocking-Gate Requirements\n15: \n16: > **Submission model:** One repository plus five annotated agent-session transcripts and one process report. The AI-use log is mandatory and must be up to date at submission.\n17: \n18: ---\n19: \n20: ## 1. Project Overview\n21: \n22: Your team will design, build, and maintain a software application that contains an AI component, using an AI coding agent under human supervision. The project applies the full software engineering lifecycle taught in this course: you will specify requirements in machine-readable form, produce architecture artifacts that constrain what the coding agent may and may not do, govern the agent's code generation and verification, and demonstrate that you can review, debug, and maintain AI-generated code.\n23: \n24: Your application is your own choice — it must contain at least one genuine AI component (an LLM-powered feature, a retrieval/augmentation pipeline, an AI-assisted decision path, etc.) and at least one safety-relevant boundary where the AI's output must be constrained by deterministic code. The reference implementation shown in lectures (VHIS) is a pattern to follow, not a project to extend.\n25: \n26: ---\n27: \n28: ## 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n29: \n30: Your team should rotate roles so that students can experience different responsibilities in producing software using an AI coding agent, project management, or software engineering processes.\n31: \n32: ### Free Runner and Strong Contributor\n33: \n34: - Some students may be less motivated or less committed, while some other students may be much more engaged.\n35: - Your report should include a section of relative contributions. The average contribution is 1.0; students with less contribution can be assigned a lower weight, and students with stronger contributions will be assigned a higher weight.\n36: \n37: ---\n38: \n39: ## 3. Deliverables\n40: \n41: ### D1 — Requirements (machine-readable)\n42: \n43: Produce a machine-readable product requirements document and a consolidated requirements registry, both in YAML, under `./docs/req/` where `.` is the project root.\n44: \n45: - `docs/req/requirements.yaml` — every requirement as an entry with an ID, type, statement, and a machine-checkable fit criterion, plus priority. Types cover functional behavior, invariants (non-negotiable rules with zero-tolerance fit criteria), quality attributes, performance, cost, governance, and security. Non-functional requirements are expressed as metric + threshold + verification. Prioritization uses MoSCoW, and states the tradeoff explicitly. Requirements discovered through analysis of any existing system or repository are included and linked to their sources.\n46: - `docs/req/req-schema.json` — the schema used by CI in GitHub to validate the registry as a date.\n47: \n48: ### D2 — Architecture Artifacts (all as markdown `.md` files)\n49: \n50: Produce the architecture documentation as a single artifact per file in `./docs/architecture/`, with `.` as the project root.\n51: \n52: 1. **Architecture blueprint** — the master constraint document that the Plan agent reads: scope, architectural drivers, system boundaries, components, authority boundaries (what is advisory vs. authoritative), agent workflow, permissions, verification strategy, observability, and change policy.\n53: 2. **Architecture Decision Record** — the chosen architecture, the alternatives considered, the rationale, consequences, and conditions that would reopen the decision. It should also present the architectural design process. In addition, for your AI component, present your designed layered context structure that the AI receives on every turn (e.g., identity, standing constraints, retrieved knowledge, conversation history, resumable state, and the current task), the assembly pipeline (e.g., deduplicate, prioritize, budget, compact, assemble), the token-budget cap with its compaction threshold, and the policy for re-injecting critical constraints after compaction.\n54: 3. **Invariant register** — every invariant with its statement, source requirement ID, enforcing component, verification method, and an operational fallback if it is ever violated (a concrete action, not \"fix the bug\").\n55: 4. **Trace matrix** — every requirement mapped to its enforcing component, its test/evidence, and its runtime monitor.\n56: 5. **Memory/state design** — what state survives across sessions, interruptions, and versions; write and retrieval policy; ownership; retention; privacy.\n57: 6. **Permission model** — file-level read/write rights for each AI coding agent's role; default is no read, no write; every path is explicitly whitelisted.\n58: 7. **Runtime policy catalog** — what the system does when each degraded or failure path is triggered.\n59: 8. **Candidate evaluation table** — the comparison that justifies the chosen architecture.\n60: 9. *[optional]* **Evaluation logbook** — the accumulated evidence behind the architecture choices.\n61: 10. *[optional]* **Risk list** — assumptions that could become defects, with review triggers.\n62: 11. *[optional]* **Option ledger** — rejected architectural options and when they should be reconsidered.\n63: \n64: ### D3 — Coding Governance\n65: \n66: Produce the governance files that control how the AI coding agent plans and builds the application:\n67: \n68: - `AGENTS.md` (at the project root directory) — the single entry point the coding agent reads. It declares the build target, the reading order for architecture artifacts, the code baseline, what is readable/modifiable/frozen, the module organization, the integration contracts between modules, and the verification requirements that the generated code must satisfy.\n69: - `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` — module organization rules: each architectural element maps to exactly one module; new work extends the existing baseline, never replaces it; every module and function references the architecture decision and invariant it implements; authority boundaries.\n70: - `docs/code-governance/mcp-tool-manifest.md` — the tools the coding agent may call, and which roles may call them.\n71: - `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` — the project-level permission model in machine-readable form, with guard rules and enforcement mechanisms.\n72: - `.opencode/rules.md` — the project-level always-on behavioral rules for the coding agent. Human-only file.\n73: - `.agent/rules.md` — the project covenant: abstraction limits, dependency constraints, test independence (at least one negative test per feature), the rule that changing safety-critical code requires an architecture decision and human approval, and context freshness (rules updated within one sprint of a requirements change).\n74: \n75: ### D4 — Verification Governance (as markdown `.md` files)\n76: \n77: Produce the verification rules that the verification agent applies, and the QA records the team maintains:\n78: \n79: - `docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md` — every fit criterion has at least one test; every invariant has at least one test that fails when the invariant is violated; every test references the requirement or invariant it verifies; every new round of work runs all previous rounds' test suites with zero regressions.\n80: - Verification is three-tiered: structural (imports, module boundaries, permissions, architectural fitness functions), regression (all prior suites pass), and behavioral (quality thresholds such as faithfulness/relevance scores, zero safety escapes).\n81: - `docs/review-memo.md` — a review memo per pull request, covering spec alignment, architecture alignment, code and test quality, and operational metadata, with security and efficiency checked throughout, ending in a verdict of APPROVE, CHANGES REQUIRED, or REJECT.\n82: - `docs/debt-register.md` — technical debt tracked across the AI-era categories: prompt rot, hallucinated dependencies, untouchable code, hidden dependencies, agent-induced bloat, evaluation debt, guardrail debt, and human/cognitive debt.\n83: - `docs/bug-diary.md` — a diary entry per significant bug: symptom, reproduction, classification, root cause, fix, and which invariant gap it exposed.\n84: \n85: ### D5 — Agent Session Transcripts\n86: \n87: One full, raw transcript of an AI coding agent session to build the system implementation from scratch. Each transcript is annotated with the student team members' marked interventions and a rationale for each, showing where the team interrupted, redirected, approved, or rejected the agent's work.\n88: \n89: Collectively, the transcripts must demonstrate the entire supervised pipeline: requirements classification, architecture candidate generation and evaluation, plan approval before code, build, verification compliance, and architecture revision based on test evidence.\n90: \n91: ### D6 — Report (as a single markdown `.md` file)\n92: \n93: This is the project summary report. The report should list all students' names and student numbers, as well as the whole team's relative contribution (see the following example). It should contain at most 10,000 words (excluding diagrams) and contain more than 15 pages in Point 12 with single-line spacing. It should present the team's software engineering process and how the team optimizes it. It should also include each member's self-reflection (one short (e.g., 300-500 words) paragraph per student, with name and student ID. Cover process quality evidence (requirement volatility, defect trends, ambiguity resolution), how the team kept artifacts co-evolving when anything changed, and what human oversight caught that the agent did not.\n94: \n95: #### Tips: Contributions of Team Members\n96: \n97: > Suggest using contributed efforts (e.g., pre-agreed manhours or story points) in determining the relative contributions of team members (as all of us are students).\n98: >\n99: > - Teams can decide their measures on contributions. The team should reward students who take up difficult tasks and project management.\n100: >\n101: > *Actual productive hours spent on the project (hrs) or story points*\n102: \n103: | Name | Sprint 1 | Sprint 2 | Sprint 3 | Sprint 4 | Sprint 5 | Total |\n104: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n105: | Zhou, A | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 60 |\n106: | Wang, B | 12 | 10 | 5 | 20 | 8 | 55 |\n107: | Chan, C | 5 | 10 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 35 |\n108: \n109: Mean contribution = (60 + 55 + 35) / 3 = 50\n110: \n111: - Zhou: 60 / Mean contribution = 60 / 50 = 1.2\n112: - Wang: 55 / Mean contribution = 55 / 50 = 1.1\n113: - Chan: 35 / Mean contribution = 35 / 50 = 0.7\n114: \n115: > If the project gets 69 (in the range of B+ [66.5, 69.5)), then Zhou gets 82.8 (A+), Wang gets 75.9 (A), and Chan gets 48.3 (C)\n116: \n117: - Marks will be pro-rated accordingly. [bounded for extreme, e.g., the presence of a free rider]\n118: - Present the contributions in the final report.\n119: - Respect your teammates, as not everyone wants A+.\n120: \n121: ### D7 — GitHub Repository (in GitHub)\n122: \n123: The team's repository contains the source code, test cases, a CI/CD pipeline with implemented blocking gates, branch protection, and a meaningful commit history. The repository README states the design of the blocking gates and\n124: \n125: ### D8 — Source and Tests\n126: \n127: `src/` and `test/` directories with the full application source code and test cases. Module names match architectural elements. Test layout separates deterministic offline tests from live tests that require API access.\n128: \n129: ### D9 — Prompt (static) (a markdown file in project root directory)\n130: \n131: A single static prompt file, `./Prompt.md`. Once the coding agent starts with `AGENTS.md`, this is the one prompt to read. It instructs the agent to begin by producing an execution plan (traceability, interface contract, scope boundaries, testing strategy, steps) and to stop for human approval before generating any code, then proceed through build and self-verification with human gates at each stage. The prompt is the launch instruction — it does not run the agent unattended to completion.\n132: \n133: ---\n134: \n135: ## 4. Submission Format\n136: \n137: Submit a zip containing the documents in the project directory structure as listed in Section 5 of this document.\n138: \n139: Repository README must include:\n140: \n141: - The project's purpose and architecture in a few paragraphs\n142: - The organization of the project files\n143: - How to run the offline tests, the live tests, and the full suite\n144: - GitHub repo that contains the real GitHub project\n145: \n146: ---\n147: \n148: ## 5. Required Repository Structure\n149: \n150: ```text\n151: <team-app>/\n152: ├── README.md                          ← project intro\n153: ├── AGENTS.md                          ← coding-agent governance (D3)\n154: ├── architecture-blueprint.md          ← master constraint document (D2.1)\n155: ├── Prompt.md                          ← static startup prompt (D9)\n156: ├── Report.md                          ← process report + reflections (D6)\n157: ├── docs/\n158: │   ├── req/\n159: │   │   ├── requirements.yaml          ← machine-readable PRD (D1)\n160: │   │   └── req-schema.json            ← CI validation schema (D1)\n161: │   ├── architecture/                  ← 11 artifact types (D2)\n162: │   │   ├── adr/001-<choice>.md\n163: │   │   ├── invariants.md\n164: │   │   ├── trace-matrix.md\n165: │   │   ├── memory-design.md\n166: │   │   ├── option-ledger.md\n167: │   │   ├── permission-model.md\n168: │   │   ├── evaluation-logbook.md\n169: │   │   ├── risk-list.md\n170: │   │   ├── evaluation-table.md\n171: │   │   └── runtime-policy-catalog.md\n172: │   ├── code-governance/               ← (D3, D4)\n173: │   │   ├── structural-constraints.md\n174: │   │   ├── verification-constraints.md\n175: │   │   └── mcp-tool-manifest.md\n176: │   ├── ai-use-log.yaml                ← (D1)\n177: │   ├── review-memo.md                 ← review records (D4)\n178: │   ├── debt-register.md               ← (D4)\n179: │   └── bug-diary.md                   ← (D4)\n180: ├── .opencode/\n181: │   ├── permissions.jsonc              ← machine-readable permissions (D3)\n182: │   └── rules.md                       ← always-on behavioral rules (D3)\n183: ├── .agent/\n184: │   └── rules.md                       ← project covenant (D3)\n185: ├── .github/workflows/\n186: │   └── ci.yml                         ← blocking gates (D4/D7)\n187: ├── prompts/\n188: │   ├── prompt_v1.0.yaml               ← versioned runtime prompts\n189: │   └── prompt_v1.1.yaml\n190: ├── src/                               ← full source (D8)\n191: ├── test/\n192: │   ├── offline/                       ← deterministic tests (D4/D8)\n193: │   └── live/                          ← API-dependent tests\n194: └── transcripts/\n195:     ├── <student-id>-<student-name>.md ← student annotated transcripts (D5)\n196:     └── ...\n197: ```\n198: \n199: ---\n200: \n201: ## 6. Blocking-Gate Requirements (D7)\n202: \n203: The CI/CD pipeline must implement the following blocking gates.\n204: \n205: 1. **Test approval gate** — no code change merges unless the tests for the change were approved before implementation began.\n206: 2. **Static analysis gates** — lint, type-checking, and dependency checks run on every commit; contract, security, API-surface, and permission checks run on any pull request touching safety-relevant paths.\n207: 3. **Schema gate** — the requirements registry validates against its JSON schema.\n208: 4. **Semantic evaluation gate** — for any prompt or model change, the pipeline replays a fixed evaluation set against quality thresholds before the change can reach production; if a threshold fails, the change is blocked and reported.\n209: 5. **Regression gate** — every change runs the full prior test suites; any regression blocks the merge.\n210: 6. **AI-use log gate** — a pull request that changes code or prompts without updating the AI-use log is blocked.\n211: \n212: **Branch protection:** Branch protection must require passing CI, and changes to safety-critical paths must require human review with an accompanying architecture decision.\n213: \n214: ---\n215: \n216: *Transcribed from `CS5351-2026-2027-project.pdf` (10 pages). Wording follows the source document; page headers, footers, and the \"Page N\" markers have been removed. Where the source is internally inconsistent (e.g., the row for Chan, C in the contributions table lists sprint values summing to 30 against a stated total of 35; the D7 paragraph ends mid-sentence), the text has been reproduced as printed rather than corrected.*\n\n(End of file - total 216 lines)\n</content>",

              "patch": "Index: docs/plans/E-ai-use-log-gate.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/plans/E-ai-use-log-gate.md\t\n+++ docs/plans/E-ai-use-log-gate.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@\n+# Plan — AI-use log gate (Gate 1)\n+\n+Member E. Approved by human before implementation (CS5351 D7 gate 6). Scope is the\n+first minimal CI gate only; later gates (schema, semantics, test-approval) are out of\n+scope for this step.\n+\n+## Traceability\n+- D7 §6.6 — AI-use log gate: a PR that changes code/prompts/CI without updating\n+  `docs/ai-use-log.yaml` is blocked.\n+- `.agent/rules.md` — at least one negative test per feature.\n+- REQ/INV ids: not yet assigned (`docs/req/` [TBD]); tests name the gate in docstrings.\n+\n+## Files\n+1. `scripts/ci_gates.py` — helpers only: three-dot diff (`ACMRD`), path gating,\n+   YAML load, entry-id extraction, entry validation. Constants `REQUIRED_FIELDS`,\n+   `GATED_PREFIXES`.\n+2. `scripts/check_ai_use_log.py` — CLI `base head [pr_id]`. Docs-only → pass; gated\n+   change requires ≥1 new entry id at head absent at base, each validating against\n+   `REQUIRED_FIELDS`; nonzero exit on failure.\n+3. `test/offline/test_ci_gates.py` — offline tests including a **real temporary git\n+   repo** exercising the actual base..head diff, plus synthetic-list negative cases.\n+4. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add `ai-use-log` job (pull_request only, `fetch-depth: 0`,\n+   base = `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`, head = `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`,\n+   PR number = `github.event.pull_request.number`); extend `lint` to include `scripts`.\n+5. `docs/ai-use-log.yaml` — one real entry for this PR; fix stale \"three real entries\"\n+   header comment.\n+6. `pyproject.toml` — add `PyYAML>=6.0` to the `dev` extra so the gate is importable in CI.\n+\n+## Exact behavior\n+- Gated prefixes: `src/`, `prompts/`, `scripts/`, `test/`, `tests/`, `.github/`.\n+- Diff: `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRD <base>...<head>` (three-dot; includes\n+  deletions).\n+- Pass if no gated path changed (docs-only).\n+- Required entry fields: `id, pr_id, date, task, agent, model, human_reviewed,\n+  changes_accepted`; `human_reviewed` must be `true`; `changes_accepted` must be bool.\n+- `human_reviewed: true` is only set in the log if the human reviews the final PR\n+  before merge; otherwise it stays `false` and the gate blocks. GitHub Actions does\n+  not run locally and is not claimed to have run.\n+\n+## Tests\n+- `test_missing_entry_fails` — gated change, no new id → fail.\n+- `test_new_entry_passes` — gated change, valid new entry → pass.\n+- `test_docs_only_passes` — only `docs/` changed → pass.\n+- `test_edited_old_entry_fails` — edit an existing entry, no new id → fail.\n+- `test_missing_required_field_fails` — new id missing a field → fail.\n+- `test_real_git_repo_diff` — build a temp repo, commit a gated file, exercise the real\n+  `changed_paths()` three-dot diff and deletions.\n+\n+## Commands\n+```\n+pytest test/offline/test_ci_gates.py -q\n+pytest -q\n+ruff check src tests test scripts\n+python -c \"import yaml;d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'));print(list(d['jobs']))\"\n+```\n",
              "additions": 55,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },

              "patch": "Index: pyproject.toml\n===================================================================\n--- pyproject.toml\t\n+++ pyproject.toml\t\n@@ -1,90 +1,91 @@\n [build-system]\n requires = [\"setuptools>=61.0\"]\n build-backend = \"setuptools.build_meta\"\n \n [project]\n name = \"tradingagents\"\n dynamic = [\"version\"]\n description = \"TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework\"\n readme = \"README.md\"\n requires-python = \">=3.11\"\n dependencies = [\n     \"cryptography>=42.0\",\n     \"langchain-core>=1.6.5\",\n     \"langchain-anthropic>=1.7.4\",\n     \"langchain-google-genai>=4.4.0\",\n     \"langchain-openai>=1.6.6\",\n     \"langgraph>=1.2.12\",\n     \"langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite>=3.1.1\",\n     \"markdown-it-py>=4.0\",\n     \"packaging>=24.0\",\n     \"pandas>=3.0.6\",\n     \"python-dotenv>=1.0.0\",\n     \"pytz>=2025.2\",\n     \"questionary>=2.1.0\",\n     \"requests>=2.32.4\",\n     \"rich>=14.0.0\",\n     \"typer>=0.21.0\",\n     \"stockstats>=0.6.5\",\n     \"typing-extensions>=4.14.0\",\n     \"yfinance>=1.7.0\",\n ]\n \n [project.optional-dependencies]\n dev = [\n     \"ruff>=0.16\",\n     \"pytest>=8.0\",\n     \"pytest-subtests>=0.13\",\n+    \"PyYAML>=6.0\",\n ]\n # Amazon Bedrock support (AWS SigV4 auth + boto3). Optional so the core install\n # stays lean: pip install \"tradingagents[bedrock]\".\n bedrock = [\n     \"langchain-aws>=1.7.9\",\n ]\n \n [project.scripts]\n tradingagents = \"cli.main:app\"\n \n [tool.setuptools.dynamic]\n version = {attr = \"tradingagents.__version__\"}\n \n [tool.setuptools.packages.find]\n where = [\"src\"]\n include = [\"tradingagents*\", \"cli*\"]\n \n [tool.setuptools.package-data]\n cli = [\"static/*\"]\n tradingagents = [\"assets/*.svg\"]\n \n [tool.pytest.ini_options]\n testpaths = [\"tests\", \"test\"]\n addopts = \"-ra --strict-markers -m \\\"not integration\\\"\"\n markers = [\n     \"unit: fast isolated unit tests\",\n     \"integration: tests requiring external services; run only when asked for, with -m integration\",\n     \"smoke: quick sanity-check tests\",\n ]\n filterwarnings = [\n     \"ignore::DeprecationWarning\",\n ]\n \n [tool.ruff]\n line-length = 100\n target-version = \"py311\"\n extend-exclude = [\"results\"]\n \n [tool.ruff.lint]\n # Standard \"good defaults\" rule set (pyflakes + pycodestyle + isort + bugbear +\n # pyupgrade + comprehensions/simplify). Line length (E501) and layout are owned\n # by the formatter; whole-repo `ruff format` adoption is deferred until the\n # open-PR backlog clears, to avoid mass merge conflicts.\n select = [\"E\", \"W\", \"F\", \"I\", \"B\", \"UP\", \"C4\", \"SIM\"]\n ignore = [\"E501\"]\n \n [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]\n \"**/__init__.py\" = [\"F401\"]   # intentional re-exports\n \n [tool.ruff.lint.isort]\n # Keep multiple aliased names from one module in a single combined import block\n # (e.g. the vendor imports in router.py) instead of one statement per name.\n combine-as-imports = true\n",

              "file": "scripts/check_ai_use_log.py",
              "patch": "Index: scripts/check_ai_use_log.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/check_ai_use_log.py\t\n+++ scripts/check_ai_use_log.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@\n+\"\"\"CLI entry point for the AI-use log gate (D7 §6.6).\n+\n+Usage:\n+    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha> [<pr_id>]\n+\n+Exit 0 when the PR passes, exit 1 (with a reason) when it is blocked. A PR that\n+touches code/prompts/scripts/tests/CI must add at least one new entry id to\n+``docs/ai-use-log.yaml`` that is not present at the base commit; every new entry\n+must carry the required fields. Docs-only PRs pass.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import subprocess\n+import sys\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+from ci_gates import (\n+    changed_paths,\n+    entry_ids,\n+    gated_changes,\n+    load_entries,\n+    validate_entry,\n+)\n+\n+LOG_PATH = \"docs/ai-use-log.yaml\"\n+\n+\n+def _read_at(ref: str, path: str) -> str:\n+    result = subprocess.run(\n+        [\"git\", \"show\", f\"{ref}:{path}\"],\n+        capture_output=True,\n+        text=True,\n+    )\n+    if result.returncode != 0:\n+        return \"\"\n+    return result.stdout\n+\n+\n+def _read_worktree(path: str) -> str:\n+    file_path = Path(path)\n+    if not file_path.exists():\n+        return \"\"\n+    return file_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n+\n+\n+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n+    if len(argv) < 3:\n+        print(\"usage: check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha> [<pr_id>]\", file=sys.stderr)\n+        return 2\n+    base, head = argv[1], argv[2]\n+    pr_id = argv[3] if len(argv) > 3 else \"unknown\"\n+\n+    changed = changed_paths(base, head)\n+    gated = gated_changes(changed)\n+    if not gated:\n+        print(f\"[ai-use-log] docs-only PR #{pr_id}: no code/prompt/CI changes, skipping\")\n+        return 0\n+\n+    base_entries = load_entries(_read_at(base, LOG_PATH))\n+    head_entries = load_entries(_read_worktree(LOG_PATH))\n+\n+    base_ids = entry_ids(base_entries)\n+    head_ids = entry_ids(head_entries)\n+    new_ids = head_ids - base_ids\n+\n+    if not new_ids:\n+        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: gated paths changed but no new log entry id added.\")\n+        print(\"  gated paths:\")\n+        for path in gated:\n+            print(f\"    - {path}\")\n+        return 1\n+\n+    problems: dict[str, list[str]] = {}\n+    for entry in head_entries:\n+        if entry.get(\"id\") in new_ids:\n+            entry_problems = validate_entry(entry)\n+            if entry_problems:\n+                problems[str(entry.get(\"id\"))] = entry_problems\n+\n+    if problems:\n+        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: new entries fail validation.\")\n+        for entry_id, reasons in problems.items():\n+            print(f\"  - {entry_id}: {', '.join(reasons)}\")\n+        return 1\n+\n+    print(f\"[ai-use-log] OK: new entry id(s) {sorted(new_ids)} for PR #{pr_id}\")\n+    return 0\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",
              "additions": 92,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },
            {
              "file": "scripts/ci_gates.py",
              "patch": "Index: scripts/ci_gates.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/ci_gates.py\t\n+++ scripts/ci_gates.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@\n+\"\"\"Helpers for the minimal CI gates (see docs/plans/E-ai-use-log-gate.md).\n+\n+Only the pieces the AI-use log gate needs: a three-dot git diff, path gating, YAML\n+loading, and entry validation. Stdlib + PyYAML only; no third-party imports beyond\n+``yaml``.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import subprocess\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+import yaml\n+\n+GATED_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = (\n+    \"src/\",\n+    \"prompts/\",\n+    \"scripts/\",\n+    \"test/\",\n+    \"tests/\",\n+    \".github/\",\n+)\n+\n+REQUIRED_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = (\n+    \"id\",\n+    \"pr_id\",\n+    \"date\",\n+    \"task\",\n+    \"agent\",\n+    \"model\",\n+    \"human_reviewed\",\n+    \"changes_accepted\",\n+)\n+\n+\n+def changed_paths(base: str, head: str, repo: str | Path = \".\") -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"Return paths changed between ``base`` and ``head`` using a three-dot diff.\n+\n+    Three dots compare against the merge-base, so the diff is exactly the PR's own\n+    changes. ``--diff-filter=ACMRD`` includes deletions as well as additions,\n+    modifications, copies and renames.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    result = subprocess.run(\n+        [\"git\", \"diff\", \"--name-only\", \"--diff-filter=ACMRD\", f\"{base}...{head}\"],\n+        cwd=str(repo),\n+        capture_output=True,\n+        text=True,\n+        check=True,\n+    )\n+    return [line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n+\n+\n+def is_gated(path: str, prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = GATED_PREFIXES) -> bool:\n+    return any(path.startswith(prefix) for prefix in prefixes)\n+\n+\n+def gated_changes(paths: list[str], prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = GATED_PREFIXES) -> list[str]:\n+    return [path for path in paths if is_gated(path, prefixes)]\n+\n+\n+def load_entries(text: str) -> list[dict]:\n+    \"\"\"Parse the AI-use log text and return its ``entries`` list (empty if absent).\"\"\"\n+    data = yaml.safe_load(text) or {}\n+    entries = data.get(\"entries\") or []\n+    return list(entries)\n+\n+\n+def entry_ids(entries: list[dict]) -> set[str]:\n+    return {entry.get(\"id\") for entry in entries if entry.get(\"id\")}\n+\n+\n+def validate_entry(entry: dict) -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"Return the reasons ``entry`` is invalid (empty list means valid).\n+\n+    Field presence is checked for every required field; value semantics are checked\n+    for the two gate-critical booleans.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    problems: list[str] = []\n+    for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:\n+        if field not in entry:\n+            problems.append(f\"missing field: {field}\")\n+    if entry.get(\"human_reviewed\") is not True:\n+        problems.append(\"human_reviewed must be true\")\n+    if not isinstance(entry.get(\"changes_accepted\"), bool):\n+        problems.append(\"changes_accepted must be a boolean\")\n+    return problems\n",
              "additions": 86,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },
            {
              "file": "test/offline/test_ci_gates.py",
              "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_ci_gates.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_ci_gates.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_ci_gates.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@\n+\"\"\"Offline tests for the AI-use log gate (D7 §6.6; docs/plans/E-ai-use-log-gate.md).\n+\n+Covers the pure helpers (synthetic path lists and YAML strings) and one test that\n+builds a real temporary git repo to exercise the actual three-dot ``base...head``\n+diff, including a deletion. No network, stdlib + PyYAML only.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+import subprocess\n+import sys\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / \"scripts\"))\n+\n+from ci_gates import (  # noqa: E402\n+    GATED_PREFIXES,\n+    changed_paths,\n+    entry_ids,\n+    gated_changes,\n+    load_entries,\n+    validate_entry,\n+)\n+\n+VALID_ENTRY = \"\"\"\n+- id: \"60252993-linan-ai-use-99\"\n+  pr_id: \"N/A\"\n+  date: \"2026-11-22\"\n+  task: \"example task\"\n+  agent: \"opencode\"\n+  model: \"custom-foundry/CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash\"\n+  human_reviewed: true\n+  changes_accepted: true\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+OLD_ENTRY = \"\"\"\n+- id: \"60252993-linan-ai-use-01\"\n+  pr_id: \"N/A\"\n+  date: \"2026-11-20\"\n+  task: \"old task\"\n+  agent: \"opencode\"\n+  model: \"custom-foundry/CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash\"\n+  human_reviewed: true\n+  changes_accepted: true\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+\n+def _log(*entries: str) -> str:\n+    return \"entries:\\n\" + \"\".join(entries)\n+\n+\n+def _gate(base_text: str, head_text: str, changed: list[str]) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n+    \"\"\"Mirror check_ai_use_log.main's decision on in-memory text.\n+\n+    Returns (passed, reason). Uses the same helpers the CLI uses so the logic and\n+    the tests cannot drift.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    gated = gated_changes(changed)\n+    if not gated:\n+        return True, \"docs-only\"\n+    base_ids = entry_ids(load_entries(base_text))\n+    head_entries = load_entries(head_text)\n+    new_ids = entry_ids(head_entries) - base_ids\n+    if not new_ids:\n+        return False, \"no new entry id\"\n+    for entry in head_entries:\n+        if entry.get(\"id\") in new_ids and validate_entry(entry):\n+            return False, f\"invalid entry {entry.get('id')}\"\n+    return True, \"ok\"\n+\n+\n+def test_missing_entry_fails():\n+    passed, reason = _gate(_log(OLD_ENTRY), _log(OLD_ENTRY), [\"src/tradingagents/x.py\"])\n+    assert passed is False\n+    assert reason == \"no new entry id\"\n+\n+\n+def test_new_entry_passes():\n+    passed, _ = _gate(_log(OLD_ENTRY), _log(OLD_ENTRY, VALID_ENTRY), [\"src/tradingagents/x.py\"])\n+    assert passed is True\n+\n+\n+def               "content": "\"\"\"Helpers for the minimal CI gates (see docs/plans/E-ai-use-log-gate.md).\n\nOnly the pieces the AI-use log gate needs: a three-dot git diff, path gating, YAML\nloading, and entry validation. Stdlib + PyYAML only; no third-party imports beyond\n``yaml``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport yaml\n\nGATED_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = (\n    \"src/\",\n    \"prompts/\",\n    \"scripts/\",\n    \"test/\",\n    \"tests/\",\n    \".github/\",\n)\n\nREQUIRED_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = (\n    \"id\",\n    \"pr_id\",\n    \"date\",\n    \"task\",\n    \"agent\",\n    \"model\",\n    \"human_reviewed\",\n    \"changes_accepted\",\n)\n\n\ndef changed_paths(base: str, head: str, repo: str | Path = \".\") -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return paths changed between ``base`` and ``head`` using a three-dot diff.\n\n    Three dots compare against the merge-base, so the diff is exactly the PR's own\n    changes. ``--diff-filter=ACMRD`` includes deletions as well as additions,\n    modifications, copies and renames.\n    \"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", \"diff\", \"--name-only\", \"--diff-filter=ACMRD\", f\"{base}...{head}\"],\n        cwd=str(repo),\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        check=True,\n    )\n    return [line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n\n\ndef is_gated(path: str, prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = GATED_PREFIXES) -> bool:\n    return any(path.startswith(prefix) for prefix in prefixes)\n\n\ndef gated_changes(paths: list[str], prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = GATED_PREFIXES) -> list[str]:\n    return [path for path in paths if is_gated(path, prefixes)]\n\n\ndef load_entries(text: str) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Parse the AI-use log text and return its ``entries`` list (empty if absent).\"\"\"\n    data = yaml.safe_load(text) or {}\n    entries = data.get(\"entries\") or []\n    return list(entries)\n\n\ndef entry_ids(entries: list[dict]) -> set[str]:\n    return {entry.get(\"id\") for entry in entries if entry.get(\"id\")}\n\n\ndef validate_entry(entry: dict) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return the reasons ``entry`` is invalid (empty list means valid).\n\n    Field presence is checked for every required field; value semantics are checked\n    for the two gate-critical booleans.\n    \"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:\n        if field not in entry:\n            problems.append(f\"missing field: {field}\")\n    if entry.get(\"human_reviewed\") is not True:\n        problems.append(\"human_reviewed must be true\")\n    if not isinstance(entry.get(\"changes_accepted\"), bool):\n        problems.append(\"changes_accepted must be a boolean\")\n    return problems\n",

            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"CLI entry point for the AI-use log gate (D7 §6.6).\n\nUsage:\n    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha> [<pr_id>]\n\nExit 0 when the PR passes, exit 1 (with a reason) when it is blocked. A PR that\ntouches code/prompts/scripts/tests/CI must add at least one new entry id to\n``docs/ai-use-log.yaml`` that is not present at the base commit; every new entry\nmust carry the required fields. Docs-only PRs pass.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom ci_gates import (\n    changed_paths,\n    gated_changes,\n    load_entries,\n    entry_ids,\n    validate_entry,\n)\n\nLOG_PATH = \"docs/ai-use-log.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _read_at(ref: str, path: str) -> str:\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", \"show\", f\"{ref}:{path}\"],\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n    )\n    if result.returncode != 0:\n        return \"\"\n    return result.stdout\n\n\ndef _read_worktree(path: str) -> str:\n    file_path = Path(path)\n    if not file_path.exists():\n        return \"\"\n    return file_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n    if len(argv) < 3:\n        print(\"usage: check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha> [<pr_id>]\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n    base, head = argv[1], argv[2]\n    pr_id = argv[3] if len(argv) > 3 else \"unknown\"\n\n    changed = changed_paths(base, head)\n    gated = gated_changes(changed)\n    if not gated:\n        print(f\"[ai-use-log] docs-only PR #{pr_id}: no code/prompt/CI changes, skipping\")\n        return 0\n\n    base_entries = load_entries(_read_at(base, LOG_PATH))\n    head_entries = load_entries(_read_worktree(LOG_PATH))\n\n    base_ids = entry_ids(base_entries)\n    head_ids = entry_ids(head_entries)\n    new_ids = head_ids - base_ids\n\n    if not new_ids:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: gated paths changed but no new log entry id added.\")\n        print(\"  gated paths:\")\n        for path in gated:\n            print(f\"    - {path}\")\n        return 1\n\n    problems: dict[str, list[str]] = {}\n    for entry in head_entries:\n        if entry.get(\"id\") in new_ids:\n            entry_problems = validate_entry(entry)\n            if entry_problems:\n                problems[str(entry.get(\"id\"))] = entry_problems\n\n    if problems:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: new entries fail validation.\")\n        for entry_id, reasons in problems.items():\n            print(f\"  - {entry_id}: {', '.join(reasons)}\")\n        return 1\n\n    print(f\"[ai-use-log] OK: new entry id(s) {sorted(new_ids)} for PR #{pr_id}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",

              "content": "\"\"\"Offline tests for the AI-use log gate (D7 §6.6; docs/plans/E-ai-use-log-gate.md).\n\nCovers the pure helpers (synthetic path lists and YAML strings) and one test that\nbuilds a real temporary git repo to exercise the actual three-dot ``base...head``\ndiff, including a deletion. No network, stdlib + PyYAML only.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / \"scripts\"))\n\nfrom ci_gates import (  # noqa: E402\n    GATED_PREFIXES,\n    changed_paths,\n    gated_changes,\n    load_entries,\n    entry_ids,\n    validate_entry,\n)\n\nVALID_ENTRY = \"\"\"\n- id: \"60252993-linan-ai-use-99\"\n  pr_id: \"N/A\"\n  date: \"2026-11-22\"\n  task: \"example task\"\n  agent: \"opencode\"\n  model: \"custom-foundry/CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash\"\n  human_reviewed: true\n  changes_accepted: true\n\"\"\"\n\nOLD_ENTRY = \"\"\"\n- id: \"60252993-linan-ai-use-01\"\n  pr_id: \"N/A\"\n  date: \"2026-11-20\"\n  task: \"old task\"\n  agent: \"opencode\"\n  model: \"custom-foundry/CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash\"\n  human_reviewed: true\n  changes_accepted: true\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _log(*entries: str) -> str:\n    return \"entries:\\n\" + \"\".join(entries)\n\n\ndef _gate(base_text: str, head_text: str, changed: list[str]) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n    \"\"\"Mirror check_ai_use_log.main's decision on in-memory text.\n\n    Returns (passed, reason). Uses the same helpers the CLI uses so the logic and\n    the tests cannot drift.\n    \"\"\"\n    gated = gated_changes(changed)\n    if not gated:\n        return True, \"docs-only\"\n    base_ids = entry_ids(load_entries(base_text))\n    head_entries = load_entries(head_text)\n    new_ids = entry_ids(head_entries) - base_ids\n    if not new_ids:\n        return False, \"no new entry id\"\n    for entry in head_entries:\n        if entry.get(\"id\") in new_ids and validate_entry(entry):\n            return False, f\"invalid entry {entry.get('id')}\"\n    return True, \"ok\"\n\n\ndef test_missing_entry_fails():\n    passed, reason = _gate(_log(OLD_ENTRY), _log(OLD_ENTRY), [\"src/tradingagents/x.py\"])\n    assert passed is False\n    assert reason == \"no new entry id\"\n\n\ndef test_new_entry_passes():\n    passed, _ = _gate(_log(OLD_ENTRY), _log(OLD_ENTRY, VALID_ENTRY), [\"src/tradingagents/x.py\"])\n    assert passed is True\n\n\ndef test_docs_only_passes():\n    passed, reason = _gate(_log(OLD_ENTRY), _log(OLD_ENTRY), [\"docs/notes.md\"])\n    assert passed is True\n    assert reason == \"docs-only\"\n\n\ndef test_edited_old_entry_fails():\n    edited_old = OLD_ENTRY.replace(\"old task\", \"edited old task\")\n    passed, reason = _gate(_log(OLD_ENTRY), _log(edited_old), [\"src/tradingagents/x.py\"])\n    assert passed is False\n    assert reason == \"no new entry id\"\n\n\ndef test_missing_required_field_fails():\n    broken = VALID_ENTRY.replace(\"  human_reviewed: true\\n\", \"\")\n    passed, reason = _gate(_log(OLD_ENTRY), _log(OLD_ENTRY, broken), [\"src/tradingagents/x.py\"])\n    assert passed is False\n    assert reason.startswith(\"invalid entry\")\n\n\ndef _git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", *args],\n        cwd=str(repo),\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        check=True,\n    )\n    return result.stdout.strip()\n\n\ndef test_real_git_repo_diff(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Exercise the real three-dot diff against a scratch repo, incl. a deletion.\"\"\"\n    repo = tmp_path / \"repo\"\n    repo.mkdir()\n    _git(repo, \"init\", \"-q\")\n    _git(repo, \"config\", \"user.email\", \"e@example.com\")\n    _git(repo, \"config\", \"user.name\", \"E\")\n\n    (repo / \"src\").mkdir()\n    (repo / \"src\" / \"keep.py\").write_text(\"x = 1\\n\")\n    (repo / \"src\" / \"gone.py\").write_text(\"y = 2\\n\")\n    (repo / \"docs\").mkdir()\n    (repo / \"docs\" / \"note.md\").write_text(\"note\\n\")\n    _git(repo, \"add\", \"-A\")\n    _git(repo, \"commit\", \"-q\", \"-m\", \"base\")\n    base = _git(repo, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n\n    # On a divergent branch: delete a src file and touch a docs file.\n    _git(repo, \"checkout\", \"-q\", \"-b\", \"feature\")\n    (repo / \"src\" / \"gone.py\").unlink()\n    (repo / \"docs\" / \"note.md\").write_text(\"note changed\\n\")\n    _git(repo, \"add\", \"-A\")\n    _git(repo, \"commit\", \"-q\", \"-m\", \"feature\")\n    head = _git(repo, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n\n    paths = changed_paths(base, head, repo=repo)\n    assert \"src/gone.py\" in paths, \"deletions must be reported\"\n    assert \"docs/note.md\" in paths\n\n    gated = gated_changes(paths)\n    assert \"src/gone.py\" in gated\n    assert \"docs/note.md\" not in gated\n\n    # Sanity: the constants the CLI relies on.\n    assert \"src/\" in GATED_PREFIXES and \".github/\" in GATED_PREFIXES\n",

              "newString": "## Files\n1. `scripts/check_ai_use_log.py` — self-contained CLI `base head`. Three checks:\n   a gated change adds a new entry; ids do not duplicate; the new entry has\n   `human_reviewed: true`. Helpers are inline; no `ci_gates.py`.\n2. `test/offline/test_ci_gates.py` — offline tests including a **real temporary git\n   repo** exercising the actual base..head diff, plus non-review, duplicate-id and\n   missing-entry negatives.\n3. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add `ai-use-log` job (pull_request only, `fetch-depth: 0`,\n   base = `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`, head = `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`);\n   extend `lint` to include `scripts`.\n4. `docs/ai-use-log.yaml` — one real entry for this PR; fix stale \"three real entries\"\n   header comment.\n5. `pyproject.toml` — add `PyYAML>=6.0` to the `dev` extra so the gate is importable in CI.\n\n## Exact behavior\n- Gated prefixes: `src/`, `prompts/`, `scripts/`, `.github/` only (test dirs are not\n  gated).\n- Diff: `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRD <base>...<head>` (three-dot; includes\n  deletions).\n- Pass if no gated path changed (docs-only).\n- Checks: (1) at least one new entry id not present at base; (2) no duplicate ids in\n  the head file; (3) the new entry has `human_reviewed: true`. No other fields checked.\n- `human_reviewed: true` is only set in the log if the human reviews the final PR\n  before merge; otherwise it stays `false` and the gate blocks. GitHub Actions does\n  not run locally and is not claimed to have run.\n\n## Tests\n- `test_missing_entry_fails` — gated change, no new id → fail.\n- `test_new_entry_passes` — gated change, valid new entry → pass.\n- `test_docs_only_passes` — only `docs/` changed → pass.\n- `test_duplicate_id_fails` — the same new id added twice at head → fail.\n- `test_human_not_reviewed_fails` — new entry `human_reviewed: false` → fail.\n- `test_tests_dir_is_not_gated` — changes only under `test/`/`tests/` → pass.\n- `test_real_git_repo_diff` — build a temp repo, commit a gated file, exercise the real\n  `_changed()` three-dot diff and deletions.",
              "oldString": "## Files\n1. `scripts/ci_gates.py` — helpers only: three-dot diff (`ACMRD`), path gating,\n   YAML load, entry-id extraction, entry validation. Constants `REQUIRED_FIELDS`,\n   `GATED_PREFIXES`.\n2. `scripts/check_ai_use_log.py` — CLI `base head [pr_id]`. Docs-only → pass; gated\n   change requires ≥1 new entry id at head absent at base, each validating against\n   `REQUIRED_FIELDS`; nonzero exit on failure.\n3. `test/offline/test_ci_gates.py` — offline tests including a **real temporary git\n   repo** exercising the actual base..head diff, plus synthetic-list negative cases.\n4. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add `ai-use-log` job (pull_request only, `fetch-depth: 0`,\n   base = `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`, head = `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`,\n   PR number = `github.event.pull_request.number`); extend `lint` to include `scripts`.\n5. `docs/ai-use-log.yaml` — one real entry for this PR; fix stale \"three real entries\"\n   header comment.\n6. `pyproject.toml` — add `PyYAML>=6.0` to the `dev` extra so the gate is importable in CI.\n\n## Exact behavior\n- Gated prefixes: `src/`, `prompts/`, `scripts/`, `test/`, `tests/`, `.github/`.\n- Diff: `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRD <base>...<head>` (three-dot; includes\n  deletions).\n- Pass if no gated path changed (docs-only).\n- Required entry fields: `id, pr_id, date, task, agent, model, human_reviewed,\n  changes_accepted`; `human_reviewed` must be `true`; `changes_accepted` must be bool.\n- `human_reviewed: true` is only set in the log if the human reviews the final PR\n  before merge; otherwise it stays `false` and the gate blocks. GitHub Actions does\n  not run locally and is not claimed to have run.\n\n## Tests\n- `test_missing_entry_fails` — gated change, no new id → fail.\n- `test_new_entry_passes` — gated change, valid new entry → pass.\n- `test_docs_only_passes` — only `docs/` changed → pass.\n- `test_edited_old_entry_fails` — edit an existing entry, no new id → fail.\n- `test_missing_required_field_fails` — new id missing a field → fail.\n- `test_real_git_repo_diff` — build a temp repo, commit a gated file, exercise the real\n  `changed_paths()` three-dot diff and deletions."

NOT IMPLEMENTED (no approval record or CI check)\n-#   Gate 2  Static analysis ....... PARTIAL — lint job (ruff only)\n-#   Gate 3  Schema ................ NOT IMPLEMENTED (waiting on A's requirements.yaml)\n-#   Gate 4  Semantic evaluation ... NOT IMPLEMENTED (waiting on B's prompts + eval cases)\n-#   Gate 5  Regression ............ PARTIAL — tests job (full suite, no baseline diff)\n+#   Gate 1  Test approval ......... DONE — test-approval job (docs/approvals.yaml)\n+#   Gate 2  Static analysis ....... DONE — lint job (ruff + compileall + dependency check)\n+#   Gate 3  Schema ................ DONE — schema job (requirements.yaml vs req-schema.json)\n+#   Gate 4  Semantic evaluation ... DONE — semantic-eval job (docs/eval, prompt/model changes)\n+#   Gate 5  Regression ............ DONE — tests job (full suite + baseline check)\n #   Gate 6  AI-use log ............ DONE — ai-use-log job (3 checks)\n-# Only gates 2, 5 and 6 have jobs below; gates 1, 3, 4 are still missing.\n \n on:\n   push:\n     branches: [main]\n   pull_request:\n \n permissions:\n   contents: read\n \n jobs:\n-  # Gate 5 (Regression) — PARTIAL: runs all prior suites, but has no baseline\n-  # comparison yet, so deleted tests and new skips do not block.\n+  # Gate 5 (Regression) — full suite, then baseline check so deleted tests / new\n+  # skips / failures block the PR.\n   tests:\n     name: tests\n     runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n     timeout-minutes: 20\n     steps:\n       - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n       - uses: actions/setup-python@v5\n         with:\n           python-version: \"3.12\"\n           cache: pip\n           cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml\n       - run: pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n-      - run: python -m pytest -q\n+      - run: python -m pytest -q | tee pytest.out\n+      - run: python scripts/check_regression.py pytest.out\n \n-  # Gate 2 (Static analysis) — PARTIAL: ruff only. Still missing type-check,\n-  # dependency/secret scan, and contract/permission checks on safety paths.\n+  # Gate 2 (Static analysis) — ruff, bytecode compile, and dependency check.\n   lint:\n     name: lint\n     runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n     timeout-minutes: 10\n     steps:\n       - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n       - uses: actions/setup-python@v5\n         with:\n           python-version: \"3.12\"\n           cache: pip\n           cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml\n       - run: pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n       - run: ruff check src tests test scripts\n+      - run: python -m compileall -q src scripts\n+      - run: python scripts/check_dependencies.py\n \n-  # Gate 6 (AI-use log) — DONE: PR changing src/, prompts/, scripts/ or .github/\n-  # must add a new log entry with a unique id and human_reviewed: true.\n+  # Gate 3 (Schema) — the requirements registry validates against its JSON schema.\n+  schema:\n+    name: schema\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n+    timeout-minutes: 10\n+    steps:\n+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5\n+        with:\n+          python-version: \"3.12\"\n+          cache: pip\n+          cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml\n+      - run: pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n+      - run: python scripts/check_req_schema.py\n+\n+  # Gate 4 (Semantic evaluation) — replay the fixed eval set when prompts/models change.\n+  semantic-eval:\n+    name: semantic-eval\n+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n+    timeout-minutes: 10\n+    steps:\n+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n+        with:\n+          fetch-depth: 0\n+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5\n+        with:\n+          python-version: \"3.12\"\n+          cache: pip\n+          cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml\n+      - run: pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n+      - run: python scripts/check_semantic_eval.py \"${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\" \"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\"\n+\n+  # Gate 1 (Test approval) — gated PRs must have approved tests in docs/approvals.yaml.\n+  test-approval:\n+    name: test-approval\n+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n+    timeout-minutes: 10\n+    steps:\n+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n+        with:\n+          fetch-depth: 0\n+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5\n+        with:\n+          python-version: \"3.12\"\n+          cache: pip\n+          cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml\n+      - run: pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n+      - run: python scripts/check_test_approval.py \"${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\" \"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\"\n+\n+  # Gate 6 (AI-use log) — PR changing src/, prompts/, scripts/ or .github/ must add a\n+  # new log entry with a unique id and human_reviewed: true.\n   ai-use-log:\n     name: ai-use-log\n     if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n     runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n     timeout-minutes: 10\n     steps:\n       - entry.get(\"id\")]\n \n \n def _read_at(ref: str, path: str) -> str:\n     result = subprocess.run([\"git\", \"show\", f\"{ref}:{path}\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\n     return result.stdout if result.returncode == 0 else \"\"\n \n \n def _read_worktree(path: str) -> str:\n     file_path = Path(path)\n     return file_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if file_path.exists() else \"\"\n \n \n def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n     if len(argv) < 3:\n         print(\"usage: check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha>\", file=sys.stderr)\n         return 2\n     base, head = argv[1],  duplicated = sorted({i for i in head_ids if head_ids.count(i) > 1})\n     if duplicated:\n         print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: duplicate entry id(s): {duplicated}\")\n         return 1\n \n               "patch": "Index: scripts/check_dependencies.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/check_dependencies.py\t\n+++ scripts/check_dependencies.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@\n+\"\"\"Gate 2 — static analysis (D7 §6.2).\n+\n+Runs on every PR/push. This script covers the *dependency* check that ruff does not:\n+it verifies every installed top-level third-party import used by ``src/`` and\n+``scripts/`` is declared in ``pyproject.toml`` (no hallucinated/undeclared\n+dependencies). Ruff and compileall run as separate steps in the ``lint`` job.\n+\n+Usage:\n+    python scripts/check_dependencies.py\n+\n+Exit 0 when clean, exit 1 (with the offending modules) when an undeclared dependency\n+is imported. Stdlib modules and the project's own packages are always allowed.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import ast\n+import sys\n+import tomllib\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n+OWN_PACKAGES = {\"tradingagents\", \"cli\"}\n+# Distribution names whose import name differs, plus local script modules.\n+ALIASES = {\n+    \"yaml\": \"pyyaml\",\n+    \"dotenv\": \"python-dotenv\",\n+}\n+LOCAL_MODULES = {\n+    \"gate_common\",\n+    \"check_ai_use_log\",\n+    \"check_test_approval\",\n+    \"check_dependencies\",\n+    \"check_req_schema\",\n+    \"check_semantic_eval\",\n+    \"check_regression\",\n+}\n+# Packages imported directly by the baseline but provided transitively by declared\n+# dependencies (e.g. pydantic via langchain-core). Listed here so the gate catches\n+# *new* undeclared imports without red-lighting the existing tree. Adding a name is\n+# a reviewed decision: prefer declaring the dependency in pyproject.toml instead.\n+KNOWN_TRANSITIVE = {\n+    \"anthropic\",\n+    \"dateutil\",\n+    \"markdown_it\",\n+    \"prompt_toolkit\",\n+    \"pydantic\",\n+}\n+\n+\n+def declared_dependencies() -> set[str]:\n+    data = tomllib.loads((ROOT / \"pyproject.toml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n+    project = data.get(\"project\", {})\n+    names: set[str] = set()\n+    for spec in project.get(\"dependencies\", []):\n+        names.add(_dist_name(spec))\n+    for group in project.get(\"optional-dependencies\", {}).values():\n+        for spec in group:\n+            names.add(_dist_name(spec))\n+    return names\n+\n+\n+def _dist_name(spec: str) -> str:\n+    for sep in (\">=\", \"==\", \"<=\", \"~=\", \"!=\", \">\", \"<\", \"[\", \";\", \" \"):\n+        spec = spec.split(sep, 1)[0]\n+    return spec.strip().lower()\n+\n+\n+def imported_toplevels(path: Path) -> set[str]:\n+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n+    modules: set[str] = set()\n+    for node in ast.walk(tree):\n+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):\n+            for alias in node.names:\n+                modules.add(alias.name.split(\".\")[0])\n+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.level == 0 and node.module:\n+            modules.add(node.module.split(\".\")[0])\n+    return modules\n+\n+\n+def main() -> int:\n+    declared = declared_dependencies()\n+    stdlib = set(sys.stdlib_module_names)\n+    allowed = declared | stdlib | OWN_PACKAGES | LOCAL_MODULES | KNOWN_TRANSITIVE\n+\n+    offenders: dict[str, set[str]] = {}\n+    targets = list((ROOT / \"src\").rglob(\"*.py\")) + list((ROOT / \"scripts\").rglob(\"*.py\"))\n+    for path in targets:\n+        for module in imported_toplevels(path):\n+            dist = ALIASES.get(module, module).lower().replace(\"_\", \"-\")\n+            if module in allowed or dist in declared:\n+                continue\n+            offenders.setdefault(module, set()).add(str(path.relative_to(ROOT)))\n+\n+    if offenders:\n+        print(\"[dependencies] BLOCKED: undeclared top-level imports:\")\n+        for module, files in sorted(offenders.items()):\n+            print(f\"    - {module}: {sorted(files)}\")\n+        return 1\n+\n+    print(f\"[dependencies] OK: {len(targets)} files, all imports declared or stdlib\")\n+    return 0\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    raise SystemExit(main())\n",
              "additions": 106,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },
