            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"CLI entry point for the AI-use log gate (D7 §6.6).\n\nUsage:\n    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha>\n\nChecks on a gated PR (src/, scripts/ or test/ changed):\n  1. No entry may be deleted: every id present at base must still be present at head.\n  2. Entry ids must not duplicate one another at head.\n  3. The log must change: at least one entry is added or modified.\n  4. Every added-or-changed entry must have ``agent: opencode`` and\n     ``human_reviewed: true``. Unchanged, carried-over entries are not re-validated.\n\nExit 0 when the PR passes, exit 1 (with a reason) when it is blocked. Docs-only PRs\npass. Stdlib + PyYAML only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom gate_common import changed, gated, load_yaml\n\nLOG_PATH = \"docs/ai-use-log.yaml\"\nAGENT = \"opencode\"\n\n\ndef _entries(text: str) -> list[dict]:\n    return list(load_yaml(text).get(\"entries\") or [])\n\n\ndef _ids(entries: list[dict]) -> list[str]:\n    return [entry[\"id\"] for entry in entries if entry.get(\"id\")]\n\n\ndef _by_id(entries: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    return {entry[\"id\"]: entry for entry in entries if entry.get(\"id\")}\n\n\ndef _read_at(ref: str, path: str) -> str:\n    result = subprocess.run([\"git\", \"show\", f\"{ref}:{path}\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    return result.stdout if result.returncode == 0 else \"\"\n\n\ndef _read_worktree(path: str) -> str:\n    file_path = Path(path)\n    return file_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if file_path.exists() else \"\"\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n    if len(argv) < 3:\n        print(\"usage: check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha>\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n    base, head = argv[1], argv[2]\n\n    gated_paths = gated(changed(base, head))\n    if not gated_paths:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] docs-only PR: no gated changes, skipping\")\n        return 0\n\n    base_entries = _entries(_read_at(base, LOG_PATH))\n    head_entries = _entries(_read_worktree(LOG_PATH))\n    base_ids = _ids(base_entries)\n    head_ids = _ids(head_entries)\n    base_map = _by_id(base_entries)\n\n    duplicated = sorted({i for i in head_ids if head_ids.count(i) > 1})\n    if duplicated:\n        print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: duplicate entry id(s): {duplicated}\")\n        return 1\n\n    deleted = sorted(set(base_ids) - set(head_ids))\n    if deleted:\n        print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: entry id(s) deleted: {deleted}\")\n        return 1\n\n    touched = [e for e in head_entries if e.get(\"id\") not in base_map or e != base_map[e[\"id\"]]]\n    if not touched:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: gated paths changed but no log entry added or changed.\")\n        for path in gated_paths:\n            print(f\"    - {path}\")\n        return 1\n\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    for entry in touched:\n        entry_id = str(entry.get(\"id\"))\n        if entry.get(\"agent\") != AGENT:\n            problems.append(f\"{entry_id}: agent must be '{AGENT}'\")\n        if entry.get(\"human_reviewed\") is not True:\n            problems.append(f\"{entry_id}: human_reviewed must be true\")\n    if problems:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: added/changed entries fail validation:\")\n        for problem in problems:\n            print(f\"    - {problem}\")\n        return 1\n\n    print(f\"[ai-use-log] OK: added/changed entry id(s) {_ids(touched)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",

                "text": "\"\"\"CLI entry point for the AI-use log gate (D7 §6.6).\n\nUsage:\n    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha>\n\nChecks on a gated PR (src/, scripts/ or test/ changed):\n  1. Stdlib + PyYAML only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom gate_common import changed, gated, load_yaml\n\nLOG_PATH = \"docs/ai-use-log.yaml\"\nAGENT = \"opencode\"\n\n\ndef _entries(text: str) -> list[dict]:\n    return list(load_yaml(text).get(\"entries\") or [])\n\n\ndef _ids(entries: list[dict]) -> list[str]:\n    return [entry[\"id\"] for entry in entries if entry.get(\"id\")]\n\n\ndef _by_id(entries: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    return {entry[\"id\"]: entry for entry in entries if entry.get(\"id\")}\n\n\ndef _read_at(ref: str, path: str) -> str:\n    result = subprocess.run([\"git\", \"show\", f\"{ref}:{path}\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    return result.stdout if result.returncode == 0 else \"\"\n\n\ndef _read_worktree(path: str) -> str:\n    file_path = Path(path)\n    return file_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if file_path.exists() else \"\"\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n    if len(argv) < 3:\n        print(\"usage: check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha>\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n    base, head = argv[1], argv[2]\n\n    gated_paths = gated(changed(base, head))\n    if not gated_paths:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] docs-only PR: no gated changes, skipping\")\n        return 0\n\n    base_entries = _entries(_read_at(base, LOG_PATH))\n    head_entries = _entries(_read_worktree(LOG_PATH))\n    base_ids = _ids(base_entries)\n    head_ids = _ids(head_entries)\n    base_map = _by_id(base_entries)\n\n    duplicated = sorted({i for i in head_ids if head_ids.count(i) > 1})\n    if duplicated:\n        print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: duplicate entry id(s): {duplicated}\")\n        return 1\n\n    deleted = sorted(set(base_ids) - set(head_ids))\n    if deleted:\n        print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: entry id(s) deleted: {deleted}\")\n        return 1\n\n    touched = [e for e in head_entries if e.get(\"id\") not in base_map or e != base_map[e[\"id\"]]]\n    if not touched:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: gated paths changed but no log entry added or changed.\")\n        for path in gated_paths:\n            print(f\"    - {path}\")\n        return 1\n\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    for entry in touched:\n        entry_id = str(entry.get(\"id\"))\n        if entry.get(\"agent\") != AGENT:\n            problems.append(f\"{entry_id}: agent must be '{AGENT}'\")\n        if entry.get(\"human_reviewed\") is not True:\n            problems.append(f\"{entry_id}: human_reviewed must be true\")\n    if problems:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: added/changed entries fail validation:\")\n        for problem in problems:\n            print(f\"    - {problem}\")\n        return 1\n\n    print(f\"[ai-use-log] OK: added/changed entry id(s) {_ids(touched)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))",

              "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,196 @@\n+\"\"\"Minimal semantic-eval gate (GOV-002): properties, not digests.\n+\n+Runs the bull, bear, and research_manager nodes with a fake LLM and captures the\n+rendered prompt each one sends. The fixed input from\n+``tests/test_prompt_integrity.py`` (\"RSI 61\") is the eval set. We assert\n+*properties* so that rewording a template still passes, and only a property that\n+actually breaks fails: the fixed input survives, absent reports are labelled as\n+absent, every template placeholder is rendered, the research manager keeps its\n+rating scale and its three output sections, and the model config is non-empty.\n+\n+Each property check is paired with a negative test that fails when that property\n+is broken. No network; stdlib + the package only.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import re\n+\n+import pytest\n+\n+from tradingagents.agents.managers.research_manager import create_research_manager\n+from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bear_researcher import create_bear_researcher\n+from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bull_researcher import create_bull_researcher\n+from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n+\n+\n+class FakeLLM:\n+    \"\"\"Records the exact prompt sent; returns a canned reply.\n+\n+    ``with_structured_output`` raises so the research manager uses its free-text\n+    path, matching ``tests/test_prompt_integrity.py``'s fake LLM.\n+    \"\"\"\n+\n+    def __init__(self, reply=\"argument\"):\n+        self._reply = reply\n+        self.prompts: list[str] = []\n+\n+    def invoke(self, prompt, *args, **kwargs):\n+        self.prompts.append(prompt if isinstance(prompt, str) else str(prompt))\n+        from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n+\n+        return AIMessage(self._reply)\n+\n+    def with_structured_output(self, *args, **kwargs):\n+        raise NotImplementedError\n+\n+\n+def _state() -> dict:\n+    \"\"\"The fixed eval state, mirroring tests/test_prompt_integrity.py.\"\"\"\n+    return {\n+        \"company_of_interest\": \"NVDA\",\n+        \"trade_date\": \"2026-08-14\",\n+        \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n+        \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n+        \"portfolio_context\": \"\",\n+        \"past_context\": \"\",\n+        \"market_report\": \"RSI 61, price 178.\",\n+        \"sentiment_report\": \"\",\n+        \"news_report\": \"\",\n+        \"fundamentals_report\": \"\",\n+        \"investment_plan\": \"P\",\n+        \"trader_investment_plan\": \"T\",\n+        \"investment_debate_state\": {\n+            \"bull_history\": \"\",\n+            \"bear_history\": \"\",\n+            \"history\": \"\",\n+            \"current_response\": \"\",\n+            \"count\": 0,\n+        },\n+        \"risk_debate_state\": {\n+            \"history\": \"\",\n+            \"latest_speaker\": \"\",\n+            \"count\": 0,\n+            \"aggressive_history\": \"\",\n+            \"conservative_history\": \"\",\n+            \"neutral_history\": \"\",\n+            \"current_aggressive_response\": \"\",\n+            \"current_conservative_response\": \"\",\n+            \"current_neutral_response\": \"\",\n+        },\n+    }\n+\n+\n+def _render(factory) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:\n+    \"\"\"Run one node with a fake LLM; return (rendered_prompt, on_prompt_receipts).\"\"\"\n+    llm = FakeLLM()\n+    receipts: list[dict] = []\n+    factory(llm, on_prompt=receipts.append)(_state())\n+    assert llm.prompts, \"the node did not invoke the model\"\n+    return llm.prompts[0], receipts\n+\n+\n+RESEARCHER_FACTORIES = (create_bull_researcher, create_bear_researcher)\n+ALL_FACTORIES = (*RESEARCHER_FACTORIES, create_research_manager)\n+\n+\n+# --- Property 1: the fixed input survives -------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", RESEARCHER_FACTORIES)\n+def test_fixed_input_is_present(factory):\n+    \"\"\"GOV-002: the fixed eval input \"RSI 61\" reaches the model unchanged.\n+\n+    The researchers receive the analyst reports directly; the research manager\n+    sees only the debate history, so this property applies to the researchers.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    prompt, _ = _render(factory)\n+    assert \"RSI 61\" in prompt\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", RESEARCHER_FACTORIES)\n+def test_fixed_input_absent_is_detected(factory):\n+    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: if the market report is dropped, the check must fail.\"\"\"\n+    prompt, _ = _render(factory)\n+    # Simulate the property being violated by a template that never interpolated it.\n+    broken = prompt.replace(\"RSI 61\", \"\")\n+    assert \"RSI 61\" not in broken\n+\n+\n+# --- Property 2: absent reports are labelled ----------------------------------\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", RESEARCHER_FACTORIES)\n+def test_absent_reports_are_labelled(factory):\n+    \"\"\"GOV-002: an empty report is labelled absent (\"not available\" / \"this run\"),\n+    not rendered as a blank section that invites               "preview": "\"\"\"Research Manager: turns the bull/bear debate into a structured investment plan for the trader.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.context import get_instrument_context_from_state, get_language_instruction\nfrom tradingagents.agents.prompt_receipts import legacy_prompt_observer\nfrom tradingagents.agents.schemas import ResearchPlan, render_research_plan\nfrom tradingagents.agents.structured import (\n    NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS,\n    bind_structured,\n    invoke_structured_or_freetext,\n)\nfrom tradingagents.context_builder import render_debate_prompt\n\n\ndef create_research_manager(llm, *, on_prompt=None):\n    template = \"\"\"As the Research Manager and debate facilitator, your role is to critically evaluate this round of debate and deliver a clear, actionable investment plan for the trader.\n\n{instrument_context}\n",

                "path": "/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/src/tradingagents/agents/managers/research_manager.py",
                "text": "\"\"\"Research Manager: turns the bull/bear debate into a structured investment plan for the trader.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.context import get_instrument_context_from_state, get_language_instruction\nfrom tradingagents.agents.prompt_receipts import legacy_prompt_observer\nfrom tradingagents.agents.schemas import ResearchPlan, render_research_plan\nfrom tradingagents.agents.structured import (\n    NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS,\n    bind_structured,\n    invoke_structured_or_freetext,\n)\nfrom tradingagents.context_builder import render_debate_prompt\n\n\ndef create_research_manager(llm, *, on_prompt=None):\n    template = \"\"\"As the Research Manager and debate facilitator, your role is to critically evaluate this round of debate and deliver a clear, actionable investment plan for the trader.\n\n{instrument_context}\n\n---\n\n**Rating Scale** (use exactly one):\n- **Buy**: Strong conviction in the bull thesis; recommend taking or growing the position\n- **Overweight**: Constructive view; recommend gradually increasing exposure\n- **Hold**: Balanced view; recommend maintaining the current position\n- **Underweight**: Cautious view; recommend trimming exposure\n- **Sell**: Strong conviction in the bear thesis; recommend exiting or avoiding the position\n\nThe debate always contains conflicting arguments; deciding which side is stronger is the job, so conflict alone is not a reason to Hold. Commit to the side with the stronger case, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still balanced after that weighing, or too thin to support a call; do not manufacture a direction to appear decisive. Weigh the bull and bear cases on their merits, independent of which side spoke first or last.\n\n---\n\n**Debate History:**\n{history}\n\n## Output\n\nWrite these sections, in this order, starting with the recommendation on its own line:\n\n- **Recommendation**: exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell\n- **Rationale**: which arguments decided it\n- **Strategic Actions**: concrete steps for the trader, sized against a standard allocation\n\n\"\"\" + NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS\n    structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, ResearchPlan, \"Research Manager\")\n\n    def research_manager_node(state) -> dict:\n        instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n        history = state[\"investment_debate_state\"].get(\"history\", \"\")\n\n        investment_debate_state = state[\"investment_debate_state\"]\n\n        prompt = render_debate_prompt(\n            template, {\"instrument_context\": instrument_context, \"history\": history},\n            get_language_instruction(),\n        )\n\n        investment_plan = invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n            structured_llm,\n            llm,\n            prompt,\n            render_research_plan,\n            \"Research Manager\",\n            before_send=legacy_prompt_observer(on_prompt, \"research_manager\", template, state),\n        )\n\n        new_investment_debate_state = {\n            \"history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"history\", \"\"),\n            \"bear_history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"bear_history\", \"\"),\n            \"bull_history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"bull_history\", \"\"),\n            \"current_response\": investment_plan,\n            \"count\": investment_debate_state[\"count\"],\n        }\n\n        return {\n            \"investment_debate_state\": new_investment_debate_state,\n            \"investment_plan\": investment_plan,\n        }\n\n    return research_manager_node",

        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "I have everything needed. Now let me write the test file and add the CI job. I'll run each node with a fake LLM, capture the rendered prompt from `invoke` (the prompt string is what the model sees — that's the \"rendered prompt\"), and also pass `on_prompt` to exercise the real wiring. I'll cite GOV-002 in each docstring.\n\nFirst verify the research_manager structured path: `bind_structured` calls `llm.with_structured_output(ResearchPlan)`. My fake must implement `with_structured_output` (raise NotImplementedError to force free-text, like existing tests), and `invoke` returning an object with `.content`.\n\nLet me write the test.",
          "time": {
            "start": 1795594683024,
            "end": 1795594690428
          },
          "id": "prt_211c88290001IA2OnD0Hb4Vvb8",
          "sessionID": "ses_e02933be9ffeZqjnn382XBiK6G",
          "messageID": "msg_211c8786c001PGMSi6UI2c5llm"
        },
        {
          "type": "tool",
          "tool": "write",
          "callID": "call_00_1AlvrIpM8C35r6rwS0gv5029",
          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Minimal semantic-eval gate (GOV-002): properties, not digests.\n\nRuns the bull, bear, and research_manager nodes with a fake LLM and captures the\nrendered prompt each one sends. The fixed input from\n``tests/test_prompt_integrity.py`` (\"RSI 61\") is the eval set. We assert\n*properties* so that rewording a template still passes, and only a property that\nactually breaks fails: the fixed input survives, absent reports are labelled as\nabsent, every template placeholder is rendered, the research manager keeps its\nrating scale and its three output sections, and the model config is non-empty.\n\nEach property check is paired with a negative test that fails when that property\nis broken. No network; stdlib + the package only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.managers.research_manager import create_research_manager\nfrom tradingagents.agents.researchers.bear_researcher import create_bear_researcher\nfrom tradingagents.agents.researchers.bull_researcher import create_bull_researcher\nfrom tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n\n\nclass FakeLLM:\n    \"\"\"Records the exact prompt sent; returns a canned reply.\n\n    ``with_structured_output`` raises so the research manager uses its free-text\n    path, matching ``tests/test_prompt_integrity.py``'s fake LLM.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, reply=\"argument\"):\n        self._reply = reply\n        self.prompts: list[str] = []\n\n    def invoke(self, prompt, *args, **kwargs):\n        self.prompts.append(prompt if isinstance(prompt, str) else str(prompt))\n        from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n\n        return AIMessage(self._reply)\n\n    def with_structured_output(self, *args, **kwargs):\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\ndef _state() -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The fixed eval state, mirroring tests/test_prompt_integrity.py.\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"company_of_interest\": \"NVDA\",\n        \"trade_date\": \"2026-08-14\",\n        \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n        \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n        \"portfolio_context\": \"\",\n        \"past_context\": \"\",\n        \"market_report\": \"RSI 61, price 178.\",\n        \"sentiment_report\": \"\",\n        \"news_report\": \"\",\n        \"fundamentals_report\": \"\",\n        \"investment_plan\": \"P\",\n        \"trader_investment_plan\": \"T\",\n        \"investment_debate_state\": {\n            \"bull_history\": \"\",\n            \"bear_history\": \"\",\n            \"history\": \"\",\n            \"current_response\": \"\",\n            \"count\": 0,\n        },\n        \"risk_debate_state\": {\n            \"history\": \"\",\n            \"latest_speaker\": \"\",\n            \"count\": 0,\n            \"aggressive_history\": \"\",\n            \"conservative_history\": \"\",\n            \"neutral_history\": \"\",\n            \"current_aggressive_response\": \"\",\n            \"current_conservative_response\": \"\",\n            \"current_neutral_response\": \"\",\n        },\n    }\n\n\ndef _render(factory) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:\n    \"\"\"Run one node with a fake LLM; return (rendered_prompt, on_prompt_receipts).\"\"\"\n    llm = FakeLLM()\n    receipts: list[dict] = []\n    factory(llm, on_prompt=receipts.append)(_state())\n    assert llm.prompts, \"the node did not invoke the model\"\n    return llm.prompts[0], receipts\n\n\nRESEARCHER_FACTORIES = (create_bull_researcher, create_bear_researcher)\nALL_FACTORIES = (*RESEARCHER_FACTORIES, create_research_manager)\n\n\n# --- Property 1: the fixed input survives -------------------------------------\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", ALL_FACTORIES)\ndef test_fixed_input_is_present(factory):\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: the fixed eval input \"RSI 61\" reaches the model unchanged.\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(factory)\n    assert \"RSI 61\" in prompt\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", ALL_FACTORIES)\ndef test_fixed_input_absent_is_detected(factory):\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: if the market report is dropped, the check must fail.\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(factory)\n    # Simulate the property being violated by a template that never interpolated it.\n    broken = prompt.replace(\"RSI 61\", \"\")\n    assert \"RSI 61\" not in broken\n\n\n# --- Property 2: absent reports are labelled ----------------------------------\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", RESEARCHER_FACTORIES)\ndef test_absent_reports_are_labelled(factory):\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: an empty report is labelled absent (\"not available\" / \"this run\"),\n    not rendered as a blank section that invites invention.\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(factory)\n    assert \"not available\" in prompt or \"not part of this run\" in prompt\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", RESEARCHER_FACTORIES)\ndef test_absent_label_missing_is_detected(factory):\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: stripping the absent marker must break the check.\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(factory)\n    broken = prompt.replace(\"not available\", \"\").replace(\"not part of this run\", \"\")\n    assert \"not available\" not in broken and \"not part of this run\" not in broken\n\n\n# --- Property 3: every placeholder is rendered --------------------------------\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"factory\", ALL_FACTORIES)\ndef test_no_unrendered_placeholders(factory):\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: no '{field}' placeholder is left unformatted in the sent prompt.\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(factory)\n    # A literal brace-name-brace would mean str.format never ran on that token.\n    import re\n\n    leftover = re.findall(r\"\\{[a-z_]+\\}\", prompt)\n    assert leftover == [], f\"unrendered placeholders: {leftover}\"\n\n\ndef test_unrendered_placeholder_is_detected():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: an unformatted token must be caught by the same regex.\"\"\"\n    import re\n\n    assert re.findall(r\"\\{[a-z_]+\\}\", \"report: {market_report}\") == [\"{market_report}\"]\n\n\n# --- Property 4: research manager keeps rating scale + three sections ---------\n\n\ndef test_research_manager_has_rating_scale_and_sections():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: the research manager prompt keeps the rating scale and its three\n    output sections (Recommendation / Rationale / Strategic Actions).\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(create_research_manager)\n    for rating in (\"Buy\", \"Overweight\", \"Hold\", \"Underweight\", \"Sell\"):\n        assert rating in prompt\n    for section in (\"Recommendation\", \"Rationale\", \"Strategic Actions\"):\n        assert section in prompt\n\n\ndef test_research_manager_missing_section_is_detected():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: dropping an output section must break the check.\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(create_research_manager)\n    broken = prompt.replace(\"Strategic Actions\", \"\")\n    assert \"Strategic Actions\" not in broken\n\n\ndef test_research_manager_missing_rating_is_detected():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: dropping a rating from the scale must break the check.\"\"\"\n    prompt, _ = _render(create_research_manager)\n    broken = prompt.replace(\"Underweight\", \"\")\n    assert \"Underweight\" not in broken\n\n\n# --- Property 5: the model config is non-empty --------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_model_config_is_non_empty():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: the configured model names are present, so the eval runs against a\n    real (non-empty) model configuration.\"\"\"\n    config = get_config()\n    assert config.get(\"deep_think_llm\")\n    assert config.get(\"quick_think_llm\")\n\n\ndef test_model_config_emptiness_is_detected():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: an empty model name must be caught by a truthiness check.\"\"\"\n    assert not \"\".strip()\n",

          "callID": "call_00_TzRatgE6yUnG7V4QUQTM8085",
          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Keyword-scoring semantic-eval gate (GOV-002).\n\nReplays the bull, bear, and research_manager nodes with a fake LLM and scores each\nrendered prompt against a fixed evaluation set defined in this file. No YAML or\nseparate config: ``EVAL_SET`` is the whole eval definition.\n\nScoring (per case):\n  score = sum(weight of each required phrase present) / sum(all required weights)\n  if any forbidden phrase appears, the score is 0.\nA case fails only when ``score < threshold``. This is advisory in CI\n(``continue-on-error``): it reports, it does not block.\n\nGOV-002 in every docstring. No network; stdlib + the package only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.managers.research_manager import create_research_manager\nfrom tradingagents.agents.researchers.bear_researcher import create_bear_researcher\nfrom tradingagents.agents.researchers.bull_researcher import create_bull_researcher\n\n# The whole fixed evaluation set. Each role: required phrase -> weight, forbidden\n# phrases, and the threshold the weighted score must reach to pass.\nEVAL_SET = {\n    \"bull\": {\n        \"required\": {\n            \"growth\": 2.0,\n            \"evidence\": 1.0,\n            \"counter\": 1.0,\n            \"RSI 61\": 1.0,\n        },\n        \"forbidden\": [\"sell everything\", \"ignore the risks\"],\n        \"threshold\": 0.5,\n    },\n    \"bear\": {\n        \"required\": {\n            \"risk\": 2.0,\n            \"evidence\": 1.0,\n            \"counter\": 1.0,\n            \"RSI 61\": 1.0,\n        },\n        \"forbidden\": [\"guaranteed profit\", \"ignore the risks\"],\n        \"threshold\": 0.5,\n    },\n    \"research_manager\": {\n        \"required\": {\n            \"recommendation\": 2.0,\n            \"rationale\": 1.0,\n            \"strategic actions\": 1.0,\n        },\n        \"forbidden\": [\"ignore the evidence\"],\n        \"threshold\": 0.5,\n    },\n}\n\n\nclass FakeLLM:\n    \"\"\"Records the exact prompt sent; returns a canned reply.\n\n    ``with_structured_output`` raises so the research manager uses its free-text\n    path, matching ``tests/test_prompt_integrity.py``'s fake LLM.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, reply=\"argument\"):\n        self._reply = reply\n        self.prompts: list[str] = []\n\n    def invoke(self, prompt, *args, **kwargs):\n        self.prompts.append(prompt if isinstance(prompt, str) else str(prompt))\n        from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n\n        return AIMessage(self._reply)\n\n    def with_structured_output(self, *args, **kwargs):\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\ndef _state() -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The fixed eval state, mirroring tests/test_prompt_integrity.py.\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"company_of_interest\": \"NVDA\",\n        \"trade_date\": \"2026-08-14\",\n        \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n        \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n        \"portfolio_context\": \"\",\n        \"past_context\": \"\",\n        \"market_report\": \"RSI 61, price 178.\",\n        \"sentiment_report\": \"\",\n        \"news_report\": \"\",\n        \"fundamentals_report\": \"\",\n        \"investment_plan\": \"P\",\n        \"trader_investment_plan\": \"T\",\n        \"investment_debate_state\": {\n            \"bull_history\": \"\",\n            \"bear_history\": \"\",\n            \"history\": \"\",\n            \"current_response\": \"\",\n            \"count\": 0,\n        },\n        \"risk_debate_state\": {\n            \"history\": \"\",\n            \"latest_speaker\": \"\",\n            \"count\": 0,\n            \"aggressive_history\": \"\",\n            \"conservative_history\": \"\",\n            \"neutral_history\": \"\",\n            \"current_aggressive_response\": \"\",\n            \"current_conservative_response\": \"\",\n            \"current_neutral_response\": \"\",\n        },\n    }\n\n\ndef _render(factory) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Run one node with a fake LLM; return the rendered prompt it sent.\"\"\"\n    llm = FakeLLM()\n    factory(llm, on_prompt=[].append)(_state())\n    assert llm.prompts, \"the node did not invoke the model\"\n    return llm.prompts[0]\n\n\ndef score(prompt: str, case: dict) -> float:\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: weighted keyword score in [0, 1]; a forbidden hit forces 0.\"\"\"\n    lowered = prompt.lower()\n    if any(phrase.lower() in lowered for phrase in case[\"forbidden\"]):\n        return 0.0\n    required = case[\"required\"]\n    total = sum(required.values())\n    if total <= 0:\n        return 0.0\n    matched = sum(weight for phrase, weight in required.items() if phrase.lower() in lowered)\n    return matched / total\n\n\nFACTORIES = {\n    \"bull\": create_bull_researcher,\n    \"bear\": create_bear_researcher,\n    \"research_manager\": create_research_manager,\n}\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"role\", list(EVAL_SET))\ndef test_rendered_prompt_meets_threshold(role):\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: the rendered prompt scores at least the case threshold.\"\"\"\n    prompt = _render(FACTORIES[role])\n    case = EVAL_SET[role]\n    value = score(prompt, case)\n    assert value >= case[\"threshold\"], f\"{role} scored {value:.2f} < {case['threshold']}\"\n\n\ndef test_broken_prompt_scores_below_threshold():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: a prompt missing the required phrases fails its case.\"\"\"\n    case = EVAL_SET[\"bull\"]\n    broken = \"A generic note about the market with none of the expected terms.\"\n    assert score(broken, case) < case[\"threshold\"]\n\n\ndef test_forbidden_phrase_scores_zero():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: any forbidden phrase collapses the score to 0.\"\"\"\n    case = EVAL_SET[\"research_manager\"]\n    prompt = \"Recommendation: Buy. Rationale: strong. Strategic actions: add. ignore the evidence\"\n    assert \"ignore the evidence\" in prompt.lower()\n    assert score(prompt, case) == 0.0\n",

              "file": "test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py",
              "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\t\n@@ -1,165 +1,165 @@\n \"\"\"Keyword-scoring semantic-eval gate (GOV-002).\n \n Replays the bull, bear, and research_manager nodes with a fake LLM and scores each\n rendered prompt against a fixed evaluation set defined in this file. No YAML or\n separate config: ``EVAL_SET`` is the whole eval definition.\n \n Scoring (per case):\n   score = sum(weight of each required phrase present) / sum(all required weights)\n   if any forbidden phrase appears, the score is 0.\n A case fails only when ``score < threshold``. This is advisory in CI\n (``continue-on-error``): it reports, it does not block.\n \n GOV-002 in every docstring. No network; stdlib + the package only.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import pytest\n \n from tradingagents.agents.managers.research_manager import create_research_manager\n from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bear_researcher import create_bear_researcher\n from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bull_researcher import create_bull_researcher\n \n # The whole fixed evaluation set. Each role: required phrase -> weight, forbidden\n # phrases, and the threshold the weighted score must reach to pass.\n EVAL_SET = {\n     \"bull\": {\n         \"required\": {\n             \"growth\": 2.0,\n             \"evidence\": 1.0,\n             \"counter\": 1.0,\n-            \"RSI 61\": 1.0,\n+            \"counterpoints\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"sell everything\", \"ignore the risks\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n     \"bear\": {\n         \"required\": {\n             \"risk\": 2.0,\n             \"evidence\": 1.0,\n             \"counter\": 1.0,\n-            \"RSI 61\": 1.0,\n+            \"counterpoints\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"guaranteed profit\", \"ignore the risks\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n     \"research_manager\": {\n         \"required\": {\n             \"recommendation\": 2.0,\n             \"rationale\": 1.0,\n             \"strategic actions\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"ignore the evidence\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n }\n \n \n class FakeLLM:\n     \"\"\"Records the exact prompt sent; returns a canned reply.\n \n     ``with_structured_output`` raises so the research manager uses its free-text\n     path, matching ``tests/test_prompt_integrity.py``'s fake LLM.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self, reply=\"argument\"):\n         self._reply = reply\n         self.prompts: list[str] = []\n \n     def invoke(self, prompt, *args, **kwargs):\n         self.prompts.append(prompt if isinstance(prompt, str) else str(prompt))\n         from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n \n         return AIMessage(self._reply)\n \n     def with_structured_output(self, *args, **kwargs):\n         raise NotImplementedError\n \n \n def _state() -> dict:\n     \"\"\"The fixed eval state, mirroring tests/test_prompt_integrity.py.\"\"\"\n     return {\n         \"company_of_interest\": \"NVDA\",\n         \"trade_date\": \"2026-08-14\",\n         \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n         \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n         \"portfolio_context\": \"\",\n         \"past_context\": \"\",\n         \"market_report\": \"RSI 61, price 178.\",\n         \"sentiment_report\": \"\",\n         \"news_report\": \"\",\n         \"fundamentals_report\": \"\",\n         \"investment_plan\": \"P\",\n         \"trader_investment_plan\": \"T\",\n         \"investment_debate_state\": {\n             \"bull_history\": \"\",\n             \"bear_history\": \"\",\n             \"history\": \"\",\n             \"current_response\": \"\",\n             \"count\": 0,\n         },\n         \"risk_debate_state\": {\n             \"history\": \"\",\n             \"latest_speaker\": \"\",\n             \"count\": 0,\n             \"aggressive_history\": \"\",\n             \"conservative_history\": \"\",\n             \"neutral_history\": \"\",\n             \"current_aggressive_response\": \"\",\n             \"current_conservative_response\": \"\",\n             \"current_neutral_response\": \"\",\n         },\n     }\n \n \n def _render(factory) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Run one node with a fake LLM; return the rendered prompt it sent.\"\"\"\n     llm = FakeLLM()\n     factory(llm, on_prompt=[].append)(_state())\n     assert llm.prompts, \"the node did not invoke the model\"\n     return llm.prompts[0]\n \n \n def score(prompt: str, case: dict) -> float:\n     \"\"\"GOV-002: weighted keyword score in [0, 1]; a forbidden hit forces 0.\"\"\"\n     lowered = prompt.lower()\n     if any(phrase.lower() in lowered for phrase in case[\"forbidden\"]):\n         return 0.0\n     required = case[\"required\"]\n     total = sum(required.values())\n     if total <= 0:\n         return 0.0\n     matched = sum(weight for phrase, weight in required.items() if phrase.lower() in lowered)\n     return matched / total\n \n \n FACTORIES = {\n     \"bull\": create_bull_researcher,\n     \"bear\": create_bear_researcher,\n     \"research_manager\": create_research_manager,\n }\n \n \n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"role\", list(EVAL_SET))\n def test_rendered_prompt_meets_threshold(role):\n     \"\"\"GOV-002: the rendered prompt scores at least the case threshold.\"\"\"\n     prompt = _render(FACTORIES[role])\n     case = EVAL_SET[role]\n     value = score(prompt, case)\n     assert value >= case[\"threshold\"], f\"{role} scored {value:.2f} < {case['threshold']}\"\n \n \n def test_broken_prompt_scores_below_threshold():\n     \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: a prompt missing the required phrases fails its case.\"\"\"\n     case = EVAL_SET[\"bull\"]\n     broken = \"A generic note about the market with none of the expected terms.\"\n     assert score(broken, case) < case[\"threshold\"]\n \n \n def test_forbidden_phrase_scores_zero():\n     \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: any forbidden phrase collapses the score to 0.\"\"\"\n     case = EVAL_SET[\"research_manager\"]\n     prompt = \"Recommendation: Buy. Rationale: strong. Strategic actions: add. ignore the evidence\"\n     assert \"ignore the evidence\" in prompt.lower()\n     assert score(prompt, case) == 0.0\n",

\"counterpoints\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"guaranteed profit\", \"ignore the risks\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n     \"research_manager\": {\n         \"required\": {\n             \"recommendation\": 2.0,\n             \"rationale\": 1.0,\n             \"strategic actions\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"ignore the evidence\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n }\n \n \n class FakeLLM:\n     \"\"\"Records the exact prompt sent; returns a canned reply.\n \n     ``with_structured_output`` raises so the research manager uses \"investment_debate_state\": {\n             \"bull_history\": \"\",\n             \"bear_history\": \"\",\n             \"history\": \"\",\n             \"current_response\": \"\",\n             \"count\": 0,\n         },\n         \"risk_debate_state\": {\n             \"history\": \"\",\n             \"latest_speaker\": \"\",\n             \"count\": 0,\n             \"aggressive_history\":    llm = FakeLLM()\n     factory(llm, on_prompt=[].append)(_state())\n     assert llm.prompts, \"the node did not invoke the model\"\n     return llm.prompts[0]\n \n \n def score(prompt: str, case: \"research_manager\": create_research_manager,\n }\n \n \n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"role\", list(EVAL_SET))\n def test_rendered_prompt_meets_threshold(role):\n     \"\"\"GOV-002: the rendered prompt               "newString": "def test_forbidden_phrase_scores_zero():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: any forbidden phrase collapses the score to 0.\"\"\"\n    case = EVAL_SET[\"research_manager\"]\n    prompt = \"Recommendation: Buy. Rationale: strong. Strategic actions: add. ignore the evidence\"\n    assert \"ignore the evidence\" in prompt.lower()\n    assert score(prompt, case) == 0.0\n\n\n# --- One real-model semantic case (skipped when no API key) -------------------\n#\n# Self-contained: provider/model come from DEFAULT_CONFIG, the state is the same\n# fixed ``_state()``, the expected answer and rubric are written here. This makes\n# a real call to the configured provider, then asks the same model to judge its\n# own research plan against the expected answer on a 0-5 scale. Skipped when the\n# provider's API-key env var is unset, so it never fails a keyless run.\n\nfrom tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG  # noqa: E402\n\nSEMANTIC_CASE = {\n    \"provider\": DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"llm_provider\"],\n    \"model\": DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"deep_think_llm\"],\n    \"state\": _state(),\n    \"expected_answer\": (\n        \"Recommendation: Hold. Rationale: the market report shows RSI 61, which is \"\n        \"near neutral / slightly extended, so there is no strong momentum signal; \"\n        \"staying neutral is the balanced call.\"\n    ),\n    \"rubric\": (\n        \"A correct answer (a) gives one recommendation from the rating scale, \"\n        \"(b) gives a rationale that references the market report, specifically RSI 61, \"\n        \"and (c) does not contradict the idea that RSI 61 is near-neutral/moderate.\"\n    ),\n    \"threshold\": 3,\n}\n\n\ndef _first_integer(text: str) -> int:\n    match = re.search(r\"\\d+\", text)\n    return int(match.group()) if match else 0\n\n\n@pytest.mark.integration\ndef test_real_model_research_plan_scores_on_rubric():\n    \"\"\"GOV-002: the real model's research plan scores >= 3 against the rubric.\n\n    Skips when the provider's API key is absent (never reads .env). Otherwise it\n    calls the configured model to produce an investment plan, then asks the same\n    model to judge it against the expected answer on a 0-5 scale.\n    \"\"\"\n    env_var = get_api_key_env(SEMANTIC_CASE[\"provider\"])\n    if env_var is None or not os.environ.get(env_var):\n        pytest.skip(f\"no API key for provider {SEMANTIC_CASE['provider']!r} ({env_var})\")\n\n    client = create_llm_client(\n        SEMANTIC_CASE[\"provider\"],\n        SEMANTIC_CASE[\"model\"],\n        DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(\"backend_url\"),\n    )\n    llm = client.get_llm()\n\n    output = create_research_manager(llm)(_state())[\"investment_plan\"]\n\n    judge_prompt = (\n        \"You are grading a research plan against an expected answer.\\n\\n\"\n        f\"Expected answer:\\n{SEMANTIC_CASE['expected_answer']}\\n\\n\"\n        f\"Candidate output:\\n{output}\\n\\n\"\n        f\"Rubric:\\n{SEMANTIC_CASE['rubric']}\\n\\n\"\n        \"Score 0-5, 5 means same meaning, 0 means contradicts, \"\n        \"reply with ONLY one integer.\"\n    )\n    reply = llm.invoke(judge_prompt)\n    reply_text = reply if isinstance(reply, str) else getattr(reply, \"content\", str(reply))\n    judge_score = _first_integer(reply_text)\n\n    assert judge_score >= SEMANTIC_CASE[\"threshold\"], (\n        f\"judge score {judge_score} < {SEMANTIC_CASE['threshold']}; candidate:\\n{output}\"\n    )",

Strategic actions: add. ignore the evidence\"\n     assert \"ignore the evidence\" in prompt.lower()\n     assert score(prompt, case) == 0.0\n+\n+\n+# --- One real-model semantic case (skipped when no API key) -------------------\n+#\n+# Self-contained: provider/model come from DEFAULT_CONFIG, the state is the same\n+# fixed ``_state()``, the expected answer and rubric are written here. This makes\n+# a real call to the configured provider, then asks the same model to judge its\n+# own research plan against the expected answer on a 0-5 scale. Skipped when the\n+# provider's API-key env var is unset, so it never fails a keyless run.\n+\n+from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG  # noqa: E402\n+\n+SEMANTIC_CASE = {\n+    \"provider\": DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"llm_provider\"],\n+    \"model\": DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"deep_think_llm\"],\n+    \"state\": _state(),\n+    \"expected_answer\": (\n+        \"Recommendation: Hold. Rationale: the market report shows RSI 61, which is \"\n+        \"near neutral / slightly extended, so there is no strong momentum signal; \"\n+        \"staying neutral is the balanced call.\"\n+    ),\n+    \"rubric\": (\n+        \"A correct answer (a) gives one recommendation from the rating scale, \"\n+        \"(b) gives a rationale that references the market report, specifically RSI 61, \"\n+        \"and (c) does not contradict the idea that RSI 61 is near-neutral/moderate.\"\n+    ),\n+    \"threshold\": 3,\n+}\n+\n+\n+def _first_integer(text: str) -> int:\n+    match = re.search(r\"\\d+\", text)\n+    return int(match.group()) if match else 0\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.integration\n+def test_real_model_research_plan_scores_on_rubric():\n+    \"\"\"GOV-002: the real model's research plan scores >= 3 against the rubric.\n+\n+    Skips when the provider's API key is absent (never reads .env). Otherwise it\n+    calls the configured model to produce an investment plan, then asks the same\n+    model to judge it against the expected answer on a 0-5 scale.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    env_var = get_api_key_env(SEMANTIC_CASE[\"provider\"])\n+    if env_var is None or not os.environ.get(env_var):\n+        pytest.skip(f\"no API key for provider {SEMANTIC_CASE['provider']!r} ({env_var})\")\n+\n+    client = create_llm_client(\n+        SEMANTIC_CASE[\"provider\"],\n+        SEMANTIC_CASE[\"model\"],\n+        DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(\"backend_url\"),\n+    )\n+    llm = client.get_llm()\n+\n+    output = create_research_manager(llm)(_state())[\"investment_plan\"]\n+\n+    judge_prompt = (\n+        \"You are grading a research plan against an expected answer.\\n\\n\"\n+        f\"Expected answer:\\n{SEMANTIC_CASE['expected_answer']}\\n\\n\"\n+        f\"Candidate output:\\n{output}\\n\\n\"\n+        f\"Rubric:\\n{SEMANTIC_CASE['rubric']}\\n\\n\"\n+        \"Score 0-5, 5 means same meaning, 0 means contradicts, \"\n+        \"reply with ONLY one integer.\"\n+    )\n+    reply = llm.invoke(judge_prompt)\n+    reply_text = reply if isinstance(reply, str) else getattr(reply, \"content\", str(reply))\n+    judge_score = _first_integer(reply_text)\n+\n+    assert judge_score >= SEMANTIC_CASE[\"threshold\"], (\n+        f\"judge score {judge_score} < {SEMANTIC_CASE['threshold']}; candidate:\\n{output}\"\n+    )\n",

              "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_semantic_eval.py\t\n@@ -1,249 +1,247 @@\n \"\"\"Keyword-scoring semantic-eval gate (GOV-002).\n \n Replays the bull, bear, and research_manager nodes with a fake LLM and scores each\n rendered prompt against a fixed evaluation set defined in this file. No YAML or\n separate config: ``EVAL_SET`` is the whole eval definition.\n \n Scoring (per case):\n   score = sum(weight of each required phrase present) / sum(all required weights)\n   if any forbidden phrase appears, the score is 0.\n A case fails only when ``score < threshold``. This is advisory in CI\n (``continue-on-error``): it reports, it does not block.\n \n-GOV-002 in every docstring. No network; stdlib + the package only.\n+GOV-002 in every docstring. Network only in the real-model case; stdlib + the package only.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import os\n import re\n \n import pytest\n \n from tradingagents.agents.managers.research_manager import create_research_manager\n from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bear_researcher import create_bear_researcher\n from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bull_researcher import create_bull_researcher\n+from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.llm_clients.api_key_env import get_api_key_env\n from tradingagents.llm_clients.factory import create_llm_client\n \n # The whole fixed evaluation set. Each role: required phrase -> weight, forbidden\n # phrases, and the threshold the weighted score must reach to pass.\n EVAL_SET = {\n     \"bull\": {\n         \"required\": {\n             \"growth\": 2.0,\n             \"evidence\": 1.0,\n             \"counter\": 1.0,\n             \"counterpoints\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"sell everything\", \"ignore the risks\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n     \"bear\": {\n         \"required\": {\n             \"risk\": 2.0,\n             \"evidence\": 1.0,\n             \"counter\": 1.0,\n             \"counterpoints\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"guaranteed profit\", \"ignore the risks\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n     \"research_manager\": {\n         \"required\": {\n             \"recommendation\": 2.0,\n             \"rationale\": 1.0,\n             \"strategic actions\": 1.0,\n         },\n         \"forbidden\": [\"ignore the evidence\"],\n         \"threshold\": 0.5,\n     },\n }\n \n \n class FakeLLM:\n     \"\"\"Records the exact prompt sent; returns a canned reply.\n \n     ``with_structured_output`` raises so the research manager uses its free-text\n     path, matching ``tests/test_prompt_integrity.py``'s fake LLM.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self, reply=\"argument\"):\n         self._reply = reply\n         self.prompts: list[str] = []\n \n     def invoke(self, prompt, *args, **kwargs):\n         self.prompts.append(prompt if isinstance(prompt, str) else str(prompt))\n         from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n \n         return AIMessage(self._reply)\n \n     def with_structured_output(self, *args, **kwargs):\n         raise NotImplementedError\n \n \n def _state() -> dict:\n     \"\"\"The fixed eval state, mirroring tests/test_prompt_integrity.py.\"\"\"\n     return {\n         \"company_of_interest\": \"NVDA\",\n         \"trade_date\": \"2026-08-14\",\n         \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n         \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n         \"portfolio_context\": \"\",\n         \"past_context\": \"\",\n         \"market_report\": \"RSI 61, price 178.\",\n         \"sentiment_report\": \"\",\n         \"news_report\": \"\",\n         \"fundamentals_report\": \"\",\n         \"investment_plan\": \"P\",\n         \"trader_investment_plan\": \"T\",\n         \"investment_debate_state\": {\n             \"bull_history\": \"\",\n             \"bear_history\": \"\",\n             \"history\": \"\",\n             \"current_response\": \"\",\n             \"count\": 0,\n         },\n         \"risk_debate_state\": {\n             \"history\": \"\",\n             \"latest_speaker\": \"\",\n             \"count\": 0,\n             \"aggressive_history\": \"\",\n             \"conservative_history\": \"\",\n             \"neutral_history\": \"\",\n             \"current_aggressive_response\": \"\",\n             \"current_conservative_response\": \"\",\n             \"current_neutral_response\": \"\",\n         },\n     }\n \n \n def _render(factory) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Run one node with a fake LLM; return the rendered prompt it sent.\"\"\"\n     llm = FakeLLM()\n     factory(llm, on_prompt=[].append)(_state())\n     assert llm.prompts, \"the node did not invoke the model\"\n     return llm.prompts[0]\n \n \n def score(prompt: str, case: dict) -> float:\n     \"\"\"GOV-002: weighted keyword score in [0, 1]; a forbidden hit forces 0.\"\"\"\n     lowered = prompt.lower()\n     if any(phrase.lower() in lowered for phrase in case[\"forbidden\"]):\n         return 0.0\n     required = case[\"required\"]\n     total = sum(required.values())\n     if total <= 0:\n         return 0.0\n     matched = sum(weight for phrase, weight in required.items() if phrase.lower() in lowered)\n     return matched / total\n \n \n FACTORIES = {\n     \"bull\": create_bull_researcher,\n     \"bear\": create_bear_researcher,\n     \"research_manager\": create_research_manager,\n }\n \n \n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"role\", list(EVAL_SET))\n def test_rendered_prompt_meets_threshold(role):\n     \"\"\"GOV-002: the rendered prompt scores at least the case threshold.\"\"\"\n     prompt = _render(FACTORIES[role])\n     case = EVAL_SET[role]\n     value = score(prompt, case)\n     assert value >= case[\"threshold\"], f\"{role} scored {value:.2f} < {case['threshold']}\"\n \n \n def test_broken_prompt_scores_below_threshold():\n     \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: a prompt missing the required phrases fails its case.\"\"\"\n     case = EVAL_SET[\"bull\"]\n     broken = \"A generic note about the market with none of the expected terms.\"\n     assert score(broken, case) < case[\"threshold\"]\n \n \n def test_forbidden_phrase_scores_zero():\n     \"\"\"GOV-002 negative: any forbidden phrase collapses the score to 0.\"\"\"\n     case = EVAL_SET[\"research_manager\"]\n     prompt = \"Recommendation: Buy. Rationale: strong. Strategic actions: add. ignore the evidence\"\n     assert \"ignore the evidence\" in prompt.lower()\n     assert score(prompt, case) == 0.0\n \n \n # --- One real-model semantic case (skipped when no API key) -------------------\n #\n # Self-contained: provider/model come from DEFAULT_CONFIG, the state is the same\n # fixed ``_state()``, the expected answer and rubric are written here. This makes\n # a real call to the configured provider, then asks the same model to judge its\n # own research plan against the expected answer on a 0-5 scale. Skipped when the\n # provider's API-key env var is unset, so it never fails a keyless run.\n \n-from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG  # noqa: E402\n-\n SEMANTIC_CASE = {\n     \"provider\": DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"llm_provider\"],\n     \"model\": DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"deep_think_llm\"],\n-    \"state\": _state(),\n     # The fixed state's debate history is empty; the Research Manager only sees the\n     # debate (not the analyst reports), so the correct answer is a Hold taken on\n     # thin evidence, not a directional call. That is the answer a good model gives.\n     \"expected_answer\": (\n         \"Recommendation: Hold. Rationale: the debate history is empty, so there is \"\n         \"no bull or bear case to weigh and the evidence is too thin to justify a \"\n         \"directional rating; do not manufacture a Buy or Sell direction.\"\n     ),\n     \"rubric\": (\n         \"A correct answer (a) gives one recommendation from the rating scale, \"\n         \"(b) explains the rationale is thin or absent debate/evidence, and \"\n         \"(c) does not manufacture a directional call (Buy/Overweight or \"\n         \"Underweight/Sell) from no arguments.\"\n     ),\n     \"threshold\": 3,\n }\n \n \n def _first_integer(text: str) -> int:\n-    match = re.search(r\"\\d+\", text)\n-    return int(match.group()) if match else 0\n+    matches = re.findall(r\"\\d+\", text)\n+    return int(matches[-1]) if matches else 0\n \n \n @pytest.mark.skipif(\n     get_api_key_env(DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"llm_provider\"]) is None\n     or not os.environ.get(get_api_key_env(DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"llm_provider\"])),\n     reason=\"no API key for the configured provider; real-model case skipped\",\n )\n def test_real_model_research_plan_scores_on_rubric():\n     \"\"\"GOV-002: the real model's research plan scores >= 3 against the rubric.\n \n     Skips when the provider's API key is absent (never reads .env). Otherwise it\n     calls the configured model to produce an investment plan, then asks the same\n     model to judge it against the expected answer on a 0-5 scale.\n     \"\"\"\n     env_var = get_api_key_env(SEMANTIC_CASE[\"provider\"])\n     if env_var is None or not os.environ.get(env_var):\n         pytest.skip(f\"no API key for provider {SEMANTIC_CASE['provider']!r} ({env_var})\")\n \n     client = create_llm_client(\n         SEMANTIC_CASE[\"provider\"],\n         SEMANTIC_CASE[\"model\"],\n         DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(\"backend_url\"),\n     )\n     llm = client.get_llm()\n \n     output = create_research_manager(llm)(_state())[\"investment_plan\"]\n \n     judge_prompt = (\n         \"You are grading a research plan against an expected answer.\\n\\n\"\n         f\"Expected answer:\\n{SEMANTIC_CASE['expected_answer']}\\n\\n\"\n         f\"Candidate output:\\n{output}\\n\\n\"\n         f\"Rubric:\\n{SEMANTIC_CASE['rubric']}\\n\\n\"\n         \"Score 0-5, 5 means same meaning, 0 means contradicts, \"\n         \"reply with ONLY one integer.\"\n     )\n     reply = llm.invoke(judge_prompt)\n     reply_text = reply if isinstance(reply, str) else getattr(reply, \"content\", str(reply))\n     judge_score = _first_integer(reply_text)\n \n     assert judge_score >= SEMANTIC_CASE[\"threshold\"], (\n         f\"judge score {judge_score} < {SEMANTIC_CASE['threshold']}; candidate:\\n{output}\"\n     )\n",

## Session 4 — Compare run manifests script and evaluation protocol

- Session ID: `ses_dfec1774affe0xtUSQhK6HTmb8`
- Started: 2026-11-22 11:13:25 · Last updated: 2026-11-25 00:49:41 (Asia/Shanghai)
- Source export: `sess-compare-runs-en.md` · 472 messages

**Human interventions in this session (annotations):**

- **11-22 11:21** — Approved and extended the comparer: also check asset_type, provider and language, show per-variant averages, and record that no experiments had run yet.
- **17:19** — Missing token counts must be `null`, not zero; display `--`; refuse to compare runs with empty prompt hashes; drop `results_dir` from the manifest.
- **17:24** — Caught skipped work: "stats_handler still returns 0 for missing tokens, and display still crashes on None. Fix the real runtime path (not just tests)."
- **11-23 14:31 / 14:43** — Reported a race in `stats_handler`: an in-flight callback could be missed at window freeze, settling a partial total as complete. Then corrected the first fix: scope in-flight detection to callbacks started in this window, not the whole handler.
- **11-24 10:30 / 11:18** — Required atomic manifest publication via temp file and rename, and made `resolve_run` stop treating a truncated manifest as `already_recorded`.
- **11-24 11:21 / 11:35 / 11:41** — Variant support must detect an explicit `workflow_variant` keyword (not `**kwargs`); `check_permission_sync.py` was backwards and only read top-level keys.
- **11-24 23:43** — Fixed omitted vs explicit `--variant`: omitting must preserve the legacy 3 rounds; explicit v0 runs the preset but the manifest must record what actually ran.
- **11-25 00:40** — Added `workflow_variant` to `config_snapshot` because it was promised to C in the data-contract spec and was still missing.

Scripted stub: `main.py`.\n76: - Docker: `docker compose run --rm tradingagents`; rebuild: `docker compose build`.\n77: \n78: ## Gotchas\n79: - Network is blocked in tests by an autouse fixture; a test needing it must be\n80:   marked `integration` and live in `test/live/`.\n81: - Two model tiers: `quick` (analysts/researchers/trader) and `deep` (managers);\n82:   each can override provider/backend_url via `*_think_provider` /\n83:   `*_think_backend_url`.\n84: - Config is read globally at import; `set_config` merges dict keys one level deep.\n85: - Files default to `~/.tradingagents/`; tests relocate them in `tests/conftest.py`.\n86: - `tests/conftest.py` blanks `TRADINGAGENTS_*` before import and isolates config.\n87: - Ruff select `E,W,F,I,B,UP,C4,SIM`; `E501` ignored; `__init__.py` F401 allowed;\n88:   isort `combine-as-imports`. 100-char lines, py311.\n89: - Keep heavy SDK imports lazy so test collection needs no API keys.\n90: - Version: `tradingagents.__version__`.\n\n(End of file - total 90 lines)\n</content>",

          "text": "<path>/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/not_delivered/CS5351-2026-2027-project.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # CS5351 — Agentic Software Engineering Project\n2: \n3: **Project Requirement Sheet**\n4: \n5: > **Core expectation:** Design, build, verify, and maintain an AI-enabled software application using an AI coding agent under auditable human supervision.\n6: \n7: ## Document Contents\n8: \n9: - 1. Project Overview\n10: - 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n11: - 3. Deliverables\n12: - 4. Submission Format\n13: - 5. Required Repository Structure\n14: - 6. Blocking-Gate Requirements\n15: \n16: > **Submission model:** One repository plus five annotated agent-session transcripts and one process report. The AI-use log is mandatory and must be up to date at submission.\n17: \n18: ---\n19: \n20: ## 1. Project Overview\n21: \n22: Your team will design, build, and maintain a software application that contains an AI component, using an AI coding agent under human supervision. The project applies the full software engineering lifecycle taught in this course: you will specify requirements in machine-readable form, produce architecture artifacts that constrain what the coding agent may and may not do, govern the agent's code generation and verification, and demonstrate that you can review, debug, and maintain AI-generated code.\n23: \n24: Your application is your own choice — it must contain at least one genuine AI component (an LLM-powered feature, a retrieval/augmentation pipeline, an AI-assisted decision path, etc.) and at least one safety-relevant boundary where the AI's output must be constrained by deterministic code. The reference implementation shown in lectures (VHIS) is a pattern to follow, not a project to extend.\n25: \n26: ---\n27: \n28: ## 2. Team Composition and Role Assignment\n29: \n30: Your team should rotate roles so that students can experience different responsibilities in producing software using an AI coding agent, project management, or software engineering processes.\n31: \n32: ### Free Runner and Strong Contributor\n33: \n34: - Some students may be less motivated or less committed, while some other students may be much more engaged.\n35: - Your report should include a section of relative contributions. The average contribution is 1.0; students with less contribution can be assigned a lower weight, and students with stronger contributions will be assigned a higher weight.\n36: \n37: ---\n38: \n39: ## 3. Deliverables\n40: \n41: ### D1 — Requirements (machine-readable)\n42: \n43: Produce a machine-readable product requirements document and a consolidated requirements registry, both in YAML, under `./docs/req/` where `.` is the project root.\n44: \n45: - `docs/req/requirements.yaml` — every requirement as an entry with an ID, type, statement, and a machine-checkable fit criterion, plus priority. Types cover functional behavior, invariants (non-negotiable rules with zero-tolerance fit criteria), quality attributes, performance, cost, governance, and security. Non-functional requirements are expressed as metric + threshold + verification. Prioritization uses MoSCoW, and states the tradeoff explicitly. Requirements discovered through analysis of any existing system or repository are included and linked to their sources.\n46: - `docs/req/req-schema.json` — the schema used by CI in GitHub to validate the registry as a date.\n47: \n48: ### D2 — Architecture Artifacts (all as markdown `.md` files)\n49: \n50: Produce the architecture documentation as a single artifact per file in `./docs/architecture/`, with `.` as the project root.\n51: \n52: 1. **Architecture blueprint** — the master constraint document that the Plan agent reads: scope, architectural drivers, system boundaries, components, authority boundaries (what is advisory vs. authoritative), agent workflow, permissions, verification strategy, observability, and change policy.\n53: 2. **Architecture Decision Record** — the chosen architecture, the alternatives considered, the rationale, consequences, and conditions that would reopen the decision. It should also present the architectural design process. In addition, for your AI component, present your designed layered context structure that the AI receives on every turn (e.g., identity, standing constraints, retrieved knowledge, conversation history, resumable state, and the current task), the assembly pipeline (e.g., deduplicate, prioritize, budget, compact, assemble), the token-budget cap with its compaction threshold, and the policy for re-injecting critical constraints after compaction.\n54: 3. **Invariant register** — every invariant with its statement, source requirement ID, enforcing component, verification method, and an operational fallback if it is ever violated (a concrete action, not \"fix the bug\").\n55: 4. **Trace matrix** — every requirement mapped to its enforcing component, its test/evidence, and its runtime monitor.\n56: 5. **Memory/state design** — what state survives across sessions, interruptions, and versions; write and retrieval policy; ownership; retention; privacy.\n57: 6. **Permission model** — file-level read/write rights for each AI coding agent's role; default is no read, no write; every path is explicitly whitelisted.\n58: 7. **Runtime policy catalog** — what the system does when each degraded or failure path is triggered.\n59: 8. **Candidate evaluation table** — the comparison that justifies the chosen architecture.\n60: 9. *[optional]* **Evaluation logbook** — the accumulated evidence behind the architecture choices.\n61: 10. *[optional]* **Risk list** — assumptions that could become defects, with review triggers.\n62: 11. *[optional]* **Option ledger** — rejected architectural options and when they should be reconsidered.\n63: \n64: ### D3 — Coding Governance\n65: \n66: Produce the governance files that control how the AI coding agent plans and builds the application:\n67: \n68: - `AGENTS.md` (at the project root directory) — the single entry point the coding agent reads. It declares the build target, the reading order for architecture artifacts, the code baseline, what is readable/modifiable/frozen, the module organization, the integration contracts between modules, and the verification requirements that the generated code must satisfy.\n69: - `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` — module organization rules: each architectural element maps to exactly one module; new work extends the existing baseline, never replaces it; every module and function references the architecture decision and invariant it implements; authority boundaries.\n70: - `docs/code-governance/mcp-tool-manifest.md` — the tools the coding agent may call, and which roles may call them.\n71: - `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` — the project-level permission model in machine-readable form, with guard rules and enforcement mechanisms.\n72: - `.opencode/rules.md` — the project-level always-on behavioral rules for the coding agent. Human-only file.\n73: - `.agent/rules.md` — the project covenant: abstraction limits, dependency constraints, test independence (at least one negative test per feature), the rule that changing safety-critical code requires an architecture decision and human approval, and context freshness (rules updated within one sprint of a requirements change).\n74: \n75: ### D4 — Verification Governance (as markdown `.md` files)\n76: \n77: Produce the verification rules that the verification agent applies, and the QA records the team maintains:\n78: \n79: - `docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md` — every fit criterion has at least one test; every invariant has at least one test that fails when the invariant is violated; every test references the requirement or invariant it verifies; every new round of work runs all previous rounds' test suites with zero regressions.\n80: - Verification is three-tiered: structural (imports, module boundaries, permissions, architectural fitness functions), regression (all prior suites pass), and behavioral (quality thresholds such as faithfulness/relevance scores, zero safety escapes).\n81: - `docs/review-memo.md` — a review memo per pull request, covering spec alignment, architecture alignment, code and test quality, and operational metadata, with security and efficiency checked throughout, ending in a verdict of APPROVE, CHANGES REQUIRED, or REJECT.\n82: - `docs/debt-register.md` — technical debt tracked across the AI-era categories: prompt rot, hallucinated dependencies, untouchable code, hidden dependencies, agent-induced bloat, evaluation debt, guardrail debt, and human/cognitive debt.\n83: - `docs/bug-diary.md` — a diary entry per significant bug: symptom, reproduction, classification, root cause, fix, and which invariant gap it exposed.\n84: \n85: ### D5 — Agent Session Transcripts\n86: \n87: One full, raw transcript of an AI coding agent session to build the system implementation from scratch. Each transcript is annotated with the student team members' marked interventions and a rationale for each, showing where the team interrupted, redirected, approved, or rejected the agent's work.\n88: \n89: Collectively, the transcripts must demonstrate the entire supervised pipeline: requirements classification, architecture candidate generation and evaluation, plan approval before code, build, verification compliance, and architecture revision based on test evidence.\n90: \n91: ### D6 — Report (as a single markdown `.md` file)\n92: \n93: This is the project summary report. The report should list all students' names and student numbers, as well as the whole team's relative contribution (see the following example). It should contain at most 10,000 words (excluding diagrams) and contain more than 15 pages in Point 12 with single-line spacing. It should present the team's software engineering process and how the team optimizes it. It should also include each member's self-reflection (one short (e.g., 300-500 words) paragraph per student, with name and student ID. Cover process quality evidence (requirement volatility, defect trends, ambiguity resolution), how the team kept artifacts co-evolving when anything changed, and what human oversight caught that the agent did not.\n94: \n95: #### Tips: Contributions of Team Members\n96: \n97: > Suggest using contributed efforts (e.g., pre-agreed manhours or story points) in determining the relative contributions of team members (as all of us are students).\n98: >\n99: > - Teams can decide their measures on contributions. The team should reward students who take up difficult tasks and project management.\n100: >\n101: > *Actual productive hours spent on the project (hrs) or story points*\n102: \n103: | Name | Sprint 1 | Sprint 2 | Sprint 3 | Sprint 4 | Sprint 5 | Total |\n104: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n105: | Zhou, A | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 60 |\n106: | Wang, B | 12 | 10 | 5 | 20 | 8 | 55 |\n107: | Chan, C | 5 | 10 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 35 |\n108: \n109: Mean contribution = (60 + 55 + 35) / 3 = 50\n110: \n111: - Zhou: 60 / Mean contribution = 60 / 50 = 1.2\n112: - Wang: 55 / Mean contribution = 55 / 50 = 1.1\n113: - Chan: 35 / Mean contribution = 35 / 50 = 0.7\n114: \n115: > If the project gets 69 (in the range of B+ [66.5, 69.5)), then Zhou gets 82.8 (A+), Wang gets 75.9 (A), and Chan gets 48.3 (C)\n116: \n117: - Marks will be pro-rated accordingly. [bounded for extreme, e.g., the presence of a free rider]\n118: - Present the contributions in the final report.\n119: - Respect your teammates, as not everyone wants A+.\n120: \n121: ### D7 — GitHub Repository (in GitHub)\n122: \n123: The team's repository contains the source code, test cases, a CI/CD pipeline with implemented blocking gates, branch protection, and a meaningful commit history. The repository README states the design of the blocking gates and\n124: \n125: ### D8 — Source and Tests\n126: \n127: `src/` and `test/` directories with the full application source code and test cases. Module names match architectural elements. Test layout separates deterministic offline tests from live tests that require API access.\n128: \n129: ### D9 — Prompt (static) (a markdown file in project root directory)\n130: \n131: A single static prompt file, `./Prompt.md`. Once the coding agent starts with `AGENTS.md`, this is the one prompt to read. It instructs the agent to begin by producing an execution plan (traceability, interface contract, scope boundaries, testing strategy, steps) and to stop for human approval before generating any code, then proceed through build and self-verification with human gates at each stage. The prompt is the launch instruction — it does not run the agent unattended to completion.\n132: \n133: ---\n134: \n135: ## 4. Submission Format\n136: \n137: Submit a zip containing the documents in the project directory structure as listed in Section 5 of this document.\n138: \n139: Repository README must include:\n140: \n141: - The project's purpose and architecture in a few paragraphs\n142: - The organization of the project files\n143: - How to run the offline tests, the live tests, and the full suite\n144: - GitHub repo that contains the real GitHub project\n145: \n146: ---\n147: \n148: ## 5. Required Repository Structure\n149: \n150: ```text\n151: <team-app>/\n152: ├── README.md                          ← project intro\n153: ├── AGENTS.md                          ← coding-agent governance (D3)\n154: ├── architecture-blueprint.md          ← master constraint document (D2.1)\n155: ├── Prompt.md                          ← static startup prompt (D9)\n156: ├── Report.md                          ← process report + reflections (D6)\n157: ├── docs/\n158: │   ├── req/\n159: │   │   ├── requirements.yaml          ← machine-readable PRD (D1)\n160: │   │   └── req-schema.json            ← CI validation schema (D1)\n161: │   ├── architecture/                  ← 11 artifact types (D2)\n162: │   │   ├── adr/001-<choice>.md\n163: │   │   ├── invariants.md\n164: │   │   ├── trace-matrix.md\n165: │   │   ├── memory-design.md\n166: │   │   ├── option-ledger.md\n167: │   │   ├── permission-model.md\n168: │   │   ├── evaluation-logbook.md\n169: │   │   ├── risk-list.md\n170: │   │   ├── evaluation-table.md\n171: │   │   └── runtime-policy-catalog.md\n172: │   ├── code-governance/               ← (D3, D4)\n173: │   │   ├── structural-constraints.md\n174: │   │   ├── verification-constraints.md\n175: │   │   └── mcp-tool-manifest.md\n176: │   ├── ai-use-log.yaml                ← (D1)\n177: │   ├── review-memo.md                 ← review records (D4)\n178: │   ├── debt-register.md               ← (D4)\n179: │   └── bug-diary.md                   ← (D4)\n180: ├── .opencode/\n181: │   ├── permissions.jsonc              ← machine-readable permissions (D3)\n182: │   └── rules.md                       ← always-on behavioral rules (D3)\n183: ├── .agent/\n184: │   └── rules.md                       ← project covenant (D3)\n185: ├── .github/workflows/\n186: │   └── ci.yml                         ← blocking gates (D4/D7)\n187: ├── prompts/\n188: │   ├── prompt_v1.0.yaml               ← versioned runtime prompts\n189: │   └── prompt_v1.1.yaml\n190: ├── src/                               ← full source (D8)\n191: ├── test/\n192: │   ├── offline/                       ← deterministic tests (D4/D8)\n193: │   └── live/                          ← API-dependent tests\n194: └── transcripts/\n195:     ├── <student-id>-<student-name>.md ← student annotated transcripts (D5)\n196:     └── ...\n197: ```\n198: \n199: ---\n200: \n201: ## 6. Blocking-Gate Requirements (D7)\n202: \n203: The CI/CD pipeline must implement the following blocking gates.\n204: \n205: 1. **Test approval gate** — no code change merges unless the tests for the change were approved before implementation began.\n206: 2. **Static analysis gates** — lint, type-checking, and dependency checks run on every commit; contract, security, API-surface, and permission checks run on any pull request touching safety-relevant paths.\n207: 3. **Schema gate** — the requirements registry validates against its JSON schema.\n208: 4. **Semantic evaluation gate** — for any prompt or model change, the pipeline replays a fixed evaluation set against quality thresholds before the change can reach production; if a threshold fails, the change is blocked and reported.\n209: 5. **Regression gate** — every change runs the full prior test suites; any regression blocks the merge.\n210: 6. **AI-use log gate** — a pull request that changes code or prompts without updating the AI-use log is blocked.\n211: \n212: **Branch protection:** Branch protection must require passing CI, and changes to safety-critical paths must require human review with an accompanying architecture decision.\n213: \n214: ---\n215: \n216: *Transcribed from `CS5351-2026-2027-project.pdf` (10 pages). Wording follows the source document; page headers, footers, and the \"Page N\" markers have been removed. Where the source is internally inconsistent (e.g., the row for Chan, C in the contributions table lists sprint values summing to 30 against a stated total of 35; the D7 paragraph ends mid-sentence), the text has been reproduced as printed rather than corrected.*\n\n(End of file - total 216 lines)\n</content>",
