Project: Multi-Agent stock analysis with dual constraints of evidence and budget.\n4: This document is the final task plan and does not mean the listed modules are already implemented. Follow the one-week schedule, OpenCode incremental development, CLI and HTML presentation, with no new frontend.\n5: \n6: ## 1. Primary ownership agreement\n7: \n8: | Member | Fixed Module Responsibility | Main Results | Cross Reviewer |\n9: |---|---|---|---|\n10: | A | evidence, requirements, and traceability | conclusions have queryable bases, and evidence time status is clear | E |\n11: | B | Collaboration protocol and context | Independent arguments, targeted responses, constraints preserved after context compression | A |\n12: | C | Workflow, budget, and recovery | Scheduling based on questions and budget, all loops bounded | D |\n13: | D | Deterministic safety and final adjudication | AI cannot bypass hard rules, failures have specific handling | B |\n14: | E | Run records, experiments, CI and delivery | Comparable, reproducible, gates truly block | C |\n15: \n16: The primary owner is responsible for content correctness, interfaces, self-testing, OpenCode supervision, and on-time delivery; reviewers do not do the work for them. E integrates the report and does not write other members' experiments and reflections.\n17: Each person uses an independent branch/working copy; multiple people must not edit in the same directory simultaneously.\n18: \n19: ## 2. Final Functional Boundaries\n20: \n21: Run: Analyst → Shared evidence → Independent bull/bear arguments → Unresolved questions → Targeted response/Budget stop → Research Manager and Trader → Deterministic check → Final Manager → Re-validation → Report and run records.\n22: \n23: - Retain the original path for baseline comparison; prefer extending over replacing the original architecture.\n24: - This week, independent arguments may be generated sequentially, but they are mutually invisible in the first round; subsequent rounds respond according to explicit responds_to.\n25: - For duplicate detection, first implement normalized text deduplication/fingerprinting; do not claim to fully identify semantic duplicates.\n26: - Report-level evidence is not the same as news-level source tracing; only a reliable source time can prove historical availability, and unknown times are explicitly marked.\n27: - The budget is about quota reservation and stage control; the provider's actual billing, hidden retries, and estimation errors are recorded as-is.\n28: - The original three risk roles are retained by default; a streamlined risk path is an optional experimental switch, and the baseline cannot be removed without validation.\n29: - Do not implement live order placement, complex portfolio ledgers, new data platforms, or new frontends.\n30: \n31: ## 3. Complete Project Directory and File Ownership\n32: \n33: Notation: A—E are the sole owners; \"All → E\" etc. means each person submits their own records, which the owner integrates; \"Retained\" means following the upstream rather than newly added results.\n34: The source code is uniformly migrated to the src layout; E organizes a separate migration PR, first verifying installation/entry points/original tests, then parallel development begins. If the layout migration is not yet complete, tasks should reference the original paths first; the two source trees must not coexist.\n35: The following is the complete delivery directory skeleton; upstream directories are marked \"fully retained\", without listing all existing files individually. New filenames are the team's plan, not specified item-by-item by the course.\n36: \n37: ```text\n38: team-app/\n39: ├── README.md                                      [E] run/test/directory/gate/GitHub URL\n40: ├── AGENTS.md                                      [D owner, C/E review] Code governance entry point\n41: ├── Prompt.md                                      [B, D review] The only static startup procedure\n42: ├── architecture-blueprint.md                       [C] the sole normative Blueprint\n43: ├── Report.md                                      [All → E] Single final report\n44: ├── opencode.jsonc                                 [E, D human review] Actual tool configuration\n45: ├── pyproject.toml                                 [E] src layout, entry point, and test discovery\n46: ├── requirements.txt                               [E] Retain and verify dependencies\n47: ├── .gitignore                                     [E] exclude credentials/caches/temporary files\n48: ├── .env.example                                   [E] Contains only variable names and empty values\n49: ├── LICENSE / CHANGELOG.md                          [E] Retain upstream copyright and change provenance\n50: ├── Dockerfile / docker-compose.yml                 [E] If Docker is retained, verify migration compatibility\n51: ├── main.py                                        [E] retains a runnable example entry point\n52: │\n53: ├── .opencode/\n54: │   ├── permissions.jsonc                          [D] Course permission source\n55: │   ├── rules.md                                   [D coordinates, maintained manually by the whole team] human-only\n56: │   └── agents/                                    [D/E] Optional restricted role configuration\n57: ├── .agent/\n58: │   └── rules.md                                   [D] project covenant\n59: ├── .github/\n60: │   ├── CODEOWNERS                                 [Proposed by D, configured by E] Human review of security/governance paths\n61: │   └── workflows/\n62: │       └── ci.yml                                 [E, D review] Six types of gates\n63: │\n64: ├── docs/\n65: │   ├── req/\n66: │   │   ├── prd.yaml                               [A] product scope/user scenarios/trade-offs\n67: │   │   ├── requirements.yaml                      [A aggregates, everyone provides their package] full requirements\n68: │   │   └── req-schema.json                        [A] CI validates the schema\n69: │   ├── architecture/\n70: │   │   ├── README.md Maintain the trace-matrix; collect the test and monitoring mappings of the other four members.\n197: \n198: ### Deliverables\n199: - evidence.py、test_evidence.py、evidence_cases.json。\n200: - prd.yaml、requirements.yaml、req-schema.json、check_requirements.py。\n201: - evidence contract, ADR-002, memory-design, trace-matrix.\n202: - One's own plan, test approvals, full sessions, experiment/bug entries, report sections, and reflections.\n203: \n204: ### Acceptance\n205: Invalid references are rejected; future times cannot enter strict historical judgment; unknown time does not masquerade as verified; snapshots read back identically; different runs are not mixed.\n206: Demonstration: trace from a conclusion's evidence ID to the original report text, then demonstrate invalid references and future metadata.\n207: \n208: ## 5.           "text": "<path>/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/docs/contracts/run-event.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # RunEvent Contract\n2: \n3: Owner: E (runtime records, experiments, CI, delivery).\n4: Status: **step 2 implemented.** `src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py` and\n5: `test/offline/test_run_recorder.py` exist (commit `a6a4a6b`); the field table below\n6: is the current v1 contract. Consumers: `scripts/compare_runs.py` (planned) and\n7: evaluation results (`docs/evaluation/results/`, planned).\n8: \n9: This contract defines the on-disk JSON \"run manifest\" that records one analysis run\n10: well enough to compare runs and to gate prompt/model changes. It is deliberately\n11: minimal in this slice; fields owned by other members are marked and are **not**\n12: validated here.\n13: \n14: ## Design rules\n15: \n16: - **Deterministic by injection.** The recorder never reads the wall clock or a random\n17:   source internally. `created_at`, `run_id`, and `version` are passed in explicitly;\n18:   serialization uses `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`.\n19:   Two calls with identical inputs produce identical bytes (\"byte-stable manifest\").\n20: - **Run identity is structured, not random.** `run_id` is supplied by the caller and is\n21:   never generated inside the recorder. Recommended shape\n22:   `<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<repeat>-<runstamp>`, e.g.\n23:   `v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200`; it must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$`.\n24:   The recorder refuses to overwrite an existing manifest file.\n25: - **Schema is versioned.** Top-level `schema_version` is an `int`. The recorder writes\n26:   `1` and rejects a manifest whose `schema_version` is not the supported value on read\n27:   (explicit error, no silent coercion).\n28: - **No secrets on disk.** Config keys whose name matches a secret pattern\n29:   (`*_api_key`, `*_key`, `backend_url`, `*_token`, `*_password`) are excluded from\n30:   `config_snapshot`; the manifest records only what is safe to compare.\n31: - **Owned fields are not validated here.** `stop_reason` and the evidence/prompt\n32:   snapshot shapes are contracts owned by C and A respectively. This slice stores them\n33:   as opaque values and does **not** assert a value domain for them.\n34: \n35: ## Field list (schema_version 1)\n36: \n37: | # | Field | Type | Req? | Inject./Caller-supplied | Owner | Notes |\n38: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n39: | 1 | `schema_version` | `int` (== 1) | required | recorder | E | Read rejects any other value. |\n40: | 2 | `run_id` | `str`, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$` | required | caller | E | Unique within the results root; the recorder refuses to overwrite an existing file. Never generated internally. No `/`, no `..`, ≤ 64 chars. |\n41: | 3 | `created_at` | `str` (ISO-8601) | required | caller | E | Not `datetime.now()` internally. |\n42: | 4 | `version` | `str` | required | caller (`tradingagents.__version__`) | E | Package version that produced the run. |\n43: | 5 | `ticker` | `str` (non-empty) | required | caller | E | `company_of_interest` for the run. |\n44: | 6 | `trade_date` | `str` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | required | caller | E | Analysis date. |\n45: | 7 | `asset_type` | `str` | required | caller | E | e.g. `stock`, `crypto`. |\n46: | 8 | `outcome` | `str` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | E | Final rating string, or `null` if the run produced none. |\n47: | 9 | `config_snapshot` | `object` (str→scalar) | required | caller | E | Run settings minus secret-pattern keys (rule above). |\n48: | 10 | `prompt_hashes` | `object` (str→str) | required (may be `{}`) | caller | B | Prompt name → hash. Shape/owner: B. Not validated here. |\n49: | 11 | `evidence_snapshot` | `object` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | A | Evidence snapshot id/pointer. Shape/owner: A. Not validated here. |\n50: | 12 | `usage` | `object` | required | caller | E | `{llm_calls:int, tool_calls:int, tokens_in:int, tokens_out:int}`. |\n51: | 13 | `duration_seconds` | `number` (>= 0) or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | E | Wall time measured by the caller, passed in. |\n52: | 14 | `failure` | `str` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | E | Failure summary if the run failed. |\n53: | 15 | `stop_reason` | `str` or `null` | required (may be null) | caller | **C** | Opaque here. Value domain owned by C's `execution_policy`; **not validated in this slice.** |\n54: \n55: All 15 keys are present on every manifest (nullable ones set to `null`). Required\n56: `str` fields reject empty strings. Missing required keys, or an unsupported\n57: `schema_version`, are rejected on write and on read.\n58: \n59: ## Run identity (`run_id`)\n60: \n61: Format is recommended, not enforced by the recorder; the recorder validates only the\n62: charset and the no-overwrite rule.\n63: \n64: | Segment | Example | Meaning |\n65: |---|---|---|\n66: | `variant` | `v2` | Architecture variant: `v0` original, `v1` trimmed, `v2` adaptive |\n67: | `ticker` | `nvda` | Lower-case symbol |\n68: | `trade_date` | `2026-11-20` | Analysis date — **not** the date the run happened |\n69: | `r<repeat>` | `r1` | 1-based repetition index for identical inputs |\n70: | `runstamp` | `20261121t1200` | Run time, UTC, `YYYYMMDDtHHMM` |\n71: \n72: Rules:\n73: \n74: - Charset `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$` — lower case only, no `/`, no `..`, ≤ 64 chars.\n75:   This is what makes the id safe to use as a directory name under the results root.\n76: - Uniqueness is enforced by the recorder: `write_manifest` raises if the target file\n77:   already exists and never overwrites.\n78: - `build_run_id(variant, ticker, trade_date, repeat, at)` is a pure helper that formats\n79:   the id. `at` is a parameter, so the recorder still never reads the clock.\n80: \n81: Why both the repeat index and the runstamp exist: the repeat index is a *design*\n82: dimension (repeated runs of identical inputs, e.g. three samples for variance), while\n83: the runstamp is the *physical* fact of when the run happened. Two runs of the same\n84: variant/ticker/date after a code change differ only by `runstamp`; without it they\n85: would collide and one result would be silently lost.\n86: \n87: ## What this contract deliberately does not define\n88: \n89: - No `stop_reason` enum (C owns it — see C §6.5 and `execution_policy.py`, planned).\n90: - No prompt-hash algorithm (B owns prompt versioning, `prompts/prompt_v1.x.yaml`).\n91: - No evidence snapshot schema (A owns `evidence.py` and `evidence.md`).\n92: - No CLI/graph/stats integration (later steps depend on C's `AgentState` and stop enum).\n93: - No CI gate. Gates (§6) are a later E step.\n94: \n95: ## Negative cases the future recorder test must cover (slice 2)\n96: \n97: - Missing required field (e.g. `version`) → rejected with a specific error.\n98: - Unsupported `schema_version` → rejected with a specific error.\n99: - Secret-pattern config key (e.g. `openai_api_key`) → absent from `config_snapshot`.\n\n(End of file - total 99 lines)\n</content>",

          "text": "<path>/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: \"\"\"Deterministic run manifest recorder (docs/contracts/run-event.md).\n2: \n3: Records one analysis run as a JSON manifest so runs can be compared and\n4: prompt/model changes can be gated. The recorder never reads the wall clock or a\n5: random source: ``created_at``, ``run_id`` and ``version`` are supplied by the\n6: caller, so identical inputs produce byte-identical output (\"byte-stable\n7: manifest\"). Fields owned by other members (``stop_reason`` for C,\n8: ``prompt_hashes`` for B, ``evidence_snapshot`` for A) are stored opaquely and are\n9: not validated here.\n10: \"\"\"\n11: \n12: from __future__ import annotations\n13: \n14: import json\n15: import re\n16: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\n17: from datetime import UTC, datetime\n18: from pathlib import Path\n19: \n20: SCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n21: \n22: RUN_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n23: \n24: _STRING_FIELDS = (\"run_id\", \"created_at\", \"version\", \"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n25: \n26: _REQUIRED_FIELDS = (\n27:     \"schema_version\",\n28:     \"run_id\",\n29:     \"created_at\",\n30:     \"version\",\n31:     \"ticker\",\n32:     \"trade_date\",\n33:     \"asset_type\",\n34:     \"outcome\",\n35:     \"config_snapshot\",\n36:     \"prompt_hashes\",\n37:     \"evidence_snapshot\",\n38:     \"usage\",\n39:     \"duration_seconds\",\n40:     \"failure\",\n41:     \"stop_reason\",\n42: )\n43: \n44: # Keys that must never reach disk: their names carry credentials or endpoints.\n45: _SECRET_SUFFIXES = (\"_api_key\", \"_key\", \"_token\", \"_password\")\n46: _SECRET_EXACT = (\"backend_url\",)\n47: \n48: \n49: def _is_secret_key(name: str) -> bool:\n50:     return name in _SECRET_EXACT or name.endswith(_SECRET_SUFFIXES)\n51: \n52: \n53: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n54: class RunEvent:\n55:     \"\"\"One run's record. Every field is required except ``schema_version``.\n56: \n57:     Omitting a required field raises ``TypeError`` at construction, so the\n58:     manifest cannot be built half-formed. ``frozen`` keeps a recorded event\n59:     immutable; adjust by constructing a new one.\n60:     \"\"\"\n61: \n62:     run_id: str\n63:     created_at: str\n64:     version: str\n65:     ticker: str\n66:     trade_date: str\n67:     asset_type: str\n68:     outcome: str | None\n69:     config_snapshot: dict\n70:     prompt_hashes: dict\n71:     evidence_snapshot: dict | None\n72:     usage: dict\n73:     duration_seconds: float | None\n74:     failure: str | None\n75:     stop_reason: str | None\n76:     schema_version: int = SCHEMA_VERSION\n77: \n78: \n79: def build_run_id(variant: str, ticker: str, trade_date: str, repeat: int, at: datetime) -> str:\n80:     \"\"\"A stable, filename-safe run id: ``<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<n>-<stamp>``.\n81: \n82:     ``at`` is passed in; the clock is never read here. Inputs are **lowercased**\n83:     (not rejected) so the id always satisfies ``RUN_ID_PATTERN`` regardless of\n84:     how the caller spelled the variant or ticker. ``at`` is normalized to UTC and\n85:     rendered ``YYYYMMDDtHHMM`` (e.g. ``20261121t1200``). ``repeat`` is a 1-based\n86:     index, so values below 1 are rejected.\n87:     \"\"\"\n88:     if repeat < 1:\n89:         raise ValueError(f\"repeat must be >= 1, got {repeat!r}\")\n90:     if at.tzinfo is None:\n91:         at = at.replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n92:     stamp = at.astimezone(UTC).strftime(\"%Y%m%dt%H%M\")\n93:     return f\"{variant.lower()}-{ticker.lower()}-{trade_date}-r{repeat}-{stamp}\"\n94: \n95: \n96: def _validated_manifest(event: RunEvent) -> dict:\n97:     \"\"\"Validate ``event`` and return the dict that is written to disk.\"\"\"\n98:     if event.schema_version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n99:         raise ValueError(\n100:             f\"unsupported schema_version {event.schema_version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\"\n101:         )\n102:     if not RUN_ID_PATTERN.match(event.run_id):\n103:         raise ValueError(f\"invalid run_id {event.run_id!r}; must match {RUN_ID_PATTERN.pattern}\")\n104:     for name in _STRING_FIELDS:\n105:         value = getattr(event, name)\n106:         if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n107:             raise ValueError(f\"required field {name!r} must be a non-empty string\")\n108: \n109:     manifest = asdict(event)\n110:     manifest[\"config_snapshot\"] = {\n111:         key: value\n112:         for key, value in event.config_snapshot.items()\n113:         if not _is_secret_key(key)\n114:     }\n115:     return manifest\n116: \n117: \n118: def write_manifest(event: RunEvent, path) -> Path:\n119:     \"\"\"Write ``event`` as a JSON manifest to ``path``; never overwrite.\n120: \n121:     Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported schema version, an invalid\n122:     ``run_id``, or an empty required string, and ``FileExistsError`` if ``path``\n123:     already exists.\n124:     \"\"\"\n125:     path = Path(path)\n126:     manifest = _validated_manifest(event)\n127:     payload = json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n128:     # \"x\" refuses to overwrite an existing file atomically.\n129:     with open(path, \"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n130:         handle.write(payload)\n131:     return path\n132: \n133: \n134: def read_manifest(path) -> dict:\n135:     \"\"\"Read a manifest, rejecting an unsupported ``schema_version`` or a missing key.\"\"\"\n136:     with open(Path(path), encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n137:         manifest = json.load(handle)\n138:     version = manifest.get(\"schema_version\")\n139:     if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n140:         raise ValueError(f\"unsupported schema_version {version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\")\n141:     missing = [name for name in _REQUIRED_FIELDS if name not in manifest]\n142:     if missing:\n143:         raise ValueError(f\"manifest missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}\")\n144:     return manifest\n\n(End of file - total 144 lines)\n</content>",

{path}\")\n70:         return 1\n71: \n72:     unreviewed = [str(e.get(\"id\")) for e in new_entries if e.get(\"human_reviewed\") is not True]\n73:     if unreviewed:\n74:         print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: new entry not human_reviewed: {unreviewed}\")\n75:         return 1\n76: \n77:     print(f\"[ai-use-log] OK: new entry id(s) {[e.get('id') for e in new_entries]}\")\n78:     return 0\n79: \n80: \n81: if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n82:     raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n\n(End of file - Stdlib + PyYAML only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom gate_common import changed, gated, load_yaml\n\nLOG_PATH = \"docs/ai-use-log.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _entries(text: str) -> list[dict]:\n    return list(load_yaml(text).get(\"entries\") or [])\n\n\ndef _ids(entries: list[dict]) -> list[str]:\n    return [entry[\"id\"] for entry in entries if entry.get(\"id\")]\n\n\ndef _read_at(ref: str, path: str) -> str:\n    result = subprocess.run([\"git\", \"show\", f\"{ref}:{path}\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    return result.stdout if result.returncode == 0 else \"\"\n\n\ndef _read_worktree(path: str) -> str:\n    file_path = Path(path)\n    return file_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if file_path.exists() else \"\"\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n    if len(argv) < 3:\n        print(\"usage: check_ai_use_log.py <base_sha> <head_sha>\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n    base, head = argv[1], argv[2]\n\n    gated_paths = gated(changed(base, head))\n    if not gated_paths:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] docs-only PR: no gated changes, skipping\")\n        return 0\n\n    base_ids = _ids(_entries(_read_at(base, LOG_PATH)))\n    head_entries = _entries(_read_worktree(LOG_PATH))\n    head_ids = _ids(head_entries)\n\n    duplicated = sorted({i for i in head_ids if head_ids.count(i) > 1})\n    if duplicated:\n        print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: duplicate entry id(s): {duplicated}\")\n        return 1\n\n    new_entries = [e for e in head_entries if e.get(\"id\") not in base_ids]\n    if not new_entries:\n        print(\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: gated paths changed but no new log entry added.\")\n        for path in gated_paths:\n            print(f\"    - {path}\")\n        return 1\n\n    unreviewed = [str(e.get(\"id\")) for e in new_entries if e.get(\"human_reviewed\") is not True]\n    if unreviewed:\n        print(f\"[ai-use-log] BLOCKED: new entry not human_reviewed: {unreviewed}\")\n        return 1\n\n    print(f\"[ai-use-log] OK: new entry id(s) {[e.get('id') for e in new_entries]}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))",

Project: Multi-Agent stock analysis with dual constraints of evidence and budget.\\n4: This document is the final task plan and does not indicate that the listed modules have been implemented. It follows a one-week schedule, OpenCode incremental development, CLI and HTML presentation, with no new frontend.\\n5: \\n6: ## 1. Primary Responsibility Agreements\\n7: \\n8: | Member | Fixed Module Responsibility | Main Results | Cross Reviewer |\\n9: |---|---|---|---|\\n10: | A | Evidence, Requirements and Traceability | Conclusions have queryable basis, evidence time status is clear | E |\\n11: | B | Collaboration Protocol and Context | Independent arguments, targeted responses, constraints preserved after context compression | A |\\n12: | C | Workflow, Budget and Recovery | Scheduling based on problem and budget, all loops bounded | D |\\n13: | D | Deterministic Safety and Final Verdict | AI cannot bypass hard rules, failures have specific handling | B |\\n14: | E | Run Records, Experiments, CI and Delivery | Comparable, reproducible, gates actually block | C |\\n15: \\n16: The primary owner is responsible for content correctness, interfaces, self-testing, OpenCode supervision and on-time delivery; reviewers do not do the work for them. E compiles the report and does not write other members' experiments and reflections.\\n17: Everyone uses an independent branch/working copy; multiple people cannot edit in the same directory simultaneously.\\n18: \\n19: ## 2. Final Functional Boundaries\\n20: \\n21: Run: analysts → shared evidence → independent bull/bear arguments → unresolved questions → targeted responses/budget stop → Research Manager and Trader → deterministic check → final manager → re-validation → report and run records.\\n22: \\n23: - Keep the original path for baseline comparison; prefer extending rather than replacing the original architecture.\\n24: - This week independent arguments can be generated sequentially, but are mutually invisible in the first round; subsequent rounds respond according to explicit responds_to.\\n25: - For duplicate detection, first implement normalized text deduplication/fingerprinting; do not claim to fully identify semantic duplicates.\\n26: - Report-level evidence is not the same as news-level provenance; only reliable source timestamps can prove historical usability, and unknown times are explicitly marked.\\n27: - Budget is quota reservation and phase control; provider actual billing, hidden retries and estimation errors are recorded truthfully.\\n28: - The original three risk roles are kept by default; the streamlined risk path is an optional experimental switch, and the base cannot be removed without validation.\\n29: - Do not implement live trading, complex portfolio ledgers, new data platforms or new frontends.\\n30: \\n31: ## 3. Missing model → incomparable (fail loud, don't guess).\n  - `prompt_hashes` compared as whole dict (name→hash).\n  - Ticker/date compared exactly.\n- `Comparison` (frozen dataclass, JSON-serializable): `baseline_run_id`, `guard` (the shared ticker/date/model/prompt hashes), `variants` (list of per-run rows: `run_id`, `outcome`, `usage`, `duration_seconds`, `failure`, `stop_reason`), plus an explicit `notes` list (e.g. \"no quality score computed; quantities are reported, not scored\").\n- CLI `main(argv)` style like the gate scripts; `--json` for machine output; exit 0 on comparison, exit 1 with reason on refusal, exit 2 on usage error. Byte-stable JSON (`sort_keys`, indent=2).\n\n**Negative cases (required):** differ in ticker / differ in trade_date / differ in model / differ in prompt hash each raise and produce no comparison; a manifest missing the model key is refused; refusal message names exactly which guard key diverged.\n\n**Files to create:**\n1. `scripts/compare_runs.py`\n2. `test/offline/test_compare_runs.py` (write tests first; fixtures built via `RunEvent` + `tmp_path`, no network)\n3. `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` — fixed eval set, metrics (usage/duration/outcome agreement, **no invented quality scores**), thresholds deferred to B/D, guard rules, refusal semantics, how `results/` is populated.\n\n**Deferred / note:** \"quality scores\" and semantic thresholds are B/D-owned (their scoring spec) — protocol marks them out of scope so we don't fabricate; today it compares only what the manifest records.\n\nShall I proceed with this plan?               "file": "docs/evaluation/protocol.md",
              "patch": "Index: docs/evaluation/protocol.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/evaluation/protocol.md\t\n+++ docs/evaluation/protocol.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@\n+# Evaluation Protocol\n+\n+Owner: E (runtime records, experiments, CI, delivery). Reviewers: B (collaboration /\n+prompt versioning) and D (deterministic safety) per the team split §3.\n+Status: **tooling only.** `scripts/compare_runs.py` and `test/offline/test_compare_runs.py`\n+exist and pass offline; **no experiments have run yet**. The comparison tables the\n+report needs (`docs/evaluation/results/`) do not exist and must not be fabricated.\n+\n+This protocol fixes *how* runs are compared and *what* a comparison may claim. It\n+does not define semantic-quality scoring: that spec is owned by B and D and is not\n+implemented in this slice (see \"Out of scope\" below). Until real runs exist, this\n+document and the tool are the only deliverables here.\n+\n+## Fixed inputs (the comparison set)\n+\n+Two runs may be compared only when these inputs are identical to the baseline. The\n+tool enforces this; a mismatch is refused, not averaged or shown side by side.\n+\n+| Guard key | Source | Why it must match |\n+|---|---|---|\n+| `ticker` | manifest top level | different company = different question |\n+| `trade_date` | manifest top level | different analysis date = different information set |\n+| `asset_type` | manifest top level | `stock` vs `crypto` changes tools and rules |\n+| model | `config_snapshot.quick_think_llm`, `deep_think_llm` | a model change is the very thing being evaluated |\n+| provider | `config_snapshot.llm_provider` (+ optional `*_think_provider`) | different backend = different outputs |\n+| language | `config_snapshot.output_language` | report text changes with language |\n+| prompt | `prompt_hashes` (name → hash) | a prompt change invalidates a like-for-like comparison |\n+\n+A missing required config key (model, provider, language) is treated as\n+**incomparable** — the tool refuses rather than guessing a default.\n+\n+## Variants\n+\n+Each run is tagged by the first segment of its `run_id`\n+(`<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<repeat>-<runstamp>`):\n+\n+| Variant | Meaning |\n+|---|---|\n+| `v0` | original upstream path (baseline for comparison) |\n+| `v1` | trimmed / simple reduction |\n+| `v2` | adaptive collaboration |\n+\n+Comparing a run against itself-other-variants is the point; comparing different\n+inputs is refused.\n+\n+## Metrics reported\n+\n+Only quantities the manifest actually records. Per run: `outcome`, `usage`\n+(`llm_calls`, `tool_calls`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`), `duration_seconds`,\n+`failure`, `stop_reason`. Per variant: **count of runs** and the **average** of each\n+numeric field (`null` values excluded from that field's average).\n+\n+The token-reduction goal from the team plan (e.g. 20–25%) is a *target*, not a\n+result: the protocol reports measured averages; it does not assert the target was\n+met. If real runs do not hit it, the results file says so.\n+\n+## Thresholds\n+\n+Thresholds for a *passing* comparison are intentionally left unset here. They belong\n+with the semantic-evaluation spec (B/D) and the CI semantic gate (§6.4). This slice\n+ships no threshold and no gate; it only produces comparable numbers.\n+\n+## Out of scope (owned elsewhere)\n+\n+- **Semantic / quality scores** (faithfulness, relevance, argument independence): B\n+  and D. This tool does not compute, infer, or approximate them. The absence of a\n+  score is the honest output.\n+- **`stop_reason` value domain**: C (`execution_policy`). Reported opaquely.\n+- **Evidence snapshot semantics**: A (`evidence.py`). Reported opaquely.\n+- **Live evaluation runs**: `test/live/test_fixed_eval.py` (later; needs API access).\n+\n+## How to run\n+\n+```bash\n+# Compare two or more manifests of the same input across variants.\n+python scripts/compare_runs.py results/v0-nvda-.../manifest.json \\\n+                             results/v2-nvda-.../manifest.json\n+python scripts/compare_runs.py ... --json     # machine-readable output\n+\n+# Offline tests (no network, no API keys).\n+pytest test/offline/test_compare_runs.py -q\n+```\n+\n+Exit codes: `0` comparable, `1` refused (reason on stderr names the differing guard\n+key), `2` usage error. Results meant for the report go under\n+`docs/evaluation/results/`, one file per comparison, with the commit and manifest\n+paths recorded — **only after the runs actually happen**.\n+\n+## Current state\n+\n+- Comparison tooling: implemented, 20 offline tests green.\n+- Experiments: **none run.** No `results/` files exist. Do not add comparison tables\n+  until real manifests are produced from real runs.\n",

              "file": "scripts/compare_runs.py",
              "patch": "Index: scripts/compare_runs.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n+++ scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,186 @@\n+\"\"\"Compare run manifests across architecture variants (E-owned; D4 / §6.5).\n+\n+Reads v1 run manifests (``docs/contracts/run-event.md``) produced by\n+``run_recorder`` and reports measured quantities per variant. It **refuses** to\n+compare runs that are not comparable: ``ticker``, ``trade_date``, ``asset_type``,\n+the model (quick/deep tier LLMs), the provider (``llm_provider`` and any tier\n+code/endpoint selectors), the output ``language``, and ``prompt_hashes`` must all\n+match the baseline. When any of them differs the comparison raises\n+``IncomparableRunsError`` rather than presenting a misleading table.\n+\n+This tool never invents quality scores. It reports only what the manifest records\n+(outcome, usage, duration, failure, stop reason) and per-variant averages of the\n+numeric fields. Semantic/quality thresholds are owned by B/D and are out of scope\n+here (see ``docs/evaluation/protocol.md``).\n+\n+Usage:\n+    python scripts/compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\n+\n+Exit 0 when the runs are comparable, 1 (with a reason on stderr) when they are\n+refused, 2 on a usage error. Stdlib + ``run_recorder`` only.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import json\n+import sys\n+from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+from tradingagents.run_recorder import read_manifest\n+\n+_TOP_LEVEL_GUARD = (\"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n+_MODEL_KEYS = (\"quick_think_llm\", \"deep_think_llm\")\n+_PROVIDER_KEYS = (\"llm_provider\", \"quick_think_provider\", \"deep_think_provider\")\n+_REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS = _MODEL_KEYS + (\"llm_provider\",)\n+_LANGUAGE_KEY = \"output_language\"\n+_USAGE_METRICS = (\"llm_calls\", \"tool_calls\", \"tokens_in\", \"tokens_out\")\n+\n+\n+class IncomparableRunsError(ValueError):\n+    \"\"\"The supplied manifests cannot be compared (a guard key differs).\"\"\"\n+\n+\n+@dataclass(frozen=True)\n+class Comparison:\n+    \"\"\"Comparable-run report. ``variants`` is per-run; ``averages`` is per-variant.\"\"\"\n+\n+    baseline_run_id: str\n+    guard: dict\n+    variants: list[dict]\n+    averages: dict\n+    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n+\n+    def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n+        return {\n+            \"baseline_run_id\": self.baseline_run_id,\n+            \"guard\": self.guard,\n+            \"variants\": self.variants,\n+            \"averages\": self.averages,\n+            \"notes\": self.notes,\n+        }\n+\n+\n+def _guard_of(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n+    \"\"\"Extract the keys that must match for a comparison to be valid.\n+\n+    ``llm_provider``, the tier models, and ``output_language`` are required; the\n+    per-tier provider selectors are optional (they default to ``None``) and are\n+    compared using their effective value. A missing required key is refused rather\n+    than guessed, so a malformed snapshot cannot silently look comparable.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n+    guard = {key: manifest.get(key) for key in _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD}\n+    required = _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS + (_LANGUAGE_KEY,)\n+    for key in required:\n+        if key not in config:\n+            raise IncomparableRunsError(\n+                f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} is missing config key {key!r}; \"\n+                \"cannot compare without it\"\n+            )\n+        guard[key] = config[key]\n+    for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS:\n+        if key in config:\n+            guard[key] = config[key]\n+    guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n+    return guard\n+\n+\n+def _check_comparable(guard: dict, baseline: dict) -> None:\n+    diffs = [key for key in baseline if guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n+    if diffs:\n+        raise IncomparableRunsError(\n+            \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \"\n+            + \", \".join(sorted(diffs))\n+        )\n+\n+\n+def _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"The variant segment of a run id (``<variant>-<ticker>-...``).\"\"\"\n+    return run_id.split(\"-\", 1)[0]\n+\n+\n+def _variant_row(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n+    return {\n+        \"run_id\": manifest.get(\"run_id\"),\n+        \"variant\": _variant_of(str(manifest.get(\"run_id\", \"\"))),\n+        \"outcome\": manifest.get(\"outcome\"),\n+        \"usage\": manifest.get(\"usage\"),\n+        \"duration_seconds\": manifest.get(\"duration_seconds\"),\n+        \"failure\": manifest.get(\"failure\"),\n+        \"stop_reason\": manifest.get(\"stop_reason\"),\n+    }\n+\n+\n+def _averages(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:\n+    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}\n+    for row in rows:\n+        grouped.setdefault(row[\"variant\"], []).append(row)\n+\n+    result: dict[str, dict] = {}\n+    for variant, group in grouped.items():\n+        summary: dict = {\"runs\": len(group)}\n+        for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n+            values = [\n+                row[\"usage\"][metric]\n+                for row in group\n+                if isinstance(row.get(\"usage\"), dict) and row[\"usage\"].get(metric) is not None\n+            ]\n+            summary[metric] = sum(values) / len(values) if values else None\n+        durations = [row[\"duration_seconds\"] for row in group if row[\"duration_seconds\"] is not None]\n+        summary[\"duration_seconds\"] = sum(durations) / len(durations) if durations else None\n+        result[variant] = summary\n+    return result\n+\n+\n+def compare_manifests(manifests: list[dict]) -> Comparison:\n+    \"\"\"Compare already-loaded manifests; raise ``IncomparableRunsError`` if invalid.\"\"\"\n+    if not manifests:\n+        raise IncomparableRunsError(\"no manifests supplied\")\n+\n+    baseline_guard = _guard_of(manifests[0])\n+    for manifest in manifests[1:]:\n+        _check_comparable(_guard_of(manifest), baseline_guard)\n+\n+    rows = [_variant_row(manifest) for manifest in manifests]\n+    return Comparison(\n+        baseline_run_id=manifests[0].get(\"run_id\"),\n+        guard=baseline_guard,\n+        variants=rows,\n+        averages=_averages(rows),\n+        notes=[\n+            \"Reported quantities are measured from run manifests; no quality score is \"\n+            \"computed or inferred here.\",\n+            \"Runs are only compared when ticker, trade_date, asset_type, model, provider, \"\n+            \"language, and prompt hashes all match the baseline.\",\n+        ],\n+    )\n+\n+\n+def compare_manifest_files(paths: list[str | Path]) -> Comparison:\n+    return compare_manifests([read_manifest(path) for path in paths])\n+\n+\n+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n+    args = [arg for arg in argv[1:] if not arg.startswith(\"-\")]\n+    as_json = \"--json\" in argv[1:]\n+    if not args:\n+        print(\"usage: compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\", file=sys.stderr)\n+        return 2\n+    try:\n+        comparison = compare_manifest_files(args)\n+    except IncomparableRunsError as exc:\n+        print(f\"[compare-runs] REFUSED: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n+        return 1\n+\n+    if as_json:\n+        print(json.dumps(comparison.to_dict(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n+    else:\n+        print(f\"[compare-runs] baseline={comparison.baseline_run_id} runs={len(comparison.variants)}\")\n+        for variant, summary in sorted(comparison.averages.items()):\n+            print(f\"  {variant}: {json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True)}\")\n+    return 0\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",
              "additions": 186,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },
            {
              "file": "test/offline/test_compare_runs.py",
              "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_compare_runs.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_compare_runs.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_compare_runs.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,230 @@\n+\"\"\"Offline tests for the run-manifest comparison tool (E-owned, D4 / §6.5).\n+\n+Written test-first. The tool compares v1 run manifests (docs/contracts/run-event.md)\n+and **refuses** when the runs are not comparable: ticker, trade_date, asset_type,\n+model (quick/deep tier LLMs), provider (llm_provider + tier providers), language\n+(output_language), or prompt hashes differ. It reports measured quantities only and\n+never invents quality scores.\n+\n+No network; manifests are built via the real recorder and written with ``tmp_path``.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+import json\n+import sys\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+import pytest\n+\n+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / \"scripts\"))\n+\n+import compare_runs  # noqa: E402\n+from compare_runs import IncomparableRunsError  # noqa: E402\n+\n+from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, write_manifest  # noqa: E402\n+\n+CONFIG = {\n+    \"llm_provider\": \"openai\",\n+    \"quick_think_llm\": \"gpt-6-luna\",\n+    \"deep_think_llm\": \"gpt-6-sol\",\n+    \"output_language\": \"English\",\n+}\n+PROMPT_HASHES = {\"market\": \"sha256:aaa\"}\n+\n+USAGE = {\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 5, \"tokens_in\": 1000, \"tokens_out\": 500}\n+\n+\n+def _event(**overrides) -> RunEvent:\n+    fields = {\n+        \"run_id\": \"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n+        \"created_at\": \"2026-11-21T12:00:00+00:00\",\n+        \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n+        \"ticker\": \"NVDA\",\n+        \"trade_date\": \"2026-11-20\",\n+        \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n+        \"outcome\": \"Buy\",\n+        \"config_snapshot\": dict(CONFIG),\n+        \"prompt_hashes\": dict(PROMPT_HASHES),\n+        \"evidence_snapshot\": None,\n+        \"usage\": dict(USAGE),\n+        \"duration_seconds\": 42.5,\n+        \"failure\": None,\n+        \"stop_reason\": \"completed\",\n+    }\n+    fields.update(overrides)\n+    return RunEvent(**fields)\n+\n+\n+def _write(tmp_path, name: str, event: RunEvent) -> Path:\n+    path = tmp_path / name\n+    write_manifest(event, path)\n+    return path\n+\n+\n+def _manifest(**overrides) -> dict:\n+    return json.loads(json.dumps(_event(**overrides).__dict__))\n+\n+\n+# --- Guard: differing key refuses ---------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n+    \"field,value\",\n+    [\n+        (\"ticker\", \"AMD\"),\n+        (\"trade_date\", \"2026-11-19\"),\n+        (\"asset_type\", \"crypto\"),\n+    ],\n+)\n+def test_top_level_guard_mismatch_refuses(field, value):\n+    baseline = _manifest()\n+    other = _manifest(**{field: value})\n+    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n+        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, other])\n+    assert field in str(exc.value)\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n+    \"key,value\",\n+    [\n+        (\"quick_think_llm\", \"gpt-6-other\"),\n+        (\"deep_think_llm\", \"gpt-6-other\"),\n+        (\"llm_provider\", \"anthropic\"),\n+        (\"output_language\", \"Chinese\"),\n+    ],\n+)\n+def test_config_guard_mismatch_refuses(key, value):\n+    baseline = _manifest()\n+    other_config = dict(CONFIG)\n+    other_config[key] = value\n+    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n+        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, _manifest(config_snapshot=other_config)])\n+    assert key in str(exc.value)\n+\n+\n+def test_prompt_hash_mismatch_refuses():\n+    baseline = _manifest()\n+    other = _manifest(prompt_hashes={\"market\": \"sha256:bbb\"})\n+    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n+        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, other])\n+    assert \"prompt_hashes\" in str(exc.value)\n+\n+\n+def test_missing_model_key_refuses():\n+    baseline = _manifest()\n+    no_model = dict(CONFIG)\n+    del no_model[\"quick_think_llm\"]\n+    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n+        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, _manifest(config_snapshot=no_model)])\n+    assert \"quick_think_llm\" in str(exc.value)\n+\n+\n+# --- Positive: comparable runs produce a report ------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_comparable_runs_report_variants():\n+    a = _manifest(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n+    b = _manifest(run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n+    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([a, b])\n+    assert [row[\"run_id\"] for row in comparison.variants] == [a[\"run_id\"], b[\"run_id\"]]\n+\n+\n+def test_single_manifest_is_comparable():\n+    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([_manifest()])\n+    assert len(comparison.variants) == 1\n+\n+\n+def test_empty_input_refuses():\n+    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError):\n+        compare_runs.compare_manifests([])\n+\n+\n+def test_no_quality_score_is_invented():\n+    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([_manifest(), _manifest()])\n+    measured = {\"variants\": comparison.variants, \"averages\": comparison.averages}\n+    payload = json.dumps(measured).lower()\n+    for banned in (\"quality\", \"score\", \"faithfulness\", \"relevance\"):\n+        assert banned not in payload\n+    assert any(\"no quality score\" in note for note in comparison.notes)\n+\n+\n+# --- Averages per variant ----------------------------------------------------\n+\n+VARIANT_RUN_1 = _manifest(\n+    run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n+    usage={\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 2, \"tokens_in\": 1000, \"tokens_out\": 500},\n+    duration_seconds=40.0,\n+)\n+VARIANT_RUN_2 = _manifest(\n+    run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r2-20261121t1300\",\n+    usage={\"llm_calls\": 20, \"tool_calls\": 4, \"tokens_in\": 3000, \"tokens_out\": 1500},\n+    duration_seconds=60.0,\n+)\n+\n+\n+def _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n+    return run_id.split(\"-\")[0]\n+\n+\n+def test_averages_per_variant():\n+    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, VARIANT_RUN_2])\n+    averages = comparison.averages\n+    assert set(averages) == {\"v2\"}\n+    v2 = averages[\"v2\"]\n+    assert v2[\"runs\"] == 2\n+    assert v2[\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(15.0)\n+    assert v2[\"tool_calls\"] == pytest.approx(3.0)\n+    assert v2[\"tokens_in\"] == pytest.approx(2000.0)\n+    assert v2[\"tokens_out\"] == pytest.approx(1000.0)\n+    assert v2[\"duration_seconds\"] == pytest.approx(50.0)\n+\n+\n+def test_averages_group_by_variant():\n+    other = _manifest(\n+        run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n+        usage={\"llm_calls\": 4, \"tool_calls\": 1, \"tokens_in\": 100, \"tokens_out\": 50},\n+        duration_seconds=10.0,\n+    )\n+    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, VARIANT_RUN_2, other])\n+    assert comparison.averages[\"v2\"][\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(15.0)\n+    assert comparison.averages[\"v0\"][\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(4.0)\n+\n+\n+def test_average_ignores_null_duration():\n+    null_dur = _manifest(\n+        run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r3-20261121t1400\",\n+        duration_seconds=None,\n+    )\n+    v2 = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, null_dur]).averages[\"v2\"]\n+    assert v2[\"duration_seconds\"] == pytest.approx(40.0)\n+\n+\n+# --- File-level + CLI --------------------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def               "content": "\"\"\"Offline tests for the run-manifest comparison tool (E-owned, D4 / §6.5).\n\nWritten test-first. It reports measured quantities only and\nnever invents quality scores.\n\nNo network; manifests are built via the real recorder and written with ``tmp_path``.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / \"scripts\"))\n\nimport compare_runs  # noqa: E402\nfrom compare_runs import IncomparableRunsError  # noqa: E402\n\nfrom tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, write_manifest  # noqa: E402\n\nCONFIG = {\n    \"llm_provider\": \"openai\",\n    \"quick_think_llm\": \"gpt-6-luna\",\n    \"deep_think_llm\": \"gpt-6-sol\",\n    \"output_language\": \"English\",\n}\nPROMPT_HASHES = {\"market\": \"sha256:aaa\"}\n\nUSAGE = {\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 5, \"tokens_in\": 1000, \"tokens_out\": 500}\n\n\ndef _event(**overrides) -> RunEvent:\n    fields = {\n        \"run_id\": \"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n        \"created_at\": \"2026-11-21T12:00:00+00:00\",\n        \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n        \"ticker\": \"NVDA\",\n        \"trade_date\": \"2026-11-20\",\n        \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n        \"outcome\": \"Buy\",\n        \"config_snapshot\": dict(CONFIG),\n        \"prompt_hashes\": dict(PROMPT_HASHES),\n        \"evidence_snapshot\": None,\n        \"usage\": dict(USAGE),\n        \"duration_seconds\": 42.5,\n        \"failure\": None,\n        \"stop_reason\": \"completed\",\n    }\n    fields.update(overrides)\n    return RunEvent(**fields)\n\n\ndef _write(tmp_path, name: str, event: RunEvent) -> Path:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    write_manifest(event, path)\n    return path\n\n\ndef _manifest(**overrides) -> dict:\n    return json.loads(json.dumps(_event(**overrides).__dict__))\n\n\n# --- Guard: differing key refuses ---------------------------------------------\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"field,value\",\n    [\n        (\"ticker\", \"AMD\"),\n        (\"trade_date\", \"2026-11-19\"),\n        (\"asset_type\", \"crypto\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_top_level_guard_mismatch_refuses(field, value):\n    baseline = _manifest()\n    other = _manifest(**{field: value})\n    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, other])\n    assert field in str(exc.value)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"key,value\",\n    [\n        (\"quick_think_llm\", \"gpt-6-other\"),\n        (\"deep_think_llm\", \"gpt-6-other\"),\n        (\"llm_provider\", \"anthropic\"),\n        (\"output_language\", \"Chinese\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_config_guard_mismatch_refuses(key, value):\n    baseline = _manifest()\n    other_config = dict(CONFIG)\n    other_config[key] = value\n    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, _manifest(config_snapshot=other_config)])\n    assert key in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_prompt_hash_mismatch_refuses():\n    baseline = _manifest()\n    other = _manifest(prompt_hashes={\"market\": \"sha256:bbb\"})\n    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, other])\n    assert \"prompt_hashes\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_missing_model_key_refuses():\n    baseline = _manifest()\n    no_model = dict(CONFIG)\n    del no_model[\"quick_think_llm\"]\n    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n        compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, _manifest(config_snapshot=no_model)])\n    assert \"quick_think_llm\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\n# --- Positive: comparable runs produce a report ------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_comparable_runs_report_variants():\n    a = _manifest(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n    b = _manifest(run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([a, b])\n    assert [row[\"run_id\"] for row in comparison.variants] == [a[\"run_id\"], b[\"run_id\"]]\n\n\ndef test_single_manifest_is_comparable():\n    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([_manifest()])\n    assert len(comparison.variants) == 1\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_refuses():\n    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError):\n        compare_runs.compare_manifests([])\n\n\ndef test_no_quality_score_is_invented():\n    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([_manifest(), _manifest()])\n    payload = json.dumps(comparison.to_dict())\n    for banned in (\"quality\", \"score\", \"faithfulness\", \"relevance\"):\n        assert banned not in payload.lower()\n\n\n# --- Averages per variant ----------------------------------------------------\n\nVARIANT_RUN_1 = _manifest(\n    run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n    usage={\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 2, \"tokens_in\": 1000, \"tokens_out\": 500},\n    duration_seconds=40.0,\n)\nVARIANT_RUN_2 = _manifest(\n _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n    return run_id.split(\"-\")[0]\n\n\ndef test_averages_per_variant():\n    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, VARIANT_RUN_2])\n    averages = comparison.averages\n    assert set(averages) == {\"v2\"}\n    v2 = averages[\"v2\"]\n    assert v2[\"runs\"] == 2\n    assert v2[\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(15.0)\n    assert v2[\"tool_calls\"] == pytest.approx(3.0)\n    assert v2[\"tokens_in\"] == pytest.approx(2000.0)\n    assert v2[\"tokens_out\"] == pytest.approx(1000.0)\n    assert v2[\"duration_seconds\"] == pytest.approx(50.0)\n\n\ndef test_averages_group_by_variant():\n    other = _manifest(\n        run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n        usage={\"llm_calls\": 4, \"tool_calls\": 1, \"tokens_in\": 100, \"tokens_out\": 50},\n        duration_seconds=10.0,\n    )\n    comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, VARIANT_RUN_2, other])\n    assert comparison.averages[\"v2\"][\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(15.0)\n    assert comparison.averages[\"v0\"][\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(4.0)\n\n\ndef test_average_ignores_null_duration():\n    null_dur = _manifest(\n        run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r3-20261121t1400\",\n        duration_seconds=None,\n    )\n    v2 = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1,               "content": "\"\"\"Compare run manifests across architecture variants (E-owned; D4 / §6.5).\n\nReads v1 run manifests (``docs/contracts/run-event.md``) produced by\n``run_recorder`` and reports measured quantities per variant. It **refuses** to\ncompare runs that are not comparable: ``ticker``, ``trade_date``, ``asset_type``,\nthe model (quick/deep tier LLMs), the provider (``llm_provider`` and any tier\ncode/endpoint selectors), the output ``language``, and ``prompt_hashes`` must all\nmatch the baseline. When any of them differs the comparison raises\n``IncomparableRunsError`` rather than presenting a misleading table.\n\nThis tool never invents quality scores. It reports only what the manifest records\n(outcome, usage, duration, failure, stop reason) and per-variant averages of the\nnumeric fields. Semantic/quality thresholds are owned by B/D and are out of scope\nhere (see ``docs/evaluation/protocol.md``).\n\nUsage:\n    python scripts/compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\n\nExit 0 when the runs are comparable, 1 (with a reason on stderr) when they are\nrefused, 2 on a usage error. Stdlib + ``run_recorder`` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\ntry:  # script mode (``python scripts/compare_runs.py``): scripts/ is on sys.path.\n    from gate_common import load_yaml  # noqa: F401  (kept for parity with gates)\nexcept ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - the script must also import as a module\n    load_yaml = None  # type: ignore[assignment]\n\nfrom tradingagents.run_recorder import read_manifest\n\n_TOP_LEVEL_GUARD = (\"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n_MODEL_KEYS = (\"quick_think_llm\", \"deep_think_llm\")\n_PROVIDER_KEYS = (\"llm_provider\", \"quick_think_provider\", \"deep_think_provider\")\n_LANGUAGE_KEY = \"output_language\"\n_USAGE_METRICS = (\"llm_calls\", \"tool_calls\", \"tokens_in\", \"tokens_out\")\n\n\nclass IncomparableRunsError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"The supplied manifests cannot be compared (a guard key differs).\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Comparison:\n    \"\"\"Comparable-run report. ``variants`` is per-run; ``averages`` is per-variant.\"\"\"\n\n    baseline_run_id: str\n    guard: dict\n    variants: list[dict]\n    averages: dict\n    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n        return {\n            \"baseline_run_id\": self.baseline_run_id,\n            \"guard\": self.guard,\n            \"variants\": self.variants,\n            \"averages\": self.averages,\n            \"notes\": self.notes,\n        }\n\n\ndef _guard_of(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Extract the keys that must match for a comparison to be valid.\"\"\"\n    config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n    guard = {key: manifest.get(key) for key in _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD}\n    for key in _MODEL_KEYS + _PROVIDER_KEYS + (_LANGUAGE_KEY,):\n        if key not in config:\n            raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} is missing config key {key!r}; \"\n                \"cannot compare without it\"\n            )\n        guard[key] = config[key]\n    guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n    return guard\n\n\ndef _check_comparable(guard: dict, baseline: dict) -> None:\n    diffs = [key for key in baseline if guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n    if diffs:\n        raise IncomparableRunsError(\n            \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \"\n            + \", \".join(sorted(diffs))\n        )\n\n\ndef _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The variant segment of a run id (``<variant>-<ticker>-...``).\"\"\"\n    return run_id.split(\"-\", 1)[0]\n\n\ndef _variant_row(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"run_id\": manifest.get(\"run_id\"),\n        \"variant\": _variant_of(str(manifest.get(\"run_id\", \"\"))),\n        \"outcome\": manifest.get(\"outcome\"),\n        \"usage\": manifest.get(\"usage\"),\n        \"duration_seconds\": manifest.get(\"duration_seconds\"),\n        \"failure\": manifest.get(\"failure\"),\n        \"stop_reason\": manifest.get(\"stop_reason\"),\n    }\n\n\ndef _averages(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:\n    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}\n    for row in rows:\n        grouped.setdefault(row[\"variant\"], []).append(row)\n\n    result: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    for variant, group in grouped.items():\n        summary: dict = {\"runs\": len(group)}\n        for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n            values = [\n                row[\"usage\"][metric]\n                for row in group\n                if isinstance(row.get(\"usage\"), dict) and row[\"usage\"].get(metric) is not None\n            ]\n            summary[metric] = sum(values) / len(values) if values else None\n        durations = [row[\"duration_seconds\"] for row in group if row[\"duration_seconds\"] is not None]\n        summary[\"duration_seconds\"] = sum(durations) / len(durations) if durations else None\n        result[variant] = summary\n    return result\n\n\ndef compare_manifests(manifests: list[dict]) -> Comparison:\n    \"\"\"Compare already-loaded manifests; raise ``IncomparableRunsError`` if invalid.\"\"\"\n    if not manifests:\n        raise IncomparableRunsError(\"no manifests supplied\")\n\n    baseline_guard = _guard_of(manifests[0])\n    for manifest in manifests[1:]:\n        _check_comparable(_guard_of(manifest), baseline_guard)\n\n    rows = [_variant_row(manifest) for manifest in manifests]\n    return Comparison(\n        baseline_run_id=manifests[0].get(\"run_id\"),\n        guard=baseline_guard,\n        variants=rows,\n        averages=_averages(rows),\n        notes=[\n            \"Reported quantities are measured from run manifests; no quality score is \"\n            \"computed or inferred here.\",\n            \"Runs are only compared when ticker, trade_date, asset_type, model, provider, \"\n            \"language, and prompt hashes all match the baseline.\",\n        ],\n    )\n\n\ndef compare_manifest_files(paths: list[str | Path]) -> Comparison:\n    return compare_manifests([read_manifest(path) for path in paths])\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n    args = [arg for arg in argv[1:] if not arg.startswith(\"-\")]\n    as_json = \"--json\" in argv[1:]\n    if not args:\n        print(\"usage: compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n    try:\n        comparison = compare_manifest_files(args)\n    except IncomparableRunsError as exc:\n        print(f\"[compare-runs] REFUSED: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    if as_json:\n        print(json.dumps(comparison.to_dict(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n    else:\n        print(f\"[compare-runs] baseline={comparison.baseline_run_id} runs={len(comparison.variants)}\")\n        for variant, summary in sorted(comparison.averages.items()):\n            print(f\"  {variant}: {json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",
              "filePath": "/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/scripts/compare_runs.py"

            "input": {
              "content": "# Evaluation Protocol\n\nOwner: E (runtime records, experiments, CI, delivery). Reviewers: B (collaboration /\nprompt versioning) and D (deterministic safety) per the team split §3.\nStatus: **tooling only.** `scripts/compare_runs.py` and `test/offline/test_compare_runs.py`\nexist and pass offline; **no experiments have run yet**. The comparison tables the\nreport needs (`docs/evaluation/results/`) do not exist and must not be fabricated.\n\nThis protocol fixes *how* runs are compared and *what* a comparison may claim. It\ndoes not define semantic-quality scoring: that spec is owned by B and D and is not\nimplemented in this slice (see \"Out of scope\" below). Until real runs exist, this\ndocument and the tool are the only deliverables here.\n\n## Fixed inputs (the comparison set)\n\nTwo runs may be compared only when these inputs are identical to the baseline. The\ntool enforces this; a mismatch is refused, not averaged or shown side by side.\n\n| Guard key | Source | Why it must match |\n|---|---|---|\n| `ticker` | manifest top level | different company = different question |\n| `trade_date` | manifest top level | different analysis date = different information set |\n| `asset_type` | manifest top level | `stock` vs `crypto` changes tools and rules |\n| model | `config_snapshot.quick_think_llm`, `deep_think_llm` | a model change is the very thing being evaluated |\n| provider | `config_snapshot.llm_provider` (+ optional `*_think_provider`) | different backend = different outputs |\n| language | `config_snapshot.output_language` | report text changes with language |\n| prompt | `prompt_hashes` (name → hash) | a prompt change invalidates a like-for-like comparison |\n\nA missing required config key (model, provider, language) is treated as\n**incomparable** — the tool refuses rather than guessing a default.\n\n## Variants\n\nEach run is tagged by the first segment of its `run_id`\n(`<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<repeat>-<runstamp>`):\n\n| Variant | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `v0` | original upstream path (baseline for comparison) |\n| `v1` | trimmed / simple reduction |\n| `v2` | adaptive collaboration |\n\nComparing a run against itself-other-variants is the point; comparing different\ninputs is refused.\n\n## Metrics reported\n\nOnly quantities the manifest actually records. Per run: `outcome`, `usage`\n(`llm_calls`, `tool_calls`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`), `duration_seconds`,\n`failure`, `stop_reason`. Per variant: **count of runs** and the **average** of each\nnumeric field (`null` values excluded from that field's average).\n\nThe token-reduction goal from the team plan (e.g. 20–25%) is a *target*, not a\nresult: the protocol reports measured averages; it does not assert the target was\nmet. If real runs do not hit it, the results file says so.\n\n## Thresholds\n\nThresholds for a *passing* comparison are intentionally left unset here. They belong\nwith the semantic-evaluation spec (B/D) and the CI semantic gate (§6.4). This slice\nships no threshold and no gate; it only produces comparable numbers.\n\n## Out of scope (owned elsewhere)\n\n- **Semantic / quality scores** (faithfulness, relevance, argument independence): B\n  and D. This tool does not compute, infer, or approximate them. The absence of a\n  score is the honest output.\n- **`stop_reason` value domain**: C (`execution_policy`). Reported opaquely.\n- **Evidence snapshot semantics**: A (`evidence.py`). Reported opaquely.\n- **Live evaluation runs**: `test/live/test_fixed_eval.py` (later; needs API access).\n\n## How to run\n\n```bash\n# Compare two or more manifests of the same input across variants.\npython scripts/compare_runs.py results/v0-nvda-.../manifest.json \\\n                             results/v2-nvda-.../manifest.json\npython scripts/compare_runs.py ... --json     # machine-readable output\n\n# Offline tests (no network, no API keys).\npytest test/offline/test_compare_runs.py -q\n```\n\nExit codes: `0` comparable, `1` refused (reason on stderr names the differing guard\nkey), `2` usage error. Results meant for the report go under\n`docs/evaluation/results/`, one file per comparison, with the commit and manifest\npaths recorded — **only after the runs actually happen**.\n\n## Current state\n\n- Comparison tooling: implemented, 20 offline tests green.\n- Experiments: **none run.** No `results/` files exist. Do not add comparison tables\n  until real manifests are produced from real runs.\n",
              "filePath": "/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/docs/evaluation/protocol.md"

              "file": "scripts/compare_runs.py",
              "patch": "Index: scripts/compare_runs.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n+++ scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n@@ -1,186 +1,226 @@\n \"\"\"Compare run manifests across architecture variants (E-owned; D4 / §6.5).\n \n Reads v1 run manifests (``docs/contracts/run-event.md``) produced by\n ``run_recorder`` and reports measured quantities per variant. It **refuses** to\n compare runs that are not comparable: ``ticker``, ``trade_date``, ``asset_type``,\n the model (quick/deep tier LLMs), the provider (``llm_provider`` and any tier\n code/endpoint selectors), the output ``language``, and ``prompt_hashes`` must all\n match the baseline. When any of them differs the comparison raises\n ``IncomparableRunsError`` rather than presenting a misleading table.\n \n This tool never invents quality scores. It reports only what the manifest records\n (outcome, usage, duration, failure, stop reason) and per-variant averages of the\n numeric fields. Semantic/quality thresholds are owned by B/D and are out of scope\n here (see ``docs/evaluation/protocol.md``).\n \n Usage:\n     python scripts/compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\n \n Exit 0 when the runs are comparable, 1 (with a reason on stderr) when they are\n refused, 2 on a usage error. Stdlib + ``run_recorder`` only.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import json\n import sys\n from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n from pathlib import Path\n \n from tradingagents.run_recorder import read_manifest\n \n _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD = (\"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n _MODEL_KEYS = (\"quick_think_llm\", \"deep_think_llm\")\n _PROVIDER_KEYS = (\"llm_provider\", \"quick_think_provider\", \"deep_think_provider\")\n _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS = _MODEL_KEYS + (\"llm_provider\",)\n _LANGUAGE_KEY = \"output_language\"\n _USAGE_METRICS = (\"llm_calls\", \"tool_calls\", \"tokens_in\", \"tokens_out\")\n \n \n class IncomparableRunsError(ValueError):\n     \"\"\"The supplied manifests cannot be compared (a guard key differs).\"\"\"\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class Comparison:\n     \"\"\"Comparable-run report. ``variants`` is per-run; ``averages`` is per-variant.\"\"\"\n \n     baseline_run_id: str\n     guard: dict\n     variants: list[dict]\n     averages: dict\n     notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n \n     def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n         return {\n             \"baseline_run_id\": self.baseline_run_id,\n             \"guard\": self.guard,\n             \"variants\": self.variants,\n             \"averages\": self.averages,\n             \"notes\": self.notes,\n         }\n \n \n def _guard_of(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Extract the keys that must match for a comparison to be valid.\n \n-    ``llm_provider``, the tier models, and ``output_language`` are required; the\n-    per-tier provider selectors are optional (they default to ``None``) and are\n-    compared using their effective value. A missing required key is refused rather\n-    than guessed, so a malformed snapshot cannot silently look comparable.\n+    ``llm_provider``, the tier models, and ``output_language`` are required; a\n+    missing required key is refused rather than guessed, so a malformed snapshot\n+    cannot silently look comparable. The optional per-tier provider selectors are\n+    collected when present; ``_provider_keys`` unions them across every manifest so\n+    a tier provider set in *any* run is compared everywhere (a manifest that omits\n+    it compares as ``None``, the config default).\n     \"\"\"\n     config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n     guard = {key: manifest.get(key) for key in _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD}\n     required = _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS + (_LANGUAGE_KEY,)\n     for key in required:\n         if key not in config:\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} is missing config key {key!r}; \"\n                 \"cannot compare without it\"\n             )\n         guard[key] = config[key]\n     for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS:\n         if key in config:\n             guard[key] = config[key]\n     guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n     return guard\n \n \n+def _provider_keys(manifests: list[dict]) -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"Provider keys present in *any* manifest, so they are compared everywhere.\"\"\"\n+    present: set[str] = set()\n+    for manifest in manifests:\n+        config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n+        present.update(key for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS if key in config)\n+    return sorted(present)\n+\n+\n def _check_comparable(guard: dict, baseline: dict) -> None:\n     diffs = [key for key in baseline if guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n     if diffs:\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 "text": "\"\"\"Compare run manifests across architecture variants (E-owned; D4 / §6.5).\n\nReads v1 run manifests (``docs/contracts/run-event.md``) produced by\n``run_recorder`` and reports measured quantities per variant. It **refuses** to\ncompare runs that are not comparable: ``ticker``, ``trade_date``, ``asset_type``,\nthe model (quick/deep tier LLMs), the provider (``llm_provider`` and any tier\ncode/endpoint selectors), the output ``language``, and ``prompt_hashes`` must all\nmatch the baseline. When any of them differs the comparison raises\n``IncomparableRunsError`` rather than presenting a misleading table.\n\nThis tool never invents quality scores. It reports only what the manifest records\n(outcome, usage, duration, failure, stop reason) and per-variant averages of the\nnumeric fields. Semantic/quality thresholds are owned by B/D and are out of scope\nhere (see ``docs/evaluation/protocol.md``).\n\nUsage:\n    python scripts/compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\n\nExit 0 when the runs are comparable, 1 (with a reason on stderr) when they are\nrefused, 2 on a usage error. Stdlib + ``run_recorder`` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom tradingagents.run_recorder import read_manifest\n\n_TOP_LEVEL_GUARD = (\"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n_MODEL_KEYS = (\"quick_think_llm\", \"deep_think_llm\")\n_PROVIDER_KEYS = (\"llm_provider\", \"quick_think_provider\", \"deep_think_provider\")\n_REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS = _MODEL_KEYS + (\"llm_provider\",)\n_LANGUAGE_KEY = \"output_language\"\n_USAGE_METRICS = (\"llm_calls\", \"tool_calls\", \"tokens_in\", \"tokens_out\")\n\n\nclass IncomparableRunsError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"The supplied manifests cannot be compared (a guard key differs).\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Comparison:\n    \"\"\"Comparable-run report. ``variants`` is per-run; ``averages`` is per-variant.\"\"\"\n\n    baseline_run_id: str\n    guard: dict\n    variants: list[dict]\n    averages: dict\n    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n        return {\n            \"baseline_run_id\": self.baseline_run_id,\n            \"guard\": self.guard,\n            \"variants\": self.variants,\n            \"averages\": self.averages,\n            \"notes\": self.notes,\n        }\n\n\ndef _guard_of(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Extract the keys that must match for a comparison to be valid.\n\n    ``llm_provider``, the tier models, and ``output_language`` are required; the\n    per-tier provider selectors are optional (they default to ``None``) and are\n    compared using their effective value. A missing required key is refused rather\n    than guessed, so a malformed snapshot cannot silently look comparable.\n    \"\"\"\n    config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n    guard = {key: manifest.get(key) for key in _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD}\n    required = _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS + (_LANGUAGE_KEY,)\n    for key in required:\n        if key not in config:\n            raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} is missing config key {key!r}; \"\n                \"cannot compare without it\"\n            )\n        guard[key] = config[key]\n    for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS:\n        if key in config:\n            guard[key] = config[key]\n    guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n    return guard\n\n\ndef _check_comparable(guard: dict, baseline: dict) -> None:\n    diffs = [key for key in baseline if guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n    if diffs:\n        raise IncomparableRunsError(\n            \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \"\n            + \", \".join(sorted(diffs))\n        )\n\n\ndef _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The variant segment of a run id (``<variant>-<ticker>-...``).\"\"\"\n    return run_id.split(\"-\", 1)[0]\n\n\ndef _variant_row(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"run_id\": manifest.get(\"run_id\"),\n        \"variant\": _variant_of(str(manifest.get(\"run_id\", \"\"))),\n        \"outcome\": manifest.get(\"outcome\"),\n        \"usage\": manifest.get(\"usage\"),\n        \"duration_seconds\": manifest.get(\"duration_seconds\"),\n        \"failure\": manifest.get(\"failure\"),\n        \"stop_reason\": manifest.get(\"stop_reason\"),\n    }\n\n\ndef _averages(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:\n    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}\n    for row in rows:\n        grouped.setdefault(row[\"variant\"], []).append(row)\n\n    result: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    for variant, group in grouped.items():\n        summary: dict = {\"runs\": len(group)}\n        for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n            values = [\n                row[\"usage\"][metric]\n                for row in group\n                if isinstance(row.get(\"usage\"), dict) and row[\"usage\"].get(metric) is not None\n            ]\n            summary[metric] = sum(values) / len(values) if values else None\n        durations = [row[\"duration_seconds\"] for row in group if row[\"duration_seconds\"] is not None]\n        summary[\"duration_seconds\"] = sum(durations) / len(durations) if durations else None\n        result[variant] = summary\n    return result\n\n\ndef compare_manifests(manifests: list[dict]) -> Comparison:\n    \"\"\"Compare already-loaded manifests; raise ``IncomparableRunsError`` if invalid.\"\"\"\n    if not manifests:\n        raise IncomparableRunsError(\"no manifests supplied\")\n\n    baseline_guard = _guard_of(manifests[0])\n    for manifest in manifests[1:]:\n        _check_comparable(_guard_of(manifest), baseline_guard)\n\n    rows = [_variant_row(manifest) for manifest in manifests]\n    return Comparison(\n        baseline_run_id=manifests[0].get(\"run_id\"),\n        guard=baseline_guard,\n        variants=rows,\n        averages=_averages(rows),\n        notes=[\n            \"Reported quantities are measured from run manifests; no quality score is \"\n            \"computed or inferred here.\",\n            \"Runs are only compared when ticker, trade_date, asset_type, model, provider, \"\n            \"language, and prompt hashes all match the baseline.\",\n        ],\n    )\n\n\ndef compare_manifest_files(paths: list[str | Path]) -> Comparison:\n    return compare_manifests([read_manifest(path) for path in paths])\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n    args = [arg for arg in argv[1:] if not arg.startswith(\"-\")]\n    as_json = \"--json\" in argv[1:]\n    if not args:\n        print(\"usage: compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n    try:\n        comparison = compare_manifest_files(args)\n    except IncomparableRunsError as exc:\n        print(f\"[compare-runs] REFUSED: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    if as_json:\n        print(json.dumps(comparison.to_dict(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n    else:\n        print(f\"[compare-runs] baseline={comparison.baseline_run_id} runs={len(comparison.variants)}\")\n        for variant, summary in sorted(comparison.averages.items()):\n            print(f\"  {variant}: {json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))",
