              "patch": "Index: scripts/compare_runs.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n+++ scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n@@ -1,226 +1,235 @@\n \"\"\"Compare run manifests across architecture variants (E-owned; D4 / §6.5).\n \n Reads v1 run manifests (``docs/contracts/run-event.md``) produced by\n ``run_recorder`` and reports measured quantities per variant. It **refuses** to\n compare runs that are not comparable: ``ticker``, ``trade_date``, ``asset_type``,\n the model (quick/deep tier LLMs), the provider (``llm_provider`` and any tier\n code/endpoint selectors), the output ``language``, and ``prompt_hashes`` must all\n match the baseline. When any of them differs the comparison raises\n ``IncomparableRunsError`` rather than presenting a misleading table.\n \n This tool never invents quality scores. It reports only what the manifest records\n (outcome, usage, duration, failure, stop reason) and per-variant averages of the\n numeric fields. Semantic/quality thresholds are owned by B/D and are out of scope\n here (see ``docs/evaluation/protocol.md``).\n \n Usage:\n     python scripts/compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\n \n Exit 0 when the runs are comparable, 1 (with a reason on stderr) when they are\n refused, 2 on a usage error. Stdlib + ``run_recorder`` only.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import json\n import sys\n from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n from pathlib import Path\n \n from tradingagents.run_recorder import read_manifest\n \n _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD = (\"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n _MODEL_KEYS = (\"quick_think_llm\", \"deep_think_llm\")\n _PROVIDER_KEYS = (\"llm_provider\", \"quick_think_provider\", \"deep_think_provider\")\n _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS = _MODEL_KEYS + (\"llm_provider\",)\n _LANGUAGE_KEY = \"output_language\"\n _USAGE_METRICS = (\"llm_calls\", \"tool_calls\", \"tokens_in\", \"tokens_out\")\n \n \n class IncomparableRunsError(ValueError):\n     \"\"\"The supplied manifests cannot be compared (a guard key differs).\"\"\"\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class Comparison:\n     \"\"\"Comparable-run report. ``variants`` is per-run; ``averages`` is per-variant.\"\"\"\n \n     baseline_run_id: str\n     guard: dict\n     variants: list[dict]\n     averages: dict\n     notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n \n     def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n         return {\n             \"baseline_run_id\": self.baseline_run_id,\n             \"guard\": self.guard,\n             \"variants\": self.variants,\n             \"averages\": self.averages,\n             \"notes\": self.notes,\n         }\n \n \n def _guard_of(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Extract the keys that must match for a comparison to be valid.\n \n     ``llm_provider``, the tier models, and ``output_language`` are required; a\n     missing required key is refused rather than guessed, so a malformed snapshot\n     cannot silently look comparable. The optional per-tier provider selectors are\n     collected when present; ``_provider_keys`` unions them across every manifest so\n     a tier provider set in *any* run is compared everywhere (a manifest that omits\n     it compares as ``None``, the config default).\n     \"\"\"\n     config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n     guard = {key: manifest.get(key) for key in _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD}\n     required = _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS + (_LANGUAGE_KEY,)\n     for key in required:\n         if key not in config:\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} is missing config key {key!r}; \"\n                 \"cannot compare without it\"\n             )\n         guard[key] = config[key]\n     for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS:\n         if key in config:\n             guard[key] = config[key]\n-    guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n+    prompt_hashes = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n+    if not prompt_hashes:\n+        # An empty/None prompt fingerprint leaves the comparison unfounded: two runs\n+        # cannot be shown to use the same prompts without a real hash (C-to-E\n+        # variant response: keep the real hashes). Refuse rather than guess.\n+        raise IncomparableRunsError(\n+            f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} has empty prompt_hashes; \"\n+            \"cannot compare without prompt fingerprints\"\n+        )\n+    guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = prompt_hashes\n     return guard\n \n \n def _provider_keys(manifests: list[dict]) -> list[str]:\n     \"\"\"Provider keys present in *any* manifest, so they are compared everywhere.\"\"\"\n     present: set[str] = set()\n     for manifest in manifests:\n         config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n         present.update(key for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS if key in config)\n     return sorted(present)\n \n \n def _check_comparable(guard: dict, baseline: dict) -> None:\n     diffs = [key for key in baseline if guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n     if diffs:\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\n             \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \"\n             + \", \".join(sorted(diffs))\n         )\n \n \n def _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"The variant segment of a run id (``<variant>-<ticker>-...``).\"\"\"\n     return run_id.split(\"-\", 1)[0]\n \n \n def _variant_row(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n     return {\n         \"run_id\": manifest.get(\"run_id\"),\n         \"variant\": _variant_of(str(manifest.get(\"run_id\", \"\"))),\n         \"outcome\": manifest.get(\"outcome\"),\n         \"usage\": manifest.get(\"usage\"),\n         \"duration_seconds\": manifest.get(\"duration_seconds\"),\n         \"failure\": manifest.get(\"failure\"),\n         \"stop_reason\": manifest.get(\"stop_reason\"),\n     }\n \n \n def _counts(values: list) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Count occurrences of each value (``None`` counted as ``null``).\"\"\"\n     counts: dict = {}\n     for value in values:\n         key = \"null\" if value is None else str(value)\n         counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1\n     return counts\n \n \n def _averages(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:\n     grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}\n     for row in rows:\n         grouped.setdefault(row[\"variant\"], []).append(row)\n \n     result: dict[str, dict] = {}\n     for variant, group in grouped.items():\n         summary: dict = {\"runs\": len(group)}\n         for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n             values = [\n                 row[\"usage\"][metric]\n                 for row in group\n                 if isinstance(row.get(\"usage\"), dict) and row[\"usage\"].get(metric) is not None\n             ]\n             summary[metric] = sum(values) / len(values) if values else None\n         durations = [row[\"duration_seconds\"] for row in group if row[\"duration_seconds\"] is not None]\n         summary[\"duration_seconds\"] = sum(durations) / len(durations) if durations else None\n         summary[\"outcome_counts\"] = _counts([row[\"outcome\"] for row in group])\n         summary[\"stop_reason_counts\"] = _counts([row[\"stop_reason\"] for row in group])\n         result[variant] = summary\n     return result\n \n \n def compare_manifests(manifests: list[dict]) -> Comparison:\n     \"\"\"Compare already-loaded manifests; raise ``IncomparableRunsError`` if invalid.\"\"\"\n     if not manifests:\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\"no manifests supplied\")\n \n     baseline_guard = _guard_of(manifests[0])\n     for manifest in manifests[1:]:\n         _check_comparable(_guard_of(manifest), baseline_guard)\n \n     # Union the provider keys across all runs so a tier provider set in any run\n     # (not just the baseline) is verified to match everywhere.\n     for key in _provider_keys(manifests):\n         values = {(m.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}).get(key) for m in manifests}\n         if len(values) > 1:\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \" + key\n             )\n         baseline_guard.setdefault(key, (manifests[0].get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}).get(key))\n \n     rows = [_variant_row(manifest) for manifest in manifests]\n     return Comparison(\n         baseline_run_id=manifests[0].get(\"run_id\"),\n         guard=baseline_guard,\n         variants=rows,\n         averages=_averages(rows),\n         notes=[\n             \"Reported quantities are measured from run manifests; no quality score is \"\n             \"computed or inferred here.\",\n             \"Runs are only compared when ticker, trade_date, asset_type, model, provider, \"\n             \"language, and prompt hashes all match the baseline.\",\n         ],\n     )\n \n \n def compare_manifest_files(paths: list[str | Path]) -> Comparison:\n     manifests = []\n     for path in paths:\n         try:\n             manifests.append(read_manifest(path))\n         except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:\n             # read_manifest raises ValueError for a bad/unsupported/short manifest\n             # and OSError (e.g. FileNotFoundError) for an unreadable path.\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(f\"cannot read manifest {str(path)!r}: {exc}\") from exc\n     return compare_manifests(manifests)\n \n \n def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n     args = [arg for arg in argv[1:] if not arg.startswith(\"-\")]\n     as_json = \"--json\" in argv[1:]\n     if not args:\n         print(\"usage: compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\", file=sys.stderr)\n         return 2\n     try:\n         comparison = compare_manifest_files(args)\n     except IncomparableRunsError as exc:\n         print(f\"[compare-runs] REFUSED: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n         return 1\n \n     if as_json:\n         print(json.dumps(comparison.to_dict(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n     else:\n         print(f\"[compare-runs] baseline={comparison.baseline_run_id} runs={len(comparison.variants)}\")\n         for variant, summary in sorted(comparison.averages.items()):\n             print(f\"  {variant}: {json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True)}\")\n     return 0\n \n \n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n     raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",

              "patch": "Index: src/cli/main.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/main.py\t\n+++ src/cli/main.py\t\n@@ -1,207 +1,210 @@\n import sys\n from enum import StrEnum\n from typing import Annotated\n \n import typer\n from rich.markup import escape\n \n from cli.display import console\n from cli.models import AnalystType, AssetType\n from cli.prompts import filter_analysts_for_asset_type, parse_analysts\n-from cli.run import _validate_variant, run_analysis\n+from cli.run import _reject_unavailable_variant, _validate_variant, run_analysis\n from tradingagents.backtest import iter_grid, run_backtest, summarize\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.llm_clients.openai_client import SIGNED_IN_PROVIDERS\n from tradingagents.portfolio import load_portfolio\n \n # prompt_toolkit's win32 output module is importable only on Windows (it asserts\n # the platform at import time), so gate on the platform rather than catching the\n # failure — that way a genuinely broken prompt_toolkit on Windows still surfaces\n # instead of silently disabling the handler below. Off Windows this stays an\n # empty tuple, which `except` accepts and never matches (#1138).\n if sys.platform == \"win32\":  # pragma: no cover - platform dependent\n     from prompt_toolkit.output.win32 import NoConsoleScreenBufferError\n \n     _NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = (NoConsoleScreenBufferError,)\n else:\n     _NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS = ()\n \n app = typer.Typer(\n     name=\"TradingAgents\",\n     help=\"TradingAgents CLI: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework\",\n     add_completion=True,  # Enable shell completion\n )\n \n \n @app.callback(invoke_without_command=True)\n def analyze(\n     ctx: typer.Context,\n     checkpoint: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None,\n         \"--checkpoint/--no-checkpoint\",\n         help=\"Enable/disable checkpoint-resume (save state after each node so a \"\n         \"crashed run can resume). Omit to honor TRADINGAGENTS_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED.\",\n     ),\n     clear_checkpoints: bool = typer.Option(\n         False,\n         \"--clear-checkpoints\",\n         help=\"Delete all saved checkpoints before running (force fresh start).\",\n     ),\n     portfolio: str = typer.Option(\n         None,\n         \"--portfolio\",\n         help=\"JSON file with current holdings and cash, so the trader, risk and \"\n         \"portfolio agents size against your actual position.\",\n     ),\n     ticker: str = typer.Option(None, \"--ticker\", help=\"Ticker to analyze, e.g. NVDA or 0700.HK; skips the prompt\"),\n     date: str = typer.Option(None, \"--date\", help=\"Analysis date, YYYY-MM-DD; skips the prompt\"),\n     analysts: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--analysts\", help=\"Comma-separated analysts, e.g. market,news; skips the prompt\"\n     ),\n     save: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--save/--no-save\", help=\"Save the report under results_dir without asking\"\n     ),\n     show: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--show/--no-show\", help=\"Show the full report at the end without asking\"\n     ),\n     html: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--html/--no-html\",\n         help=\"Save the report as one HTML page too, complete_report.html, without asking (default: yes)\",\n     ),\n     variant: str = typer.Option(\n         \"v0\", \"--variant\",\n         help=\"Architecture variant for the run manifest: v0 (original), v1 (trimmed), v2 (adaptive).\",\n     ),\n ):\n     \"\"\"Run an analysis. This is what a bare `tradingagents` does.\n \n     Flags answer their questions; with provider, models, depth and language also\n     set through TRADINGAGENTS_* variables, the run asks nothing.\n     \"\"\"\n     if ctx.invoked_subcommand is not None:\n         return\n     if clear_checkpoints:\n         from tradingagents.graph.checkpointer import clear_all_checkpoints\n         n = clear_all_checkpoints(DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"data_cache_dir\"])\n         console.print(f\"[yellow]Cleared {n} checkpoint(s).[/yellow]\")\n     try:\n         variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n     except ValueError as exc:\n         console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n+    # Refuse v1/v2 here too, before run_analysis is even called, so an unavailable\n+    # variant is rejected before any model call.\n+    _reject_unavailable_variant(variant)\n     portfolio_context = None\n     if portfolio:\n         try:\n             portfolio_context = load_portfolio(portfolio)\n         except ValueError as exc:\n             console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n             raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n \n     try:\n         flags = {\"ticker\": ticker, \"date\": date, \"analysts\": analysts, \"save\": save, \"show\": show, \"html\": html}\n         run_analysis(checkpoint=checkpoint, portfolio=portfolio_context, flags=flags, variant=variant)\n     except _NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS:\n         # A terminal with no console buffer cannot host the interactive prompts.\n         # Emit one actionable line on stderr instead of a prompt_toolkit\n         # traceback; plain text, since rich may not render here either (#1138).\n         typer.echo(\n             \"Error: no Windows console available. The interactive CLI needs a real \"\n             \"console buffer — run it from Windows Terminal, PowerShell, or cmd.exe \"\n             \"rather than a piped or embedded terminal.\",\n             err=True,\n         )\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n \n \n @app.command()\n def backtest(\n     tickers: str = typer.Argument(..., help=\"Comma-separated tickers, e.g. NVDA,AAPL\"),\n     start: str = typer.Option(..., \"--start\", help=\"First analysis date, YYYY-MM-DD\"),\n     end: str = typer.Option(..., \"--end\", help=\"Last analysis date, YYYY-MM-DD\"),\n     every: int = typer.Option(7, \"--every\", help=\"Days between analysis dates\"),\n     analysts: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--analysts\", help=\"Comma-separated analysts to run: market, sentiment, news, fundamentals; omit for all the asset type allows\"\n     ),\n     asset_type: str = typer.Option(\"stock\", \"--asset-type\", help=\"stock or crypto\"),\n     portfolio: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--portfolio\", help=\"JSON file with holdings and cash, held constant across the grid\"\n     ),\n     run_id: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--run-id\", help=\"Continue an earlier sweep: its cells are skipped and its log reused\"\n     ),\n ):\n     \"\"\"Score past decisions over a grid of tickers and dates.\"\"\"\n \n     try:\n         dates = iter_grid(start, end, every)\n         book = load_portfolio(portfolio) if portfolio else None\n         kind = AssetType(asset_type.strip().lower())\n         # The analysts are named and checked as for an analysis; without a\n         # choice, every analyst the asset type allows runs.\n         chosen = (parse_analysts(analysts, kind) if analysts\n                   else filter_analysts_for_asset_type(list(AnalystType), kind))\n     except ValueError as exc:\n         console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n \n     names = [t.strip() for t in tickers.split(\",\") if t.strip()]\n     if not names:\n         console.print(\"[red]No ticker to analyze; pass them comma-separated, e.g. NVDA,AAPL[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n \n     def show_progress(done, total, ticker, date):\n         console.print(f\"[dim][{done}/{total}] {ticker} {date}[/dim]\")\n \n     kwargs = {\"asset_type\": kind.value, \"portfolio\": book, \"run_id\": run_id, \"progress\": show_progress,\n               \"selected_analysts\": [a.value for a in chosen]}\n \n     try:\n         result = run_backtest(names, dates, DEFAULT_CONFIG, **kwargs)\n     except Exception as exc:  # a missing key or an unknown analyst is a setup error\n         console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n     console.print(summarize(result).render())\n     console.print(f\"\\nRan {result.cells_run} cells, skipped {result.skipped}. Log: {result.log_path}\")\n     console.print(f\"Continue or settle this sweep: --run-id {result.run_id}\")\n     for ticker, date, reason in result.failures:\n         console.print(f\"[yellow]failed:[/yellow] {ticker} {date}: {reason}\")\n     for ticker, reason in result.settlement_failures:\n         console.print(f\"[yellow]unsettled:[/yellow] {ticker}: {reason}\")\n \n \n # The plans `login` and `logout` take: the providers signed in to, not keyed.\n Plan = StrEnum(\"Plan\", {name: name for name in SIGNED_IN_PROVIDERS})\n \n \n @app.command()\n def login(plan: Annotated[Plan, typer.Argument(help=\"The plan to sign in with\")]):\n     \"\"\"Sign in with your ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan, for the chatgpt provider.\"\"\"\n     from tradingagents.llm_clients import chatgpt_auth\n \n     try:\n         # One unwrapped line, so the sign-in address can be copied whole.\n         email = chatgpt_auth.sign_in(\n             say=lambda line: console.print(line, soft_wrap=True, markup=False, highlight=False))\n     except chatgpt_auth.ChatGPTAuthError as exc:\n         console.print(f\"[red]{escape(str(exc))}[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n     console.print(f\"[green]Signed in to ChatGPT as {escape(email)}.[/green]\")\n \n \n @app.command()\n def logout(plan: Annotated[Plan, typer.Argument(help=\"The plan to sign out of\")]):\n     \"\"\"Sign out of your ChatGPT plan: revoke this machine's access and forget it.\"\"\"\n     from tradingagents.llm_clients import chatgpt_auth\n \n     outcome = chatgpt_auth.sign_out()\n     if outcome == \"revoked\":\n         console.print(\"Signed out of ChatGPT.\")\n     elif outcome == \"forgotten\":\n         console.print(\"[yellow]Signed out here, but OpenAI could not be reached to revoke the sign-in; \"\n                       \"it stays valid at OpenAI until it expires.[/yellow]\")\n     else:\n         console.print(\"Not signed in to ChatGPT.\")\n \n \n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n     app()\n",
              "additions": 4,

              "patch": "Index: src/cli/run.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/run.py\t\n+++ src/cli/run.py\t\n@@ -1,649 +1,678 @@\n \"\"\"Running one analysis from the CLI: build the graph, stream it into the live view, save the report.\"\"\"\n \n import os\n import re\n import sys\n import time\n import webbrowser\n from dataclasses import replace\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from functools import wraps\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import typer\n from rich.live import Live\n \n from cli.display import (\n     ANALYST_ORDER,\n     AnalystWallTimeTracker,\n     classify_message_type,\n     console,\n     create_layout,\n     display_complete_report,\n     message_buffer,\n     update_analyst_statuses,\n     update_display,\n     update_research_team_status,\n )\n from cli.selections import depth_from_env, get_user_selections, unattended_gaps\n from cli.stats_handler import StatsCallbackHandler\n from tradingagents import __version__\n from tradingagents.agents.rating import is_review, run_rating\n from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.graph.analyst_execution import (\n     build_analyst_execution_plan,\n )\n from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, build_run_id, write_manifest\n \n _VALID_VARIANTS = (\"v0\", \"v1\", \"v2\")\n \n \n def _validate_variant(value: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Accept only a known, lowercase architecture variant slug (``v0``/``v1``/``v2``).\n \n     The value becomes the first segment of the manifest ``run_id`` and a directory\n     name under the results root, so an unknown or unsafe value is rejected rather\n     than interpolated.\n     \"\"\"\n     if value not in _VALID_VARIANTS:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid variant {value!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_VALID_VARIANTS)}\"\n         )\n     return value\n \n \n \n def _run_directory(config: dict, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Where this run writes, with the ticker validated as a path component.\n \n     Every other path that interpolates a ticker checks it first; a value of\n     \"..\" here would place the run outside the results directory.\n     \"\"\"\n     return Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker_component(ticker) / trade_date\n \n \n def _manifest_config_snapshot(config: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Scalars from ``config`` that are safe to record in a run manifest.\n \n     The recorder already drops secret-pattern keys; keeping only scalar values\n     here also excludes nested objects and lists that are not comparable settings.\n     \"\"\"\n     return {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in config.items()\n         if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None\n     }\n \n \n def write_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     config: dict,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     outcome: str | None,\n     usage: dict,\n     failure: str | None,\n     variant: str,\n     repeat: int,\n     at: datetime,\n     version: str,\n     duration_seconds: float | None = None,\n     started_at: float | None = None,\n     clock=None,\n+    stop_reason: str | None = None,\n ) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write this run's manifest to ``<results_dir>/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json``.\n \n-    Fields owned by other members are placeholders until they land: ``stop_reason``\n-    (C) is ``None``, ``prompt_hashes`` (B) is ``{}``, ``evidence_snapshot`` (A) is\n-    ``None``. ``duration_seconds`` is measured from ``started_at`` and ``clock``\n-    (``time.time`` by default) when not supplied; passing both keeps it testable.\n+    ``stop_reason`` is read from the run's final state by the caller (C owns the\n+    value domain); it is ``None`` when the graph did not reach a terminal state.\n+    ``prompt_hashes`` (B) is ``{}`` and ``evidence_snapshot`` (A) is ``None`` until\n+    those members' contracts land. ``duration_seconds`` is measured from\n+    ``started_at`` and ``clock`` (``time.time`` by default) when not supplied;\n+    passing both keeps it testable.\n     \"\"\"\n     run_id = build_run_id(variant, ticker, trade_date, repeat, at)\n     if duration_seconds is None and started_at is not None:\n         now = (clock or time.time)()\n         duration_seconds = max(0.0, now - started_at)\n \n     event = RunEvent(\n         run_id=run_id,\n         created_at=at.astimezone(UTC).isoformat(),\n         version=version,\n         ticker=ticker,\n         trade_date=trade_date,\n         asset_type=asset_type,\n         outcome=outcome,\n         config_snapshot=_manifest_config_snapshot(config),\n         prompt_hashes={},\n         evidence_snapshot=None,\n         usage=usage,\n         duration_seconds=duration_seconds,\n         failure=failure,\n-        stop_reason=None,\n+        stop_reason=stop_reason,\n     )\n     runs_dir = Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"runs\"\n     run_id = _unique_run_id(runs_dir, run_id)\n     event = replace(event, run_id=run_id)\n     manifest_dir = runs_dir / run_id\n     manifest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     return write_manifest(event, manifest_dir / \"manifest.json\")\n \n \n def _unique_run_id(runs_dir: Path, run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A run_id whose directory does not exist yet, so a same-minute retry is safe.\n \n     ``build_run_id`` has minute resolution, so two runs started in the same minute\n     (or a retry) produce the same id. Appending ``-<n>`` keeps the id within the\n     recorder's 64-char pattern and never overwrites an earlier manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     pattern = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n     candidate = run_id\n     suffix = 2\n     while (runs_dir / candidate).exists():\n         candidate = f\"{run_id}-{suffix}\"\n         if not pattern.match(candidate):\n             raise ValueError(f\"no free run_id derived from {run_id!r} within 64 chars\")\n         suffix += 1\n     return candidate\n \n \n def _make_manifest_writer(config: dict, selections: dict, stats_handler, started_at=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     \"\"\"Return a ``write(failure=..., outcome=...)`` bound to this run's inputs.\n \n     ``variant`` selects the architecture under test and becomes the first segment\n     of the manifest ``run_id``; ``repeat`` is 1 and ``created_at`` is now, both\n     supplied here so the recorder never reads the clock itself. ``started_at`` is\n     the run's start (``time.time()``); forwarding it lets the manifest record a\n     real duration.\n     \"\"\"\n \n-    def write(*, failure, outcome):\n+    def write(*, failure, outcome, stop_reason=None):\n         return write_run_manifest(\n             config=config,\n             ticker=selections[\"ticker\"],\n             trade_date=selections[\"analysis_date\"],\n             asset_type=selections[\"asset_type\"],\n             outcome=outcome,\n             usage=stats_handler.get_stats(),\n             failure=failure,\n             variant=variant,\n             repeat=1,\n             at=datetime.now(UTC),\n             version=__version__,\n             started_at=started_at,\n+            stop_reason=stop_reason,\n         )\n \n     return write\n \n \n def _finalize_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     write,\n     graph,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     portfolio,\n     final_state,\n     failure: BaseException | None,\n ) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Write the manifest, then dispose of (or keep) the checkpoint.\n \n     The manifest is written **before** the checkpoint is cleared, so a crash in\n     teardown never loses the record. A failed run still writes a manifest with\n     ``failure`` set and keeps its checkpoint for resume; the failure is re-raised.\n+    ``stop_reason`` is read from ``final_state`` (C's field) with a ``None``\n+    fallback when the run did not reach a terminal state.\n     \"\"\"\n     outcome = None if final_state is None else run_rating(final_state)\n-    write(failure=None if failure is None else str(failure), outcome=outcome)\n+    stop_reason = (final_state or {}).get(\"stop_reason\") if failure is None else None\n+    write(failure=None if failure is None else str(failure), outcome=outcome, stop_reason=stop_reason)\n \n     if failure is not None:\n         raise failure\n \n     if final_state is not None:\n         graph.record_decision(ticker, trade_date, final_state)\n     graph.clear_checkpoint_on_success(ticker, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n \n \n def _announce_checkpoint_state(graph, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Say whether this run resumed a saved one, where the user can see it.\n \n     The graph logs this, but nothing in the CLI configures logging and the live\n     view owns the screen, so a resume was invisible.\n     \"\"\"\n     if getattr(graph, \"_resuming\", False):\n         message_buffer.add_message(\n             \"System\", f\"Resuming the saved run for {ticker} on {trade_date}\"\n         )\n     else:\n         message_buffer.add_message(\"System\", f\"Starting fresh for {ticker} on {trade_date}\")\n \n \n def _build_run_config(selections: dict, checkpoint: bool | None) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Assemble the run config from interactive selections, honoring env precedence.\n \n     Round counts and checkpoint follow \"explicit env/flag wins\": an env-applied\n     value on DEFAULT_CONFIG is preserved unless the user overrode it on the CLI.\n     \"\"\"\n     config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n     # Research depth sets both round counts, but an explicit env override\n     # (TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS / _MAX_RISK_ROUNDS) wins over the\n     # interactive selection — leave the env-applied value in place (#977).\n     rounds = ((\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS\", \"max_debate_rounds\"),\n               (\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_RISK_ROUNDS\", \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"))\n     depth_was_asked = not depth_from_env()\n     for env_var, key in rounds:\n         if not os.environ.get(env_var):\n             config[key] = selections[\"research_depth\"]\n         elif depth_was_asked:\n             # The depth question appeared (it is skipped only when both are\n             # set), so say which half of the answer the environment overrode.\n             console.print(\n                 f\"[green]✓ {key} from environment:[/green] {config[key]} \"\n                 f\"(set by {env_var}, so the research depth you chose does not apply to it)\"\n             )\n     config[\"quick_think_llm\"] = selections[\"quick_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"deep_think_llm\"] = selections[\"deep_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"backend_url\"] = selections[\"backend_url\"]\n     config[\"llm_provider\"] = selections[\"llm_provider\"].lower()\n     # Provider-specific thinking configuration. Only the main provider's is\n     # asked; a tier on another provider keeps its configured value (#1440).\n     for key in (\"google_thinking_level\", \"openai_reasoning_effort\", \"anthropic_effort\"):\n         if selections.get(key) is not None:\n             config[key] = selections[key]\n     config[\"output_language\"] = selections.get(\"output_language\", \"English\")\n     # --checkpoint/--no-checkpoint overrides only when explicitly given; omitting\n     # the flag preserves TRADINGAGENTS_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED / the default (#976).\n     if checkpoint is not None:\n         config[\"checkpoint_enabled\"] = checkpoint\n     return config\n \n \n+def _reject_unavailable_variant(variant: str, config: dict | None = None) -> None:\n+    \"\"\"Refuse v1/v2 until C's ``workflow_variant`` key is wired into the graph.\n+\n+    v0 is always allowed. A non-v0 variant is allowed only when ``config`` actually\n+    carries ``workflow_variant`` (C's enable switch); otherwise this raises\n+    ``typer.Exit`` before any model call, so a v0-compatible run is never labelled\n+    v1/v2.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    if variant == \"v0\":\n+        return\n+    if (config if config is not None else DEFAULT_CONFIG).get(\"workflow_variant\"):\n+        return\n+    console.print(\n+        f\"[red]Variant {variant!r} is not available yet: the workflow only \"\n+        f\"implements v0. Run with --variant v0.[/red]\"\n+    )\n+    raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n+\n+\n def run_analysis(checkpoint: bool | None = None, portfolio=None, flags=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     flags = flags or {}\n     variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n+    # v1/v2 are not implemented in the workflow yet (C's `workflow_variant` key is\n+    # not wired into the graph). Refuse them before any setup or model call.\n+    _reject_unavailable_variant(variant)\n     # With no terminal nothing can answer a prompt: name every question still\n     # open before any model is called, rather than stopping at the first one.\n     if not (sys.stdin and sys.stdin.isatty()):\n         gaps = unattended_gaps(flags)\n         if gaps:\n             console.print(\"[red]No terminal to answer the setup questions. Set:[/red]\")\n             for gap in gaps:\n                 console.print(f\"  {gap}\")\n             raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n \n     selections = get_user_selections(flags)\n \n     config = _build_run_config(selections, checkpoint)\n \n     stats_handler = StatsCallbackHandler()\n \n     # Normalize analyst selection to predefined order (selection is a 'set', order is fixed)\n     selected_set = {analyst.value for analyst in selections[\"analysts\"]}\n     selected_analyst_keys = [a for a in ANALYST_ORDER if a in selected_set]\n     analyst_execution_plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analyst_keys)\n     analyst_wall_time_tracker = AnalystWallTimeTracker(analyst_execution_plan)\n \n     graph = TradingAgentsGraph(\n         selected_analyst_keys,\n         config=config,\n         debug=True,\n         callbacks=[stats_handler],\n     )\n \n     message_buffer.init_for_analysis(selected_analyst_keys)\n \n     # Track start time for elapsed display\n     start_time = time.time()\n \n     results_dir = _run_directory(config, selections[\"ticker\"], selections[\"analysis_date\"])\n     results_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     report_dir = results_dir / \"reports\"\n     report_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     log_file = results_dir / \"message_tool.log\"\n     log_file.touch(exist_ok=True)\n \n     def save_message_decorator(obj, func_name):\n         func = getattr(obj, func_name)\n \n         @wraps(func)\n         def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):\n             func(*args, **kwargs)\n             timestamp, message_type, content = obj.messages[-1]\n             content = content.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")  # Replace newlines with spaces\n             with open(log_file, \"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n                 f.write(f\"{timestamp} [{message_type}] {content}\\n\")\n         return wrapper\n \n     def save_tool_call_decorator(obj, func_name):\n         func = getattr(obj, func_name)\n \n         @wraps(func)\n         def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):\n             func(*args, **kwargs)\n             timestamp, tool_name, args = obj.tool_calls[-1]\n             args_str = \", \".join(f\"{k}={v}\" for k, v in args.items())\n             with open(log_file, \"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n                 f.write(f\"{timestamp} [Tool Call] {tool_name}({args_str})\\n\")\n         return wrapper\n \n     def save_report_section_decorator(obj, func_name):\n         func = getattr(obj, func_name)\n \n         @wraps(func)\n         def wrapper(section_name, content):\n             func(section_name, content)\n             if section_name in obj.report_sections and obj.report_sections[section_name] is not None:\n                 content = obj.report_sections[section_name]\n                 if content:\n                     file_name = f\"{section_name}.md\"\n                     text = \"\\n\".join(str(item) for item in content) if isinstance(content, list) else content\n                     with open(report_dir / file_name, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n                         f.write(text)\n         return wrapper\n \n     message_buffer.add_message = save_message_decorator(message_buffer, \"add_message\")\n     message_buffer.add_tool_call = save_tool_call_decorator(message_buffer, \"add_tool_call\")\n     message_buffer.update_report_section = save_report_section_decorator(message_buffer, \"update_report_section\")\n \n     layout = create_layout()\n \n     # It is validated as a safe lowercase slug and threaded through\n ``run_analysis`` into the run manifest's ``run_id`` instead of the old hardcoded\n ``v0``. These tests cover the validator, the CLI plumbing, and the manifest.\n \"\"\"\n \n import pytest\n from typer.testing import CliRunner\n \n import cli.main as m\n import cli.run as cli_run\n \n # --- validator ---------------------------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_variant_accepts_v0_v1_v2():\n     for value in (\"v0\", \"v1\", \"v2\"):\n         assert cli_run._validate_variant(value) == value\n \n \n def test_variant_rejects_uppercase():\n     with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n         cli_run._validate_variant(\"V2\")\n \n \n def test_variant_rejects_path_traversal():\n     with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n         cli_run._validate_variant(\"../x\")\n \n \n def test_variant_rejects_unknown_slug():\n     for bad in (\"v3\", \"v\", \"\", \"v10\", \"variant\"):\n         with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n             cli_run._validate_variant(bad)\n \n \n # --- CLI plumbing ------------------------------------------------------------\n \n \n def _runner(monkeypatch, calls):\n     monkeypatch.setattr(m, \"run_analysis\", lambda **kw: calls.append(kw))\n     calls.clear()\n     return CliRunner()\n \n \n def test_variant_default_is_v0(monkeypatch):\n     calls = []\n     runner = _runner(monkeypatch, calls)\n     assert runner.invoke(m.app, []).exit_code == 0\n     assert calls[0][\"variant\"] == \"v0\"\n \n \n-def test_variant_option_passed_through(monkeypatch):\n+def test_variant_option_v0_passed_through(monkeypatch):\n     calls = []\n     runner = _runner(monkeypatch, calls)\n-    assert runner.invoke(m.app, [\"--variant\", \"v2\"]).exit_code == 0\n-    assert calls[0][\"variant\"] == \"v2\"\n+    assert runner.invoke(m.app, [\"--variant\", \"v0\"]).exit_code == 0\n+    assert calls[0][\"variant\"] == \"v0\"\n \n \n+def test_variant_option_v2_refused_until_workflow_variant(monkeypatch):\n+    # v2 is valid input but not implemented yet; it is refused before run_analysis.\n+    calls = []\n+    runner = _runner(monkeypatch, calls)\n+    assert runner.invoke(m.app, [\"--variant\", \"v2\"]).exit_code != 0\n+    assert calls == []\n+\n+\n def test_invalid_variant_exits_before_running(monkeypatch):\n     calls = []\n     runner = _runner(monkeypatch, calls)\n     result = runner.invoke(m.app, [\"--variant\", \"V2\"])\n     assert result.exit_code != 0\n     assert calls == []\n \n \n # --- manifest uses the variant ----------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_make_manifest_writer_uses_variant(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n     captured = {}\n \n     def fake_write_run_manifest(**kwargs):\n         captured.update(kwargs)\n         return tmp_path / \"manifest.json\"\n \n     monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"write_run_manifest\", fake_write_run_manifest)\n \n     class _Stats:\n         def get_stats(self):\n             return {\"llm_calls\": 0, \"tool_calls\": 0, \"tokens_in\": 0, \"tokens_out\": 0}\n \n     selections = {\"ticker\": \"NVDA\", \"analysis_date\": \"2026-11-20\", \"asset_type\": \"stock\"}\n     config = {\"results_dir\": str(tmp_path), \"llm_provider\": \"openai\"}\n     write = cli_run._make_manifest_writer(\n         config, selections, _Stats(), started_at=None, variant=\"v2\"\n     )\n     write(failure=None, outcome=\"Buy\")\n     assert captured[\"variant\"] == \"v2\"\n \n \n def test_manifest_run_id_reflects_variant(tmp_path):\n     path = cli_run.write_run_manifest(\n         config={\"results_dir\": str(tmp_path), \"llm_provider\": \"openai\"},\n         ticker=\"NVDA\",\n         trade_date=\"2026-11-20\",\n         asset_type=\"stock\",\n         outcome=\"Buy\",\n         usage={\"llm_calls\": 1, \"tool_calls\": 0, \"tokens_in\": 1, \"tokens_out\": 0},\n         duration_seconds=1.0,\n         failure=None,\n         variant=\"v2\",\n         repeat=1,\n         at=cli_run.datetime(2026, 11, 21, 12, 0, tzinfo=cli_run.UTC),\n         version=\"0.7.1\",\n     )\n     assert path.parent.name.startswith(\"v2-\")\n",

The current main branch has merged the independent budget module and the RunEvent v1 recorder. C is responsible for workflow configuration, routing, and state; E is responsible for the CLI, manifest, and comparison. The graph-wide stop field and the two variants are not yet wired in. For the CLI writes and comparison script mentioned by E, please provide traceable commits so we can integrate against the same version.\n4: \n5: ## Stop Reasons and How to Read Them\n6: \n7: C plans to write `AgentState.stop_reason`, using the same value in the program-entry `final_state` and the final public state received by the CLI. E writes the existing RunEvent v1 `stop_reason` in the terminal state. Keep `str | null` and the existing field structure.\n8: \n9: | Whole-run stop reason | When written | Current status |\n10: |---|---|---|\n11: | `completed` | The workflow normally produces a final result. If only the added rounds are trimmed but it then ends normally, this value is still written. | Proposed; graph wiring pending |\n12: | `INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET_FINAL_REVIEW` | Insufficient initial reservation, or insufficient budget during the run to admit the required final review. For the latter, per the reviewed scheme, record `stop_detail=\"overspend\"`. | Policy code merged, graph-wide mapping pending |\n13: | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` | A version-valid Research Manager output calls for review or downgrade, with no executable candidate to hand to the Trader. For example, the budget is only enough for reservation and there is only the opening Bull. | B/D handoff rules confirmed; graph wiring pending approval |\n14: | `MISSING_OR_UNSUPPORTED_MANAGER_VERSION` | Manager handoff version missing or unsupported, refuse to enter the Trader. | Handoff code confirmed, graph integration pending approval |\n15: | `INVALID_OUTPUT_NO_RECOVERY` | Required structured artifact invalid and recovery paths exhausted. | Design rule exists, pending full-graph integration |\n16: | `validation_stopped` | D's deterministic validation requires stopping, and there is no more specific C termination reason. | C's proposed mapping; D's authoritative verdict and reason retained separately |\n17: | `RESEARCH_MANAGER_DENIED_INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET` | In future plans, if a budget is set for the Research Manager and admission is denied, record it as the stop reason for that run. | An existing design rule; the current wiring scope does not meter the Research Manager |\n18: \n19: `research_stop_reason` separately stores the research phase reason, planning to use the already-merged `INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET_FOLLOW_UP`, and retaining `ALL_RESOLVED`, `NO_ELIGIBLE_RESPONDER`, `NO_PROGRESS`, `HARD_CAP` and other semantics for the full adaptive scheme review. Example: in the 2-unit use case, the research phase reason is `INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET_FOLLOW_UP`, and the proposed reason for the whole run is `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. D's `verdict`, `reason_code` and `executable` are kept separately. Old runs or exceptions that did not reach the graph terminal state can remain `null`, with E's `failure` recording the failure reason.\n20: \n21: ## Variant Switch\n22: \n23: It is proposed that C provide an explicit configuration key `workflow_variant`, accepting lowercase `v0`, `v1`, `v2`. E's CLI can offer `--variant {v0,v1,v2}` in the same command, pass the option to C, and generate `run_id` from the **actually enabled** variant. This is an integration proposal and requires plan and test approval. Unknown values or variants not yet delivered should be explicitly rejected before calling the model, so that runs on the compatibility path are not labeled as V1 or V2.\n24: \n25: | Configuration value | Behavior and acceptance |\n26: |---|---|\n27: | `v0`, the default when unset | Original workflow; the fixed three-role risk path and existing CLI/report behavior remain. Used for controls on the same candidate version; the frozen baseline retains its own regression records. |\n28: | `v1` | Fixed pruning, where pre-approved rules decide which optional work to skip. Keep the same pruning rules for different budgets and problem contents. The default debate already has only one Bull/Bear pair, so you cannot claim pruning just by setting the limit to 1. If fixed round reduction is used, the plan is to use two groups for V0 and one group for V1 in the control experiment and record configuration differences, retaining the default settings and the three risk roles. The specific pruning rules are pending independent approval. |\n29: | `v2` | Dynamically route based on unresolved questions, eligible responder roles, and remaining budget; retain the hard cap and D validation. The proposed budget-admission wiring is a component milestone. Only after full dynamic routing and the switch are in place will V2 be delivered to E for formal comparison. |\n30: \n31: Please have E confirm the configuration key and CLI argument, the comparator's actual version and matching fields. The three groups should fix the ticker, date, asset type, model, provider, language, starting memory and common evidence input. If variants naturally use different role prompts, please clarify with B the prompt fingerprinting rules and comparability conditions used by the comparator, and retain the real hashes.\n32: \n33: ## Usage, Paths, and Delivery\n34: \n35: C plans to give per-stage admission, rejection, reservation, commitment, actual reporting or under-reporting, overspend, and stop reasons. Per-call records are settled in admission order. Estimates or reservations must not accumulate into actual tokens. Explicit and verifiable zero records are 0; under-reporting continues to be marked unknown, and the total token amount follows E's unknown-usage contract. Application-layer fallbacks, failed calls, and SDK retries are distinguished according to E's observable boundary. Paths and loop limits remain, for now, in C's experiments and test evidence; RunEvent v1 keeps the existing 15 fields.\n36: \n37: `run_id` and a pure `checkpoint_thread_id` belong to explicit resume wiring; see `C-to-E-evidence-checkpoint-contract-alignment.md`. New main-graph and resume tests have not yet been run. C separately retains D5's original session and human-intervention annotations, as well as D6's C section and personal reflection.\n\n(End of file - total 37 lines)\n</content>",

If only extra rounds are cut but it then ends normally, still write this value. | Proposed, awaiting graph integration |\n| `INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET_FINAL_REVIEW` | Insufficient initial reservation, or insufficient budget during the run to admit the required final review. For the latter, per the reviewed scheme, record `stop_detail=\"overspend\"`. | Policy code merged, graph-wide mapping pending |\n| `REVIEW_REQUIRED` | A version-valid Research Manager output calls for review or downgrade, with no executable candidate to hand to the Trader. For example, the budget is only enough for reservation and there is only the opening Bull. | B/D handoff rules confirmed; graph wiring pending approval |\n| `MISSING_OR_UNSUPPORTED_MANAGER_VERSION` | Manager handoff version missing or unsupported, refuse to enter the Trader. | Handoff code confirmed, graph integration pending approval |\n| `INVALID_OUTPUT_NO_RECOVERY` | A required structured artifact is invalid and the recovery path has been exhausted. | An existing design rule, awaiting integration into the full graph |\n| `validation_stopped` | D's deterministic validation requires stopping, and there is no more specific C termination reason. | C's proposed mapping; D's authoritative verdict and reason retained separately |\n| `RESEARCH_MANAGER_DENIED_INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET` | If a later scheme sets a budget for the research manager and admission is denied, record it as the run's stop reason. | Design rule already in place; current wiring scope does not meter the Research Manager |\n\n`research_stop_reason` stores the research-stage reason separately; the plan is to use the already-merged `INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET_FOLLOW_UP`, while retaining semantics such as `ALL_RESOLVED`, `NO_ELIGIBLE_RESPONDER`, `NO_PROGRESS`, and `HARD_CAP` for the full adaptive-scheme review. Reviewers: B (collaboration /\n prompt versioning) and D (deterministic safety) per the team split §3.\n-Status: **tooling only.** `scripts/compare_runs.py` and `test/offline/test_compare_runs.py`\n-exist and pass offline; **no experiments have run yet**. The comparison tables the\n-report needs (`docs/evaluation/results/`) do not exist and must not be fabricated.\n+Status: **tooling implemented; V0 has run three times.** `scripts/compare_runs.py` and\n+`test/offline/test_compare_runs.py` exist and pass offline. Three V0 manifests were\n+recorded under `outputs/runs/` on 2026-11-22 (NVDA, `--variant v0`). Those runs have\n+**empty `prompt_hashes`** (B has not delivered prompt fingerprints yet), so the tool\n+**refuses** to compare them; no comparison table exists yet and none may be fabricated.\n \n This protocol fixes *how* runs are compared and *what* a comparison may claim. It\n does not define semantic-quality scoring: that spec is owned by B and D and is not\n-implemented in this slice (see \"Out of scope\" below). Until real runs exist, this\n-document and the tool are the only deliverables here.\n+implemented in this slice (see \"Out of scope\" below).\n \n ## Fixed inputs (the comparison set)\n \n Two runs may be compared only when these inputs are identical to the baseline. The\n tool enforces this; a mismatch is refused, not averaged or shown side by side.\n \n | Guard key | Source | Why it must match |\n |---|---|---|\n | `ticker` | manifest top level | different company = different question |\n | `trade_date` | manifest top level | different analysis date = different information set |\n | `asset_type` | manifest top level | `stock` vs `crypto` changes tools and rules |\n | model | `config_snapshot.quick_think_llm`, `deep_think_llm` | a model change is the very thing being evaluated |\n | provider | `config_snapshot.llm_provider` (+ optional `*_think_provider`) | different backend = different outputs |\n | language | `config_snapshot.output_language` | report text changes with language |\n | prompt | `prompt_hashes` (name → hash) | a prompt change invalidates a like-for-like comparison |\n \n A missing required config key (model, provider, language) is treated as\n-**incomparable** — the tool refuses rather than guessing a default.\n+**incomparable** — the tool refuses rather than guessing a default. An **empty\n+`prompt_hashes`** (`{}` or `null`) is also refused: without a real prompt fingerprint\n+the runs cannot be shown to use the same prompts. This is why the three V0 runs are\n+not yet comparable. `results_dir` is a machine-local output path and is **not**\n+recorded in the manifest, so it can never be a spurious difference.\n \n ## Variants\n \n Each run is tagged by the first segment of its `run_id`\n (`<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<repeat>-<runstamp>`):\n \n | Variant | Meaning |\n |---|---|\n | `v0` | original upstream path (baseline for comparison) |\n | `v1` | trimmed / simple reduction |\n | `v2` | adaptive collaboration |\n \n Comparing a run against itself-other-variants is the point; comparing different\n inputs is refused.\n \n ## Metrics reported\n \n Only quantities the manifest actually records. Per run: `outcome`, `usage`\n (`llm_calls`, `tool_calls`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`), `duration_seconds`,\n `failure`, `stop_reason`. Per variant: **count of runs** and the **average** of each\n numeric field (`null` values excluded from that field's average).\n \n+A **missing token count stays `null`, never `0`**: an unreported count is unknown,\n+not zero. In the human-readable table it prints as `--`; in `--json` it is `null`.\n+\n The token-reduction goal from the team plan (e.g. 20–25%) is a *target*, not a\n result: the protocol reports measured averages; it does not assert the target was\n met. If real runs do not hit it, the results file says so.\n \n ## Thresholds\n \n Thresholds for a *passing* comparison are intentionally left unset here. They belong\n with the semantic-evaluation spec (B/D) and the CI semantic gate (§6.4). This slice\n ships no threshold and no gate; it only produces comparable numbers.\n \n ## Out of scope (owned elsewhere)\n \n - **Semantic / quality scores** (faithfulness, relevance, argument independence): B\n   and D. This tool does not compute, infer, or approximate them. The absence of a\n   score is the honest output.\n - **`stop_reason` value domain**: C (`execution_policy`). Reported opaquely.\n - **Evidence snapshot semantics**: A (`evidence.py`). Reported opaquely.\n - **Live evaluation runs**: `test/live/test_fixed_eval.py` (later; needs API access).\n \n ## How to run\n \n ```bash\n # Compare two or more manifests of the same input across variants.\n python scripts/compare_runs.py results/v0-nvda-.../manifest.json \\\n                              results/v2-nvda-.../manifest.json\n python scripts/compare_runs.py ... --json     # machine-readable output\n \n # Offline tests (no network, no API keys).\n pytest test/offline/test_compare_runs.py -q\n ```\n \n Exit codes: `0` comparable, `1` refused (reason on stderr names the differing guard\n key), `2` usage error. Results meant for the report go under\n `docs/evaluation/results/`, one file per comparison, with the commit and manifest\n paths recorded — **only after the runs actually happen**.\n \n ## Current state\n \n-- Comparison tooling: implemented, 20 offline tests green.\n-- Experiments: **none run.** No `results/` files exist. Do not add comparison tables\n-  until real manifests are produced from real runs.\n+- Comparison tooling: implemented, offline tests green.\n+- Experiments: **V0 run three times** on 2026-11-22 (NVDA), manifests under\n+  `outputs/runs/v0-nvda-2026-11-22-r1-*`. They have empty `prompt_hashes`, so they\n+  are **refused** by the tool and no `docs/evaluation/results/` table exists yet.\n+  Once B delivers prompt fingerprints (and a re-run carries them), the V0 manifests\n+  become comparable. Do not write a comparison table from the empty-hash manifests.\n",

              "file": "scripts/compare_runs.py",
              "patch": "Index: scripts/compare_runs.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n+++ scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n@@ -1,235 +1,249 @@\n \"\"\"Compare run manifests across architecture variants (E-owned; D4 / §6.5).\n \n Reads v1 run manifests (``docs/contracts/run-event.md``) produced by\n ``run_recorder`` and reports measured quantities per variant. It **refuses** to\n compare runs that are not comparable: ``ticker``, ``trade_date``, ``asset_type``,\n the model (quick/deep tier LLMs), the provider (``llm_provider`` and any tier\n code/endpoint selectors), the output ``language``, and ``prompt_hashes`` must all\n match the baseline. When any of them differs the comparison raises\n ``IncomparableRunsError`` rather than presenting a misleading table.\n \n This tool never invents quality scores. It reports only what the manifest records\n (outcome, usage, duration, failure, stop reason) and per-variant averages of the\n numeric fields. Semantic/quality thresholds are owned by B/D and are out of scope\n here (see ``docs/evaluation/protocol.md``).\n \n Usage:\n     python scripts/compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\n \n Exit 0 when the runs are comparable, 1 (with a reason on stderr) when they are\n refused, 2 on a usage error. Stdlib + ``run_recorder`` only.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import json\n import sys\n from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n from pathlib import Path\n \n from tradingagents.run_recorder import read_manifest\n \n _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD = (\"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n _MODEL_KEYS = (\"quick_think_llm\", \"deep_think_llm\")\n _PROVIDER_KEYS = (\"llm_provider\", \"quick_think_provider\", \"deep_think_provider\")\n _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS = _MODEL_KEYS + (\"llm_provider\",)\n _LANGUAGE_KEY = \"output_language\"\n _USAGE_METRICS = (\"llm_calls\", \"tool_calls\", \"tokens_in\", \"tokens_out\")\n \n \n class IncomparableRunsError(ValueError):\n     \"\"\"The supplied manifests cannot be compared (a guard key differs).\"\"\"\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class Comparison:\n     \"\"\"Comparable-run report. ``variants`` is per-run; ``averages`` is per-variant.\"\"\"\n \n     baseline_run_id: str\n     guard: dict\n     variants: list[dict]\n     averages: dict\n     notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n \n     def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n         return {\n             \"baseline_run_id\": self.baseline_run_id,\n             \"guard\": self.guard,\n             \"variants\": self.variants,\n             \"averages\": self.averages,\n             \"notes\": self.notes,\n         }\n \n \n def _guard_of(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Extract the keys that must match for a comparison to be valid.\n \n     ``llm_provider``, the tier models, and ``output_language`` are required; a\n     missing required key is refused rather than guessed, so a malformed snapshot\n     cannot silently look comparable. The optional per-tier provider selectors are\n     collected when present; ``_provider_keys`` unions them across every manifest so\n     a tier provider set in *any* run is compared everywhere (a manifest that omits\n     it compares as ``None``, the config default).\n     \"\"\"\n     config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n     guard = {key: manifest.get(key) for key in _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD}\n     required = _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS + (_LANGUAGE_KEY,)\n     for key in required:\n         if key not in config:\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} is missing config key {key!r}; \"\n                 \"cannot compare without it\"\n             )\n         guard[key] = config[key]\n     for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS:\n         if key in config:\n             guard[key] = config[key]\n     prompt_hashes = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n     if not prompt_hashes:\n         # An empty/None prompt fingerprint leaves the comparison unfounded: two runs\n         # cannot be shown to use the same prompts without a real hash (C-to-E\n         # variant response: keep the real hashes). Refuse rather than guess.\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\n             f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} has empty prompt_hashes; \"\n             \"cannot compare without prompt fingerprints\"\n         )\n     guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = prompt_hashes\n     return guard\n \n \n def _provider_keys(manifests: list[dict]) -> list[str]:\n     \"\"\"Provider keys present in *any* manifest, so they are compared everywhere.\"\"\"\n     present: set[str] = set()\n     for manifest in manifests:\n         config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n         present.update(key for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS if key in config)\n     return sorted(present)\n \n \n def _check_comparable(guard: dict, baseline: dict) -> None:\n     diffs = [key for key in baseline if guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n     if diffs:\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\n             \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \"\n             + \", \".join(sorted(diffs))\n         )\n \n \n def _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"The variant segment of a run id (``<variant>-<ticker>-...``).\"\"\"\n     return run_id.split(\"-\", 1)[0]\n \n \n def _variant_row(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n-    return {\n+    usage = manifest.get(\"usage\")\n+    row = {\n         \"run_id\": manifest.get(\"run_id\"),\n         \"variant\": _variant_of(str(manifest.get(\"run_id\", \"\"))),\n         \"outcome\": manifest.get(\"outcome\"),\n-        \"usage\": manifest.get(\"usage\"),\n+        \"usage\": usage,\n         \"duration_seconds\": manifest.get(\"duration_seconds\"),\n         \"failure\": manifest.get(\"failure\"),\n         \"stop_reason\": manifest.get(\"stop_reason\"),\n     }\n+    # Surface each numeric metric explicitly. A missing value stays None (null),\n+    # never coerced to 0: an unreported count is unknown, not zero.\n+    for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n+        row[metric] = usage.get(metric) if isinstance(usage, dict) else None\n+    return row\n \n \n+def _format_metric(value) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"Render a metric for humans: ``--`` for null/unknown, else the number.\"\"\"\n+    return \"--\" if value is None else str(value)\n+\n+\n def _counts(values: list) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Count occurrences of each value (``None`` counted as ``null``).\"\"\"\n     counts: dict = {}\n     for value in values:\n         key = \"null\" if value is None else str(value)\n         counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1\n     return counts\n \n \n def _averages(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:\n     grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}\n     for row in rows:\n         grouped.setdefault(row[\"variant\"], []).append(row)\n \n     result: dict[str, dict] = {}\n     for variant, group in grouped.items():\n         summary: dict = {\"runs\": len(group)}\n         for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n             values = [\n                 row[\"usage\"][metric]\n                 for row in group\n                 if isinstance(row.get(\"usage\"), dict) and row[\"usage\"].get(metric) is not None\n             ]\n             summary[metric] = sum(values) / len(values) if values else None\n         durations = [row[\"duration_seconds\"] for row in group if row[\"duration_seconds\"] is not None]\n         summary[\"duration_seconds\"] = sum(durations) / len(durations) if durations else None\n         summary[\"outcome_counts\"] = _counts([row[\"outcome\"] for row in group])\n         summary[\"stop_reason_counts\"] = _counts([row[\"stop_reason\"] for row in group])\n         result[variant] = summary\n     return result\n \n \n def compare_manifests(manifests: list[dict]) -> Comparison:\n     \"\"\"Compare already-loaded manifests; raise ``IncomparableRunsError`` if invalid.\"\"\"\n     if not manifests:\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\"no manifests supplied\")\n \n     baseline_guard = _guard_of(manifests[0])\n     for manifest in manifests[1:]:\n         _check_comparable(_guard_of(manifest), baseline_guard)\n \n     # Union the provider keys across all runs so a tier provider set in any run\n     # (not just the baseline) is verified to match everywhere.\n     for key in _provider_keys(manifests):\n         values = {(m.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}).get(key) for m in manifests}\n         if len(values) > 1:\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \" + key\n             )\n         baseline_guard.setdefault(key, (manifests[0].get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}).get(key))\n \n     rows = [_variant_row(manifest) for manifest in manifests]\n     return Comparison(\n         baseline_run_id=manifests[0].get(\"run_id\"),\n         guard=baseline_guard,\n         variants=rows,\n         averages=_averages(rows),\n         notes=[\n             \"Reported quantities are measured from run manifests; no quality score is \"\n             \"computed or inferred here.\",\n             \"Runs are only compared when ticker, trade_date, asset_type, model, provider, \"\n             \"language, and prompt hashes all match the baseline.\",\n         ],\n     )\n \n \n def compare_manifest_files(paths: list[str | Path]) -> Comparison:\n     manifests = []\n     for path in paths:\n         try:\n             manifests.append(read_manifest(path))\n         except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:\n             # read_manifest raises ValueError for a bad/unsupported/short manifest\n             # and OSError (e.g. FileNotFoundError) for an unreadable path.\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(f\"cannot read manifest {str(path)!r}: {exc}\") from exc\n     return compare_manifests(manifests)\n \n \n def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n     args = [arg for arg in argv[1:] if not arg.startswith(\"-\")]\n     as_json = \"--json\" in argv[1:]\n     if not args:\n         print(\"usage: compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\", file=sys.stderr)\n         return 2\n     try:\n         comparison = compare_manifest_files(args)\n     except IncomparableRunsError as exc:\n         print(f\"[compare-runs] REFUSED: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n         return 1\n \n     if as_json:\n         print(json.dumps(comparison.to_dict(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n     else:\n         print(f\"[compare-runs] baseline={comparison.baseline_run_id} runs={len(comparison.variants)}\")\n+        header = (\"runs\",) + _USAGE_METRICS + (\"duration_seconds\",)\n+        print(\"  variant        \" + \"  \".join(f\"{name:>16}\" for name in header))\n         for variant, summary in sorted(comparison.averages.items()):\n-            print(f\"  {variant}: {json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True)}\")\n+            cells = \"  \".join(f\"{_format_metric(summary.get(name)):>16}\" for name in header)\n+            print(f\"  {variant:<14} {cells}\")\n     return 0\n \n \n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n     raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",
              "additions": 17,
              "deletions": 3,
              "status": "modified"

              "file": "src/cli/run.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/cli/run.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/run.py\t\n+++ src/cli/run.py\t\n@@ -1,678 +1,681 @@\n \"\"\"Running one analysis from the CLI: build the graph, stream it into the live view, save the report.\"\"\"\n \n import os\n import re\n import sys\n import time\n import webbrowser\n from dataclasses import replace\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from functools import wraps\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import typer\n from rich.live import Live\n \n from cli.display import (\n     ANALYST_ORDER,\n     AnalystWallTimeTracker,\n     classify_message_type,\n     console,\n     create_layout,\n     display_complete_report,\n     message_buffer,\n     update_analyst_statuses,\n     update_display,\n     update_research_team_status,\n )\n from cli.selections import depth_from_env, get_user_selections, unattended_gaps\n from cli.stats_handler import StatsCallbackHandler\n from tradingagents import __version__\n from tradingagents.agents.rating import is_review, run_rating\n from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.graph.analyst_execution import (\n     build_analyst_execution_plan,\n )\n from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, build_run_id, write_manifest\n \n _VALID_VARIANTS = (\"v0\", \"v1\", \"v2\")\n \n \n def _validate_variant(value: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Accept only a known, lowercase architecture variant slug (``v0``/``v1``/``v2``).\n \n     The value becomes the first segment of the manifest ``run_id`` and a directory\n     name under the results root, so an unknown or unsafe value is rejected rather\n     than interpolated.\n     \"\"\"\n     if value not in _VALID_VARIANTS:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid variant {value!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_VALID_VARIANTS)}\"\n         )\n     return value\n \n \n \n def _run_directory(config: dict, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Where this run writes, with the ticker validated as a path component.\n \n     Every other path that interpolates a ticker checks it first; a value of\n     \"..\" here would place the run outside the results directory.\n     \"\"\"\n     return Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker_component(ticker) / trade_date\n \n \n def _manifest_config_snapshot(config: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Scalars from ``config`` that are safe to record in a run manifest.\n \n     The recorder already drops secret-pattern keys; keeping only scalar values\n     here also excludes nested objects and lists that are not comparable settings.\n+    ``results_dir`` is a machine-local output path, not a comparable setting, so it\n+    is left out of the manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     return {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in config.items()\n-        if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None\n+        if key != \"results_dir\"\n+        and (isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None)\n     }\n \n \n def write_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     config: dict,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     outcome: str | None,\n     usage: dict,\n     failure: str | None,\n     variant: str,\n     repeat: int,\n     at: datetime,\n     version: str,\n     duration_seconds: float | None = None,\n     started_at: float | None = None,\n     clock=None,\n     stop_reason: str | None = None,\n ) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write this run's manifest to ``<results_dir>/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json``.\n \n     ``stop_reason`` is read from the run's final state by the caller (C owns the\n     value domain); it is ``None`` when the graph did not reach a terminal state.\n     ``prompt_hashes`` (B) is ``{}`` and ``evidence_snapshot`` (A) is ``None`` until\n     those members' contracts land. ``duration_seconds`` is measured from\n     ``started_at`` and ``clock`` (``time.time`` by default) when not supplied;\n     passing both keeps it testable.\n     \"\"\"\n     run_id = build_run_id(variant, ticker, trade_date, repeat, at)\n     if duration_seconds is None and started_at is not None:\n         now = (clock or time.time)()\n         duration_seconds = max(0.0, now - started_at)\n \n     event = RunEvent(\n         run_id=run_id,\n         created_at=at.astimezone(UTC).isoformat(),\n         version=version,\n         ticker=ticker,\n         trade_date=trade_date,\n         asset_type=asset_type,\n         outcome=outcome,\n         config_snapshot=_manifest_config_snapshot(config),\n         prompt_hashes={},\n         evidence_snapshot=None,\n         usage=usage,\n         duration_seconds=duration_seconds,\n         failure=failure,\n         stop_reason=stop_reason,\n     )\n     runs_dir = Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"runs\"\n     run_id = _unique_run_id(runs_dir, run_id)\n     event = replace(event, run_id=run_id)\n     manifest_dir = runs_dir / run_id\n     manifest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     return write_manifest(event, manifest_dir / \"manifest.json\")\n \n \n def _unique_run_id(runs_dir: Path, run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A run_id whose directory does not exist yet, so a same-minute retry is safe.\n \n     ``build_run_id`` has minute resolution, so two runs started in the same minute\n     (or a retry) produce the same id. Appending ``-<n>`` keeps the id within the\n     recorder's 64-char pattern and never overwrites an earlier manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     pattern = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n     candidate = run_id\n     suffix = 2\n     while (runs_dir / candidate).exists():\n         candidate = f\"{run_id}-{suffix}\"\n         if not pattern.match(candidate):\n             raise ValueError(f\"no free run_id derived from {run_id!r} within 64 chars\")\n         suffix += 1\n     return candidate\n \n \n def _make_manifest_writer(config: dict, selections: dict, stats_handler, started_at=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     \"\"\"Return a ``write(failure=..., outcome=...)`` bound to this run's inputs.\n \n     ``variant`` selects the architecture under test and becomes the first segment\n     of the manifest ``run_id``; ``repeat`` is 1 and ``created_at`` is now, both\n     supplied here so the recorder never reads the clock itself. ``started_at`` is\n     the run's start (``time.time()``); forwarding it lets the manifest record a\n     real duration.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def write(*, failure, outcome, stop_reason=None):\n         return write_run_manifest(\n             config=config,\n             ticker=selections[\"ticker\"],\n             trade_date=selections[\"analysis_date\"],\n             asset_type=selections[\"asset_type\"],\n             outcome=outcome,\n             usage=stats_handler.get_stats(),\n             failure=failure,\n             variant=variant,\n             repeat=1,\n             at=datetime.now(UTC),\n             version=__version__,\n             started_at=started_at,\n             stop_reason=stop_reason,\n         )\n \n     return write\n \n \n def _finalize_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     write,\n     graph,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     portfolio,\n     final_state,\n     failure: BaseException | None,\n ) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Write the manifest, then dispose of (or keep) the checkpoint.\n \n     The manifest is written **before** the checkpoint is cleared, so a crash in\n     teardown never loses the record. A failed run still writes a manifest with\n     ``failure`` set and keeps its checkpoint for resume; the failure is re-raised.\n     ``stop_reason`` is read from ``final_state`` (C's field) with a ``None``\n     fallback when the run did not reach a terminal state.\n     \"\"\"\n     outcome = None if final_state is None else run_rating(final_state)\n     stop_reason = (final_state or {}).get(\"stop_reason\") if failure is None else None\n     write(failure=None if failure is None else str(failure), outcome=outcome, stop_reason=stop_reason)\n \n     if failure is not None:\n         raise failure\n \n     if final_state is not None:\n         graph.record_decision(ticker, trade_date, final_state)\n     graph.clear_checkpoint_on_success(ticker, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n \n \n def _announce_checkpoint_state(graph, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Say whether this run resumed a saved one, where the user can see it.\n \n     The graph logs this, but nothing in the CLI configures logging and the live\n     view owns the screen, so a resume was invisible.\n     \"\"\"\n     if getattr(graph, \"_resuming\", False):\n         message_buffer.add_message(\n             \"System\", f\"Resuming the saved run for {ticker} on {trade_date}\"\n         )\n     else:\n         message_buffer.add_message(\"System\", f\"Starting fresh for {ticker} on {trade_date}\")\n \n \n def _build_run_config(selections: dict, checkpoint: bool | None) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Assemble the run config from interactive selections, honoring env precedence.\n \n     Round counts and checkpoint follow \"explicit env/flag wins\": an env-applied\n     value on DEFAULT_CONFIG is preserved unless the user overrode it on the CLI.\n     \"\"\"\n     config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n     #
