The tool compares v1 run manifests (docs/contracts/run-event.md)\n and **refuses** when the runs are not comparable: ticker, trade_date, asset_type,\n model (quick/deep tier LLMs), provider (llm_provider + tier providers), language\n (output_language), or prompt hashes differ. It reports measured quantities only and\n never invents quality scores.\n \n No network; manifests are built via the real recorder and written with ``tmp_path``.\n \"\"\"\n \n import json\n import sys\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import pytest\n \n sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / \"scripts\"))\n \n import compare_runs  # noqa: E402\n from compare_runs import IncomparableRunsError  # noqa: E402\n \n from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, write_manifest  # noqa: E402\n \n CONFIG = {\n     \"llm_provider\": \"openai\",\n     \"quick_think_llm\": \"gpt-6-luna\",\n     \"deep_think_llm\": \"gpt-6-sol\",\n     \"output_language\": \"English\",\n }\n PROMPT_HASHES = {\"market\": \"sha256:aaa\"}\n \n USAGE = {\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 5, \"tokens_in\": 1000, \"tokens_out\": 500}\n \n \n def _event(**overrides) -> RunEvent:\n     fields = {\n         \"run_id\": \"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n         \"created_at\": \"2026-11-21T12:00:00+00:00\",\n         \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n         \"ticker\": \"NVDA\",\n         \"trade_date\": \"2026-11-20\",\n         \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n         \"outcome\": \"Buy\",\n         \"config_snapshot\": dict(CONFIG),\n         \"prompt_hashes\": dict(PROMPT_HASHES),\n         \"evidence_snapshot\": None,\n         \"usage\": dict(USAGE),\n         \"duration_seconds\": 42.5,\n         \"failure\": None,\n         \"stop_reason\": \"completed\",\n     }\n     fields.update(overrides)\n     return RunEvent(**fields)\n \n \n def _write(tmp_path, name: str, event: RunEvent) -> Path:\n     path = tmp_path / name\n     write_manifest(event, path)\n     return path\n \n \n def _manifest(**overrides) -> dict:\n     return json.loads(json.dumps(_event(**overrides).__dict__))\n \n \n # --- Guard: differing key refuses ---------------------------------------------\n \n \n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\n     \"field,value\",\n     [\n         (\"ticker\", \"AMD\"),\n         (\"trade_date\", \"2026-11-19\"),\n         (\"asset_type\", \"crypto\"),\n     ],\n )\n def test_top_level_guard_mismatch_refuses(field, value):\n     baseline = _manifest()\n     other = _manifest(**{field: value})\n     with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n         compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, other])\n     assert field in str(exc.value)\n \n \n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\n     \"key,value\",\n     [\n         (\"quick_think_llm\", \"gpt-6-other\"),\n         (\"deep_think_llm\", \"gpt-6-other\"),\n         (\"llm_provider\", \"anthropic\"),\n         (\"output_language\", \"Chinese\"),\n     ],\n )\n def test_config_guard_mismatch_refuses(key, value):\n     baseline = _manifest()\n     other_config = dict(CONFIG)\n     other_config[key] = value\n     with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n         compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, _manifest(config_snapshot=other_config)])\n     assert key in str(exc.value)\n \n \n def test_prompt_hash_mismatch_refuses():\n     baseline = _manifest()\n     other = _manifest(prompt_hashes={\"market\": \"sha256:bbb\"})\n     with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n         compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, other])\n     assert \"prompt_hashes\" in str(exc.value)\n \n \n def test_missing_model_key_refuses():\n     baseline = _manifest()\n     no_model = dict(CONFIG)\n     del no_model[\"quick_think_llm\"]\n     with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n         compare_runs.compare_manifests([baseline, _manifest(config_snapshot=no_model)])\n     assert \"quick_think_llm\" in str(exc.value)\n \n \n # --- Positive: comparable runs produce a report ------------------------------\n \n \n def test_comparable_runs_report_variants():\n     a = _manifest(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n     b = _manifest(run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n     comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([a, b])\n     assert [row[\"run_id\"] for row in comparison.variants] == [a[\"run_id\"], b[\"run_id\"]]\n \n \n def test_single_manifest_is_comparable():\n     comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([_manifest()])\n     assert len(comparison.variants) == 1\n \n \n def test_empty_input_refuses():\n     with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError):\n         compare_runs.compare_manifests([])\n \n \n def test_no_quality_score_is_invented():\n     comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([_manifest(), _manifest()])\n     measured = {\"variants\": comparison.variants, \"averages\": comparison.averages}\n     payload = json.dumps(measured).lower()\n     for banned in (\"quality\", \"score\", \"faithfulness\", \"relevance\"):\n         assert banned not in payload\n     assert any(\"no quality score\" in note for note in comparison.notes)\n \n \n # --- Averages per variant ----------------------------------------------------\n \n VARIANT_RUN_1 = _manifest(\n     run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n     usage={\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 2, \"tokens_in\": 1000, \"tokens_out\": 500},\n     duration_seconds=40.0,\n )\n VARIANT_RUN_2 = _manifest(\n     run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r2-20261121t1300\",\n     usage={\"llm_calls\": 20, \"tool_calls\": 4, \"tokens_in\": 3000, \"tokens_out\": 1500},\n     duration_seconds=60.0,\n )\n \n \n def _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n     return run_id.split(\"-\")[0]\n \n \n def test_averages_per_variant():\n     comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, VARIANT_RUN_2])\n     averages = comparison.averages\n     assert set(averages) == {\"v2\"}\n     v2 = averages[\"v2\"]\n     assert v2[\"runs\"] == 2\n     assert v2[\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(15.0)\n     assert v2[\"tool_calls\"] == pytest.approx(3.0)\n     assert v2[\"tokens_in\"] == pytest.approx(2000.0)\n     assert v2[\"tokens_out\"] == pytest.approx(1000.0)\n     assert v2[\"duration_seconds\"] == pytest.approx(50.0)\n \n \n def test_averages_group_by_variant():\n     other = _manifest(\n         run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n         usage={\"llm_calls\": 4, \"tool_calls\": 1, \"tokens_in\": 100, \"tokens_out\": 50},\n         duration_seconds=10.0,\n     )\n     comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, VARIANT_RUN_2, other])\n     assert comparison.averages[\"v2\"][\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(15.0)\n     assert comparison.averages[\"v0\"][\"llm_calls\"] == pytest.approx(4.0)\n \n \n def test_average_ignores_null_duration():\n     null_dur = _manifest(\n         run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r3-20261121t1400\",\n         duration_seconds=None,\n     )\n     v2 = compare_runs.compare_manifests([VARIANT_RUN_1, null_dur]).averages[\"v2\"]\n     assert v2[\"duration_seconds\"] == pytest.approx(40.0)\n \n \n # --- File-level + CLI --------------------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_compare_files(tmp_path):\n     first = _write(tmp_path, \"a.json\", _event(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\"))\n     second = _write(tmp_path, \"b.json\", _event(run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\"))\n     comparison = compare_runs.compare_manifest_files([first, second])\n     assert len(comparison.variants) == 2\n \n \n def test_cli_prints_comparison_and_exits_zero(tmp_path, capsys):\n     first = _write(tmp_path, \"a.json\", _event(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\"))\n     second = _write(tmp_path, \"b.json\", _event(run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\"))\n     code = compare_runs.main([\"compare_runs.py\", str(first), str(second)])\n     assert code == 0\n     out = capsys.readouterr().out\n     assert \"v0\" in out and \"v2\" in out\n \n \n def test_cli_refuses_and_exits_one(tmp_path, capsys):\n     first = _write(tmp_path, \"a.json\", _event())\n     second = _write(tmp_path, \"b.json\", _event(ticker=\"AMD\"))\n     code = compare_runs.main([\"compare_runs.py\", str(first), str(second)])\n     assert code == 1\n     assert \"ticker\" in capsys.readouterr().err\n \n \n def test_cli_usage_error_exits_two(capsys):\n     code = compare_runs.main([\"compare_runs.py\"])\n     assert code == 2\n \n \n+# --- Missing token counts are null, shown as -- ------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def _usage_missing_tokens(**overrides):\n+    event = _event(**overrides)\n+    usage = {\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 5}  # token counts absent\n+    return RunEvent(**{**event.__dict__, \"usage\": usage})\n+\n+\n+def test_missing_token_metric_is_null_not_zero():\n+    event = _usage_missing_tokens(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n+    row = compare_runs.compare_manifests([event.__dict__]).variants[0]\n+    # The reporter must not invent 0 for an unreported token count.\n+    assert row[\"tokens_in\"] is None\n+    assert row[\"tokens_out\"] is None\n+\n+\n+def test_format_metric_shows_dash_for_null():\n+    assert compare_runs._format_metric(None) == \"--\"\n+    assert compare_runs._format_metric(0) == \"0\"\n+    assert compare_runs._format_metric(1234) == \"1234\"\n+\n+\n+def test_cli_shows_dash_for_missing_tokens(tmp_path, capsys):\n+    event = _usage_missing_tokens(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n+    path = tmp_path / \"m.json\"\n+    write_manifest(event, path)\n+    code = compare_runs.main([\"compare_runs.py\", str(path)])\n+    assert code == 0\n+    out = capsys.readouterr().out\n+    assert \"--\" in out\n+\n+\n+# --- Empty prompt hashes are refused -----------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_refuse_empty_prompt_hashes():\n+    event = _event(prompt_hashes={}, run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n+    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n+        compare_runs.compare_manifests([event.__dict__])\n+    assert \"prompt_hashes\" in str(exc.value)\n+\n+\n # --- Outcome / stop_reason counts per variant --------------------------------\n \n \n def test_outcome_and_stop_reason_counts_per_variant():\n     a = _manifest(\n         run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\",\n         outcome=\"Buy\",\n         stop_reason=\"completed\",\n     )\n     b = _manifest(\n         run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r2-20261121t1300\",\n         outcome=\"Buy\",\n         stop_reason=\"budget\",\n     )\n     c = _manifest(\n         run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r3-20261121t1400\",\n         outcome=None,\n         stop_reason=\"completed\",\n     )\n     summary = compare_runs.compare_manifests([a, b, c]).averages[\"v2\"]\n     assert summary[\"outcome_counts\"] == {\"Buy\": 2, \"null\": 1}\n     assert summary[\"stop_reason_counts\"] == {\"completed\": 2, \"budget\": 1}\n \n \n def test_counts_labelled_per_variant():\n     v0 = _manifest(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\", outcome=\"Hold\")\n     v2 = _manifest(run_id=\"v2-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\", outcome=\"Buy\")\n     averages = compare_runs.compare_manifests([v0, v2]).averages\n     assert averages[\"v0\"][\"outcome_counts\"] == {\"Hold\": 1}\n     assert averages[\"v2\"][\"outcome_counts\"] == {\"Buy\": 1}\n \n \n #               "newString": "def test_cli_usage_error_exits_two(capsys):\n    code = compare_runs.main([\"compare_runs.py\"])\n    assert code == 2\n\n\n# --- Missing token counts are null, shown as -- ------------------------------\n\n\ndef _usage_missing_tokens(**overrides):\n    event = _event(**overrides)\n    usage = {\"llm_calls\": 10, \"tool_calls\": 5}  # token counts absent\n    return RunEvent(**{**event.__dict__, \"usage\": usage})\n\n\ndef test_missing_token_metric_is_null_not_zero():\n    event = _usage_missing_tokens(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n    row = compare_runs.compare_manifests([event.__dict__]).variants[0]\n    # The reporter must not invent 0 for an unreported token count.\n    assert row[\"tokens_in\"] is None\n    assert row[\"tokens_out\"] is None\n\n\ndef test_format_metric_shows_dash_for_null():\n    assert compare_runs._format_metric(None) == \"--\"\n    assert compare_runs._format_metric(0) == \"0\"\n    assert compare_runs._format_metric(1234) == \"1234\"\n\n\ndef test_cli_shows_dash_for_missing_tokens(tmp_path, capsys):\n    event = _usage_missing_tokens(run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n    path = tmp_path / \"m.json\"\n    write_manifest(event, path)\n    code = compare_runs.main([\"compare_runs.py\", str(path)])\n    assert code == 0\n    out = capsys.readouterr().out\n    assert \"--\" in out\n\n\n# --- Empty prompt hashes are refused -----------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_refuse_empty_prompt_hashes():\n    event = _event(prompt_hashes={}, run_id=\"v0-nvda-2026-11-20-r1-20261121t1200\")\n    with pytest.raises(IncomparableRunsError) as exc:\n        compare_runs.compare_manifests([event.__dict__])\n    assert \"prompt_hashes\" in str(exc.value)",

Call counters are genuinely measured, so 0 is correct there.\n+    assert stats[\"llm_calls\"] == 0\n+    assert stats[\"tool_calls\"] == 0\n+\n+\n+def test_reported_usage_yields_numbers():\n+    handler = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    handler.tokens_in = 0  # __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self.llm_calls = 0\n        self.tool_calls = 0\n        self.tokens_in = 0\n        self.tokens_out = 0\n\n    def on_llm_start(\n        self,\n        serialized: dict[str, Any],\n        prompts: list[str],\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment LLM call counter when an LLM starts.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.llm_calls += 1\n\n    def on_chat_model_start(\n        self,\n        serialized: dict[str, Any],\n        messages: list[list[Any]],\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment LLM call counter when a chat model starts.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.llm_calls += 1\n\n    def on_llm_end(self, response: LLMResult, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Extract token usage from LLM response.\"\"\"\n        try:\n            generation = response.generations[0][0]\n        except (IndexError, TypeError):\n            return\n\n        usage_metadata = None\n        if hasattr(generation, \"message\"):\n            message = generation.message\n            if isinstance(message, AIMessage) and hasattr(message, \"usage_metadata\"):\n                usage_metadata = message.usage_metadata\n\n        if usage_metadata:\n            with self._lock:\n                self.tokens_in += usage_metadata.get(\"input_tokens\", 0)\n                self.tokens_out += usage_metadata.get(\"output_tokens\", 0)\n\n    def on_tool_start(\n        self,\n        serialized: dict[str, Any],\n        input_str: str,\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment tool call counter when a tool starts.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.tool_calls += 1\n\n    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Return current statistics.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            return {\n                \"llm_calls\": self.llm_calls,\n                \"tool_calls\": self.tool_calls,\n                \"tokens_in\": self.tokens_in,\n                \"tokens_out\": self.tokens_out,\n            }",

That fixes the real runtime path (display calls the helper) and is cleanly testable.\n\nLet me write tests first: a new test file or append to `test/offline/test_c_integration_seams.py`? Better a focused file `test/offline/test_token_usage.py`.",
          "time": {

          "callID": "call_00_nCbP39gSh6UIeU3nk1R58277",
          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Offline tests for token-usage reporting: missing tokens are null, shown as --.\n\nThe runtime path (not just compare_runs) must not report 0 for an unreported token\ncount. ``StatsCallbackHandler.get_stats`` returns ``None`` for tokens when no call\never reported usage, and the live display renders ``--`` for them without crashing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.display import _format_token_line\nfrom cli.stats_handler import StatsCallbackHandler\n\n# --- stats handler: missing tokens are null ----------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_no_usage_reported_tokens_are_none():\n    stats = StatsCallbackHandler().get_stats()\n    assert stats[\"tokens_in\"] is None\n    assert stats[\"tokens_out\"] is None\n    # Call counters are genuinely measured, so 0 is correct there.\n    assert stats[\"llm_calls\"] == 0\n    assert stats[\"tool_calls\"] == 0\n\n\ndef test_reported_usage_yields_numbers():\n    handler = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    handler.tokens_in = 0  # simulate a call that reported zero\n    handler._usage_reported = True\n    stats = handler.get_stats()\n    assert stats[\"tokens_in\"] == 0\n    assert stats[\"tokens_out\"] == 0\n\n\ndef test_partial_usage_accumulates():\n    handler = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    handler._usage_reported = True\n    handler.tokens_in = 1234\n    handler.tokens_out = 56\n    stats = handler.get_stats()\n    assert stats[\"tokens_in\"] == 1234\n    assert stats[\"tokens_out\"] == 56\n\n\n# --- display: -- for null, no crash ------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_token_line_dash_when_none():\n    line = _format_token_line({\"tokens_in\": None, \"tokens_out\": None})\n    assert line == \"Tokens: --\"\n\n\ndef test_token_line_dash_when_zero_and_unreported_semantics():\n    # Explicit zeros still format as a real (zero) count; only None is unknown.\n    line = _format_token_line({\"tokens_in\": 0, \"tokens_out\": 0})\n    assert line == \"Tokens: 0\\u2191 0\\u2193\"\n\n\ndef test_token_line_formats_numbers():\n    line = _format_token_line({\"tokens_in\": 2000, \"tokens_out\": 500})\n    assert line == \"Tokens: 2.0k\\u2191 500\\u2193\"\n\n\ndef test_token_line_single_none_side_is_dash():\n    # If one side is unknown, do not fabricate a number for it.\n    line = _format_token_line({\"tokens_in\": None, \"tokens_out\": 500})\n    assert line == \"Tokens: --\"\n",

              "newString": "def format_tokens(n):\n    \"\"\"Format token count for display.\"\"\"\n    if n >= 1000:\n        return f\"{n/1000:.1f}k\"\n    return str(n)\n\n\ndef _format_token_line(stats):\n    \"\"\"The token line for the live display, ``Tokens: --`` when unknown.\n\n    A ``None`` token count means usage was never reported; it is shown as ``--``\n    rather than a fabricated zero, and never compared with ``>``.\n    \"\"\"\n    tokens_in = stats.get(\"tokens_in\")\n    tokens_out = stats.get(\"tokens_out\")\n    if tokens_in is None or tokens_out is None:\n        return \"Tokens: --\"\n    return f\"Tokens: {format_tokens(tokens_in)}\\u2191 {format_tokens(tokens_out)}\\u2193\"",

A late callback only updates\n+the global record; it never writes back into a handle that has already closed.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n import threading\n+from contextlib import contextmanager\n+from contextvars import ContextVar\n+from dataclasses import dataclass\n from typing import Any\n \n from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\n from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n from langchain_core.outputs import LLMResult\n \n+# Statuses that make a settled window unknown (any one -> None for the window).\n+_UNKNOWN_STATUSES = frozenset({\"partial\", \"invalid\", \"missing\", \"failed\"})\n \n+# The collector for the innermost active ``track`` in the current context, if any.\n+_active_collector: ContextVar[list[str] | None] = ContextVar(\n+    \"stats_active_collector\", default=None\n+)\n+\n+\n+@dataclass(frozen=True)\n+class CallUsage:\n+    \"\"\"One LLM call's usage, keyed by the LangChain ``run_id``.\"\"\"\n+\n+    call_id: str\n+    node: str | None\n+    status: str  # reported | explicit_zero | partial | invalid | missing | failed\n+    source: str  # usage_metadata | token_usage | none\n+    input_tokens: int | None\n+    output_tokens: int | None\n+    total_tokens: int | None  # E local input+output; None:\n+        run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n+        if run_id is None:\n+            return\n+        call_id = str(run_id)\n+        metadata = kwargs.get(\"metadata\") or {}\n+        node = _as_int(data.get(\"output_tokens\", data.get(\"completion_tokens\")))\n+        if input_tokens is None and output_tokens is None:\n+            status = \"invalid\"\n+        elif input_tokens is      return tuple(self._calls.values())\n \n+    def call(self, call_id: str) -> CallUsage | None:\n+        with self._lock:\n+            return self._calls.get(call_id)\n+\n+    @contextmanager\n+    def track(self, stage: str):\n+        \"\"\"Collect the call ids seen while this stage is active (context-isolated).\"\"\"\n+        handle = TrackHandle(stage)\n+        token =               "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_stats_calls.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_stats_calls.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_stats_calls.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,253 @@\n+\"\"\"Offline tests for E2 per-call usage (docs/handoffs/E-interfaces-v1.md §E2).\n+\n+Covers the frozen interface: ``CallUsage``, ``calls()``, ``call(id)``, ``track(stage)``\n+with ContextVar isolation. Required cases: concurrency, late callbacks,\n+missing / failed / explicit-zero, and one invoke producing two starts counted as two\n+callbacks (llm_calls == 2). Also pins the settlement rule: a window whose calls are\n+all ``reported``/``explicit_zero`` sums once; any ``partial/invalid/missing/failed``\n+makes the window ``None``.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import threading\n+import uuid\n+\n+from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n+from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, LLMResult\n+\n+from cli.stats_handler import CallUsage, StatsCallbackHandler\n+\n+\n+def _result(input_tokens=None, output_tokens=None) -> LLMResult:\n+    meta = None\n+    if input_tokens is not None or output_tokens is not None:\n+        total = (input_tokens or 0) + (output_tokens or 0)\n+        meta = {\"input_tokens\": input_tokens, \"output_tokens\": output_tokens, \"total_tokens\": total}\n+    msg = AIMessage(content=\"ok\", usage_metadata=meta)\n+    return LLMResult(generations=[[ChatGeneration(message=msg)]])\n+\n+\n+def _result_token_usage(**token_usage) -> LLMResult:\n+    msg = AIMessage(content=\"ok\", response_metadata={\"token_usage\": token_usage})\n+    return LLMResult(generations=[[ChatGeneration(message=msg)]])\n+\n+\n+def _rid() -> uuid.UUID:\n+    return uuid.uuid4()\n+\n+\n+def _start(handler, rid, node=None):\n+    meta = {\"langgraph_node\": node} if node else None\n+    handler.on_chat_model_start({}, [[]], run_id=rid, metadata=meta)\n+\n+\n+def _end(handler, rid, input_tokens=None, output_tokens=None):\n+    handler.on_llm_end(_result(input_tokens, output_tokens), run_id=rid)\n+\n+\n+# --- shape of CallUsage ------------------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_calls_returns_callusage_tuple():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid = _rid()\n+    _start(h, rid, node=\"market_analyst\")\n+    _end(h, rid, 10, 5)\n+    calls = h.calls()\n+    assert isinstance(calls, tuple)\n+    cu = calls[0]\n+    assert isinstance(cu, CallUsage)\n+    assert cu.call_id == str(rid)\n+    assert cu.node == \"market_analyst\"\n+    assert cu.status == \"reported\"\n+    assert cu.source == \"usage_metadata\"\n+    assert cu.input_tokens == 10\n+    assert cu.output_tokens == 5\n+    assert cu.total_tokens == 15  # E local input+output, not provider total\n+\n+\n+def test_call_lookup_by_id():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid = _rid()\n+    _start(h, rid)\n+    _end(h, rid, 1, 1)\n+    assert h.call(str(rid)).status == \"reported\"\n+    assert h.call(\"does-not-exist\") is None\n+\n+\n+# --- explicit zero / missing / partial / invalid / failed --------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_explicit_zero_is_reported_not_missing():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid = _rid()\n+    _start(h, rid)\n+    _end(h, rid, 0, 0)\n+    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n+    assert cu.status == \"explicit_zero\"\n+    assert cu.input_tokens == 0 and cu.output_tokens == 0\n+    assert cu.total_tokens == 0\n+\n+\n+def test_missing_when_no_usage_metadata():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid = _rid()\n+    _start(h, rid)\n+    _end(h, rid)  # no usage_metadata\n+    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n+    assert cu.status == \"missing\"\n+    assert cu.source == \"none\"\n+    assert cu.input_tokens is None and cu.output_tokens is None\n+\n+\n+def test_partial_when_one_token_missing():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid = _rid()\n+    _start(h, rid)\n+    # A provider reporting only prompt tokens: partial, source token_usage.\n+    h.on_llm_end(_result_token_usage(prompt_tokens=10), run_id=rid)\n+    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n+    assert cu.status == \"partial\"\n+    assert cu.source == \"token_usage\"\n+\n+\n+def test_failed_on_error():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid = _rid()\n+    _start(h, rid)\n+    h.on_llm_error(RuntimeError(\"boom\"), run_id=rid)\n+    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n+    assert cu.status == \"failed\"\n+    assert cu.input_tokens is None and cu.output_tokens is None\n+\n+\n+# --- one invoke, two starts -> two callbacks --------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_two_starts_are_two_calls_and_two_llm_calls():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid_a, rid_b = _rid(), _rid()\n+    # One invoke emitting two start callbacks (e.g. retry inside the SDK wrapper).\n+    _start(h, rid_a)\n+    _start(h, rid_b)\n+    assert len(h.calls()) == 2\n+    assert h.get_stats()[\"llm_calls\"] == 2  # callback events, not retries collapsed\n+\n+\n+# --- late callbacks ---------------------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_late_end_after_freeze_does_not_rewrite_handle():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    rid = _rid()\n+    with == frozen  # not rewritten\n+    assert h.call(str(rid)).status == \"reported\"  # global record did update\n+\n+\n+def test_end_without_start_is_recorded_globally():\n+    h =    results[name] = (str(rid), handle.call_ids)\n+\n+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(f\"t{i}\",)) for i in range(6)]\n+    for t in threads:\n+        t.start()\n+    for t in threads:\n+        t.join()\n+\n+    for name, (rid, ids) in results.items():\n+        assert ids == (rid,), f\"{name} leaked another thread's call id\"\n+\n+\n+def test_nested_tracks_isolated():\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    outer_rid, inner_rid = _rid(), _rid()\n+    with h.track(\"outer\") as outer:\n+        _start(h, outer_rid)\n+        with h.track(\"inner\") as inner:\n+            _start(h, inner_rid)\n+        assert outer.call_ids == (str(outer_rid),)\n+        assert inner.call_ids == (str(inner_rid),)\n+\n+\n+# --- settlement via get_stats()                 "text": "import threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\nfrom langchain_core.outputs import LLMResult\n\n\nclass StatsCallbackHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n    \"\"\"Callback handler that tracks LLM calls, tool calls, and token usage.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self.llm_calls = 0\n        self.tool_calls = 0\n        self.tokens_in = 0\n        self.tokens_out = 0\n        # True once any call reports usage. Until then token counts are unknown,\n        # not measured zero: get_stats() reports them as None.\n        self._usage_reported = False\n\n    def on_llm_start(\n        self,\n        serialized: self.llm_calls += 1\n\n    def on_chat_model_start(\n        self,\n        serialized: dict[str, Any],\n        messages: list[list[Any]],\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment LLM call counter when a chat model starts.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.llm_calls += 1\n\n    def on_llm_end(self, response: LLMResult, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Extract token usage from LLM response.\"\"\"\n        try:\n            generation = response.generations[0][0]\n        except (IndexError, TypeError):\n            return\n\n        usage_metadata = None\n        if hasattr(generation, \"message\"):\n            message = generation.message\n            if isinstance(message, AIMessage) and hasattr(message, \"usage_metadata\"):\n    input_str: str,\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment tool call counter when a tool starts.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.tool_calls += 1\n\n    def           "type": "text",
          "text": "Now I understand the data model. Design:\n\n- On start (`on_llm_start`/`on_chat_model_start`): record a pending call keyed by `run_id` with `node` from `metadata[\"langgraph_node\"]`; increment `llm_calls`. A second start with the same id would be a distinct event; but one invoke producing two starts = two callbacks → two calls (spec: \"one invoke with two starts → 2\"). Different run_ids → distinct CallUsage entries.\n- On end (`on_llm_end`): update the call's status/source/tokens. If usage_metadata present: `reported` (both tokens known) or `partial` (one missing). If no metadata: `missing`. If usage is `{0,0}` explicitly → `explicit_zero`. Invalid (negative/non-int) → `invalid`.\n- `on_llm_error`: → `failed`.\n- Late callback (end without a recorded start, or for an already-finalized id): only update global record; don't touch frozen handles.\n- `calls()` returns finalized + pending as tuple.\n- `call(call_id)` returns the CallUsage or None.\n- `track(stage)` returns `TrackHandle` with `.call_ids`; uses a ContextVar to associate callbacks in this async/thread context with a stage. `call_ids` snapshot the ids seen while the stage was active (frozen at handle creation via context, per \"do not write back to an already-frozen handle\").\n\nThe `ContextVar` isolation: \"ContextVar isolation for concurrency\" — each `track(stage)` sets a ContextVar holding a collector; callbacks record the run_id into the current context's active stage collector. Since callbacks fire in the same context (LangChain callbacks run in the caller's context for sync), calls during a `track` block get associated. Test: two concurrent tracks (threads) each see only their own call_ids.\n\nLet me look at how E2 expects track: `track(stage) -> TrackHandle # .call_ids, ContextVar isolates concurrency`. So `track` is a context manager likely. Let me design `track` as a context manager that yields a handle with `.call_ids`. On exit, freeze `.call_ids` (a tuple). ContextVar isolates concurrent tracks.\n\nLet me check default `_usage_reported` interaction: I'll refactor token aggregation to be derived from `calls()` settlement rules rather than manual counters. Settlement: window (all calls) → if all reported/explicit_zero, sum; any partial/invalid/missing/failed → None. But `get_stats()` should keep existing semantics. Let me keep `get_stats()` aggregating via `calls()`.\n\nBut careful: existing tests expect `get_stats()` after setting `handler.tokens_in`/`_usage_reported` directly (test_token_usage.py). Those set attributes directly, not via calls. If I make `get_stats` derive from `calls()`, those tests break. Let me re-read those tests to decide compatibility.\n\nThe test `test_reported_usage_yields_numbers` sets `handler.tokens_in=0; handler._usage_reported=True` then asserts `get_stats` tokens 0. And `test_partial_usage_accumulates` sets `tokens_in=1234; tokens_out=56`. If I derive from calls, these would break. But the task says \"Implement E2 ... aggregation entry still get_stats()\". I should preserve the manual-attribute behavior for backward compat, OR update those tests. The instruction: \"Test first: concurrency, late callbacks, missing/failed/explicit-zero, and one invoke producing two starts counted as two callbacks.\" It doesn't say preserve the old direct-attribute tests, but I shouldn't break passing tests unnecessarily. \n\nI'll make `get_stats()` aggregate from `calls()` when calls exist, falling back to the manual counters (`_usage_reported`/`tokens_in`/`tokens_out`) when no calls were recorded. That preserves both. Actually cleaner: keep `llm_calls`/`tool_calls` counters as-is, and compute tokens: if `self._calls` is non-empty → settle from calls; else → legacy behavior. This keeps existing tests green and adds E2.\n\nLet me check existing tests referencing stats internals more broadly.",

          "text": "Note: `AIMessage` always has `usage_metadata` attribute (None when unset). So \"missing\" = `usage_metadata is None`. Now write the tests.",
          "time": {

            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Offline tests for E2 per-call usage (docs/handoffs/E-interfaces-v1.md §E2).\n\nCovers the frozen interface: ``CallUsage``, ``calls()``, ``call(id)``, ``track(stage)``\nwith ContextVar isolation. Required cases: concurrency, late callbacks,\nmissing / failed / explicit-zero, and one invoke producing two starts counted as two\ncallbacks (llm_calls == 2). Also pins the settlement rule: a window whose calls are\nall ``reported``/``explicit_zero`` sums once; any ``partial/invalid/missing/failed``\nmakes the window ``None``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport threading\nimport uuid\n\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\nfrom langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, LLMResult\n\nfrom cli.stats_handler import CallUsage, StatsCallbackHandler\n\n\ndef _result(input_tokens=None, output_tokens=None) -> LLMResult:\n    meta = None\n    if input_tokens is not None or output_tokens is not None:\n        meta = {\"input_tokens\": input_tokens, \"output_tokens\": output_tokens}\n        meta = {k: v for k, v in meta.items() if v is not None}\n    msg = AIMessage(content=\"ok\", usage_metadata=meta)\n    return LLMResult(generations=[[ChatGeneration(message=msg)]])\n\n\ndef _rid() -> uuid.UUID:\n    return uuid.uuid4()\n\n\ndef _start(handler, rid, node=None):\n    meta = {\"langgraph_node\": node} if node else None\n    handler.on_chat_model_start({}, [[]], run_id=rid, metadata=meta)\n\n\ndef _end(handler, rid, input_tokens=None, output_tokens=None):\n    handler.on_llm_end(_result(input_tokens, output_tokens), run_id=rid)\n\n\n# --- shape of CallUsage ------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_calls_returns_callusage_tuple():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _start(h, rid, node=\"market_analyst\")\n    _end(h, rid, 10, 5)\n    calls = h.calls()\n    assert isinstance(calls, tuple)\n    cu = calls[0]\n    assert isinstance(cu, CallUsage)\n    assert cu.call_id == str(rid)\n    assert cu.node == \"market_analyst\"\n    assert cu.status == \"reported\"\n    assert cu.source == \"usage_metadata\"\n    assert cu.input_tokens == 10\n    assert cu.output_tokens == 5\n    assert cu.total_tokens == 15  # E local input+output, not provider total\n\n\ndef test_call_lookup_by_id():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _start(h, rid)\n    _end(h, rid, 1, 1)\n    assert h.call(str(rid)).status == \"reported\"\n    assert h.call(\"does-not-exist\") is None\n\n\n# --- explicit zero / missing / partial / invalid / failed --------------------\n\n\ndef test_explicit_zero_is_reported_not_missing():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _start(h, rid)\n    _end(h, rid, 0, 0)\n    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n    assert cu.status == \"explicit_zero\"\n    assert cu.input_tokens == 0 and cu.output_tokens == 0\n    assert cu.total_tokens == 0\n\n\ndef test_missing_when_no_usage_metadata():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _start(h, rid)\n    _end(h, rid)  # no usage_metadata\n    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n    assert cu.status == \"missing\"\n    assert cu.source == \"none\"\n    assert cu.input_tokens is None and cu.output_tokens is None\n\n\ndef test_partial_when_one_token_missing():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _start(h, rid)\n    _end(h, rid, 10, None)\n    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n    assert cu.status == \"partial\"\n\n\ndef test_failed_on_error():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _start(h, rid)\n    h.on_llm_error(RuntimeError(\"boom\"), run_id=rid)\n    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n    assert cu.status == \"failed\"\n    assert cu.input_tokens is None and cu.output_tokens is None\n\n\n# --- one invoke, two starts -> two callbacks --------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_two_starts_are_two_calls_and_two_llm_calls():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid_a, rid_b = _rid(), _rid()\n    # One invoke emitting two start callbacks (e.g. retry inside the SDK wrapper).\n    _start(h, rid_a)\n    _start(h, rid_b)\n    assert len(h.calls()) == 2\n    assert h.get_stats()[\"llm_calls\"] == 2  # callback events, not retries collapsed\n\n\n# --- late callbacks ---------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_late_end_after_freeze_does_not_rewrite_handle():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    with h.track(\"market\") as handle:\n        _start(h, rid)\n    frozen = handle.call_ids\n    # A late end arrives after the stage window closed.\n    _end(h, rid, 99, 1)\n    assert handle.call_ids == frozen  # not rewritten\n    assert h.call(str(rid)).status == \"reported\"  # global record did update\n\n\ndef test_end_without_start_is_recorded_globally():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _end(h, rid, 4, 2)  # no start seen\n    cu = h.call(str(rid))\n    assert cu is not None\n    assert cu.status == \"reported\"\n\n\n# --- track(stage) + ContextVar isolation ------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_track_collects_call_ids_in_context():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    with h.track(\"news\") as handle:\n        _start(h, rid)\n        _end(h, rid, 1, 1)\n    assert str(rid) in handle.call_ids\n\n\ndef test_track_is_isolated_across_threads():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    results = {}\n\n    def worker(name):\n        rid = _rid()\n        with h.track(name) as handle:\n            _start(h, rid)\n            _end(h, rid, 1, 1)\n        results[name] = (str(rid), handle.call_ids)\n\n    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(f\"t{i}\",)) for i in range(6)]\n    for t in threads:\n        t.start()\n    for t in threads:\n        t.join()\n\n    for name, (rid, ids) in results.items():\n        assert ids == (rid,), f\"{name} leaked another thread's call id\"\n\n\ndef test_nested_tracks_isolated():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    outer_rid, inner_rid = _rid(), _rid()\n    with h.track(\"outer\") as outer:\n        _start(h, outer_rid)\n        with h.track(\"inner\") as inner:\n            _start(h, inner_rid)\n        assert outer.call_ids == (str(outer_rid),)\n        assert inner.call_ids == (str(inner_rid),)\n\n\n# --- settlement via get_stats() ---------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_get_stats_sums_all_reported_window():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    for inp, out in ((10, 5), (20, 10)):\n        rid = _rid()\n        _start(h, rid)\n        _end(h, rid, inp, out)\n    stats = h.get_stats()\n    assert stats[\"tokens_in\"] == 30\n    assert stats[\"tokens_out\"] == 15\n\n\ndef test_get_stats_sums_explicit_zero_with_reported():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    for inp, out in ((0, 0), (10, 5)):\n        rid = _rid()\n        _start(h, rid)\n        _end(h, rid, inp, out)\n    assert h.get_stats()[\"tokens_in\"] == 10\n\n\ndef test_get_stats_none_when_any_missing():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    a, b = _rid(), _rid()\n    _start(h, a)\n    _end(h, a, 10, 5)\n    _start(h, b)\n    _end(h, b)  # missing\n    assert h.get_stats()[\"tokens_in\"] is None\n    assert h.get_stats()[\"tokens_out\"] is None\n\n\ndef test_get_stats_none_when_any_failed():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    a = _rid()\n    _start(h, a)\n    h.on_llm_error(RuntimeError(\"x\"), run_id=a)\n    assert h.get_stats()[\"tokens_in\"] is None\n\n\ndef test_total_tokens_is_local_sum():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    rid = _rid()\n    _start(h, rid)\n    _end(h, rid, 7, 3)\n    assert h.call(str(rid)).total_tokens == 10\n",

        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "Now implement E2 in `stats_handler.py`. Design:\n\n- `CallUsage` frozen dataclass with the 8 fields.\n- `_calls: dict[str, CallUsage]` (ordered) keyed by call_id, holding current state.\n- On start: create a CallUsage with `status=\"missing\", source=\"none\", input=None, output=None` placeholder (pending), record it; increment `llm_calls`. If id already exists (re-start), overwrite — but per \"two starts → two callbacks\", distinct run_ids so distinct entries; re-start same id is unusual, overwrite is fine.\n- On end: compute status/source/tokens; update entry (create if absent — late/without start).\n- On error: status `failed`.\n- ContextVar `_active_stage` holds a list (collector) of call_ids; start/end append id if a stage active. Actually `track` should capture ids of calls that happen while active. Append on start (each call counted once) to the current collector.\n- `track(stage)` is a context manager yielding `TrackHandle(stage)`. `.call_ids` returns tuple frozen at exit; while active returns current snapshot. The test expects `handle.call_ids == (outer_rid,)` while inner is active (i.e., outer's ids so far), and after exit equal frozen. Use a mutable internal list; property returns tuple of it. \"not rewritten after freeze\": after exit, stop appending — so handle unfreezes? Simplest: keep the list; after exit set a frozen flag so further appends ignored. But appends go to the ContextVar collector which is this handle's list. On exit, we pop the ContextVar; subsequent callbacks won't find it (unless another active). So it's naturally frozen once popped. Good — but nested: `track` must restore previous ContextVar token.\n\nLet me implement. For settle in `get_stats`: if `self._calls` non-empty → aggregate tokens from calls; any status in {partial,invalid,missing,failed} → None; else sum input/output (reported/explicit_zero). Else legacy counters.\n\nBut there's a subtlety: pending calls (started, no end yet) have status \"missing\" placeholder → would make aggregate None. During a live run that's correct (incomplete). Fine.\n\nLet me write the module.",
          "time": {
            "start": 1795344070046,
            "end": 1795344086177
          },
          "id": "prt_202d8759e001MEhAwQNgColl2B",
          "sessionID": "ses_dfec1774affe0xtUSQhK6HTmb8",

          "callID": "call_00_cdlkt8D7P7vQlIvf6Szs3124",
          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Callback handler tracking LLM/tool calls and per-call token usage (E2).\n\nPer-call usage follows ``docs/handoffs/E-interfaces-v1.md`` §E2: every LLM call is a\n``CallUsage`` keyed by its LangChain ``run_id``. The aggregate entry stays\n``get_stats()``; ``llm_calls`` counts start-callback events (one invoke emitting two\nstarts counts as two), not SDK retries.\n\nSettlement rule for a window of calls: if every call is ``reported`` or\n``explicit_zero`` the tokens sum once; if any call is ``partial``/``invalid``/\n``missing``/``failed`` the window is ``None`` (unknown), never a fabricated number.\n\n``track(stage)`` scopes the call ids seen while it is active using a ``ContextVar``,\nso concurrent threads/tasks do not see each other's ids. A late callback only updates\nthe global record; it never writes back into a handle that has already closed.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport threading\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom contextvars import ContextVar\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, replace\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\nfrom langchain_core.outputs import LLMResult\n\n# Statuses that make a settled window unknown (any one -> None for the window).\n_UNKNOWN_STATUSES = frozenset({\"partial\", \"invalid\", \"missing\", \"failed\"})\n\n# The collector for the innermost active ``track`` in the current context, if any.\n_active_collector: ContextVar[list[str] | None] = ContextVar(\n    \"stats_active_collector\", default=None\n)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass CallUsage:\n    \"\"\"One LLM call's usage, keyed by the LangChain ``run_id``.\"\"\"\n\n    call_id: str\n    node: str | None\n    status: str  # reported | explicit_zero | partial | invalid | missing | failed\n    source: str  # usage_metadata | token_usage | none\n    input_tokens: int | None\n    output_tokens: int | None\n    total_tokens: int | None  # E local input+output; provider ``total`` not trusted\n\n\nclass TrackHandle:\n    \"\"\"The result of ``track(stage)``: the call ids seen while the stage was active.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, stage: str) -> None:\n        self.stage = stage\n        self._ids: list[str] = []\n\n    def _record(self, call_id: str) -> None:\n        if call_id not in self._ids:\n            self._ids.append(call_id)\n\n    @property\n    def call_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        return tuple(self._ids)\n\n\ndef _as_int(value: Any) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"A non-negative int from ``value``, or ``None`` when it is not a valid count.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return None\n    if isinstance(value, int) and value >= 0:\n        return value\n    return None\n\n\nclass StatsCallbackHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n    \"\"\"Track LLM calls, tool calls, and per-call token usage.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self.llm_calls = 0\n        self.tool_calls = 0\n        # Legacy manual counters (kept for callers that set them directly, e.g. tests).\n        self.tokens_in = 0\n        self.tokens_out = 0\n        self._usage_reported = False\n        # Per-call records, insertion-ordered by first observation.\n        self._calls: dict[str, CallUsage] = {}\n\n    # --- callbacks ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def on_llm_start(self, serialized, prompts, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        self._on_start(kwargs)\n\n    def on_chat_model_start(self, serialized, messages, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        self._on_start(kwargs)\n\n    def _on_start(self, kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n        run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n        if run_id is None:\n            return\n        call_id = str(run_id)\n        metadata = kwargs.get(\"metadata\") or {}\n        node = metadata.get(\"langgraph_node\")\n        with self._lock:\n            self.llm_calls += 1\n            # A start without a completed end is \"missing\" until an end arrives.\n            self._calls[call_id] = CallUsage(\n                call_id=call_id,\n                node=node,\n                status=\"missing\",\n                source=\"none\",\n                input_tokens=None,\n                output_tokens=None,\n                total_tokens=None,\n            )\n        self._collect(call_id)\n\n    def on_llm_end(self, response: LLMResult, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n        if run_id is None:\n            return\n        call_id = str(run_id)\n        usage = self._extract_usage(response)\n        with self._lock:\n            node = self._calls[call_id].node if call_id in self._calls else None\n            self._calls[call_id] = self._settle(call_id, node, usage)\n        self._collect(call_id)\n\n    def on_llm_error(self, error: BaseException, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n        if run_id is None:\n            return\n        call_id = str(run_id)\n        with self._lock:\n            node = self._calls[call_id].node if call_id in self._calls else None\n            self._calls[call_id] = CallUsage(\n                call_id=call_id,\n                node=node,\n                status=\"failed\",\n                source=\"none\",\n                input_tokens=None,\n                output_tokens=None,\n                total_tokens=None,\n            )\n        self._collect(call_id)\n\n    def on_tool_start(self, serialized, input_str, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self.tool_calls += 1\n\n    # --- usage extraction / settlement -------------------------------------\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _extract_usage(response: LLMResult) -> tuple[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Return ``(source, usage_dict)`` from a response; ``(\"none\", None)`` if absent.\"\"\"\n        try:\n            generation = response.generations[0][0]\n        except (IndexError, TypeError):\n            return \"none\", None\n        message = getattr(generation, \"message\", None)\n        if not isinstance(message, AIMessage):\n            return \"none\", None\n        usage_metadata = getattr(message, \"usage_metadata\", None)\n        if usage_metadata:\n            return \"usage_metadata\", usage_metadata\n        token_usage = getattr(message, \"response_metadata\", {}).get(\"token_usage\")\n        if token_usage:\n            return \"token_usage\", token_usage\n        return \"none\", None\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _settle(call_id: str, node: str | None, usage: tuple[str, Any]) -> CallUsage:\n        source, data = usage\n        if data is None:\n            return CallUsage(call_id, node, \"missing\", \"none\", None, None, None)\n        input_tokens = _as_int(data.get(\"input_tokens\", data.get(\"prompt_tokens\")))\n        output_tokens = _as_int(data.get(\"output_tokens\", data.get(\"completion_tokens\")))\n        if input_tokens is None and output_tokens is None:\n            status = \"invalid\"\n        elif input_tokens is None or output_tokens is None:\n            status = \"partial\"\n        elif input_tokens == 0 and output_tokens == 0:\n            status = \"explicit_zero\"\n        else:\n            status = \"reported\"\n        total = (\n            input_tokens + output_tokens\n            if input_tokens is not None and output_tokens is not None\n            else None\n        )\n        return CallUsage(\n            call_id, node, status, source, input_tokens, output_tokens, total\n        )\n\n    # --- query --------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def calls(self) -> tuple[CallUsage, ...]:\n        with self._lock:\n            return tuple(self._calls.values())\n\n    def call(self, call_id: str) -> CallUsage | None:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self._calls.get(call_id)\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def track(self, stage: str):\n        \"\"\"Collect the call ids seen while this stage is active (context-isolated).\"\"\"\n        handle = TrackHandle(stage)\n        token = _active_collector.set(handle._ids)\n        try:\n            yield handle\n        finally:\n            _active_collector.reset(token)\n\n    def _collect(self, call_id: str) -> None:\n        collector = _active_collector.get()\n        if collector is not None:\n            collector.append(call_id) if call_id not in collector else None\n\n    # --- aggregate ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Aggregate stats; token counts are null when unknown.\n\n        When at least one call has been observed, tokens settle over the recorded\n        calls: none are invented for a window containing a partial/invalid/missing/\n        failed call. With no recorded calls, the legacy manual counters apply (still\n        ``None`` until usage was reported).\n        \"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            if self._calls:\n                return self._settle_window()\n            return {\n                \"llm_calls\": self.llm_calls,\n                \"tool_calls\": self.tool_calls,\n                \"tokens_in\": self.tokens_in if self._usage_reported else None,\n                \"tokens_out\": self.tokens_out if self._usage_reported else None,\n            }\n\n    def _settle_window(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        calls = list(self._calls.values())\n        if any(call.status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES for call in calls):\n            tokens_in = tokens_out = None\n        else:\n            tokens_in = sum(call.input_tokens for call in calls)\n            tokens_out = sum(call.output_tokens for call in calls)\n        return {\n            \"llm_calls\": self.llm_calls,\n            \"tool_calls\": self.tool_calls,\n            \"tokens_in\": tokens_in,\n            \"tokens_out\": tokens_out,\n        }\n",
              "filePath": "/Users/erkangxue/CScourse/5351小组作业/TradingAgents-Coursework/src/cli/stats_handler.py"

              "patch": "Index: scripts/compare_runs.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n+++ scripts/compare_runs.py\t\n@@ -1,249 +1,286 @@\n \"\"\"Compare run manifests across architecture variants (E-owned; D4 / §6.5).\n \n Reads v1 run manifests (``docs/contracts/run-event.md``) produced by\n ``run_recorder`` and reports measured quantities per variant. It **refuses** to\n compare runs that are not comparable: ``ticker``, ``trade_date``, ``asset_type``,\n the model (quick/deep tier LLMs), the provider (``llm_provider`` and any tier\n code/endpoint selectors), the output ``language``, and ``prompt_hashes`` must all\n match the baseline. When any of them differs the comparison raises\n ``IncomparableRunsError`` rather than presenting a misleading table.\n \n This tool never invents quality scores. It reports only what the manifest records\n (outcome, usage, duration, failure, stop reason) and per-variant averages of the\n numeric fields. Semantic/quality thresholds are owned by B/D and are out of scope\n here (see ``docs/evaluation/protocol.md``).\n \n Usage:\n     python scripts/compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\n \n Exit 0 when the runs are comparable, 1 (with a reason on stderr) when they are\n refused, 2 on a usage error. Stdlib + ``run_recorder`` only.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import json\n import sys\n from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n from pathlib import Path\n \n from tradingagents.run_recorder import read_manifest\n \n _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD = (\"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n _MODEL_KEYS = (\"quick_think_llm\", \"deep_think_llm\")\n _PROVIDER_KEYS = (\"llm_provider\", \"quick_think_provider\", \"deep_think_provider\")\n _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS = _MODEL_KEYS + (\"llm_provider\",)\n _LANGUAGE_KEY = \"output_language\"\n _USAGE_METRICS = (\"llm_calls\", \"tool_calls\", \"tokens_in\", \"tokens_out\")\n \n \n class IncomparableRunsError(ValueError):\n     \"\"\"The supplied manifests cannot be compared (a guard key differs).\"\"\"\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class Comparison:\n     \"\"\"Comparable-run report. ``variants`` is per-run; ``averages`` is per-variant.\"\"\"\n \n     baseline_run_id: str\n     guard: dict\n     variants: list[dict]\n     averages: dict\n     notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n \n     def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n         return {\n             \"baseline_run_id\": self.baseline_run_id,\n             \"guard\": self.guard,\n             \"variants\": self.variants,\n             \"averages\": self.averages,\n             \"notes\": self.notes,\n         }\n \n \n def _guard_of(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Extract the keys that must match for a comparison to be valid.\n \n     ``llm_provider``, the tier models, and ``output_language`` are required; a\n     missing required key is refused rather than guessed, so a malformed snapshot\n     cannot silently look comparable. The optional per-tier provider selectors are\n     collected when present; ``_provider_keys`` unions them across every manifest so\n     a tier provider set in *any* run is compared everywhere (a manifest that omits\n     it compares as ``None``, the config default).\n     \"\"\"\n     config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n     guard = {key: manifest.get(key) for key in _TOP_LEVEL_GUARD}\n     required = _REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS + (_LANGUAGE_KEY,)\n     for key in required:\n         if key not in config:\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} is missing config key {key!r}; \"\n                 \"cannot compare without it\"\n             )\n         guard[key] = config[key]\n     for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS:\n         if key in config:\n             guard[key] = config[key]\n     prompt_hashes = manifest.get(\"prompt_hashes\")\n     if not prompt_hashes:\n         # An empty/None prompt fingerprint leaves the comparison unfounded: two runs\n         # cannot be shown to use the same prompts without a real hash (C-to-E\n         # variant response: keep the real hashes). Refuse rather than guess.\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\n             f\"manifest {manifest.get('run_id')!r} has empty prompt_hashes; \"\n             \"cannot compare without prompt fingerprints\"\n         )\n     guard[\"prompt_hashes\"] = prompt_hashes\n     return guard\n \n \n def _provider_keys(manifests: list[dict]) -> list[str]:\n     \"\"\"Provider keys present in *any* manifest, so they are compared everywhere.\"\"\"\n     present: set[str] = set()\n     for manifest in manifests:\n         config = manifest.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}\n         present.update(key for key in _PROVIDER_KEYS if key in config)\n     return sorted(present)\n \n \n def _check_comparable(guard: dict, baseline: dict) -> None:\n-    diffs = [key for key in baseline if guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n+    # Compare the guard keys the manifest actually contributes. ``evidence_mode`` is\n+    # validated once for the whole set (see compare_manifests), not per manifest.\n+    diffs = [key for key in guard if key in baseline and guard.get(key) != baseline[key]]\n     if diffs:\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\n             \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \"\n             + \", \".join(sorted(diffs))\n         )\n \n \n def _variant_of(run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"The variant segment of a run id (``<variant>-<ticker>-...``).\"\"\"\n     return run_id.split(\"-\", 1)[0]\n \n \n-def _variant_row(manifest: dict) -> dict:\n+def _variant_row(manifest: dict, evidence_mode: str | None = None) -> dict:\n     usage = manifest.get(\"usage\")\n     row = {\n         \"run_id\": manifest.get(\"run_id\"),\n         \"variant\": _variant_of(str(manifest.get(\"run_id\", \"\"))),\n         \"outcome\": manifest.get(\"outcome\"),\n         \"usage\": usage,\n         \"duration_seconds\": manifest.get(\"duration_seconds\"),\n         \"failure\": manifest.get(\"failure\"),\n         \"stop_reason\": manifest.get(\"stop_reason\"),\n+        \"evidence_mode\": evidence_mode,\n     }\n     # Surface each numeric metric explicitly. A missing value stays None (null),\n     # never coerced to 0: an unreported count is unknown, not zero.\n     for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n         row[metric] = usage.get(metric) if isinstance(usage, dict) else None\n     return row\n \n \n def _format_metric(value) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Render a metric for humans: ``--`` for null/unknown, else the number.\"\"\"\n     return \"--\" if value is None else str(value)\n \n \n def _counts(values: list) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Count occurrences of each value (``None`` counted as ``null``).\"\"\"\n     counts: dict = {}\n     for value in values:\n         key = \"null\" if value is None else str(value)\n         counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1\n     return counts\n \n \n def _averages(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:\n     grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}\n     for row in rows:\n         grouped.setdefault(row[\"variant\"], []).append(row)\n \n     result: dict[str, dict] = {}\n     for variant, group in grouped.items():\n         summary: dict = {\"runs\": len(group)}\n         for metric in _USAGE_METRICS:\n             values = [\n                 row[\"usage\"][metric]\n                 for row in group\n                 if isinstance(row.get(\"usage\"), dict) and row[\"usage\"].get(metric) is not None\n             ]\n             summary[metric] = sum(values) / len(values) if values else None\n         durations = [row[\"duration_seconds\"] for row in group if row[\"duration_seconds\"] is not None]\n         summary[\"duration_seconds\"] = sum(durations) / len(durations) if durations else None\n         summary[\"outcome_counts\"] = _counts([row[\"outcome\"] for row in group])\n         summary[\"stop_reason_counts\"] = _counts([row[\"stop_reason\"] for row in group])\n         result[variant] = summary\n     return result\n \n \n-def compare_manifests(manifests: list[dict]) -> Comparison:\n-    \"\"\"Compare already-loaded manifests; raise ``IncomparableRunsError`` if invalid.\"\"\"\n+def compare_manifests(manifests: list[dict], evidence_modes: list[str | None] | None = None) -> Comparison:\n+    \"\"\"Compare already-loaded manifests; raise ``IncomparableRunsError`` if invalid.\n+\n+    ``evidence_modes`` aligns with ``manifests`` (E4 ``evidence-mode.json``): the mode\n+    is a control that must match across every run, so strict and report_reference\n+    runs are never compared together. When omitted, every mode is ``None`` (no\n+    sidecar), which is itself required to be uniform.\n+    \"\"\"\n     if not manifests:\n         raise IncomparableRunsError(\"no manifests supplied\")\n+    modes = list(evidence_modes) if evidence_modes is not None else [None] * len(manifests)\n+    if len(modes) != len(manifests):\n+        raise IncomparableRunsError(\"evidence_modes must align with manifests\")\n+    if len(set(modes)) > 1:\n+        raise IncomparableRunsError(\n+            \"runs are not comparable; evidence_mode differs (strict vs report_reference \"\n+            \"are never compared together): \" + \", \".join(repr(m) for m in modes)\n+        )\n+    shared_mode = modes[0]\n \n     baseline_guard = _guard_of(manifests[0])\n+    baseline_guard[\"evidence_mode\"] = shared_mode\n     for manifest in manifests[1:]:\n         _check_comparable(_guard_of(manifest), baseline_guard)\n \n     # Union the provider keys across all runs so a tier provider set in any run\n     # (not just the baseline) is verified to match everywhere.\n     for key in _provider_keys(manifests):\n         values = {(m.get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}).get(key) for m in manifests}\n         if len(values) > 1:\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(\n                 \"runs are not comparable; these guard keys differ from the baseline: \" + key\n             )\n         baseline_guard.setdefault(key, (manifests[0].get(\"config_snapshot\") or {}).get(key))\n \n-    rows = [_variant_row(manifest) for manifest in manifests]\n+    rows = [_variant_row(manifest, modes[i]) for i, manifest in enumerate(manifests)]\n     return Comparison(\n         baseline_run_id=manifests[0].get(\"run_id\"),\n         guard=baseline_guard,\n         variants=rows,\n         averages=_averages(rows),\n         notes=[\n             \"Reported quantities are measured from run manifests; no quality score is \"\n             \"computed or inferred here.\",\n             \"Runs are only compared when ticker, trade_date, asset_type, model, provider, \"\n-            \"language, and prompt hashes all match the baseline.\",\n+            \"language, prompt hashes, and evidence_mode all match the baseline.\",\n         ],\n     )\n \n \n+def _evidence_mode_of(manifest_path: Path) -> str | None:\n+    \"\"\"Read the E4 ``evidence-mode.json`` beside a manifest; ``None`` when absent.\n+\n+    A missing sidecar means the run predates E4 or recorded no mode; it compares\n+    as ``None`` and so is only comparable with other sidecar-less runs.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    sidecar = Path(manifest_path).parent / \"evidence-mode.json\"\n+    if not sidecar.exists():\n+        return None\n+    try:\n+        data = json.loads(sidecar.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:\n+        raise IncomparableRunsError(f\"cannot read evidence-mode {str(sidecar)!r}: {exc}\") from exc\n+    return data.get(\"evidence_mode\")\n+\n+\n def compare_manifest_files(paths: list[str | Path]) -> Comparison:\n     manifests = []\n+    modes = []\n     for path in paths:\n         try:\n             manifests.append(read_manifest(path))\n         except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:\n             # read_manifest raises ValueError for a bad/unsupported/short manifest\n             # and OSError (e.g. FileNotFoundError) for an unreadable path.\n             raise IncomparableRunsError(f\"cannot read manifest {str(path)!r}: {exc}\") from exc\n-    return compare_manifests(manifests)\n+        modes.append(_evidence_mode_of(Path(path)))\n+    return compare_manifests(manifests, evidence_modes=modes)\n \n \n def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n     args = [arg for arg in argv[1:] if not arg.startswith(\"-\")]\n     as_json = \"--json\" in argv[1:]\n     if not args:\n         print(\"usage: compare_runs.py <manifest> [<manifest> ...] [--json]\", file=sys.stderr)\n         return 2\n     try:\n         comparison = compare_manifest_files(args)\n     except IncomparableRunsError as exc:\n         print(f\"[compare-runs] REFUSED: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n         return 1\n \n     if as_json:\n         print(json.dumps(comparison.to_dict(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n     else:\n         print(f\"[compare-runs] baseline={comparison.baseline_run_id} runs={len(comparison.variants)}\")\n         header = (\"runs\",) + _USAGE_METRICS + (\"duration_seconds\",)\n         print(\"  variant        \" + \"  \".join(f\"{name:>16}\" for name in header))\n         for variant, summary in sorted(comparison.averages.items()):\n             cells = \"  \".join(f\"{_format_metric(summary.get(name)):>16}\" for name in header)\n             print(f\"  {variant:<14} {cells}\")\n     return 0\n \n \n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n     raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))\n",

              "file": "src/cli/run.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/cli/run.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/run.py\t\n+++ src/cli/run.py\t\n@@ -1,681 +1,721 @@\n \"\"\"Running one analysis from the CLI: build the graph, stream it into the live view, save the report.\"\"\"\n \n+import json\n import os\n import re\n import sys\n import time\n import webbrowser\n from dataclasses import replace\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from functools import wraps\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import typer\n from rich.live import Live\n \n from cli.display import (\n     ANALYST_ORDER,\n     AnalystWallTimeTracker,\n     classify_message_type,\n     console,\n     create_layout,\n     display_complete_report,\n     message_buffer,\n     update_analyst_statuses,\n     update_display,\n     update_research_team_status,\n )\n from cli.selections import depth_from_env, get_user_selections, unattended_gaps\n from cli.stats_handler import StatsCallbackHandler\n from tradingagents import __version__\n from tradingagents.agents.rating import is_review, run_rating\n from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.graph.analyst_execution import (\n     build_analyst_execution_plan,\n )\n from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, build_run_id, write_manifest\n \n _VALID_VARIANTS = (\"v0\", \"v1\", \"v2\")\n \n \n def _validate_variant(value: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Accept only a known, lowercase architecture variant slug (``v0``/``v1``/``v2``).\n \n     The value becomes the first segment of the manifest ``run_id`` and a directory\n     name under the results root, so an unknown or unsafe value is rejected rather\n     than interpolated.\n     \"\"\"\n     if value not in _VALID_VARIANTS:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid variant {value!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_VALID_VARIANTS)}\"\n         )\n     return value\n \n \n \n def _run_directory(config: dict, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Where this run writes, with the ticker validated as a path component.\n \n     Every other path that interpolates a ticker checks it first; a value of\n     \"..\" here would place the run outside the results directory.\n     \"\"\"\n     return Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker_component(ticker) / trade_date\n \n \n def _manifest_config_snapshot(config: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Scalars from ``config`` that are safe to record in a run manifest.\n \n     The recorder already drops secret-pattern keys; keeping only scalar values\n     here also excludes nested objects and lists that are not comparable settings.\n     ``results_dir`` is a machine-local output path, not a comparable setting, so it\n     is left out of the manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     return {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in config.items()\n         if key != \"results_dir\"\n         and (isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None)\n     }\n \n \n def write_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     config: dict,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     outcome: str | None,\n     usage: dict,\n     failure: str | None,\n     variant: str,\n     repeat: int,\n     at: datetime,\n     version: str,\n     duration_seconds: float | None = None,\n     started_at: float | None = None,\n     clock=None,\n     stop_reason: str | None = None,\n+    evidence_mode: str = \"report_reference\",\n ) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write this run's manifest to ``<results_dir>/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json``.\n \n     ``stop_reason`` is read from the run's final state by the caller (C owns the\n     value domain); it is ``None`` when the graph did not reach a terminal state.\n     ``prompt_hashes`` (B) is ``{}`` and ``evidence_snapshot`` (A) is ``None`` until\n     those members' contracts land. ``duration_seconds`` is measured from\n     ``started_at`` and ``clock`` (``time.time`` by default) when not supplied;\n     passing both keeps it testable.\n+\n+    A per-run ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar (E4) is written next to the manifest\n+    recording the evidence mode and the facts the run observed. It does not change\n+    the RunEvent v1 15 fields.\n     \"\"\"\n     run_id = build_run_id(variant, ticker, trade_date, repeat, at)\n     if duration_seconds is None and started_at is not None:\n         now = (clock or time.time)()\n         duration_seconds = max(0.0, now - started_at)\n \n     event = RunEvent(\n         run_id=run_id,\n         created_at=at.astimezone(UTC).isoformat(),\n         version=version,\n         ticker=ticker,\n         trade_date=trade_date,\n         asset_type=asset_type,\n         outcome=outcome,\n         config_snapshot=_manifest_config_snapshot(config),\n         prompt_hashes={},\n         evidence_snapshot=None,\n         usage=usage,\n         duration_seconds=duration_seconds,\n         failure=failure,\n         stop_reason=stop_reason,\n     )\n     runs_dir = Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"runs\"\n     run_id = _unique_run_id(runs_dir, run_id)\n     event = replace(event, run_id=run_id)\n     manifest_dir = runs_dir / run_id\n     manifest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n-    return write_manifest(event, manifest_dir / \"manifest.json\")\n+    path = write_manifest(event, manifest_dir / \"manifest.json\")\n+    write_evidence_mode(manifest_dir / \"evidence-mode.json\", run_id, evidence_mode)\n+    return path\n \n \n+_EVIDENCE_MODES = (\"strict\", \"report_reference\")\n+\n+\n+def write_evidence_mode(path, run_id: str, evidence_mode: str) -> Path:\n+    \"\"\"Write the E4 ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar recording this run's mode.\n+\n+    E records facts only; the authoritative action and the mode approval belong to\n+    D/C, so those fields are ``None`` here unless a caller later fills them in.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    if evidence_mode not in _EVIDENCE_MODES:\n+        raise ValueError(\n+            f\"invalid evidence_mode {evidence_mode!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_EVIDENCE_MODES)}\"\n+        )\n+    sidecar = {\n+        \"schema_version\": 1,\n+        \"run_id\": run_id,\n+        \"evidence_mode\": evidence_mode,\n+        \"scenario\": None,\n+        \"policy_version\": None,\n+        \"unknown_time_fields\": [],\n+        \"limitations\": [],\n+        \"authoritative_action\": None,\n+        \"authoritative_reason\": None,\n+        \"decided_by\": None,\n+        \"snapshot_ref\": {\"snapshot_id\": None, \"artifact_key\": None},\n+    }\n+    path = Path(path)\n+    path.write_text(json.dumps(sidecar, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n+    return path\n+\n+\n def _unique_run_id(runs_dir: Path, run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A run_id whose directory does not exist yet, so a same-minute retry is safe.\n \n     ``build_run_id`` has minute resolution, so two runs started in the same minute\n     (or a retry) produce the same id. Appending ``-<n>`` keeps the id within the\n     recorder's 64-char pattern and never overwrites an earlier manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     pattern = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n     candidate = run_id\n     suffix = 2\n     while (runs_dir / candidate).exists():\n         candidate = f\"{run_id}-{suffix}\"\n         if not pattern.match(candidate):\n             raise ValueError(f\"no free run_id derived from {run_id!r} within 64 chars\")\n         suffix += 1\n     return candidate\n \n \n def _make_manifest_writer(config: dict, selections: dict, stats_handler, started_at=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     \"\"\"Return a ``write(failure=..., outcome=...)`` bound to this run's inputs.\n \n     ``variant`` selects the architecture under test and becomes the first segment\n     of the manifest ``run_id``; ``repeat`` is 1 and ``created_at`` is now, both\n     supplied here so the recorder never reads the clock itself. ``started_at`` is\n     the run's start (``time.time()``); forwarding it lets the manifest record a\n     real duration.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def write(*, failure, outcome, stop_reason=None):\n         return write_run_manifest(\n             config=config,\n             ticker=selections[\"ticker\"],\n             trade_date=selections[\"analysis_date\"],\n             asset_type=selections[\"asset_type\"],\n             outcome=outcome,\n             usage=stats_handler.get_stats(),\n             failure=failure,\n             variant=variant,\n             repeat=1,\n             at=datetime.now(UTC),\n             version=__version__,\n             started_at=started_at,\n             stop_reason=stop_reason,\n+            evidence_mode=config.get(\"evidence_mode\", \"report_reference\"),\n         )\n \n     return write\n \n \n def _finalize_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     write,\n     graph,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     portfolio,\n     final_state,\n     failure: BaseException | None,\n ) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Write the manifest, then dispose of (or keep) the checkpoint.\n \n     The manifest is written **before** the checkpoint is cleared, so a crash in\n     teardown never loses the record. A failed run still writes a manifest with\n     ``failure`` set and keeps its checkpoint for resume; the failure is re-raised.\n     ``stop_reason`` is read from ``final_state`` (C's field) with a ``None``\n     fallback when the run did not reach a terminal state.\n     \"\"\"\n     outcome = None if final_state is None else run_rating(final_state)\n     stop_reason = (final_state or {}).get(\"stop_reason\") if failure is None else None\n     write(failure=None if failure is None else str(failure), outcome=outcome, stop_reason=stop_reason)\n \n     if failure is not None:\n         raise failure\n \n     if final_state is not None:\n         graph.record_decision(ticker, trade_date, final_state)\n     graph.clear_checkpoint_on_success(ticker, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n \n \n def _announce_checkpoint_state(graph, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Say whether this run resumed a saved one, where the user can see it.\n \n     The graph logs this, but nothing in the CLI configures logging and the live\n     view owns the screen, so a resume was invisible.\n     \"\"\"\n     if getattr(graph, \"_resuming\", False):\n         message_buffer.add_message(\n             \"System\", f\"Resuming the saved run for {ticker} on {trade_date}\"\n         )\n     else:\n         message_buffer.add_message(\"System\", f\"Starting fresh for {ticker} on {trade_date}\")\n \n \n def _build_run_config(selections: dict, checkpoint: bool | None) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Assemble the run config from interactive selections, honoring env precedence.\n \n     Round counts and checkpoint follow \"explicit env/flag wins\": an env-applied\n     value on DEFAULT_CONFIG is preserved unless the user overrode it on the CLI.\n     \"\"\"\n     config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n     #
