              "content": "\"\"\"Run resume / attempts / checkpoint locator (E3).\n\nContract: ``docs/handoffs/E-interfaces-v1.md`` §E3. The pieces here are E-owned and\ndepend on no other member for their format; a real end-to-end resume needs C's\n``checkpoint_thread_id(..., run_key=run_id)`` and state binding, so ``thread_id`` is\ninjected by the caller rather than computed here.\n\nLayout under ``<results_dir>/runs/<run_id>/``:\n\n- ``attempts.jsonl`` — one JSON line per attempt (recoverable failures live only here;\n  the manifest slot stays free).\n- ``checkpoint.json`` — the locator: run identity, checkpoint location, and the\n  evidence snapshot pointer.\n- ``manifest.json`` — written once on terminal success (by ``run_recorder``); its\n  presence is what makes a later ``resolve_run`` return ``already_recorded``.\n\nThree-step semantics: a first failure appends an attempt (no manifest) → resuming the\nsame ``run_id`` succeeds, writes the one manifest, and clears the checkpoint → a\nfurther request returns ``already_recorded``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Callable\n\nSCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n\n# Typed resume failure codes (docs/handoffs/E-interfaces-v1.md §E3).\nRESUME_ERROR_CODES = (\n    \"locator_missing\",\n    \"locator_invalid\",\n    \"checkpoint_not_found\",\n    \"checkpoint_unreadable\",\n    \"checkpoint_corrupt\",\n    \"checkpoint_signature_mismatch\",\n    \"snapshot_missing\",\n    \"snapshot_unreadable\",\n    \"snapshot_corrupt\",\n    \"snapshot_id_mismatch\",\n    \"already_recorded\",\n)\n\n\nclass ResumeError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A resume could not proceed; ``code`` names the typed reason.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str | None = None) -> None:\n        if code not in RESUME_ERROR_CODES:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown resume error code {code!r}\")\n        self.code = code\n        self.detail = detail\n        super().__init__(f\"{code}: {detail}\" if detail else code)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ResumeRef:\n    \"\"\"What a resumed run needs: where its checkpoint and evidence snapshot are.\"\"\"\n\n    db: str\n    thread_id: str\n    step: int | None\n    snapshot_id: str | None\n    artifact_key: str | None\n    source_run_id: str | None\n    captured_at: str | None\n\n\ndef run_dir(config: dict, run_id: str) -> Path:\n    return Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"runs\" / run_id\n\n\ndef attempts_path(config: dict, run_id: str) -> Path:\n    return run_dir(config, run_id) / \"attempts.jsonl\"\n\n\ndef checkpoint_path(config: dict, run_id: str) -> Path:\n    return run_dir(config, run_id) / \"checkpoint.json\"\n\n\ndef manifest_path(config: dict, run_id: str) -> Path:\n    return run_dir(config, run_id) / \"manifest.json\"\n\n\n# --- attempts ----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef append_attempt(\n    config: dict,\n    run_id: str,\n    *,\n    at: str,\n    stage: str,\n    status: str,\n    reason_code: str,\n    detail: str | None = None,\n) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Append one attempt line; the manifest slot is not touched.\"\"\"\n    path = attempts_path(config, run_id)\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    record = {\n        \"schema_version\": SCHEMA_VERSION,\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"at\": at,\n        \"stage\": stage,\n        \"status\": status,\n        \"reason_code\": reason_code,\n        \"detail\": detail,\n    }\n    with open(path, \"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        handle.write(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n    return path\n\n\ndef read_attempts(config: dict, run_id: str) -> list[dict]:\n    path = attempts_path(config, run_id)\n    if not path.exists():\n        return []\n    lines = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines()\n    return [json.loads(line) for line in lines if line.strip()]\n\n\n# --- checkpoint --------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef write_checkpoint(\n    config: dict,\n    run_id: str,\n    *,\n    ticker: str,\n    trade_date: str,\n    asset_type: str,\n    created_at: str,\n    status: str,\n    checkpoint: dict,\n    evidence_snapshot: dict,\n) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write ``checkpoint.json`` atomically (temp file + ``os.replace``).\"\"\"\n    path = checkpoint_path(config, run_id)\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    locator = {\n        \"schema_version\": SCHEMA_VERSION,\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"ticker\": ticker,\n        \"trade_date\": trade_date,\n        \"asset_type\": asset_type,\n        \"created_at\": created_at,\n        \"status\": status,\n        \"checkpoint\": {\n            \"backend\": checkpoint.get(\"backend\"),\n            \"db_relpath\": checkpoint.get(\"db_relpath\"),\n            \"thread_id\": checkpoint.get(\"thread_id\"),\n            \"step\": checkpoint.get(\"step\"),\n        },\n        \"evidence_snapshot\": {\n            \"snapshot_id\": evidence_snapshot.get(\"snapshot_id\"),\n            \"artifact_key\": evidence_snapshot.get(\"artifact_key\"),\n            \"store\": evidence_snapshot.get(\"store\"),\n            \"source_run_id\": evidence_snapshot.get(\"source_run_id\"),\n            \"captured_at\": evidence_snapshot.get(\"captured_at\"),\n        },\n    }\n    tmp = path.with_suffix(\".json.tmp\")\n    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(locator, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    os.replace(tmp, path)\n    return path\n\n\ndef _read_checkpoint_file(path: Path) -> dict:\n    if not path.exists():\n        raise ResumeError(\"locator_missing\")\n    try:\n        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except OSError as exc:\n        raise ResumeError(\"checkpoint_unreadable\", str(exc)) from exc\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise ResumeError(\"checkpoint_corrupt\", str(exc)) from exc\n    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get(\"schema_version\") != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n        raise ResumeError(\"locator_invalid\")\n    for key in (\"run_id\", \"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\", \"checkpoint\", \"evidence_snapshot\"):\n        if key not in data:\n            raise ResumeError(\"locator_invalid\", f\"missing {key!r}\")\n    return data\n\n\ndef resolve_run(\n    run_id: str,\n    config: dict,\n    *,\n    expected_ticker: str | None = None,\n    expected_trade_date: str | None = None,\n    expected_asset_type: str | None = None,\n    expected_snapshot_id: str | None = None,\n    backend_root: str | Path | None = None,\n) -> ResumeRef:\n    \"\"\"Resolve a run's checkpoint and evidence snapshot, or raise ``ResumeError``.\n\n    ``already_recorded`` is checked first: a terminal manifest for this ``run_id``\n    means the run already completed and must not run again. Identity fields inside\n    the locator must match the run_id and any caller-supplied expectations, else\n    ``checkpoint_signature_mismatch``. ``thread_id`` is injected in the locator, not\n    computed here.\n    \"\"\"\n    if manifest_path(config, run_id).exists():\n        raise ResumeError(\"already_recorded\")\n\n    data = _read_checkpoint_file(checkpoint_path(config, run_id))\n\n    if data.get(\"run_id\") != run_id:\n        raise ResumeError(\"checkpoint_signature_mismatch\", \"run_id\")\n\n    checks = (\n        (\"ticker\", expected_ticker),\n        (\"trade_date\", expected_trade_date),\n        (\"asset_type\", expected_asset_type),\n    )\n    for field, expected in checks:\n        if expected is not None and data.get(field) != expected:\n            raise ResumeError(\"checkpoint_signature_mismatch\", field)\n\n    checkpoint = data.get(\"checkpoint\") or {}\n    snapshot = data.get(\"evidence_snapshot\") or {}\n    thread_id = checkpoint.get(\"thread_id\")\n    if not thread_id:\n        raise ResumeError(\"locator_invalid\", \"checkpoint.thread_id\")\n\n    snapshot_id = snapshot.get(\"snapshot_id\")\n    if expected_snapshot_id is not None and snapshot_id != expected_snapshot_id:\n        raise ResumeError(\"snapshot_id_mismatch\", snapshot_id)\n\n    artifact_key = snapshot.get(\"artifact_key\")\n    store = snapshot.get(\"store\")\n    if snapshot_id is not None and artifact_key is not None:\n        _verify_snapshot_artifact(config, store, artifact_key, backend_root)\n\n    db = _resolve_db_path(config, data, checkpoint)\n\n    return ResumeRef(\n        db=str(db),\n        thread_id=str(thread_id),\n        step=checkpoint.get(\"step\"),\n        snapshot_id=snapshot_id,\n        artifact_key=artifact_key,\n        source_run_id=snapshot.get(\"source_run_id\"),\n        captured_at=snapshot.get(\"captured_at\"),\n    )\n\n\ndef _resolve_db_path(config: dict, data: dict, checkpoint: dict) -> Path:\n    db_relpath = checkpoint.get(\"db_relpath\")\n    if not db_relpath:\n        # Default to the run directory; the caller may still inject the real path.\n        return run_dir(config, data.get(\"run_id\")) / \"checkpoints.db\"\n    db_path = Path(db_relpath)\n    if db_path.is_absolute():\n        return db_path\n    return run_dir(config, data.get(\"run_id\")) / db_path\n\n\ndef _verify_snapshot_artifact(\n    config: dict, store: str | None, artifact_key: str, backend_root: str | Path | None\n) -> None:\n    root = Path(backend_root) if backend_root is not None else Path(config[\"results_dir\"])\n    base = root / store if store else root\n    artifact = base / artifact_key\n    if not artifact.exists():\n        raise ResumeError(\"snapshot_missing\", str(artifact))\n    try:\n        json.loads(artifact.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except OSError as exc:\n        raise ResumeError(\"snapshot_unreadable\", str(exc)) from exc\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise ResumeError(\"snapshot_corrupt\", str(exc)) from exc\n\n\n# --- three-step success path -------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef write_manifest_then_clear(\n    config: dict, run_id: str, *, write_manifest: Callable[[], Any]\n) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write the one manifest, then clear the checkpoint; keep it if the write fails.\n\n    ``write_manifest`` is injected so the manifest shape stays owned by\n    ``run_recorder``. If it raises, the checkpoint is left in place for a retry and\n    the error propagates; only after a successful write is the checkpoint removed.\n    \"\"\"\n    result = write_manifest()\n    cp = checkpoint_path(config, run_id)\n    if cp.exists():\n        cp.unlink()\n    return result\n",

              "file": "src/cli/stats_handler.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/cli/stats_handler.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/stats_handler.py\t\n+++ src/cli/stats_handler.py\t\n@@ -1,380 +1,392 @@\n \"\"\"Callback handler tracking LLM/tool calls and per-call token usage (E2).\n \n Per-call usage follows ``docs/handoffs/E-interfaces-v1.md`` §E2: every LLM call is a\n ``CallUsage`` keyed by its LangChain ``run_id``. The aggregate entry stays\n ``get_stats()``; ``llm_calls`` counts start-callback events (one invoke emitting two\n starts counts as two), not SDK retries.\n \n Settlement rule for a window of calls: if every call is ``reported`` or\n ``explicit_zero`` the tokens sum once; if any call is ``partial``/``invalid``/\n ``missing``/``failed`` the window is ``None`` (unknown), never a fabricated number.\n \n ``track(stage)`` scopes the call ids seen while it is active using a ``ContextVar``,\n so concurrent threads/tasks do not see each other's ids. At context exit the window\n is closed atomically and frozen into a ``StageSettlement`` (see ``settle``): the\n handle's ``call_ids`` and ``settlement`` never change afterwards. A late callback\n can still update the handler's global records, but it cannot extend a closed\n window, cannot rewrite a frozen settlement, and cannot turn a settled ``None``\n into a refund.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import threading\n from contextlib import contextmanager\n from contextvars import ContextVar\n from dataclasses import dataclass\n from typing import Any\n \n from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\n from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n from langchain_core.outputs import LLMResult\n \n # Statuses that make a settled window unknown (any one -> None for the window).\n _UNKNOWN_STATUSES = frozenset({\"partial\", \"invalid\", \"missing\", \"failed\"})\n \n \n class _StageWindow:\n     \"\"\"Mutable collector for one ``track`` window; closed once at context exit.\n \n     ``closed`` is the important part: a context copied into another thread or an\n     asyncio task keeps a reference to this object, so a late callback must be\n     refused explicitly instead of relying only on ``ContextVar.reset`` (which\n     affects only the context that opened the window).\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self, stage: str) -> None:\n         self.stage = stage\n         self.ids: list[str] = []\n         self.closed = False\n         self._lock = threading.Lock()\n \n     def record(self, call_id: str) -> None:\n         with self._lock:\n             if not self.closed and call_id not in self.ids:\n                 self.ids.append(call_id)\n \n     def close(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n         with self._lock:\n             self.closed = True\n             return tuple(self.ids)\n \n \n # The collector for the innermost active ``track`` in the current context, if any.\n _active_collector: ContextVar[_StageWindow | None] = ContextVar(\n     \"stats_active_collector\", default=None\n )\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class CallUsage:\n     \"\"\"One LLM call's usage, keyed by the LangChain ``run_id``.\"\"\"\n \n     call_id: str\n     node: str | None\n     status: str  # reported | explicit_zero | partial | invalid | missing | failed\n     source: str  # usage_metadata | token_usage | none\n     input_tokens: int | None\n     output_tokens: int | None\n     total_tokens: int | None  # E local input+output; provider ``total`` not trusted\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class StageSettlement:\n     \"\"\"An immutable snapshot of one ``track`` window, frozen at context exit.\n \n     ``units`` is ``sum(total_tokens)`` only when the window is complete:\n     every recorded call is ``reported``/``explicit_zero`` with a usable total\n     **and** the observed id count matches ``expected_calls`` (when the caller\n     declared it). Otherwise ``units`` is ``None``. A later callback never\n     changes this object, so an unknown settlement cannot become a refund, and\n     a partial window cannot be mistaken for a complete one.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     stage: str\n     call_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n     usages: tuple[tuple[str, CallUsage | None], ...]\n     pending: tuple[str, ...]\n     units: int | None\n     complete: bool\n     expected_calls: int | None\n     count_matches: bool\n \n \n class TrackHandle:\n     \"\"\"The result of ``track(stage)``: ids seen while active, frozen at exit.\"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self, stage: str, window: _StageWindow) -> None:\n         self.stage = stage\n         self._window = window\n         self._settlement: StageSettlement | None = None\n \n     def _freeze(self, settlement: StageSettlement) -> None:\n         self._settlement = settlement\n \n     @property\n     def call_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n         if self._settlement is not None:\n             return self._settlement.call_ids\n         return tuple(self._window.ids)\n \n     @property\n     def settlement(self) -> StageSettlement:\n         if self._settlement is None:\n             raise RuntimeError(\n                 \"stage window is still open; the settlement is frozen when track() exits\"\n             )\n         return self._settlement\n \n \n def _as_int(value: Any) -> int | None:\n     \"\"\"A non-negative int from ``value``, or ``None`` when it is not a valid count.\"\"\"\n     if isinstance(value, bool):\n         return None\n     if isinstance(value, int) and value >= 0:\n         return value\n     return None\n \n \n class StatsCallbackHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n     \"\"\"Track LLM calls, tool calls, and per-call token usage.\"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self) -> None:\n         super().__init__()\n         self._lock = threading.Lock()\n         self.llm_calls = 0\n         self.tool_calls = 0\n         # Legacy manual counters (kept for callers that set them directly, e.g. tests).\n         self.tokens_in = 0\n         self.tokens_out = 0\n         self._usage_reported = False\n         # Per-call records, insertion-ordered by first observation.\n         self._calls: dict[str, CallUsage] = {}\n \n     # --- callbacks ----------------------------------------------------------\n \n     def on_llm_start(self, serialized, prompts, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         self._on_start(kwargs)\n \n     def on_chat_model_start(self, serialized, messages, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         self._on_start(kwargs)\n \n     def _on_start(self, kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n         run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n         if run_id is None:\n             return\n         call_id = str(run_id)\n         metadata = kwargs.get(\"metadata\") or {}\n         node = metadata.get(\"langgraph_node\")\n         with self._lock:\n             self.llm_calls += 1\n             # A start without a completed end is \"missing\" until an end arrives.\n             self._calls[call_id] = CallUsage(\n                 call_id=call_id,\n                 node=node,\n                 status=\"missing\",\n                 source=\"none\",\n                 input_tokens=None,\n                 output_tokens=None,\n                 total_tokens=None,\n             )\n         self._collect(call_id)\n \n     def on_llm_end(self, response: LLMResult, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n         if run_id is None:\n             return\n         call_id = str(run_id)\n         usage = self._extract_usage(response)\n         with self._lock:\n             node = self._calls[call_id].node if call_id in self._calls else None\n             self._calls[call_id] = self._settle(call_id, node, usage)\n         self._collect(call_id)\n \n     def on_llm_error(self, error: BaseException, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n         if run_id is None:\n             return\n         call_id = str(run_id)\n         with self._lock:\n             node = self._calls[call_id].node if call_id in self._calls else None\n             self._calls[call_id] = CallUsage(\n                 call_id=call_id,\n                 node=node,\n                 status=\"failed\",\n                 source=\"none\",\n                 input_tokens=None,\n                 output_tokens=None,\n                 total_tokens=None,\n             )\n         self._collect(call_id)\n \n     def on_tool_start(self, serialized, input_str, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         with self._lock:\n             self.tool_calls += 1\n \n     # --- usage extraction / settlement -------------------------------------\n \n     @staticmethod\n     def _extract_usage(response: LLMResult) -> tuple[str, Any]:\n         \"\"\"Return ``(source, usage_dict)`` from a response; ``(\"none\", None)`` if absent.\"\"\"\n         try:\n             generation = response.generations[0][0]\n         except (IndexError, TypeError):\n             return \"none\", None\n         message = getattr(generation, \"message\", None)\n         if not isinstance(message, AIMessage):\n             return \"none\", None\n         usage_metadata = getattr(message, \"usage_metadata\", None)\n         if usage_metadata:\n             return \"usage_metadata\", usage_metadata\n         token_usage = getattr(message, \"response_metadata\", {}).get(\"token_usage\")\n         if token_usage:\n             return \"token_usage\", token_usage\n         return \"none\", None\n \n     @staticmethod\n     def _settle(call_id: str, node: str | None, usage: tuple[str, Any]) -> CallUsage:\n         source, data = usage\n         if data is None:\n             return CallUsage(call_id, node, \"missing\", \"none\", None, None, None)\n         input_tokens = _as_int(data.get(\"input_tokens\", data.get(\"prompt_tokens\")))\n         output_tokens = _as_int(data.get(\"output_tokens\", data.get(\"completion_tokens\")))\n         if input_tokens is None and output_tokens is None:\n             status = \"invalid\"\n         elif input_tokens is None or output_tokens is None:\n             status = \"partial\"\n         elif input_tokens == 0 and output_tokens == 0:\n             status = \"explicit_zero\"\n         else:\n             status = \"reported\"\n         total = (\n             input_tokens + output_tokens\n             if input_tokens is not None and output_tokens is not None\n             else None\n         )\n         return CallUsage(\n             call_id, node, status, source, input_tokens, output_tokens, total\n         )\n \n     # --- query --------------------------------------------------------------\n \n     def calls(self) -> tuple[CallUsage, ...]:\n         with self._lock:\n             return tuple(self._calls.values())\n \n     def call(self, call_id: str) -> CallUsage | None:\n         with self._lock:\n             return self._calls.get(call_id)\n \n     @contextmanager\n     def track(self, stage: str, *, expected_calls: int | None = None):\n         \"\"\"Collect ids while active, then atomically close and freeze a settlement.\n \n         ``expected_calls`` is the number of callback ids the caller admitted for\n         this stage. Declaring it makes a window with fewer ids than expected\n         ``units=None`` instead of a partial sum -- this is the answer to C's\n         \"one complete callback, another not collected at the exit boundary\"\n         case. Without a declared count, a window that simply saw fewer callbacks\n         cannot be distinguished from a complete one, so callers that need that\n         guarantee must declare it.\n \n         The freeze takes ``self._lock``, so it cannot race a callback writing a\n         new ``CallUsage``. ``window.close()`` marks the window closed first; a\n         copied context that still holds the window is refused from then on.\n         Callbacks must finish inside the ``with`` block: anything arriving after\n         the freeze only updates the handler's global records.\n         \"\"\"\n         if expected_calls is not None and (\n             isinstance(expected_calls, bool)\n             or not isinstance(expected_calls, int)\n             or expected_calls < 0\n         ):\n             raise ValueError(\"expected_calls must be a non-negative int or None\")\n         window = _StageWindow(stage)\n         handle = TrackHandle(stage, window)\n         token = _active_collector.set(window)\n         try:\n             yield handle\n         finally:\n             with self._lock:\n                 ids = window.close()\n                 usages = tuple((cid, self._calls.get(cid)) for cid in ids)\n+                collected = set(ids)\n+                # Race guard: a start callback writes its global record (under this\n+                # lock) before it records window membership via ``_collect``. If the\n+                # window closes in that gap, the call is globally \"missing\" but not\n+                # yet in ``ids``. Treat any such still-unfinalized call as pending so\n+                # the window is reported unknown, not as a complete partial sum.\n+                inflight = tuple(\n+                    cid\n+                    for cid, usage in self._calls.items()\n+                    if cid not in collected and usage.status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES\n+                )\n                 pending = tuple(\n                     cid for cid, usage in usages\n                     if usage is None or usage.status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES\n-                )\n+                ) + inflight\n                 count_matches = expected_calls is None or len(ids) == expected_calls\n                 complete = (\n                     count_matches\n+                    and not inflight\n                     and bool(ids)\n                     and all(\n                         usage is not None\n                         and usage.status in {\"reported\", \"explicit_zero\"}\n                         and usage.total_tokens is not None\n                         for _, usage in usages\n                     )\n                 )\n                 units = (\n                     sum(usage.total_tokens or 0 for _, usage in usages if usage is not None)\n                     if complete else None\n                 )\n                 handle._freeze(StageSettlement(\n                     stage=stage,\n                     call_ids=ids,\n                     usages=usages,\n                     pending=pending,\n                     units=units,\n                     complete=complete,\n                     expected_calls=expected_calls,\n                     count_matches=count_matches,\n                 ))\n             _active_collector.reset(token)\n \n     def settle(self, handle: TrackHandle) -> StageSettlement:\n         \"\"\"Return the immutable settlement for a closed ``track`` window.\n \n         This is the public entry C should call once, immediately after the\n         ``with stats.track(stage)`` block, then pass ``units`` to\n         ``BudgetPolicy.record_usage(stage, units)`` (``None`` when unknown).\n         \"\"\"\n         return handle.settlement\n \n     def _collect(self, call_id: str) -> None:\n         window = _active_collector.get()\n         if window is not None:\n             window.record(call_id)\n \n     # --- aggregate ----------------------------------------------------------\n \n     def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n         \"\"\"Aggregate stats; token counts are null when unknown.\n \n         When at least one call has been observed, tokens settle over the recorded\n         calls: none are invented for a window containing a partial/invalid/missing/\n         failed call. With no recorded calls, the legacy manual counters apply (still\n         ``None`` until usage was reported).\n         \"\"\"\n         with self._lock:\n             if self._calls:\n                 return self._settle_window()\n             return {\n                 \"llm_calls\": self.llm_calls,\n                 \"tool_calls\": self.tool_calls,\n                 \"tokens_in\": self.tokens_in if self._usage_reported else None,\n                 \"tokens_out\": self.tokens_out if self._usage_reported else None,\n             }\n \n     def _settle_window(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n         calls = list(self._calls.values())\n         if any(call.status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES for call in calls):\n             tokens_in = tokens_out = None\n         else:\n             tokens_in = sum(call.input_tokens for call in calls)\n             tokens_out = sum(call.output_tokens for call in calls)\n         return {\n             \"llm_calls\": self.llm_calls,\n             \"tool_calls\": self.tool_calls,\n             \"tokens_in\": tokens_in,\n             \"tokens_out\": tokens_out,\n         }\n",
              "additions": 13,

          "text": "There's a race in src/cli/stats_handler.py. 1, \"output_tokens\": 1, \"total_tokens\": units,\n32:             },\n33:         )\n34:         return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=message)])\n35: \n36: \n37: def _invoke(model, handler, run_id, units):\n38:     return model.invoke(str(units), config={\"callbacks\": [handler], \"run_id\": run_id})\n39: \n40: \n41: def test_synchronous_invokes_complete_before_window_exit():\n42:     handler = StatsCallbackHandler()\n43:     model = ScriptedUsageModel(cache=False)\n44:     with handler.track(\"follow_up\") as handle:\n45:         _invoke(model, handler, FIRST, 5)\n46:         _invoke(model, handler, SECOND, 7)\n47:         assert handle.call_ids == (str(FIRST), str(SECOND))\n48: \n49:     settlement = handler.settle(handle)\n50:     assert handle.call_ids == settlement.call_ids == (str(FIRST), str(SECOND))\n51:     assert settlement.pending == ()\n52:     assert settlement.complete is True\n53:     assert settlement.units == 12\n54:     assert tuple((row.status, row.total_tokens) for _, row in settlement.usages) == (\n55:         (\"reported\", 5), (\"reported\", 7),\n56:     )\n57: \n58: \n59: def test_inflight_start_before_membership_can_freeze_partial_numeric_total(monkeypatch):\n60:     handler = StatsCallbackHandler()\n61:     model = ScriptedUsageModel(cache=False)\n62:     before_membership, resume_callback = Event(), Event()\n63:     original_collect = handler._collect\n64: \n65:     def gate_collection(call_id):\n66:         # Test instrumentation only: pause after the global start write and\n67:         # before the unmodified membership operation. No lock is held here.\n68:         if call_id == str(SECOND):\n69:             before_membership.set()\n70:             assert resume_callback.wait(TIMEOUT), \"callback release timed out\"\n71:         original_collect(call_id)\n72: \n73:     monkeypatch.setattr(handler, \"_collect\", gate_collection)\n74:     with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool:\n75:         try:\n76:             with handler.track(\"follow_up\") as handle:\n77:                 _invoke(model, handler, FIRST, 5)\n78:                 inherited = copy_context()\n79:                 job = pool.submit(inherited.run, _invoke, model, handler, SECOND, 7)\n80:                 assert before_membership.wait(TIMEOUT), \"second start never reached the gate\"\n81:                 assert not job.done()\n82:                 assert handler.call(str(FIRST)).status == \"reported\"\n83:                 assert handler.call(str(SECOND)).status == \"missing\"\n84:                 assert handle.call_ids == (str(FIRST),)\n85: \n86:             settlement = handler.settle(handle)\n87:             assert handle.call_ids == settlement.call_ids == (str(FIRST),)\n88:             assert settlement.pending == ()\n89:             assert settlement.complete is True\n90:             assert settlement.units == 5\n91:             assert handler.call(str(SECOND)).status == \"missing\"\n92:         finally:\n93:             resume_callback.set()\n94:         job.result(timeout=TIMEOUT)\n95: \n96:     assert [(row.call_id, row.status, row.total_tokens) for row in handler.calls()] == [\n97:         (str(FIRST), \"reported\", 5), (str(SECOND), \"reported\", 7),\n98:     ]\n99:     assert handler.settle(handle) is settlement\n100:     assert handle.call_ids == settlement.call_ids == (str(FIRST),)\n101:     assert (settlement.pending, settlement.complete, settlement.units) == ((), True, 5)\n\n(End of file - total 101 lines)\n</content>",

A later callback never\n    changes this object, so an unknown settlement cannot become a refund, and\n    a partial window cannot be mistaken for a complete one.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    stage: str\n    call_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n    usages: tuple[tuple[str, CallUsage | None], ...]\n    pending: tuple[str, ...]\n    units: int | None\n    complete: bool\n    expected_calls: int | None\n    count_matches: bool\n\n\nclass TrackHandle:\n    \"\"\"The result of ``track(stage)``: ids seen while active, frozen at exit.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, stage: str, window: _StageWindow) -> None:\n        self.stage = stage\n        self._window = window\n        self._settlement: StageSettlement | None = None\n\n    def _freeze(self, settlement: StageSettlement) -> None:\n        self._settlement = settlement\n\n    @property\n    def call_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        if self._settlement is not None:\n            return self._settlement.call_ids\n        return tuple(self._window.ids)\n\n    @property\n    def settlement(self) -> StageSettlement:\n        if self._settlement is None:\n            raise RuntimeError(\n                \"stage window is still open; the settlement is frozen when track() exits\"\n            )\n        return self._settlement\n\n\ndef _as_int(value: Any) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"A non-negative int from ``value``, or ``None`` when it is not a valid count.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return None\n    if isinstance(value, int) and value >= 0:\n        return value\n    return None\n\n\nclass StatsCallbackHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n    \"\"\"Track LLM calls, tool calls, and per-call token usage.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self.llm_calls = 0\n        self.tool_calls = 0\n        # Legacy manual counters (kept for callers that set them directly, e.g. tests).\n        self.tokens_in = 0\n        self.tokens_out = 0\n        self._usage_reported = False\n        # Per-call records, insertion-ordered by first observation.\n        self._calls: dict[str, CallUsage] = {}\n\n    # --- callbacks ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def on_llm_start(self, serialized, prompts, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        self._on_start(kwargs)\n\n    def on_chat_model_start(self, serialized, messages, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n        self._on_start(kwargs)\n\n    def _on_start(self, kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n        run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n        if run_id is None:\n            return\n        call_id = str(run_id)\n        metadata = kwargs.get(\"metadata\") or {}\n        node = metadata.get(\"langgraph_node\")\n        with self._lock:\n            self.llm_calls += 1\n            # is refused from then on.\n        Callbacks must finish inside the ``with`` block: anything arriving after\n        the freeze only updates the handler's global records.\n        \"\"\"\n        if     try:\n            yield handle\n        finally:\n            with self._lock:\n                ids = window.close()\n                usages = tuple((cid, self._calls.get(cid)) for cid in ids)\n                pending = tuple(\n                    cid for cid, usage in usages\n                    if usage is None or usage.status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES\n                )\n                count_matches = expected_calls is None or len(ids) == expected_calls\n                complete = (\n                    count_matches\n                    and bool(ids)\n                    and all(\n                        usage is not None\n                        and usage.status in {\"reported\", \"explicit_zero\"}\n                        and usage.total_tokens is not None\n                        for _, usage in usages\n                    )\n                )\n                units = (\n                    sum(usage.total_tokens or 0 for _, usage in usages if usage is not None)\n                    if complete else None\n                )\n                handle._freeze(StageSettlement(\n                    stage=stage,\n                    call_ids=ids,\n                    usages=usages,\n                    pending=pending,\n                    units=units,\n                    complete=complete,\n                    expected_calls=expected_calls,\n                    count_matches=count_matches,\n                ))\n            _active_collector.reset(token)\n\n    def settle(self, handle: TrackHandle) -> StageSettlement:\n        \"\"\"Return the immutable _active_collector.get()\n        if window is not None:\n            window.record(call_id)\n\n    # --- aggregate ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Aggregate stats; token counts are null when unknown.\n\n        When at least one call has been observed, tokens settle over the recorded\n        calls: none are           "type": "text",
          "text": "All 181 offline tests pass, ruff clean. Only `src/cli/stats_handler.py` changed; nothing committed.\n\n## What I fixed\n\nThe race: `_on_start` writes the global `self._calls[call_id]` record under `self._lock`, then records window membership via `_collect` *after* releasing the lock. If the `track()` window closes in that gap, the callback is globally `missing` but not in the window's `ids`, so the freeze computed `complete=True` and summed only the collected calls — reporting a partial total as complete.\n\nFix (in the `track` finally-block, still under `self._lock`): scan the global records for calls that are **not yet collected into this window** but are still unfinalized (`status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES`, e.g. `\"missing\"`). Any such in-flight call is added to `pending` and forces `complete=False` / `units=None`. Because the scan runs under the same lock the global write takes, a start either completed its global write (now seen as in-flight → window unknown) or hadn't started yet (not visible → legitimately excluded). No other behavior changed.\n\n## How the tests went\n\n- **C's repro** (`docs/handoffs/test_usage_window_inflight_close (1).py`), run with `PYTHONPATH=src`:\n  - `test_synchronous_invokes_complete_before_window_exit` — **passes** (the normal complete path: `units=12, complete=True`).\n  - `test_inflight_start_before_membership_can_freeze_partial_numeric_total` — **now fails at line 88+**. This is expected: that test is explicitly \"characterization of nanli's close boundary, **not** a desired contract\" — its assertions encode the *old buggy* outcome (`pending == ()`, `complete is True`, `units == 5`). With the fix it correctly diverges: a direct check prints `complete=False units=None pending=(...SECOND)`.\n- Existing offline suite: **181 passed**; `test_stats_calls.py` + `test_token_usage.py` 24 passed. `ruff check` clean.\n\nNote: the handler already had `settle()`/`StageSettlement`/`expected_calls` from a prior revision — I only patched the close-boundary detection. I did not modify C's repro file or any other file, and did not commit.",

              "patch": "Index: src/cli/stats_handler.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/stats_handler.py\t\n+++ src/cli/stats_handler.py\t\n@@ -1,392 +1,416 @@\n \"\"\"Callback handler tracking LLM/tool calls and per-call token usage (E2).\n \n Per-call usage follows ``docs/handoffs/E-interfaces-v1.md`` §E2: every LLM call is a\n ``CallUsage`` keyed by its LangChain ``run_id``. The aggregate entry stays\n ``get_stats()``; ``llm_calls`` counts start-callback events (one invoke emitting two\n starts counts as two), not SDK retries.\n \n Settlement rule for a window of calls: if every call is ``reported`` or\n ``explicit_zero`` the tokens sum once; if any call is ``partial``/``invalid``/\n ``missing``/``failed`` the window is ``None`` (unknown), never a fabricated number.\n \n ``track(stage)`` scopes the call ids seen while it is active using a ``ContextVar``,\n so concurrent threads/tasks do not see each other's ids. At context exit the window\n is closed atomically and frozen into a ``StageSettlement`` (see ``settle``): the\n handle's ``call_ids`` and ``settlement`` never change afterwards. A late callback\n can still update the handler's global records, but it cannot extend a closed\n window, cannot rewrite a frozen settlement, and cannot turn a settled ``None``\n into a refund.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import threading\n from contextlib import contextmanager\n from contextvars import ContextVar\n from dataclasses import dataclass\n from typing import Any\n \n from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\n from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n from langchain_core.outputs import LLMResult\n \n # Statuses that make a settled window unknown (any one -> None for the window).\n _UNKNOWN_STATUSES = frozenset({\"partial\", \"invalid\", \"missing\", \"failed\"})\n \n \n class _StageWindow:\n     \"\"\"Mutable collector for one ``track`` window; closed once at context exit.\n \n     ``closed`` is the important part: a context copied into another thread or an\n     asyncio task keeps a reference to this object, so a late callback must be\n     refused explicitly instead of relying only on ``ContextVar.reset`` (which\n     affects only the context that opened the window).\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self, stage: str) -> None:\n         self.stage = stage\n         self.ids: list[str] = []\n+        # Call ids whose start callback fired while this window was active. Recorded\n+        # at start time (before the delayed ``_collect`` membership step), so an\n+        # in-flight start that has not yet joined ``ids`` is still known to *this*\n+        # window and cannot be confused with an old unrelated unfinished call.\n+        self.started: set[str] = set()\n         self.closed = False\n         self._lock = threading.Lock()\n \n+    def record_started(self, call_id: str) -> None:\n+        with self._lock:\n+            if not self.closed:\n+                self.started.add(call_id)\n+\n     def record(self, call_id: str) -> None:\n         with self._lock:\n             if not self.closed and call_id not in self.ids:\n                 self.ids.append(call_id)\n \n     def close(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n         with self._lock:\n             self.closed = True\n             return tuple(self.ids)\n \n+    def started_ids(self) -> set[str]:\n+        with self._lock:\n+            return set(self.started)\n \n+\n # The collector for the innermost active ``track`` in the current context, if any.\n _active_collector: ContextVar[_StageWindow | None] = ContextVar(\n     \"stats_active_collector\", default=None\n )\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class CallUsage:\n     \"\"\"One LLM call's usage, keyed by the LangChain ``run_id``.\"\"\"\n \n     call_id: str\n     node: str | None\n     status: str  # reported | explicit_zero | partial | invalid | missing | failed\n     source: str  # usage_metadata | token_usage | none\n     input_tokens: int | None\n     output_tokens: int | None\n     total_tokens: int | None  # E local input+output; provider ``total`` not trusted\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class StageSettlement:\n     \"\"\"An immutable snapshot of one ``track`` window, frozen at context exit.\n \n     ``units`` is ``sum(total_tokens)`` only when the window is complete:\n     every recorded call is ``reported``/``explicit_zero`` with a usable total\n     **and** the observed id count matches ``expected_calls`` (when the caller\n     declared it). Otherwise ``units`` is ``None``. A later callback never\n     changes this object, so an unknown settlement cannot become a refund, and\n     a partial window cannot be mistaken for a complete one.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     stage: str\n     call_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n     usages: tuple[tuple[str, CallUsage | None], ...]\n     pending: tuple[str, ...]\n     units: int | None\n     complete: bool\n     expected_calls: int | None\n     count_matches: bool\n \n \n class TrackHandle:\n     \"\"\"The result of ``track(stage)``: ids seen while active, frozen at exit.\"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self, stage: str, window: _StageWindow) -> None:\n         self.stage = stage\n         self._window = window\n         self._settlement: StageSettlement | None = None\n \n     def _freeze(self, settlement: StageSettlement) -> None:\n         self._settlement = settlement\n \n     @property\n     def call_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n         if self._settlement is not None:\n             return self._settlement.call_ids\n         return tuple(self._window.ids)\n \n     @property\n     def settlement(self) -> StageSettlement:\n         if self._settlement is None:\n             raise RuntimeError(\n                 \"stage window is still open; the settlement is frozen when track() exits\"\n             )\n         return self._settlement\n \n \n def _as_int(value: Any) -> int | None:\n     \"\"\"A non-negative int from ``value``, or ``None`` when it is not a valid count.\"\"\"\n     if isinstance(value, bool):\n         return None\n     if isinstance(value, int) and value >= 0:\n         return value\n     return None\n \n \n class StatsCallbackHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n     \"\"\"Track LLM calls, tool calls, and per-call token usage.\"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(self) -> None:\n         super().__init__()\n         self._lock = threading.Lock()\n         self.llm_calls = 0\n         self.tool_calls = 0\n         # Legacy manual counters (kept for callers that set them directly, e.g. tests).\n         self.tokens_in = 0\n         self.tokens_out = 0\n         self._usage_reported = False\n         # Per-call records, insertion-ordered by first observation.\n         self._calls: dict[str, CallUsage] = {}\n \n     # --- callbacks ----------------------------------------------------------\n \n     def on_llm_start(self, serialized, prompts, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         self._on_start(kwargs)\n \n     def on_chat_model_start(self, serialized, messages, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         self._on_start(kwargs)\n \n     def _on_start(self, kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n         run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n         if run_id is None:\n             return\n         call_id = str(run_id)\n         metadata = kwargs.get(\"metadata\") or {}\n         node = metadata.get(\"langgraph_node\")\n         with self._lock:\n             self.llm_calls += 1\n             # A start without a completed end is \"missing\" until an end arrives.\n             self._calls[call_id] = CallUsage(\n                 call_id=call_id,\n                 node=node,\n                 status=\"missing\",\n                 source=\"none\",\n                 input_tokens=None,\n                 output_tokens=None,\n                 total_tokens=None,\n             )\n+            # Tell the active window this call started here, before the (possibly\n+            # delayed) ``_collect`` membership step. This is what lets the freeze\n+            # see an in-flight start without scanning (and being polluted by)\n+            # unrelated, older unfinished calls.\n+            window = _active_collector.get()\n+            if window is not None:\n+                window.record_started(call_id)\n         self._collect(call_id)\n \n     def on_llm_end(self, response: LLMResult, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n         if run_id is None:\n             return\n         call_id = str(run_id)\n         usage = self._extract_usage(response)\n         with self._lock:\n             node = self._calls[call_id].node if call_id in self._calls else None\n             self._calls[call_id] = self._settle(call_id, node, usage)\n         self._collect(call_id)\n \n     def on_llm_error(self, error: BaseException, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         run_id = kwargs.get(\"run_id\")\n         if run_id is None:\n             return\n         call_id = str(run_id)\n         with self._lock:\n             node = self._calls[call_id].node if call_id in self._calls else None\n             self._calls[call_id] = CallUsage(\n                 call_id=call_id,\n                 node=node,\n                 status=\"failed\",\n                 source=\"none\",\n                 input_tokens=None,\n                 output_tokens=None,\n                 total_tokens=None,\n             )\n         self._collect(call_id)\n \n     def on_tool_start(self, serialized, input_str, **kwargs: Any) -> None:\n         with self._lock:\n             self.tool_calls += 1\n \n     # --- usage extraction / settlement -------------------------------------\n \n     @staticmethod\n     def _extract_usage(response: LLMResult) -> tuple[str, Any]:\n         \"\"\"Return ``(source, usage_dict)`` from a response; ``(\"none\", None)`` if absent.\"\"\"\n         try:\n             generation = response.generations[0][0]\n         except (IndexError, TypeError):\n             return \"none\", None\n         message = getattr(generation, \"message\", None)\n         if not isinstance(message, AIMessage):\n             return \"none\", None\n         usage_metadata = getattr(message, \"usage_metadata\", None)\n         if usage_metadata:\n             return \"usage_metadata\", usage_metadata\n         token_usage = getattr(message, \"response_metadata\", {}).get(\"token_usage\")\n         if token_usage:\n             return \"token_usage\", token_usage\n         return \"none\", None\n \n     @staticmethod\n     def _settle(call_id: str, node: str | None, usage: tuple[str, Any]) -> CallUsage:\n         source, data = usage\n         if data is None:\n             return CallUsage(call_id, node, \"missing\", \"none\", None, None, None)\n         input_tokens = _as_int(data.get(\"input_tokens\", data.get(\"prompt_tokens\")))\n         output_tokens = _as_int(data.get(\"output_tokens\", data.get(\"completion_tokens\")))\n         if input_tokens is None and output_tokens is None:\n             status = \"invalid\"\n         elif input_tokens is None or output_tokens is None:\n             status = \"partial\"\n         elif input_tokens == 0 and output_tokens == 0:\n             status = \"explicit_zero\"\n         else:\n             status = \"reported\"\n         total = (\n             input_tokens + output_tokens\n             if input_tokens is not None and output_tokens is not None\n             else None\n         )\n         return CallUsage(\n             call_id, node, status, source, input_tokens, output_tokens, total\n         )\n \n     # --- query --------------------------------------------------------------\n \n     def calls(self) -> tuple[CallUsage, ...]:\n         with self._lock:\n             return tuple(self._calls.values())\n \n     def call(self, call_id: str) -> CallUsage | None:\n         with self._lock:\n             return self._calls.get(call_id)\n \n     @contextmanager\n     def track(self, stage: str, *, expected_calls: int | None = None):\n         \"\"\"Collect ids while active, then atomically close and freeze a settlement.\n \n         ``expected_calls`` is the number of callback ids the caller admitted for\n         this stage. Declaring it makes a window with fewer ids than expected\n         ``units=None`` instead of a partial sum -- this is the answer to C's\n         \"one complete callback, another not collected at the exit boundary\"\n         case. Without a declared count, a window that simply saw fewer callbacks\n         cannot be distinguished from a complete one, so callers that need that\n         guarantee must declare it.\n \n         The freeze takes ``self._lock``, so it cannot race a callback writing a\n         new ``CallUsage``. ``window.close()`` marks the window closed first; a\n         copied context that still holds the window is refused from then on.\n         Callbacks must finish inside the ``with`` block: anything arriving after\n         the freeze only updates the handler's global records.\n         \"\"\"\n         if expected_calls is not None and (\n             isinstance(expected_calls, bool)\n             or not isinstance(expected_calls, int)\n             or expected_calls < 0\n         ):\n             raise ValueError(\"expected_calls must be a non-negative int or None\")\n         window = _StageWindow(stage)\n         handle = TrackHandle(stage, window)\n         token = _active_collector.set(window)\n         try:\n             yield handle\n         finally:\n             with self._lock:\n                 ids = window.close()\n                 usages = tuple((cid, self._calls.get(cid)) for cid in ids)\n                 collected = set(ids)\n-                # Race guard: a start callback writes its global record (under this\n-                # lock) before it records window membership via ``_collect``. If the\n-                # window closes in that gap, the call is globally \"missing\" but not\n-                # yet in ``ids``. Treat any such still-unfinalized call as pending so\n-                # the window is reported unknown, not as a complete partial sum.\n+                # Race guard, scoped to this window: a start callback writes its\n+                # global record (and registers in ``window.started``) under this\n+                # lock, before the possibly-delayed ``_collect`` membership step.\n+                # Any call that started in this window but is not yet in ``ids`` and\n+                # is still unfinalized is in flight: report the window unknown\n+                # rather than a complete partial sum. Calls from earlier windows are\n+                # not in this window's ``started`` set and so cannot poison it.\n                 inflight = tuple(\n                     cid\n-                    for cid, usage in self._calls.items()\n-                    if cid not in collected and usage.status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES\n+                    for cid in sorted(window.started_ids() - collected)\n+                    if (self._calls.get(cid) is None\n+                        or self._calls[cid].status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES)\n                 )\n                 pending = tuple(\n                     cid for cid, usage in usages\n                     if usage is None or usage.status in _UNKNOWN_STATUSES\n                 ) + inflight\n                 count_matches = expected_calls is None or len(ids) == expected_calls\n                 complete = (\n                     count_matches\n                     and not inflight\n                     and bool(ids)\n                     and all(\n                         usage is not None\n                         and usage.status in {\"reported\", \"explicit_zero\"}\n                         and usage.total_tokens is not None\n                         for _, usage in usages\n                     )\n                 )\n                 units = (\n                     sum(usage.total_tokens or 0 for _, usage in usages if usage is not None)\n                     if complete else None\n                 )\n                 handle._freeze(StageSettlement(\n                     stage=stage,\n                     call_ids=ids,\n                     usages=usages,\n                     pending=pending,\n                     units=units,\n                     complete=complete,\n                     expected_calls=expected_calls,\n           "text": "The core problem: the global scan can't tell \"started in this window\" from \"old unfinished call\". I need to record, per window, which callbacks *started* during the window — even those whose `_collect` hasn't run yet.\n\nThe cleanest approach: `_on_start` already knows which window is active in its (copied) context via `_active_collector.get()`. If I add a separate registration inside `_on_start` that doesn't go through `_collect`, the test's gate wouldn't delay it, and the in-flight call would be known to the window immediately — then it'd be *included* (membership recorded at start), which is the other acceptable outcome (\"or the callback gets included\"). But C wants the boundary tested; his test blocks at the membership seam specifically.\n\nLet me reconsider: the user says \"Limit it to callbacks started in this window\". So each window should track the set of callbacks that started while it was the active collector. The natural place: `_on_start` under the handler lock, look up the active window and record the start in a per-window \"started\" set — independent of `_collect`. Then at freeze, in-flight = started-in-window ids not collected. This scopes correctly and excludes old unfinished calls.\n\nBut registering at start means it's recorded before `_collect`'s gate — in C's repro, the start registration happens, then `_collect` is gated. That still produces C's desired unknown outcome AND is scoped to the window.\n\nDoes this conflict with `_collect` being the \"membership\" seam? The window membership used for settlement `call_ids` is `ids` (via `_collect`). The `started` set is only used to detect in-flight. Fine.\n\nLet me implement: add `started: set[str]` to `_StageWindow`, and a method `record_started`. In `_on_start`, after writing global and while holding the lock, also record into the currently active window's `started` set. But careful: `_active_collector.get()` in `_on_start` — in a copied context it returns the same window object. Good.               "newString": "def test_nested_tracks_isolated():\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    outer_rid, inner_rid = _rid(), _rid()\n    with h.track(\"outer\") as outer:\n        _start(h, outer_rid)\n        with h.track(\"inner\") as inner:\n            _start(h, inner_rid)\n        assert outer.call_ids == (str(outer_rid),)\n        assert inner.call_ids == (str(inner_rid),)\n\n\n# --- close-boundary race, scoped to the window ------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_inflight_start_in_window_makes_settlement_unknown():\n    # C's case: a call started while the window is active (its global record is\n    # written and it is registered as started) but its ``_collect`` membership has\n    # not run when the window closes. The window must report unknown, not a\n    # partial sum, even though the collected call alone looks complete.\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    first, second = _rid(), _rid()\n    with h.track(\"follow_up\") as handle:\n        _start(h, first)\n        # Simulate the in-flight start: global record + started registration happen,\n        # but membership (``_collect``) is delayed until after the window closes.\n        real_collect = h._collect\n        h._collect = lambda call_id: None\n        _start(h, second)\n        h._collect = real_collect\n\n    settlement = h.settle(handle)\n    assert handle.call_ids == (str(first),)\n    assert str(second) in settlement.pending\n    assert settlement.complete is False\n    assert settlement.units is None\n\n\ndef test_old_unfinished_call_does_not_poison_later_window():\n    # A callback from an earlier window that never finished is in the *old*\n    # window's started set, not a later window's, so a later complete window is\n    # not dragged to unknown by it.\n    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n    stale = _rid()\n    later = _rid()\n    with h.track(\"first\") as w1:  # start and leave unfinished\n        _start(h, stale)\n    # ... later window completes normally ...\n    with h.track(\"second\") as w2:\n        _start(h, later)\n        _end(h, later, 8, 4)\n\n    s1 = h.settle(w1)\n    s2 = h.settle(w2)\n    assert s1.complete is False  # the stale call is in-flight for its own window\n    assert s2.complete is True\n    assert s2.units == 12\n    assert s2.pending == ()\n\n\n# --- settlement via get_stats() ---------------------------------------------",

The window must report unknown, not a\n+    # partial sum, even though the collected call alone looks complete.\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    first, second = _rid(), _rid()\n+    with h.track(\"follow_up\") as handle:\n+        _start(h, first)\n+        # Simulate the in-flight start: global record + started registration happen,\n+        # but membership (``_collect``) is delayed until after the window closes.\n+        real_collect = h._collect\n+        h._collect = lambda call_id: None\n+        _start(h, second)\n+        h._collect = real_collect\n+\n+    settlement = h.settle(handle)\n+    assert handle.call_ids == (str(first),)\n+    assert str(second) in settlement.pending\n+    assert settlement.complete is False\n+    assert settlement.units is None\n+\n+\n+def test_old_unfinished_call_does_not_poison_later_window():\n+    # A callback from an earlier window that never finished is in the *old*\n+    # window's started set, not a later window's, so a later complete window is\n+    # not dragged to unknown by it.\n+    h = StatsCallbackHandler()\n+    stale = _rid()\n+    later = _rid()\n+    with h.track(\"first\") as w1:  # start and leave unfinished\n+        _start(h, stale)\n+    # ... later window completes normally ...\n+    with h.track(\"second\") as w2:\n+        _start(h, later)\n+        _end(h, later, 8, 4)\n+\n+    s1 = h.settle(w1)\n+    s2 = h.settle(w2)\n+    assert s1.complete is False  # the stale call is in-flight for its own window\n+    assert s2.complete is True\n+    assert s2.units == 12\n+    assert s2.pending == ()\n+\n+\n # --- settlement via get_stats() ---------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_get_stats_sums_all_reported_window():\n",

              "patch": "Index: src/tradingagents/reporting.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/tradingagents/reporting.py\t\n+++ src/tradingagents/reporting.py\t\n@@ -1,136 +1,179 @@\n \"\"\"Reusable report-tree writer shared by the CLI and the programmatic API.\n \n Writes a run's per-section markdown (analysts, research, trading, risk,\n portfolio) plus a consolidated ``complete_report.md`` under ``save_path``. The\n CLI and ``TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports`` both call this, so a headless / API\n run produces the same on-disk report tree a CLI run does.\n \"\"\"\n \n from datetime import datetime\n from pathlib import Path\n \n from tradingagents.agents.rating import run_rating\n \n \n def analyst_names(keys) -> list[str]:\n     \"\"\"The analysts as users select them: the sentiment analyst's key is \"social\".\"\"\"\n     return [\"sentiment\" if key == \"social\" else key for key in keys or []]\n \n \n+def _blocked_guard(final_state: dict) -> dict | None:\n+    \"\"\"The trusted ``guard_result`` when it makes the run non-executable, else ``None``.\n+\n+    A non-executable verdict (``executable is False``, i.e. BLOCK / REVIEW) means the\n+    trader and portfolio proposals must not reach the report. Runs with no\n+    ``guard_result`` (absence is not PASS, but is also not a block) and PASS runs\n+    return ``None`` and are reported unchanged.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    guard = final_state.get(\"guard_result\")\n+    if isinstance(guard, dict) and guard.get(\"executable\") is False:\n+        return guard\n+    return None\n+\n+\n+def guard_disposition(guard: dict) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"The non-executable disposition line shown in place of the decision.\"\"\"\n+    verdict = guard.get(\"verdict\", \"REVIEW\")\n+    reason = guard.get(\"reason_code\") or \"UNKNOWN\"\n+    return f\"GUARD {verdict} ({reason}): non-executable disposition\"\n+\n+\n def _header(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> str:\n     \"\"\"The report's title and what produced it: analysis date, version, models, analysts, vendors.\"\"\"\n     lines = [f\"# Trading Analysis Report: {ticker}\", \"\"]\n     if final_state.get(\"trade_date\"):\n         lines.append(f\"- Analysis date: {final_state['trade_date']}\")\n-    if final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\"):\n+    guard = _blocked_guard(final_state)\n+    if guard is not None:\n+        # A blocked/review run has no tradeable rating; show the guard disposition.\n+        lines.append(f\"- {guard_disposition(guard)}\")\n+    elif final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\"):\n         lines.append(f\"- Rating: {run_rating(final_state)}\")\n     lines.append(f\"- Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\")\n     if settings:\n         s = settings.get\n         deep_provider = s(\"deep_think_provider\") or s(\"llm_provider\", \"?\")\n         quick_provider = s(\"quick_think_provider\") or s(\"llm_provider\", \"?\")\n         if deep_provider == quick_provider:\n             models = f\"{deep_provider}, deep {s('deep_think_llm', '?')}, quick {s('quick_think_llm', '?')}\"\n         else:   # each tier on its own provider (#1440)\n             models = (f\"deep {deep_provider} {s('deep_think_llm', '?')}, \"\n                       f\"quick {quick_provider} {s('quick_think_llm', '?')}\")\n         lines.append(f\"- TradingAgents {s('version', '?')}: {models}\")\n         lines.append(f\"- Analysts: {', '.join(analyst_names(s('analysts')))}; \"\n                      f\"research debate rounds {s('max_debate_rounds', '?')}, \"\n                      f\"risk debate rounds {s('max_risk_discuss_rounds', '?')}\")\n         vendors = {**(s(\"data_vendors\") or {}), **(s(\"tool_vendors\") or {})}\n         if vendors:\n             lines.append(\"- Data vendors: \" + \", \".join(f\"{k} {v}\" for k, v in vendors.items()))\n     if final_state.get(\"memory_note\"):\n         lines.append(f\"- Memory log: {final_state['memory_note']}\")\n     return \"\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\\n\"\n \n \n # The report's sections in order: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, state path)]).\n _SECTIONS = (\n     (\"I. Analyst Team Reports\", \"1_analysts\", (\n         (\"Market Analyst\", \"market.md\", (\"market_report\",)),\n         (\"Sentiment Analyst\", \"sentiment.md\", (\"sentiment_report\",)),\n         (\"News Analyst\", \"news.md\", (\"news_report\",)),\n         (\"Fundamentals Analyst\", \"fundamentals.md\", (\"fundamentals_report\",)),\n     )),\n     (\"II. Research Team Decision\", \"2_research\", (\n         (\"Bull Researcher\", \"bull.md\", (\"investment_debate_state\", \"bull_history\")),\n         (\"Bear Researcher\", \"bear.md\", (\"investment_debate_state\", \"bear_history\")),\n         (\"Research Manager\", \"manager.md\", (\"investment_plan\",)),\n     )),\n     (\"III. Trading Team Plan\", \"3_trading\", (\n         (\"Trader\", \"trader.md\", (\"trader_investment_plan\",)),\n     )),\n     (\"IV. Risk Management Team Decision\", \"4_risk\", (\n         (\"Aggressive Analyst\", \"aggressive.md\", (\"risk_debate_state\", \"aggressive_history\")),\n         (\"Conservative Analyst\", \"conservative.md\", (\"risk_debate_state\", \"conservative_history\")),\n         (\"Neutral Analyst\", \"neutral.md\", (\"risk_debate_state\", \"neutral_history\")),\n     )),\n     (\"V. Portfolio Manager Decision\", \"5_portfolio\", (\n         (\"Portfolio Manager\", \"decision.md\", (\"final_trade_decision\",)),\n     )),\n )\n \n \n def _report_parts(final_state: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]]]:\n-    \"\"\"The sections with something to say: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, text)]).\"\"\"\n+    \"\"\"The sections with something to say: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, text)]).\n+\n+    A non-executable guard hides the trade proposals: the Trading Team plan is\n+    dropped entirely, and the Portfolio Manager decision is replaced by the guard\n+    verdict and reason. Analyst, research, and risk evidence are kept. Everything\n+    else (PASS runs, runs without a ``guard_result``) is unchanged.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    guard = _blocked_guard(final_state)\n     parts = []\n     for heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:\n+        if guard is not None and folder == \"3_trading\":\n+            # No trader proposal on a non-executable run.\n+            continue\n         written = []\n         for agent, filename, path in agents:\n+            if guard is not None and _matches_decision(path):\n+                written.append((agent, filename, guard_disposition(guard)))\n+                continue\n             value = final_state\n             for key in path:\n                 value = (value or {}).get(key)\n             if value:\n                 written.append((agent, filename, value))\n         if written:\n             parts.append((heading, folder, written))\n     return parts\n \n \n+def _matches_decision(path: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:\n+    \"\"\"True for the Portfolio Manager decision path (``final_trade_decision``).\"\"\"\n+    return path == (\"final_trade_decision\",)\n+\n+\n def write_report_tree(final_state: dict, ticker: str, save_path, settings: dict | None = None,\n                       html: bool = True) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Save a completed run's reports to ``save_path``; return the complete-report path.\n \n     ``settings`` (``TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()``) adds what produced the run\n     to the report's header. ``html`` also writes ``complete_report.html``, one\n     self-contained page of the same report (#1419).\n     Reusing a directory replaces the generated report files, removing sections\n     absent from this run and disabled HTML. Other files and directories are kept.\n     \"\"\"\n     save_path = Path(save_path)\n     save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     parts = _report_parts(final_state)\n     sections = []\n     for heading, folder, written in parts:\n         (save_path / folder).mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n         for _agent, filename, text in written:\n             (save_path / folder / filename).write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n         content = \"\\n\\n\".join(f\"### {agent}\\n{text}\" for agent, _filename, text in written)\n         sections.append(f\"## {heading}\\n\\n{content}\")\n \n     (save_path / \"complete_report.md\").write_text(\n         _header(ticker, final_state, settings) + \"\\n\\n\".join(sections), encoding=\"utf-8\"\n     )\n     if html:\n         from tradingagents.report_html import render_report\n \n         (save_path / \"complete_report.html\").write_text(\n             render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts), encoding=\"utf-8\"\n         )\n     else:\n         (save_path / \"complete_report.html\").unlink(missing_ok=True)\n \n     # Reconcile only the filenames owned by this writer; never clear the tree,\n     # since callers may keep notes or other artifacts alongside the reports.\n     current_files = {\n         (folder, filename)\n         for _heading, folder, written in parts\n         for _agent, filename, _text in written\n     }\n     for _heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:\n         for _agent, filename, _path in agents:\n             if (folder, filename) not in current_files:\n                 (save_path / folder / filename).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n     return save_path / \"complete_report.md\"\n",
              "additions": 45,
              "deletions": 2,
              "status": "modified"
            },

              "file": "test/offline/test_guard_report_masking.py",
              "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_guard_report_masking.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_guard_report_masking.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_guard_report_masking.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,184 @@\n+\"\"\"Guard-to-report masking: a non-executable verdict drops the trade proposals.\n+\n+When ``final_state[\"guard_result\"]`` has ``executable is False`` (BLOCK / REVIEW),\n+the public report must not contain the trader plan or the portfolio proposal; the\n+decision is replaced by the guard verdict and reason. Analyst evidence stays. Runs\n+with no ``guard_result`` are unchanged, and PASS (executable True) keeps proposals.\n+\n+Covers both ``reporting.write_report_tree`` (markdown tree + section files) and\n+``report_html.render_report`` so the HTML page cannot leak either.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import re\n+from html import unescape\n+\n+from tradingagents.reporting import write_report_tree\n+\n+TICKER = \"AAPL\"\n+ANALYST_EVIDENCE = \"ANALYST-EVIDENCE: volume was above its monthly median.\"\n+TRADER_TEXT = (\n+    \"**Rating**: Buy [TRADER-RATING]\\n\\n\"\n+    \"**Entry Price**: 123.456789\\n\\n\"\n+    \"**Action**: Buy [TRADER-ACTION]\\n\\n\"\n+    \"FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: Buy [TRADER-PROPOSAL]\"\n+)\n+PM_TEXT = (\n+    \"Rating: Overweight 678.987654 [PM-PRICE]\\n\\n\"\n+    \"Action: Buy [PM-ACTION]\\n\\n\"\n+    \"FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: Buy [PM-PROPOSAL]\"\n+)\n+PROPOSAL_LINE = \"FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL:\"\n+\n+TRADER_MARKERS = [\"TRADER-RATING\", \"123.456789\", \"TRADER-ACTION\", \"TRADER-PROPOSAL\"]\n+PM_MARKERS = [\"Rating: Overweight\", \"678.987654\", \"PM-ACTION\", \"PM-PROPOSAL\"]\n+\n+\n+def _state(guard_result=None):\n+    state = {\n+        \"company_of_interest\": TICKER,\n+        \"trade_date\": \"2026-01-09\",\n+        \"market_report\": ANALYST_EVIDENCE,\n+        \"investment_plan\": \"Research notes on the volume pattern.\",\n+        \"trader_investment_plan\": TRADER_TEXT,\n+        \"final_trade_decision\": PM_TEXT,\n+    }\n+    if guard_result is not None:\n+        state[\"guard_result\"] = guard_result\n+    return state\n+\n+\n+def _guard(verdict, executable, reason_code):\n+    return {\n+        \"contract\": \"validation-decision/1.1\",\n+        \"verdict\": verdict,\n+        \"reason_code\": reason_code,\n+        \"checkpoint\": \"final\",\n+        \"executable\": executable,\n+        \"rules_hit\": [],\n+    }\n+\n+\n+def _text(path):\n+    raw = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n+    if path.suffix == \".html\":\n+        raw = unescape(re.sub(r\"<[^>]+>\", \"\", raw))\n+    return \" \".join(raw.replace(\"**\", \"\").split())\n+\n+\n+def _artifacts(root):\n+    return {p.relative_to(root).as_posix(): _text(p) for p in root.rglob(\"*\") if p.is_file()}\n+\n+\n+def _assert_no_leak(artifacts):\n+    forbidden = TRADER_MARKERS + PM_MARKERS + [f\"{PROPOSAL_LINE} Buy [TRADER-PROPOSAL]\",\n+                                              f\"{PROPOSAL_LINE} Buy [PM-PROPOSAL]\"]\n+    leaks = [\n+        f\"{name}: {marker!r}\"\n+        for name, text in sorted(artifacts.items())\n+        for marker in forbidden if marker in text\n+    ]\n+    assert not leaks, \"\\n\".join(leaks)\n+    assert all(PROPOSAL_LINE not in text for text in artifacts.values())\n+\n+\n+# --- non-executable: BLOCK / REVIEW -----------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_block_drops_trader_and_replaces_decision(tmp_path):\n+    final_state = _state(_guard(\"BLOCK\", False, \"CAP_EXCEEDED\"))\n+    write_report_tree(final_state, TICKER, tmp_path, html=True)\n+    artifacts = _artifacts(tmp_path)\n+\n+    # Analyst evidence and research kept; trader section gone.\n+    assert ANALYST_EVIDENCE in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"]\n+    assert ANALYST_EVIDENCE in artifacts[\"1_analysts/market.md\"]\n+    assert \"3_trading/trader.md\" not in artifacts\n+    # Decision file exists but carries the guard disposition, not the proposal.\n+    disposition = \"GUARD BLOCK (CAP_EXCEEDED): non-executable disposition\"\n+    assert disposition in artifacts[\"5_portfolio/decision.md\"]\n+    assert disposition in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"]\n+    assert disposition in artifacts[\"complete_report.html\"]\n+\n+    _assert_no_leak(artifacts)\n+\n+\n+def test_review_drops_trader_and_replaces_decision(tmp_path):\n+    final_state = _state(_guard(\"REVIEW\", False, \"POSITION_UNKNOWN\"))\n+    write_report_tree(final_state, TICKER, tmp_path, html=False)\n+    artifacts = _artifacts(tmp_path)\n+    assert ANALYST_EVIDENCE in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"]\n+    assert \"3_trading/trader.md\" not in artifacts\n+    disposition = \"GUARD REVIEW (POSITION_UNKNOWN): non-executable disposition\"\n+    assert disposition in artifacts[\"5_portfolio/decision.md\"]\n+    # No HTML written when html=False.\n+    assert \"complete_report.html\" not in artifacts\n+    _assert_no_leak(artifacts)\n+\n+\n+# --- executable: PASS keeps proposals ---------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_pass_keeps_trader_and_portfolio_proposals(tmp_path):\n+    final_state = _state(_guard(\"PASS\", True, \"PASS\"))\n+    write_report_tree(final_state, TICKER, tmp_path, html=True)\n+    artifacts = _artifacts(tmp_path)\n+    assert \"3_trading/trader.md\" in artifacts\n+    for marker in TRADER_MARKERS:\n+        assert marker in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"], marker\n+        assert marker in artifacts[\"3_trading/trader.md\"], marker\n+    for marker in PM_MARKERS:\n+        assert marker in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"], marker\n+    assert PROPOSAL_LINE in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"]\n+\n+\n+# --- no guard_result: unchanged behaviour -----------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_no_guard_result_is_unchanged(tmp_path):\n+    final_state = _state(guard_result=None)\n+    write_report_tree(final_state, TICKER, tmp_path, html=False)\n+    artifacts = _artifacts(tmp_path)\n+    assert \"3_trading/trader.md\" in artifacts\n+    assert artifacts[\"3_trading/trader.md\"] == \" \".join(TRADER_TEXT.replace(\"**\", \"\").split())\n+    for marker in TRADER_MARKERS:\n+        assert marker in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"], marker\n+    for marker in PM_MARKERS:\n+        assert marker in artifacts[\"complete_report.md\"], marker\n+\n+\n+def test_guard_result_executable_true_but_unknown_verdict_behaves_as_executable(tmp_path):\n+    # Only executable is False masks; executable True (any verdict label) keeps proposals.\n+    final_state = _state({\"executable\": True})\n+    write_report_tree(final_state, TICKER, tmp_path, html=False)\n+    artifacts = _artifacts(tmp_path)\n+    assert \"3_trading/trader.md\" in artifacts\n+\n+\n+# --- rewrite: PASS then BLOCK in the same directory -------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_pass_then_block_removes_trader_section_file(tmp_path):\n+    write_report_tree(_state(_guard(\"PASS\", True, \"PASS\")), TICKER, tmp_path, html=True)\n+    assert (tmp_path / \"3_trading\" / \"trader.md\").exists()\n+\n+    write_report_tree(_state(_guard(\"BLOCK\", False, \"CAP_EXCEEDED\")), TICKER, tmp_path, html=True)\n+    artifacts = _artifacts(tmp_path)\n+    # The stale executable proposal section file is reconciled away.\n+    assert \"3_trading/trader.md\" not in artifacts\n+    assert (tmp_path / \"3_trading\" / \"trader.md\").exists() is False\n+    _assert_no_leak(artifacts)\n+\n+\n+# --- HTML renderer directly -------------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_render_report_blocked_suppresses_rating(tmp_path):\n+    final_state = _state(_guard(\"BLOCK\", False, \"CAP_EXCEEDED\"))\n+    write_report_tree(final_state, TICKER, tmp_path, html=True)\n+    page = _text(tmp_path / \"complete_report.html\")\n+    # The tradeable rating the PM wrote must not appear in the masthead.\n+    assert \"Overweight\" not in page\n+    assert \"GUARD BLOCK (CAP_EXCEEDED)\" in page\n+    _assert_no_leak(_artifacts(tmp_path))\n",
