Analyst Team Reports\", \"1_analysts\", (\n        (\"Market Analyst\", \"market.md\", (\"market_report\",)),\n        (\"Sentiment Analyst\", \"sentiment.md\", (\"sentiment_report\",)),\n        (\"News Analyst\", \"news.md\", (\"news_report\",)),\n        (\"Fundamentals Analyst\", \"fundamentals.md\", (\"fundamentals_report\",)),\n    )),\n    (\"II. Research Team Decision\", \"2_research\", (\n        (\"Bull Researcher\", \"bull.md\", (\"investment_debate_state\", \"bull_history\")),\n        (\"Bear Researcher\", \"bear.md\", (\"investment_debate_state\", \"bear_history\")),\n        (\"Research Manager\", \"manager.md\", (\"investment_plan\",)),\n    )),\n    (\"III. Trading Team Plan\", \"3_trading\", (\n        (\"Trader\", \"trader.md\", (\"trader_investment_plan\",)),\n    )),\n    (\"IV. Risk Management Team Decision\", \"4_risk\", (\n        (\"Aggressive Analyst\", \"aggressive.md\", (\"risk_debate_state\", \"aggressive_history\")),\n        (\"Conservative Analyst\", \"conservative.md\", (\"risk_debate_state\", \"conservative_history\")),\n        (\"Neutral Analyst\", \"neutral.md\", (\"risk_debate_state\", \"neutral_history\")),\n    )),\n    (\"V. Portfolio Manager Decision\", \"5_portfolio\", (\n        (\"Portfolio Manager\", \"decision.md\", (\"final_trade_decision\",)),\n    )),\n)\n\n\ndef _report_parts(final_state: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]]]:\n    \"\"\"The sections with something to say: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, text)]).\"\"\"\n    parts = []\n    for heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:\n        written = []\n        for agent, filename, path in agents:\n            value = final_state\n            for key in path:\n                value = (value or {}).get(key)\n            if value:\n                written.append((agent, filename, value))\n        if written:\n            parts.append((heading, folder, written))\n    return parts\n\n\ndef write_report_tree(final_state: dict, ticker: str, save_path, settings: dict | None = None,\n                      html: bool = True) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Save a completed run's reports to ``save_path``; return the complete-report path.\n\n    ``settings`` (``TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()``) adds what produced the run\n    to the report's header. ``html`` also writes ``complete_report.html``, one\n    self-contained page of the same report (#1419).\n    Reusing a directory replaces the generated report files, removing sections\n    absent from this run and disabled HTML.             "output": "\"\"\"Shared 5-tier rating vocabulary and a deterministic heuristic parser.\n\nThe same five-tier scale (Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell) is used by:\n- The Research Manager (investment plan recommendation)\n- The Portfolio Manager (final position decision; its free-text fallback is read here)\n- The memory log (rating tag stored alongside each decision entry)\n\nCentralising it here avoids drift between those call sites.\n\n``extract_rating`` returns ``None`` when no rating can be found, and every\ncaller turns that into ``REVIEW`` rather than a tradeable position: a decision\nnobody can read is not a Hold, and a Hold recorded in its place is quoted back to\nthe next run as a call that was never made (#1170).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\n\n# Canonical, ordered 5-tier scale (most bullish to most bearish).\nRATINGS_5_TIER: tuple[str, ...] = (\n    \"Buy\", \"Overweight\", \"Hold\", \"Underweight\", \"Sell\",\n)\n\n# Signal emitted when the model's decision has no recognizable rating. It is not\n# a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than\n# silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum\n# (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.\nRATING_REVIEW = \"REVIEW\"\n\n_RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}\n\n# Matches \"Rating: X\" / \"rating - X\" / \"Rating — **X**\" — tolerates markdown\n# bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. \"rating\"\n# must start a word, so \"Operating margin: Sell-side\" is not a label.\n_RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<![a-z])rating\\b[^:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(\\w+)\",\n                              re.IGNORECASE)\n\n# The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to\n# open with (\"- **Rating**: X\", \"**Final Rating**: X\", \"## Our rating - X\"): an\n# optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the\n# decision itself before \"rating\". \"Consensus rating: Buy\" or \"Trader's rating:\n# Buy\" is someone else's rating.\n_OWN_QUALIFIER = r\"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\\s+)*\"\n_RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(\n    r\"\\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\\u2022]|\\d+[.)])\\s+)?[\\s*_#]*\" + _OWN_QUALIFIER\n    + r\"rating[^\\w:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(?P<value>\\w+)\",\n    re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# A line presenting the scale rather than a decision (\"Rating Scale: Buy, ...\").\n_RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r\"rating\\s*(scale|options|legend)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\ndef extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.\n\n    Reads an explicit \"Rating: X\" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the\n    NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``\n    matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own\n",

Overweight\", \"678.987654\", \"PM-ACTION\", \"PM-PROPOSAL\"]\n\n\ndef _state(guard_result=None):\n    state = {\n        \"company_of_interest\": TICKER,\n        \"trade_date\": \"2026-01-09\",\n \"rules_hit\": [],\n    }\n\n\ndef _text(path):\n    raw = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    if path.suffix == \".html\":\n        raw = unescape(re.sub(r\"<[^>]+>\", \"\", raw))\n    return \" Runs with no\n+    ``guard_result`` (absence is not PASS, but is also not a block) and PASS runs\n+    return ``None`` and are reported unchanged.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    guard = final_state.get(\"guard_result\")\n+    if isinstance(guard, dict) and guard.get(\"executable\") is False:\n+        return guard\n+    return None\n+\n+\n+def guard_disposition(guard: dict) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"The non-executable disposition line shown in place of the decision.\"\"\"\n+    verdict = guard.get(\"verdict\", \"REVIEW\")\n+    reason = guard.get(\"reason_code\") or \"UNKNOWN\"\n+    return f\"GUARD {verdict} ({reason}): non-executable disposition\"\n+\n+\n def _header(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> str:\n     \"\"\"The report's title and what produced it: analysis date, version, models, analysts, vendors.\"\"\"\n     lines = [f\"# Trading Analysis Report: {ticker}\", \"\"]\n     if final_state.get(\"trade_date\"):\n         lines.append(f\"- Analysis date: {final_state['trade_date']}\")\n-    if final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\"):\n+    guard = _blocked_guard(final_state)\n+    if guard is not None:\n+        # A blocked/review run has no tradeable rating; show the guard disposition.\n+        lines.append(f\"- {guard_disposition(guard)}\")\n+    elif final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\"):\n         lines.append(f\"- Rating: {run_rating(final_state)}\")\n     lines.append(f\"- Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\")\n     if settings:\n         s = settings.get\n",

              "newString": "def _report_parts(final_state: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]]]:\n    \"\"\"The sections with something to say: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, text)]).\n\n    A non-executable guard hides the trade proposals: the Trading Team plan is\n    dropped entirely, and the Portfolio Manager decision is replaced by the guard\n    verdict and reason.         {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "All green. Not committed.\n\n## Summary\n\nImplemented guard-to-report masking so a non-executable verdict can't leak the trade proposal into either the markdown tree or the HTML page.\n\n**`src/tradingagents/reporting.py`**\n- Added `_blocked_guard(final_state)` → returns the `guard_result` only when it's a dict with `executable is False`; otherwise `None`.\n- Added `guard_disposition(guard)` → `GUARD {verdict} ({reason_code}): non-executable disposition` (matches C's probe string).\n- `_report_parts`: when blocked, drops the whole **Trading Team Plan** section (`3_trading/trader.md`) and replaces the **Portfolio Manager decision** (`final_trade_decision`) with the disposition line. Analyst (`1_analysts`), research (`2_research`) and risk (`4_risk`) evidence are kept. PASS and no-`guard_result` runs are unchanged.\n- `_header`: when blocked, shows the guard disposition instead of `Rating: …`.\n- The existing reconciliation loop removes stale files, so a PASS→BLOCK rewrite deletes the old `trader.md`.\n\n**`src/tradingagents/report_html.py`**\n- `render_report`: when blocked, suppresses the masthead `run_rating` (no leaked \"Overweight\") and adds a `Guard` detail row with the disposition. It renders the same `parts` from `_report_parts`, so the trader/PM masking is identical — the page can't leak either.\n\n**Tests** — `test/offline/test_guard_report_masking.py` (7): BLOCK and REVIEW drop the trader section and replace the decision (markdown tree + section file + HTML); PASS keeps both proposals; no-`guard_result` unchanged; executable-True keeps proposals; PASS→BLOCK rewrite removes `trader.md`; HTML masthead suppresses the rating and shows the disposition. Every masked case asserts no TRADER/PM markers and no `FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL:` leak across all generated files.\n\n**Results**\n- New tests: 7 passed. Existing `tests/test_reporting.py` + `tests/test_report_html.py`: 34 passed total.\n- Full suite: **1602 passed, 1 skipped** (optional bedrock). `ruff check src tests test` clean.\n- C's standalone probe `docs/handoffs/.../test_blocked_report_masking.py` can't run here: it depends on D/C's `portfolio_manager.create_portfolio_manager` producing `guard_result` and on integration-branch `schemas` — those producers aren't in this baseline. My tests exercise the identical masking contract (same markers, disposition string, and per-file leak checks) with a synthetic `guard_result`.\n\nNo other files touched. Not committed.",

              "file": "src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\t\n+++ src/tradingagents/run_recorder.py\t\n@@ -1,144 +1,163 @@\n \"\"\"Deterministic run manifest recorder (docs/contracts/run-event.md).\n \n Records one analysis run as a JSON manifest so runs can be compared and\n prompt/model changes can be gated. The recorder never reads the wall clock or a\n random source: ``created_at``, ``run_id`` and ``version`` are supplied by the\n caller, so identical inputs produce byte-identical output (\"byte-stable\n manifest\"). Fields owned by other members (``stop_reason`` for C,\n ``prompt_hashes`` for B, ``evidence_snapshot`` for A) are stored opaquely and are\n not validated here.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import json\n+import os\n import re\n+import tempfile\n from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from pathlib import Path\n \n SCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n \n RUN_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n \n _STRING_FIELDS = (\"run_id\", \"created_at\", \"version\", \"ticker\", \"trade_date\", \"asset_type\")\n \n _REQUIRED_FIELDS = (\n     \"schema_version\",\n     \"run_id\",\n     \"created_at\",\n     \"version\",\n     \"ticker\",\n     \"trade_date\",\n     \"asset_type\",\n     \"outcome\",\n     \"config_snapshot\",\n     \"prompt_hashes\",\n     \"evidence_snapshot\",\n     \"usage\",\n     \"duration_seconds\",\n     \"failure\",\n     \"stop_reason\",\n )\n \n # Keys that must never reach disk: their names carry credentials or endpoints.\n _SECRET_SUFFIXES = (\"_api_key\", \"_key\", \"_token\", \"_password\")\n _SECRET_EXACT = (\"backend_url\",)\n \n \n def _is_secret_key(name: str) -> bool:\n     return name in _SECRET_EXACT or name.endswith(_SECRET_SUFFIXES)\n \n \n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class RunEvent:\n     \"\"\"One run's record. Every field is required except ``schema_version``.\n \n     Omitting a required field raises ``TypeError`` at construction, so the\n     manifest cannot be built half-formed. ``frozen`` keeps a recorded event\n     immutable; adjust by constructing a new one.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     run_id: str\n     created_at: str\n     version: str\n     ticker: str\n     trade_date: str\n     asset_type: str\n     outcome: str | None\n     config_snapshot: dict\n     prompt_hashes: dict\n     evidence_snapshot: dict | None\n     usage: dict\n     duration_seconds: float | None\n     failure: str | None\n     stop_reason: str | None\n     schema_version: int = SCHEMA_VERSION\n \n \n def build_run_id(variant: str, ticker: str, trade_date: str, repeat: int, at: datetime) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A stable, filename-safe run id: ``<variant>-<ticker>-<trade_date>-r<n>-<stamp>``.\n \n     ``at`` is passed in; the clock is never read here. Inputs are **lowercased**\n     (not rejected) so the id always satisfies ``RUN_ID_PATTERN`` regardless of\n     how the caller spelled the variant or ticker. ``at`` is normalized to UTC and\n     rendered ``YYYYMMDDtHHMM`` (e.g. ``20261121t1200``). ``repeat`` is a 1-based\n     index, so values below 1 are rejected.\n     \"\"\"\n     if repeat < 1:\n         raise ValueError(f\"repeat must be >= 1, got {repeat!r}\")\n     if at.tzinfo is None:\n         at = at.replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n     stamp = at.astimezone(UTC).strftime(\"%Y%m%dt%H%M\")\n     return f\"{variant.lower()}-{ticker.lower()}-{trade_date}-r{repeat}-{stamp}\"\n \n \n def _validated_manifest(event: RunEvent) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Validate ``event`` and return the dict that is written to disk.\"\"\"\n     if event.schema_version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"unsupported schema_version {event.schema_version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\"\n         )\n     if not RUN_ID_PATTERN.match(event.run_id):\n         raise ValueError(f\"invalid run_id {event.run_id!r}; must match {RUN_ID_PATTERN.pattern}\")\n     for name in _STRING_FIELDS:\n         value = getattr(event, name)\n         if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n             raise ValueError(f\"required field {name!r} must be a non-empty string\")\n \n     manifest = asdict(event)\n     manifest[\"config_snapshot\"] = {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in event.config_snapshot.items()\n         if not _is_secret_key(key)\n     }\n     return manifest\n \n \n def write_manifest(event: RunEvent, path) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write ``event`` as a JSON manifest to ``path``; never overwrite.\n \n+    The bytes are written to a temp file in the same directory, then published to\n+    ``path`` in one atomic step, so an interruption never leaves a half-written\n+    manifest at the final path. Publishing uses ``os.link``, which fails with\n+    ``FileExistsError`` if ``path`` already exists (no overwrite), and is removed\n+    on any failure.\n+\n     Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported schema version, an invalid\n     ``run_id``, or an empty required string, and ``FileExistsError`` if ``path``\n     already exists.\n     \"\"\"\n     path = Path(path)\n     manifest = _validated_manifest(event)\n     payload = json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n-    # \"x\" refuses to overwrite an existing file atomically.\n-    with open(path, \"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n-        handle.write(payload)\n+\n+    directory = path.parent if str(path.parent) else Path(\".\")\n+    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n+    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\")\n+    tmp_path = Path(tmp_name)\n+    try:\n+        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n+            handle.write(payload)\n+            handle.flush()\n+            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n+        # Single atomic publish; refuses to overwrite an existing manifest.\n+        os.link(tmp_path, path)\n+    finally:\n+        tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n     return path\n \n \n def read_manifest(path) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Read a manifest, rejecting an unsupported ``schema_version`` or a missing key.\"\"\"\n     with open(Path(path), encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n         manifest = json.load(handle)\n     version = manifest.get(\"schema_version\")\n     if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n         raise ValueError(f\"unsupported schema_version {version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\")\n     missing = [name for name in _REQUIRED_FIELDS if name not in manifest]\n     if missing:\n         raise ValueError(f\"manifest missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}\")\n     return manifest\n",
              "additions": 22,
              "deletions": 3,
              "status": "modified"
            },

                "text": "\n\ndef write_manifest(event: RunEvent, path) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write ``event`` as a JSON manifest to ``path``; never overwrite.\n\n    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported schema version, an invalid\n    ``run_id``, or an empty required string, and ``FileExistsError`` if ``path``\n    already exists.\n    \"\"\"\n    path = Path(path)\n    manifest = _validated_manifest(event)\n    payload = json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n    # \"x\" refuses to overwrite an existing file atomically.\n    with open(path, \"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        handle.write(payload)\n    return path\n\n\ndef read_manifest(path) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Read a manifest, rejecting an unsupported ``schema_version`` or a missing key.\"\"\"\n    with open(Path(path), encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        manifest = json.load(handle)\n    version = manifest.get(\"schema_version\")\n    if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:\n        raise ValueError(f\"unsupported schema_version {version!r}; expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}\")\n    missing = [name for name in _REQUIRED_FIELDS if name not in manifest]\n    if missing:\n        raise ValueError(f\"manifest missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}\")\n    return manifest",

              "newString": "def write_manifest(event: RunEvent, path) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write ``event`` as a JSON manifest to ``path``; never overwrite.\n\n    The bytes are written to a temp file in the same directory, then published to\n    ``path`` in one atomic step, so an interruption never leaves a half-written\n    manifest at the final path. Publishing uses ``os.link``, which fails with\n    ``FileExistsError`` if ``path`` already exists (no overwrite), and is removed\n    on any failure.\n\n    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported schema version, an invalid\n    ``run_id``, or an empty required string, and ``FileExistsError`` if ``path``\n    already exists.\n    \"\"\"\n    path = Path(path)\n    manifest = _validated_manifest(event)\n    payload = json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n\n    directory = path.parent if str(path.parent) else Path(\".\")\n    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\")\n    tmp_path = Path(tmp_name)\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            handle.write(payload)\n            handle.flush()\n            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n        # Single atomic publish; refuses to overwrite an existing manifest.\n        os.link(tmp_path, path)\n    finally:\n        tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n    return path",

              "newString": "def test_interrupted_write_leaves_no_half_written_final_file(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    # If the write is interrupted before the atomic publish, nothing must appear at\n    # the final path: the bytes go to a temp file in the same directory first.\n    path = tmp_path / \"manifest.json\"\n\n    import tradingagents.run_recorder as rec\n\n    def explode(src, dst):\n        raise OSError(\"simulated crash before publish\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(rec.os, \"link\", explode)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError):\n        write_manifest(_make_event(), path)\n\n    assert not path.exists(), \"no half-written file may reach the final path\"\n    # The temp file was cleaned up on the failure path too.\n    assert [p for p in tmp_path.iterdir()] == []",

asset_type, created_at, status,\n   checkpoint:{backend,db_relpath,thread_id,step},\n   evidence_snapshot:{snapshot_id,artifact_key,store,source_run_id,captured_at}}``.\n - ``resolve_run(run_id, config) -> ResumeRef`` with typed ``ResumeError.code``.\n \n Three-step semantics: first failure appends an attempt (manifest unclaimed) → resuming\n the same id succeeds, writes the one manifest, and {\n         \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path),\n         \"ticker\": \"NVDA\",\n         \"trade_date\": \"2026-11-20\",\n         \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n     }\n \n \n def       \"step\": 7,\n     }\n     kwargs.update(overrides)\n     return kwargs\n \n \n def _snapshot_kwargs(**overrides):\n     kwargs = {\n         \"snapshot_id\": \"snap-abc\",\n         \"artifact_key\": \"v1/deadbeef.json\",\n         \"store\": \"evidence\",\n         \"source_run_id\": RUN_ID,\n         \"captured_at\": AT,\n     }\n     kwargs.update(overrides)\n     return kwargs\n \n \n def _write_checkpoint(tmp_path, *, run_id=RUN_ID, ticker=\"NVDA\", trade_date=\"2026-11-20\",\n                       asset_type=\"stock\", checkpoint=None, snapshot=None):\n     return write_checkpoint(\n         _config(tmp_path),\n         run_id,\n         ticker=ticker,\n         trade_date=trade_date,\n         asset_type=asset_type,\n         created_at=AT,\n         status=\"incomplete\",\n         checkpoint=checkpoint if checkpoint is not None else _checkpoint_kwargs(),\n         evidence_snapshot=snapshot if snapshot is not None else _snapshot_kwargs(),\n     )\n \n \n # --- attempts.jsonl ----------------------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_first_failure_appends_attempt_and_manifest_slot_free(tmp_path):\n     append_attempt(\n         _config(tmp_path),\n         RUN_ID,\n         at=AT,\n         stage=\"graph\",\n         status=\"failed\",\n         reason_code=\"checkpoint_unreadable\",\n         detail=\"boom\",\n     )\n     attempts_file = Path(tmp_path) / \"runs\" / RUN_ID / \"attempts.jsonl\"\n     assert attempts_file.exists()\n     line = json.loads(attempts_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines()[0])\n     assert line == {\n         \"schema_version\": 1,\n         \"run_id\": RUN_ID,\n         \"at\": AT,\n         \"stage\": \"graph\",\n         \"status\": \"failed\",\n         \"reason_code\": \"checkpoint_unreadable\",\n         \"detail\": \"boom\",\n     }\n     assert not (Path(tmp_path) / \"runs\" / RUN_ID / \"manifest.json\").exists()\n \n \n def assert data[\"run_id\"] == RUN_ID\n     assert data[\"checkpoint\"][\"thread_id\"] == RUN_ID\n     assert data[\"evidence_snapshot\"][\"snapshot_id\"] == \"snap-abc\"\n \n \n # --- resolve_run               "file": "src/cli/run.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/cli/run.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/run.py\t\n+++ src/cli/run.py\t\n@@ -1,721 +1,767 @@\n \"\"\"Running one analysis from the CLI: build the graph, stream it into the live view, save the report.\"\"\"\n \n+import inspect\n import json\n import os\n import re\n import sys\n import time\n import webbrowser\n from dataclasses import replace\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from functools import wraps\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import typer\n from rich.live import Live\n \n from cli.display import (\n     ANALYST_ORDER,\n     AnalystWallTimeTracker,\n     classify_message_type,\n     console,\n     create_layout,\n     display_complete_report,\n     message_buffer,\n     update_analyst_statuses,\n     update_display,\n     update_research_team_status,\n )\n from cli.selections import depth_from_env, get_user_selections, unattended_gaps\n from cli.stats_handler import StatsCallbackHandler\n from tradingagents import __version__\n from tradingagents.agents.rating import is_review, run_rating\n from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.graph.analyst_execution import (\n     build_analyst_execution_plan,\n )\n from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, build_run_id, write_manifest\n \n _VALID_VARIANTS = (\"v0\", \"v1\", \"v2\")\n \n \n def _validate_variant(value: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Accept only a known, lowercase architecture variant slug (``v0``/``v1``/``v2``).\n \n     The value becomes the first segment of the manifest ``run_id`` and a directory\n     name under the results root, so an unknown or unsafe value is rejected rather\n     than interpolated.\n     \"\"\"\n     if value not in _VALID_VARIANTS:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid variant {value!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_VALID_VARIANTS)}\"\n         )\n     return value\n \n \n \n def _run_directory(config: dict, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Where this run writes, with the ticker validated as a path component.\n \n     Every other path that interpolates a ticker checks it first; a value of\n     \"..\" here would place the run outside the results directory.\n     \"\"\"\n     return Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker_component(ticker) / trade_date\n \n \n def _manifest_config_snapshot(config: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Scalars from ``config`` that are safe to record in a run manifest.\n \n     The recorder already drops secret-pattern keys; keeping only scalar values\n     here also excludes nested objects and lists that are not comparable settings.\n     ``results_dir`` is a machine-local output path, not a comparable setting, so it\n     is left out of the manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     return {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in config.items()\n         if key != \"results_dir\"\n         and (isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None)\n     }\n \n \n def write_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     config: dict,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     outcome: str | None,\n     usage: dict,\n     failure: str | None,\n     variant: str,\n     repeat: int,\n     at: datetime,\n     version: str,\n     duration_seconds: float | None = None,\n     started_at: float | None = None,\n     clock=None,\n     stop_reason: str | None = None,\n     evidence_mode: str = \"strict\",\n ) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write this run's manifest to ``<results_dir>/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json``.\n \n     ``stop_reason`` is read from the run's final state by the caller (C owns the\n     value domain); it is ``None`` when the graph did not reach a terminal state.\n     ``prompt_hashes`` (B) is ``{}`` and ``evidence_snapshot`` (A) is ``None`` until\n     those members' contracts land. ``duration_seconds`` is measured from\n     ``started_at`` and ``clock`` (``time.time`` by default) when not supplied;\n     passing both keeps it testable.\n \n     A per-run ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar (E4) is written next to the manifest\n     recording the evidence mode and the facts the run observed. It does not change\n     the RunEvent v1 15 fields.\n     \"\"\"\n     run_id = build_run_id(variant, ticker, trade_date, repeat, at)\n     if duration_seconds is None and started_at is not None:\n         now = (clock or time.time)()\n         duration_seconds = max(0.0, now - started_at)\n \n     event = RunEvent(\n         run_id=run_id,\n         created_at=at.astimezone(UTC).isoformat(),\n         version=version,\n         ticker=ticker,\n         trade_date=trade_date,\n         asset_type=asset_type,\n         outcome=outcome,\n         config_snapshot=_manifest_config_snapshot(config),\n         prompt_hashes={},\n         evidence_snapshot=None,\n         usage=usage,\n         duration_seconds=duration_seconds,\n         failure=failure,\n         stop_reason=stop_reason,\n     )\n     runs_dir = Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"runs\"\n     run_id = _unique_run_id(runs_dir, run_id)\n     event = replace(event, run_id=run_id)\n     manifest_dir = runs_dir / run_id\n     manifest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     path = write_manifest(event, manifest_dir / \"manifest.json\")\n     write_evidence_mode(manifest_dir / \"evidence-mode.json\", run_id, evidence_mode)\n     return path\n \n \n _EVIDENCE_MODES = (\"strict\", \"report_reference\")\n \n \n def write_evidence_mode(path, run_id: str, evidence_mode: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write the E4 ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar recording this run's mode.\n \n     E records facts only; the authoritative action and the mode approval belong to\n     D/C, so those fields are ``None`` here unless a caller later fills them in.\n     \"\"\"\n     if evidence_mode not in _EVIDENCE_MODES:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid evidence_mode {evidence_mode!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_EVIDENCE_MODES)}\"\n         )\n     sidecar = {\n         \"schema_version\": 1,\n         \"run_id\": run_id,\n         \"evidence_mode\": evidence_mode,\n         \"scenario\": None,\n         \"policy_version\": None,\n         \"unknown_time_fields\": [],\n         \"limitations\": [],\n         \"authoritative_action\": None,\n         \"authoritative_reason\": None,\n         \"decided_by\": None,\n         \"snapshot_ref\": {\"snapshot_id\": None, \"artifact_key\": None},\n     }\n     path = Path(path)\n     path.write_text(json.dumps(sidecar, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n     return path\n \n \n def _unique_run_id(runs_dir: Path, run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A run_id whose directory does not exist yet, so a same-minute retry is safe.\n \n     ``build_run_id`` has minute resolution, so two runs started in the same minute\n     (or a retry) produce the same id. Appending ``-<n>`` keeps the id within the\n     recorder's 64-char pattern and never overwrites an earlier manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     pattern = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n     candidate = run_id\n     suffix = 2\n     while (runs_dir / candidate).exists():\n         candidate = f\"{run_id}-{suffix}\"\n         if not pattern.match(candidate):\n             raise ValueError(f\"no free run_id derived from {run_id!r} within 64 chars\")\n         suffix += 1\n     return candidate\n \n \n def _make_manifest_writer(config: dict, selections: dict, stats_handler, started_at=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     \"\"\"Return a ``write(failure=..., outcome=...)`` bound to this run's inputs.\n \n     ``variant`` selects the architecture under test and becomes the first segment\n     of the manifest ``run_id``; ``repeat`` is 1 and ``created_at`` is now, both\n     supplied here so the recorder never reads the clock itself. ``started_at`` is\n     the run's start (``time.time()``); forwarding it lets the manifest record a\n     real duration.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def write(*, failure, outcome, stop_reason=None):\n         return write_run_manifest(\n             config=config,\n             ticker=selections[\"ticker\"],\n             trade_date=selections[\"analysis_date\"],\n             asset_type=selections[\"asset_type\"],\n             outcome=outcome,\n             usage=stats_handler.get_stats(),\n             failure=failure,\n             variant=variant,\n             repeat=1,\n             at=datetime.now(UTC),\n             version=__version__,\n             started_at=started_at,\n             stop_reason=stop_reason,\n             evidence_mode=config.get(\"evidence_mode\", \"strict\"),\n         )\n \n     return write\n \n \n def _finalize_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     write,\n     graph,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     portfolio,\n     final_state,\n     failure: BaseException | None,\n ) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Write the manifest, then dispose of (or keep) the checkpoint.\n \n     The manifest is written **before** the checkpoint is cleared, so a crash in\n     teardown never loses the record. A failed run still writes a manifest with\n     ``failure`` set and keeps its checkpoint for resume; the failure is re-raised.\n     ``stop_reason`` is read from ``final_state`` (C's field) with a ``None``\n     fallback when the run did not reach a terminal state.\n     \"\"\"\n     outcome = None if final_state is None else run_rating(final_state)\n     stop_reason = (final_state or {}).get(\"stop_reason\") if failure is None else None\n     write(failure=None if failure is None else str(failure), outcome=outcome, stop_reason=stop_reason)\n \n     if failure is not None:\n         raise failure\n \n     if final_state is not None:\n         graph.record_decision(ticker, trade_date, final_state)\n     graph.clear_checkpoint_on_success(ticker, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n \n \n def _announce_checkpoint_state(graph, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Say whether this run resumed a saved one, where the user can see it.\n \n     The graph logs this, but nothing in the CLI configures logging and the live\n     view owns the screen, so a resume was invisible.\n     \"\"\"\n     if getattr(graph, \"_resuming\", False):\n         message_buffer.add_message(\n             \"System\", f\"Resuming the saved run for {ticker} on {trade_date}\"\n         )\n     else:\n         message_buffer.add_message(\"System\", f\"Starting fresh for {ticker} on {trade_date}\")\n \n \n def _build_run_config(selections: dict, checkpoint: bool | None) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Assemble the run config from interactive selections, honoring env precedence.\n \n     Round counts and checkpoint follow \"explicit env/flag wins\": an env-applied\n     value on DEFAULT_CONFIG is preserved unless the user overrode it on the CLI.\n     \"\"\"\n     config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n     # Research depth sets both round counts, but an explicit env override\n     # (TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS / _MAX_RISK_ROUNDS) wins over the\n     # interactive selection — leave the env-applied value in place (#977).\n     rounds = ((\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS\", \"max_debate_rounds\"),\n               (\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_RISK_ROUNDS\", \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"))\n     depth_was_asked = not depth_from_env()\n     for env_var, key in rounds:\n         if not os.environ.get(env_var):\n             config[key] = selections[\"research_depth\"]\n         elif depth_was_asked:\n             # The depth question appeared (it is skipped only when both are\n             # set), so say which half of the answer the environment overrode.\n             console.print(\n                 f\"[green]✓ {key} from environment:[/green] {config[key]} \"\n                 f\"(set by {env_var}, so the research depth you chose does not apply to it)\"\n             )\n     config[\"quick_think_llm\"] = selections[\"quick_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"deep_think_llm\"] = selections[\"deep_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"backend_url\"] = selections[\"backend_url\"]\n     config[\"llm_provider\"] = selections[\"llm_provider\"].lower()\n     # Provider-specific thinking configuration. Only the main provider's is\n     # asked; a tier on another provider keeps its configured value (#1440).\n     for key in (\"google_thinking_level\", \"openai_reasoning_effort\", \"anthropic_effort\"):\n         if selections.get(key) is not None:\n             config[key] = selections[key]\n     config[\"output_language\"] = selections.get(\"output_language\", \"English\")\n     # --checkpoint/--no-checkpoint overrides only when explicitly given; omitting\n     # the flag preserves TRADINGAGENTS_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED / the default (#976).\n     if checkpoint is not None:\n         config[\"checkpoint_enabled\"] = checkpoint\n     return config\n \n \n-def _reject_unavailable_variant(variant: str, config: dict | None = None) -> None:\n-    \"\"\"Refuse v1/v2 until C's ``workflow_variant`` key is wired into the graph.\n+def _graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls) -> bool:\n+    \"\"\"Whether ``graph_cls.__init__`` accepts a ``workflow_variant`` keyword.\n \n-    v0 is always allowed. A non-v0 variant is allowed only when ``config`` actually\n-    carries ``workflow_variant`` (C's enable switch); otherwise this raises\n-    ``typer.Exit`` before any model call, so a v0-compatible run is never labelled\n-    v1/v2.\n+    Detection is by signature: an explicit ``workflow_variant`` parameter, or a\n+    ``**kwargs`` catch-all, means the graph can take (and forward) the variant. Run with --variant v0.[/red]\"\n-    )\n-    raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n+    if variant == \"v2\":\n+        console.print(\n+            \"[red]Variant 'v2' is not available yet: the adaptive workflow is not \"\n+            \"delivered. Run with --variant v0.[/red]\"\n+        )\n+        raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n \n \n+def _build_graph(graph_cls, selected_analyst_keys, config, callbacks, *, workflow_variant):\n+    \"\"\"Construct the graph, forwarding ``workflow_variant`` only when accepted.\"\"\"\n+    kwargs = {\"config\": config, \"debug\": True, \"callbacks\": callbacks}\n+    if _graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls):\n+        kwargs[\"workflow_variant\"] = workflow_variant\n+    return graph_cls(selected_analyst_keys, **kwargs)\n+\n+\n+def _effective_manifest_variant(graph, requested: str) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"The variant the graph actually enabled, from ``run_settings()``, else requested.\"\"\"\n+    run_settings = getattr(graph, \"run_settings\", None)\n+    if not callable(run_settings):\n+        return requested\n+    try:\n+        settings = run_settings()\n+    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n+        return requested\n+    if not isinstance(settings, dict):\n+        return requested\n+    return settings.get(\"workflow_variant\") or requested\n+\n+\n def run_analysis(checkpoint: bool | None = None, portfolio=None, flags=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     flags = flags or {}\n     variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n-    # v1/v2 are not implemented in the workflow yet (C's `workflow_variant` key is\n-    # not wired into the graph).           "type": "text",
          "text": "The new spec:\n- Refuse **v2 before any model call** (always — even if graph supports workflow_variant? \"refuse v2 before any model call\" — v2 isn't delivered; refuse it always until explicitly supported). \n- **v1**: allow only when graph accepts `workflow_variant`, forward it.\n- v0: always allowed.\n\nBut `test_run_analysis_rejects_v1_before_model_call` and `test_cli_variant_v1_exits_nonzero` assume v1 always refused — now v1 is refused only if graph doesn't accept `workflow_variant`. The real `TradingAgentsGraph` doesn't → still refused in that default. Those tests monkeypatch `TradingAgentsGraph` with a lambda that doesn't accept the kwarg → detection sees no `workflow_variant` → v1 refused. That still holds! But `test_run_analysis_rejects_v1...` monkeypatches to `lambda *a, **k` which DOES accept kwargs (has `**k`) → my detection would treat `**kwargs` as accepting → v1 allowed → graph constructed (`started` appended) → test fails.\n\nI need to decide: does a `**kwargs` signature count as \"accepts workflow_variant\"? Per the task: \"Detect whether TradingAgentsGraph accepts the workflow_variant keyword\". A `**kwargs` does accept it. But that makes the monkeypatched lambda \"accept\". I should update that test to use a stub without `**kwargs`, since the intent is \"graph that doesn't support it\". I'll rewrite these tests appropriately and add a proper stub-graph test suite.\n\nLet me now design the new helpers and rewrite tests. I'll:\n- Replace `_reject_unavailable_variant(variant, config)` with `_reject_unavailable_variant(variant, graph_cls)`:\n  - v0 → return\n  - v2 → always refuse (typer.Exit)\n  - v1 → if not `_graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls)` → refuse\n- Add `_graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls)`.\n- Add `_effective_manifest_variant(graph, requested)` reading `run_settings().get(\"workflow_variant\", requested)`.\n- Forward variant into graph construction when supported.\n\nLet me write the new test file, then update the old tests in test_c_integration_seams.py to match.",

              "content": "\"\"\"Variant forwarding: detect workflow_variant support instead of a config key.\n\nThe old gate read a ``config[\"workflow_variant\"]`` key that never existed, so v1/v2\nwere always refused. the value is forwarded to the graph.\n- The manifest run_id and config_snapshot use the variant the graph's\n  ``run_settings()`` reports (falling back to the requested one when absent).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport inspect\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime\n\nimport pytest\n\nimport cli.run as cli_run\n\nFIXED_AT = datetime(2026, 11, 22, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)\n\n\nclass _SupportsVariant:\n    \"\"\"Stub graph whose __init__ accepts workflow_variant and reports it.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, analysts=None, config=None, debug=False, callbacks=None, workflow_variant=\"v0\"):\n        self.config = config or {}\n        self.selected_analysts = analysts or []\n        self.workflow_variant = workflow_variant\n        self.received_variant = workflow_variant\n\n    def run_settings(self):\n        return {\"version\": \"0.7.1\", \"workflow_variant\": self.workflow_variant}\n\n\nclass _NoVariant:\n    \"\"\"Stub graph whose __init__ does NOT accept workflow_variant.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, analysts=None, config=None, debug=False, callbacks=None):\n        self.config = config or {}\n        self.selected_analysts = analysts or []\n\n    def run_settings(self):\n        return {\"version\": \"0.7.1\"}\n\n\ndef _graph_cls_without_kwargs():\n    class _Strict:\n        def __init__(self, analysts=None, config=None, debug=False, callbacks=None):\n            pass\n\n        def run_settings(self):\n            return {}\n\n    return _Strict\n\n\n# --- signature detection ----------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_detects_explicit_keyword():\n    assert cli_run._graph_accepts_workflow_variant(_SupportsVariant) is True\n\n\ndef test_detects_absence():\n    assert cli_run._graph_accepts_workflow_variant(_NoVariant) is False\n\n\ndef test_var_kwargs_counts_as_accepting():\n    class _VarKwargs:\n        def __init__(self, **kwargs):\n            pass\n\n    assert cli_run._graph_accepts_workflow_variant(_VarKwargs) is True\n\n\n# --- refusal rules -----------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef pytest.raises(cli_run.typer.Exit):\n        cli_run._reject_unavailable_variant(\"v1\", _NoVariant)\n\n\ndef test_v1_allowed_when_graph_supports_variant():\n assert cli_run._effective_manifest_variant(_NoSettings(), \"v1\") == \"v1\"\n\n\n# --- manifest wiring uses effective variant ---------------------------------\n\n\ndef \"manifest.json\"\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"write_run_manifest\", fake_write_run_manifest)\n\n    class _Stats:\n        def get_stats(self):\n            return {\"llm_calls\": 0,           "type": "text",
          "text": "All green, not committed.\n\n## Summary\n\nThe old gate read a nonexistent `config[\"workflow_variant\"]` key, so v1/v2 were always refused. Replaced with signature detection in `src/cli/run.py`:\n\n- **`_graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls)`** — inspects `graph_cls.__init__` for an explicit `workflow_variant` parameter or a `**kwargs` catch-all.\n- **`_reject_unavailable_variant(variant, graph_cls)`** — v0 always allowed; **v2 refused before any model call** (not delivered) regardless of graph; **v1 allowed only when the graph accepts `workflow_variant`**, else refused with a clear message.\n- **`_build_graph(...)`** — forwards `workflow_variant=variant` to the graph only when accepted.\n- **`_effective_manifest_variant(graph, requested)`** — the variant from `graph.run_settings()[\"workflow_variant\"]`, falling back to the requested one.\n- `run_analysis` now gates with `TradingAgentsGraph`, builds via `_build_graph`, and writes `manifest_variant` (the effective variant) into both manifest call sites, so the run_id first segment and config_snapshot reflect what the graph actually enabled.\n\n**Tests**\n- New `test/offline/test_variant_forwarding.py` (13) with stub graphs: detection (explicit kw / absent / `**kwargs`), v0 allowed, v2 refused even when supported, v1 refused when unsupported / allowed when supported, forwarding, no-forward when unsupported, effective variant from `run_settings`/fallback/missing, and manifest writer uses the effective variant.\n- Updated the obsolete config-key helper tests in `test_c_integration_seams.py` to the new signature-driven behavior (v1 refused before graph construction when unsupported; CLI `--variant v2` exits nonzero).\n\n**Results**: 25 relevant tests pass; full suite **1617 passed / 1 skipped** (optional bedrock); `ruff check src tests test` clean.               "file": "scripts/check_permission_sync.py",
              "patch": "Index: scripts/check_permission_sync.py\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/check_permission_sync.py\t\n+++ scripts/check_permission_sync.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@\n+\"\"\"Permission-sync gate (D3 / D7 §6.2).\n+\n+``.opencode/permissions.jsonc`` is the course artifact describing the intended\n+policy; ``opencode.jsonc`` is what OpenCode actually reads. This gate fails when the\n+two drift in the ways that matter:\n+\n+- every path the artifact marks ``human_only`` or ``protected`` must be covered by\n+  ``opencode.jsonc`` (its ``deny``, ``human_only`` or ``protected`` lists), and\n+- both files' ``default`` must be ``deny`` (default is no read, no write).\n+\n+Usage::\n+\n+    python scripts/check_permission_sync.py [--root <dir>]\n+\n+Exit 0 in sync, 1 on drift (with each problem printed), 2 when an input file is\n+missing (setup defect, not a content defect). Stdlib only; JSONC is parsed with a\n+small comment/trailing-comma stripper that respects string literals.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import fnmatch\n+import json\n+import re\n+import sys\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+OPENCODE = \"opencode.jsonc\"\n+PERMISSIONS = \".opencode/permissions.jsonc\"\n+\n+# Lists whose paths must be covered by the enforced config, and the lists that may\n+# provide the coverage.\n+_REQUIRED_KEYS = (\"human_only\", \"protected\")\n+_COVER_KEYS = (\"deny\", \"human_only\", \"protected\")\n+\n+\n+def _strip_jsonc(text: str) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"Remove ``//`` and ``/* */`` comments and trailing commas, preserving strings.\"\"\"\n+    out = []\n+    i, n = 0, len(text)\n+    in_string = False\n+    while i < n:\n+        ch = text[i]\n+        if in_string:\n+            out.append(ch)\n+            if ch == \"\\\\\" and i + 1 < n:  # keep the escaped char verbatim\n+                out.append(text[i + 1])\n+                i += 2\n+                continue\n+            if ch == '\"':\n+                in_string = False\n+            i += 1\n+            continue\n+        if ch == '\"':\n+            in_string = True\n+            out.append(ch)\n+            i += 1\n+            continue\n+        if ch == \"/\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == \"/\":\n+            i += 2\n+            while i < n and text[i] != \"\\n\":\n+                i += 1\n+            continue\n+        if ch == \"/\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == \"*\":\n+            i += 2\n+            while i + 1 < n and not (text[i] == \"*\" and text[i + 1] == \"/\"):\n+                i += 1\n+            i += 2\n+            continue\n+        out.append(ch)\n+        i += 1\n+    stripped = \"\".join(out)\n+    # Remove trailing commas before a closing brace/bracket (strings are intact).\n+    return re.sub(r\",(\\s*[}\\]])\", r\"\\1\", stripped)\n+\n+\n+def load_jsonc(text: str) -> dict:\n+    \"\"\"Parse JSONC text (comments + trailing commas) into a dict.\"\"\"\n+    return json.loads(_strip_jsonc(text))\n+\n+\n+def _covers(pattern_keys: dict, required: str) -> bool:\n+    \"\"\"Whether any configured pattern covers ``required`` (exact, glob, or dir).\"\"\"\n+    for key in _COVER_KEYS:\n+        for pattern in pattern_keys.get(key) or []:\n+            if pattern == required:\n+                return True\n+            if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(required, pattern):\n+                return True\n+            # A ``dir/**`` pattern covers everything beneath it.\n+            if pattern.endswith(\"/**\"):\n+                prefix = pattern[:-3]\n+                if required == prefix or required.startswith(prefix + \"/\"):\n+                    return True\n+    return False\n+\n+\n+def check(permissions: dict, opencode: dict) -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"Return human-readable drift problems (empty list means in sync).\"\"\"\n+    problems: list[str] = []\n+\n+    if permissions.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n+        problems.append(\n+            f\"{PERMISSIONS}: default is {permissions.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\"\n+        )\n+    if opencode.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n+        problems.append(f\"{OPENCODE}: default is {opencode.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\")\n+\n+    for key in _REQUIRED_KEYS:\n+        for required in permissions.get(key) or []:\n+            if not _covers(opencode, required):\n+                problems.append(\n+                    f\"{OPENCODE} does not cover {key} path {required!r} \"\n+                    f\"from {PERMISSIONS}\"\n+                )\n+    return problems\n+\n+\n+def _parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[Path | None, int]:\n+    \"\"\"Parse args given without the program name (e.g. ``[\"--root\", dir]``).\"\"\"\n+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n+    args = list(argv)\n+    if \"--root\" in args:\n+        idx = args.index(\"--root\")\n+        try:\n+            root = Path(args[idx + 1])\n+        except IndexError:\n+            print(\"usage: check_permission_sync.py [--root <dir>]\", file=sys.stderr)\n+            return None, 2\n+    return root, 0\n+\n+\n+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n+    root, code = _parse_args(argv)\n+    if root is None:\n+        return code\n+\n+    opencode_path = root / OPENCODE\n+    permissions_path = root / PERMISSIONS\n+    for path in (opencode_path, permissions_path):\n+        if not path.exists():\n+            print(f\"[permission-sync] MISSING: {path}\", file=sys.stderr)\n+            return 2\n+\n+    try:\n+        opencode = load_jsonc(opencode_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n+        permissions = load_jsonc(permissions_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n+    except ValueError as exc:\n+        print(f\"[permission-sync] BLOCKED: cannot parse JSONC: {exc}\")\n+        return 1\n+\n+    problems = check(permissions, opencode)\n+    if problems:\n+        print(f\"[permission-sync] BLOCKED: {len(problems)} drift problem(s):\")\n+        for problem in problems:\n+            print(f\"    - {problem}\")\n+        return 1\n+    print(\"[permission-sync] OK: opencode.jsonc covers the protected paths and both default to deny\")\n+    return 0\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))\n",
              "additions": 163,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },

test/offline/test_permission_sync.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@\n+\"\"\"Offline tests for the permission-sync gate (D3 / D7 §6.2).\n+\n+``scripts/check_permission_sync.py`` keeps ``opencode.jsonc`` (the enforced config)\n+in sync with ``.opencode/permissions.jsonc`` (the course artifact): every path the\n+artifact marks ``human_only`` or ``protected`` must be covered by opencode.jsonc, and\n+both files' ``default`` must be ``deny``.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+import sys\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / \"scripts\"))\n+\n+import check_permission_sync as gate  # noqa: E402\n+\n+\n+def _perms(**overrides):\n+    base = {\n+        \"default\": \"deny\",\n+        \"allow\": [],\n+        \"deny\": [\"**/.env\"],\n+        \"human_only\": [\".agent/rules.md\"],\n+        \"protected\": [\"src/tradingagents/dataflows/**\"],\n+    }\n+    base.update(overrides)\n+    return base\n+\n+\n+def _opencode(**overrides):\n+    base = {\n+        \"default\": \"deny\",\n+        \"allow\": [],\n+        \"deny\": [\"**/.env\", \"src/tradingagents/dataflows/**\"],\n+        \"human_only\": [\".agent/rules.md\"],\n+    }\n+    base.update(overrides)\n+    return base\n+\n+\n+# --- JSONC loading -----------------------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_load_jsonc_strips_line_comments_and_trailing_commas():\n+    text = \"\"\"\n+    {\n+      // a line comment\n+      \"default\": \"deny\",\n+      \"list\": [\"a\", \"b\",],  /* trailing comma + block comment */\n+    }\n+    \"\"\"\n+    data = gate.load_jsonc(text)\n+    assert data == {\"default\": \"deny\", \"list\": [\"a\", \"b\"]}\n+\n+\n+def test_load_jsonc_keeps_comment_markers_inside_strings():\n+    text = '{\"url\": \"https://example.test/a//b\", \"note\": \"not /* a comment */\"}'\n+    data = gate.load_jsonc(text)\n+    assert data[\"url\"] == \"https://example.test/a//b\"\n+    assert data[\"note\"] == \"not /* a comment */\"\n+\n+\n+# --- happy path --------------------------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_in_sync_passes():\n+    assert gate.check(_perms(), _opencode()) == []\n+\n+\n+# --- default must be deny ----------------------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_permissions_default_not_deny_blocks():\n+    problems = gate.check(_perms(default=\"allow\"), _opencode())\n+    assert any(\"permissions\" in p and \"default\" in p for p in problems)\n+\n+\n+def test_opencode_default_not_deny_blocks():\n+    problems = gate.check(_perms(), _opencode(default=\"ask\"))\n+    assert any(\"opencode\" in p and \"default\" in p for p in problems)\n+\n+\n+# --- coverage of human_only / protected -------------------------------------\n+\n+\n+def test_uncovered_human_only_blocks():\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\", \"transcripts/**\"])\n+    problems = gate.check(perms, _opencode())  # opencode lacks transcripts/**\n+    assert any(\"transcripts/**\" in p for p in problems)\n+\n+\n+def test_uncovered_protected_blocks():\n+    perms = _perms(protected=[\"docs/req/requirements.yaml\"])\n+    problems = gate.check(perms, _opencode())  # opencode doesn't deny it\n+    assert any(\"docs/req/requirements.yaml\" in p for p in problems)\n+\n+\n+def test_covered_by_deny_glob_passes():\n+    perms = _perms(protected=[\"src/tradingagents/dataflows/router.py\"])\n+    opencode = _opencode(deny=[\"**/.env\", \"src/tradingagents/dataflows/**\"])\n+    # a concrete file under a denied glob directory is covered\n+    assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n+\n+\n+def test_covered_by_human_only_list_passes():\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\"])\n+    opencode = _opencode(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\"])\n+    assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n+\n+\n+def test_fnmatch_glob_coverage():\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\"transcripts/alice.md\"])\n+               "content": "\"\"\"Permission-sync gate (D3 / D7 §6.2).\n\n``.opencode/permissions.jsonc`` is the course artifact describing the intended\npolicy; ``opencode.jsonc`` is what OpenCode actually reads. This gate fails when the\ntwo drift in the ways that matter:\n\n- every path the artifact marks ``human_only`` or ``protected`` must be covered by\n  ``opencode.jsonc`` (its ``deny``, ``human_only`` or ``protected`` lists), and\n- both files' ``default`` must be ``deny`` (default is no read, no write).\n\nUsage::\n\n    python scripts/check_permission_sync.py [--root <dir>]\n\nExit 0 in sync, 1 on drift (with each problem printed), 2 when an input file is\nmissing (setup defect, not a content defect). Stdlib only; JSONC is parsed with a\nsmall comment/trailing-comma stripper that respects string literals.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport fnmatch\nimport json\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nOPENCODE = \"opencode.jsonc\"\nPERMISSIONS = \".opencode/permissions.jsonc\"\n\n# Lists whose paths must be covered by the enforced config, and the lists that may\n# provide the coverage.\n_REQUIRED_KEYS = (\"human_only\", \"protected\")\n_COVER_KEYS = (\"deny\", \"human_only\", \"protected\")\n\n\ndef _strip_jsonc(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove ``//`` and ``/* */`` comments and trailing commas, preserving strings.\"\"\"\n    out = []\n    i, n = 0, len(text)\n    in_string = False\n    while i < n:\n        ch = text[i]\n        if in_string:\n            out.append(ch)\n            if ch == \"\\\\\" and i + 1 < n:  # keep the escaped char verbatim\n                out.append(text[i + 1])\n                i += 2\n                continue\n            if ch == '\"':\n                in_string = False\n            i += 1\n            continue\n        if ch == '\"':\n            in_string = True\n            out.append(ch)\n            i += 1\n            continue\n        if ch == \"/\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == \"/\":\n            i += 2\n            while i < n and text[i] != \"\\n\":\n                i += 1\n            continue\n        if ch == \"/\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == \"*\":\n            i += 2\n            while i + 1 < n and not (text[i] == \"*\" and text[i + 1] == \"/\"):\n                i += 1\n            i += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(ch)\n        i += 1\n    stripped = \"\".join(out)\n    # Remove trailing commas before a closing brace/bracket (strings are intact).\n    return re.sub(r\",(\\s*[}\\]])\", r\"\\1\", stripped)\n\n\ndef load_jsonc(text: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Parse JSONC text (comments + trailing commas) into a dict.\"\"\"\n    return json.loads(_strip_jsonc(text))\n\n\ndef _covers(pattern_keys: dict, required: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether any configured pattern covers ``required`` (exact, glob, or dir).\"\"\"\n    for key in _COVER_KEYS:\n        for pattern in pattern_keys.get(key) or []:\n            if pattern == required:\n                return True\n            if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(required, pattern):\n                return True\n            # A ``dir/**`` pattern covers everything beneath it.\n            if pattern.endswith(\"/**\"):\n                prefix = pattern[:-3]\n                if required ==               "file": "src/cli/run.py",
              "patch": "Index: src/cli/run.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/run.py\t\n+++ src/cli/run.py\t\n@@ -1,767 +1,766 @@\n \"\"\"Running one analysis from the CLI: build the graph, stream it into the live view, save the report.\"\"\"\n \n import inspect\n import json\n import os\n import re\n import sys\n import time\n import webbrowser\n from dataclasses import replace\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from functools import wraps\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import typer\n from rich.live import Live\n \n from cli.display import (\n     ANALYST_ORDER,\n     AnalystWallTimeTracker,\n     classify_message_type,\n     console,\n     create_layout,\n     display_complete_report,\n     message_buffer,\n     update_analyst_statuses,\n     update_display,\n     update_research_team_status,\n )\n from cli.selections import depth_from_env, get_user_selections, unattended_gaps\n from cli.stats_handler import StatsCallbackHandler\n from tradingagents import __version__\n from tradingagents.agents.rating import is_review, run_rating\n from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.graph.analyst_execution import (\n     build_analyst_execution_plan,\n )\n from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, build_run_id, write_manifest\n \n _VALID_VARIANTS = (\"v0\", \"v1\", \"v2\")\n \n \n def _validate_variant(value: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Accept only a known, lowercase architecture variant slug (``v0``/``v1``/``v2``).\n \n     The value becomes the first segment of the manifest ``run_id`` and a directory\n     name under the results root, so an unknown or unsafe value is rejected rather\n     than interpolated.\n     \"\"\"\n     if value not in _VALID_VARIANTS:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid variant {value!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_VALID_VARIANTS)}\"\n         )\n     return value\n \n \n \n def _run_directory(config: dict, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Where this run writes, with the ticker validated as a path component.\n \n     Every other path that interpolates a ticker checks it first; a value of\n     \"..\" here would place the run outside the results directory.\n     \"\"\"\n     return Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker_component(ticker) / trade_date\n \n \n def _manifest_config_snapshot(config: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Scalars from ``config`` that are safe to record in a run manifest.\n \n     The recorder already drops secret-pattern keys; keeping only scalar values\n     here also excludes nested objects and lists that are not comparable settings.\n     ``results_dir`` is a machine-local output path, not a comparable setting, so it\n     is left out of the manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     return {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in config.items()\n         if key != \"results_dir\"\n         and (isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None)\n     }\n \n \n def write_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     config: dict,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     outcome: str | None,\n     usage: dict,\n     failure: str | None,\n     variant: str,\n     repeat: int,\n     at: datetime,\n     version: str,\n     duration_seconds: float | None = None,\n     started_at: float | None = None,\n     clock=None,\n     stop_reason: str | None = None,\n     evidence_mode: str = \"strict\",\n ) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write this run's manifest to ``<results_dir>/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json``.\n \n     ``stop_reason`` is read from the run's final state by the caller (C owns the\n     value domain); it is ``None`` when the graph did not reach a terminal state.\n     ``prompt_hashes`` (B) is ``{}`` and ``evidence_snapshot`` (A) is ``None`` until\n     those members' contracts land. ``duration_seconds`` is measured from\n     ``started_at`` and ``clock`` (``time.time`` by default) when not supplied;\n     passing both keeps it testable.\n \n     A per-run ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar (E4) is written next to the manifest\n     recording the evidence mode and the facts the run observed. It does not change\n     the RunEvent v1 15 fields.\n     \"\"\"\n     run_id = build_run_id(variant, ticker, trade_date, repeat, at)\n     if duration_seconds is None and started_at is not None:\n         now = (clock or time.time)()\n         duration_seconds = max(0.0, now - started_at)\n \n     event = RunEvent(\n         run_id=run_id,\n         created_at=at.astimezone(UTC).isoformat(),\n         version=version,\n         ticker=ticker,\n         trade_date=trade_date,\n         asset_type=asset_type,\n         outcome=outcome,\n         config_snapshot=_manifest_config_snapshot(config),\n         prompt_hashes={},\n         evidence_snapshot=None,\n         usage=usage,\n         duration_seconds=duration_seconds,\n         failure=failure,\n         stop_reason=stop_reason,\n     )\n     runs_dir = Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"runs\"\n     run_id = _unique_run_id(runs_dir, run_id)\n     event = replace(event, run_id=run_id)\n     manifest_dir = runs_dir / run_id\n     manifest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     path = write_manifest(event, manifest_dir / \"manifest.json\")\n     write_evidence_mode(manifest_dir / \"evidence-mode.json\", run_id, evidence_mode)\n     return path\n \n \n _EVIDENCE_MODES = (\"strict\", \"report_reference\")\n \n \n def write_evidence_mode(path, run_id: str, evidence_mode: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write the E4 ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar recording this run's mode.\n \n     E records facts only; the authoritative action and the mode approval belong to\n     D/C, so those fields are ``None`` here unless a caller later fills them in.\n     \"\"\"\n     if evidence_mode not in _EVIDENCE_MODES:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid evidence_mode {evidence_mode!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_EVIDENCE_MODES)}\"\n         )\n     sidecar = {\n         \"schema_version\": 1,\n         \"run_id\": run_id,\n         \"evidence_mode\": evidence_mode,\n         \"scenario\": None,\n         \"policy_version\": None,\n         \"unknown_time_fields\": [],\n         \"limitations\": [],\n         \"authoritative_action\": None,\n         \"authoritative_reason\": None,\n         \"decided_by\": None,\n         \"snapshot_ref\": {\"snapshot_id\": None, \"artifact_key\": None},\n     }\n     path = Path(path)\n     path.write_text(json.dumps(sidecar, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n     return path\n \n \n def _unique_run_id(runs_dir: Path, run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A run_id whose directory does not exist yet, so a same-minute retry is safe.\n \n     ``build_run_id`` has minute resolution, so two runs started in the same minute\n     (or a retry) produce the same id. Appending ``-<n>`` keeps the id within the\n     recorder's 64-char pattern and never overwrites an earlier manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     pattern = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n     candidate = run_id\n     suffix = 2\n     while (runs_dir / candidate).exists():\n         candidate = f\"{run_id}-{suffix}\"\n         if not pattern.match(candidate):\n             raise ValueError(f\"no free run_id derived from {run_id!r} within 64 chars\")\n         suffix += 1\n     return candidate\n \n \n def _make_manifest_writer(config: dict, selections: dict, stats_handler, started_at=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     \"\"\"Return a ``write(failure=..., outcome=...)`` bound to this run's inputs.\n \n     ``variant`` selects the architecture under test and becomes the first segment\n     of the manifest ``run_id``; ``repeat`` is 1 and ``created_at`` is now, both\n     supplied here so the recorder never reads the clock itself. ``started_at`` is\n     the run's start (``time.time()``); forwarding it lets the manifest record a\n     real duration.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def write(*, failure, outcome, stop_reason=None):\n         return write_run_manifest(\n             config=config,\n             ticker=selections[\"ticker\"],\n             trade_date=selections[\"analysis_date\"],\n             asset_type=selections[\"asset_type\"],\n             outcome=outcome,\n             usage=stats_handler.get_stats(),\n             failure=failure,\n             variant=variant,\n             repeat=1,\n             at=datetime.now(UTC),\n             version=__version__,\n             started_at=started_at,\n             stop_reason=stop_reason,\n             evidence_mode=config.get(\"evidence_mode\", \"strict\"),\n         )\n \n     return write\n \n \n def _finalize_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     write,\n     graph,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     portfolio,\n     final_state,\n     failure: BaseException | None,\n ) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Write the manifest, then dispose of (or keep) the checkpoint.\n \n     The manifest is written **before** the checkpoint is cleared, so a crash in\n     teardown never loses the record. A failed run still writes a manifest with\n     ``failure`` set and keeps its checkpoint for resume; the failure is re-raised.\n     ``stop_reason`` is read from ``final_state`` (C's field) with a ``None``\n     fallback when the run did not reach a terminal state.\n     \"\"\"\n     outcome = None if final_state is None else run_rating(final_state)\n     stop_reason = (final_state or {}).get(\"stop_reason\") if failure is None else None\n     write(failure=None if failure is None else str(failure), outcome=outcome, stop_reason=stop_reason)\n \n     if failure is not None:\n         raise failure\n \n     if final_state is not None:\n         graph.record_decision(ticker, trade_date, final_state)\n     graph.clear_checkpoint_on_success(ticker, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n \n \n def _announce_checkpoint_state(graph, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Say whether this run resumed a saved one, where the user can see it.\n \n     The graph logs this, but nothing in the CLI configures logging and the live\n     view owns the screen, so a resume was invisible.\n     \"\"\"\n     if getattr(graph, \"_resuming\", False):\n         message_buffer.add_message(\n             \"System\", f\"Resuming the saved run for {ticker} on {trade_date}\"\n         )\n     else:\n         message_buffer.add_message(\"System\", f\"Starting fresh for {ticker} on {trade_date}\")\n \n \n def _build_run_config(selections: dict, checkpoint: bool | None) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Assemble the run config from interactive selections, honoring env precedence.\n \n     Round counts and checkpoint follow \"explicit env/flag wins\": an env-applied\n     value on DEFAULT_CONFIG is preserved unless the user overrode it on the CLI.\n     \"\"\"\n     config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n     # Research depth sets both round counts, but an explicit env override\n     # (TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS / _MAX_RISK_ROUNDS) wins over the\n     # interactive selection — leave the env-applied value in place (#977).\n     rounds = ((\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS\", \"max_debate_rounds\"),\n               (\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_RISK_ROUNDS\", \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"))\n     depth_was_asked = not depth_from_env()\n     for env_var, key in rounds:\n         if not os.environ.get(env_var):\n             config[key] = selections[\"research_depth\"]\n         elif depth_was_asked:\n             # The depth question appeared (it is skipped only when both are\n             # set), so say which half of the answer the environment overrode.\n             console.print(\n                 f\"[green]✓ {key} from environment:[/green] {config[key]} \"\n                 f\"(set by {env_var}, so the research depth you chose does not apply to it)\"\n             )\n     config[\"quick_think_llm\"] = selections[\"quick_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"deep_think_llm\"] = selections[\"deep_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"backend_url\"] = selections[\"backend_url\"]\n     config[\"llm_provider\"] = selections[\"llm_provider\"].lower()\n     # Provider-specific thinking configuration. Only the main provider's is\n     # asked; a tier on another provider keeps its configured value (#1440).\n     for key in (\"google_thinking_level\", \"openai_reasoning_effort\", \"anthropic_effort\"):\n         if selections.get(key) is not None:\n             config[key] = selections[key]\n     config[\"output_language\"] = selections.get(\"output_language\", \"English\")\n     # --checkpoint/--no-checkpoint overrides only when explicitly given; omitting\n     # the flag preserves TRADINGAGENTS_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED / the default (#976).\n     if checkpoint is not None:\n         config[\"checkpoint_enabled\"] = checkpoint\n     return config\n \n \n def _graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls) -> bool:\n-    \"\"\"Whether ``graph_cls.__init__`` accepts a ``workflow_variant`` keyword.\n+    \"\"\"Whether ``graph_cls.__init__`` has an explicit ``workflow_variant`` parameter.\n \n-    Detection is by signature: an explicit ``workflow_variant`` parameter, or a\n-    ``**kwargs`` catch-all, means the graph can take (and forward) the variant. A\n-    graph class that cannot introspect raises ``False`` rather than guessing.\n+    Only an explicit, named parameter counts. A bare ``**kwargs`` catch-all is *not*\n+    treated as support: a legacy graph that swallows unknown kwargs would otherwise be\n+    handed v1 and silently ignore it, mislabelling a v0-compatible run. A graph class\n+    that cannot introspect returns ``False`` rather than guessing.\n     \"\"\"\n     try:\n         params = inspect.signature(graph_cls.__init__).parameters\n     except (TypeError, ValueError):\n         return False\n-    if \"workflow_variant\" in params:\n-        return True\n-    return any(p.kind is inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD for p in params.values())\n+    return \"workflow_variant\" in params\n \n \n def _reject_unavailable_variant(variant: str, graph_cls=None) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Refuse a variant that the workflow cannot run, before any model call.\n \n     v0 is always allowed. v2 is not delivered yet and is refused regardless of the\n     graph. v1 is allowed only when ``graph_cls`` accepts ``workflow_variant``;\n     otherwise a v0-compatible run must not be mislabelled v1.\n     \"\"\"\n     if variant == \"v0\":\n         return\n     if variant == \"v2\":\n         console.print(\n             \"[red]Variant 'v2' is not available yet: the adaptive workflow is not \"\n             \"delivered. Use --variant v0 (or v1 if the graph supports it).[/red]\"\n         )\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n     if graph_cls is None or not _graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls):\n         console.print(\n             f\"[red]Variant {variant!r} is not available: this graph does not accept \"\n             \"workflow_variant. Run with --variant v0.[/red]\"\n         )\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n \n \n def _build_graph(graph_cls, selected_analyst_keys, config, callbacks, *, workflow_variant):\n     \"\"\"Construct the graph, forwarding ``workflow_variant`` only when accepted.\"\"\"\n     kwargs = {\"config\": config, \"debug\": True, \"callbacks\": callbacks}\n     if _graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls):\n         kwargs[\"workflow_variant\"] = workflow_variant\n     return graph_cls(selected_analyst_keys, **kwargs)\n \n \n def _effective_manifest_variant(graph, requested: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"The variant the graph actually enabled, from ``run_settings()``, else requested.\"\"\"\n     run_settings = getattr(graph, \"run_settings\", None)\n     if not callable(run_settings):\n         return requested\n     try:\n         settings = run_settings()\n     except (TypeError, ValueError):\n         return requested\n     if not isinstance(settings, dict):\n         return requested\n     return settings.get(\"workflow_variant\") or requested\n \n \n def run_analysis(checkpoint: bool | None = None, portfolio=None, flags=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     flags = flags or {}\n     variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n     # Refuse a variant the graph cannot run before any setup or model call: v2 is\n     # not delivered, and v1 needs a graph that accepts workflow_variant.\n     _reject_unavailable_variant(variant, TradingAgentsGraph)\n     # With no terminal nothing can answer a prompt: name every question still\n     # open before any model is called, rather than stopping at the first one.\n     if not (sys.stdin and sys.stdin.isatty()):\n         gaps = unattended_gaps(flags)\n         if gaps:\n             console.print(\"[red]No terminal to answer the setup questions. Set:[/red]\")\n             for gap in gaps:\n                 console.print(f\"  {gap}\")\n             raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n \n     selections = get_user_selections(flags)\n \n     config = _build_run_config(selections, checkpoint)\n \n     stats_handler = StatsCallbackHandler()\n \n     # Normalize analyst selection to predefined order (selection is a 'set', order is fixed)\n     selected_set = {analyst.value for analyst in selections[\"analysts\"]}\n     selected_analyst_keys = [a for a in ANALYST_ORDER if a in selected_set]\n     analyst_execution_plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analyst_keys)\n     analyst_wall_time_tracker = AnalystWallTimeTracker(analyst_execution_plan)\n \n     graph = _build_graph(\n         TradingAgentsGraph,\n         selected_analyst_keys,\n         config,\n         [stats_handler],\n         workflow_variant=variant,\n     )\n     # The variant the graph actually enabled drives the manifest identity.\n     manifest_variant = _effective_manifest_variant(graph, variant)\n \n     message_buffer.init_for_analysis(selected_analyst_keys)\n \n     # Track start time for elapsed display\n     start_time = time.time()\n \n     results_dir = _run_directory(config, selections[\"ticker\"], selections[\"analysis_date\"])\n     results_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     report_dir = results_dir / \"reports\"\n     report_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     log_file = results_dir / \"message_tool.log\"\n     log_file.touch(exist_ok=True)\n \n     def save_message_decorator(obj, func_name):\n         func = getattr(obj, func_name)\n \n         @wraps(func)\n         def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):\n             func(*args, **kwargs)\n             timestamp, message_type, content = obj.messages[-1]\n             content = content.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")  #               "newString": "def test_var_kwargs_alone_is_not_support():\n    # A legacy graph that swallows unknown kwargs must NOT be treated as supporting\n    # workflow_variant: it would accept v1 and silently ignore it (mislabelling).\n    class _VarKwargs:\n        def __init__(self, **kwargs):\n            self.received = dict(kwargs)\n\n    assert cli_run._graph_accepts_workflow_variant(_VarKwargs) is False\n\n\ndef test_legacy_var_kwargs_graph_refuses_v1_and_does_not_forward():\n    class _Legacy:\n        def __init__(self, **kwargs):\n            self.received = dict(kwargs)\n\n        def run_settings(self):\n            return {}\n\n    # v1 is refused before construction ...\n    with pytest.raises(cli_run.typer.Exit):\n        cli_run._reject_unavailable_variant(\"v1\", _Legacy)\n    # ... and v0 construction never forwards a workflow_variant.\n    graph = cli_run._build_graph(_Legacy, [\"market\"], {}, None, workflow_variant=\"v0\")\n    assert \"workflow_variant\" not in graph.received",

isinstance(entry, str):\n+            rules.append((\"*\", entry))\n+        elif isinstance(entry, dict):\n+            rules.extend((pattern, str(effect)) for pattern, effect in entry.items())\n+\n+    for rule in opencode.get(\"permissions\") or []:\n+        if isinstance(rule, dict) and rule.get(\"action\") == action:\n+            rules.append((str(rule.get(\"resource\", \"*\")), str(rule.get(\"effect\", \"\"))))\n+\n+    return rules\n+\n+\n+def _matches(required: str, pattern: str) -> bool:\n+    if pattern == required or fnmatch.fnmatchcase(required, pattern):\n+        return True\n+    # A ``dir/**`` or ``dir/*`` pattern covers everything beneath it.\n+    if pattern.endswith(\"/**\") or pattern.endswith(\"/*\"):\n+        prefix = pattern.rsplit(\"/\", 1)[0]\n+
