problems: list[str] = []\n \n     if permissions.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n         problems.append(\n             f\"{PERMISSIONS}: default is {permissions.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\"\n         )\n     if opencode.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n         problems.append(f\"{OPENCODE}: default is {opencode.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\")\n \n     for key in _REQUIRED_KEYS:\n Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n     args = list(argv)\n     if \"--root\" in args:\n         idx = args.index(\"--root\")\n         try:\n             root = Path(args[idx + 1])\n         except IndexError:\n             print(\"usage: check_permission_sync.py [--root <dir>]\", file=sys.stderr)\n             return None, 2\n     return root, 0\n \n \n def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:\n     root, code = _parse_args(argv)\n     if root is None:\n         return code\n \n     opencode_path = root / OPENCODE\n     permissions_path = root / PERMISSIONS\n     for path in (opencode_path, load_jsonc(opencode_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n         permissions = load_jsonc(permissions_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n     except ValueError as exc:\n         print(f\"[permission-sync] BLOCKED: cannot parse JSONC: {exc}\")\n         return 1\n \n     problems = check(permissions, opencode)\n     if problems:\n         print(f\"[permission-sync] BLOCKED: {len(problems)} drift problem(s):\")\n         for problem in problems:\n             print(f\"    - {problem}\")\n         return 1\n     print(\"[permission-sync] OK: opencode.jsonc covers the protected paths and both default to deny\")\n     return 0\n \n \n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n     raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))\n",

              "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_permission_sync.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_permission_sync.py\t\n+++ test/offline/test_permission_sync.py\t\n@@ -1,146 +1,214 @@\n \"\"\"Offline tests for the permission-sync gate (D3 / D7 §6.2).\n \n ``scripts/check_permission_sync.py`` keeps ``opencode.jsonc`` (the enforced config)\n in sync with ``.opencode/permissions.jsonc`` (the course artifact): every path the\n artifact marks ``human_only`` or ``protected`` must be covered by opencode.jsonc, and\n both files' ``default`` must be ``deny``.\n \"\"\"\n \n import sys\n from pathlib import Path\n \n sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / \"scripts\"))\n \n import check_permission_sync as gate  # noqa: E402\n \n \n def _perms(**overrides):\n     base = {\n         \"default\": \"deny\",\n         \"allow\": [],\n         \"deny\": [\"**/.env\"],\n         \"human_only\": [\".agent/rules.md\"],\n         \"protected\": [\"src/tradingagents/dataflows/**\"],\n     }\n     base.update(overrides)\n     return base\n \n \n def _opencode(**overrides):\n     base = {\n         \"default\": \"deny\",\n         \"allow\": [],\n         \"deny\": [\"**/.env\", \"src/tradingagents/dataflows/**\"],\n         \"human_only\": [\".agent/rules.md\"],\n     }\n     base.update(overrides)\n     return base\n \n \n # --- JSONC loading -----------------------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_load_jsonc_strips_line_comments_and_trailing_commas():\n     text = \"\"\"\n     {\n       // a line comment\n       \"default\": \"deny\",\n       \"list\": [\"a\", \"b\",],  /* trailing comma + block comment */\n     }\n     \"\"\"\n     data = gate.load_jsonc(text)\n     assert data == {\"default\": \"deny\", \"list\": [\"a\", \"b\"]}\n \n \n def test_load_jsonc_keeps_comment_markers_inside_strings():\n     text = '{\"url\": \"https://example.test/a//b\", \"note\": \"not /* a comment */\"}'\n     data = gate.load_jsonc(text)\n     assert data[\"url\"] == \"https://example.test/a//b\"\n     assert data[\"note\"] == \"not /* a comment */\"\n \n \n # --- happy path --------------------------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_in_sync_passes():\n     assert gate.check(_perms(), _opencode()) == []\n \n \n # --- default must be deny ----------------------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_permissions_default_not_deny_blocks():\n     problems = gate.check(_perms(default=\"allow\"), _opencode())\n     assert any(\"permissions\" in p and \"default\" in p for p in problems)\n \n \n def test_opencode_default_not_deny_blocks():\n     problems = gate.check(_perms(), _opencode(default=\"ask\"))\n     assert any(\"opencode\" in p and \"default\" in p for p in problems)\n \n \n # --- coverage of human_only / protected -------------------------------------\n \n \n def test_uncovered_human_only_blocks():\n     perms = _perms(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\", \"transcripts/**\"])\n     problems = gate.check(perms, _opencode())  # opencode lacks transcripts/**\n     assert any(\"transcripts/**\" in p for p in problems)\n \n \n def test_uncovered_protected_blocks():\n     perms = _perms(protected=[\"docs/req/requirements.yaml\"])\n     problems = gate.check(perms, _opencode())  # opencode doesn't deny it\n     assert any(\"docs/req/requirements.yaml\" in p for p in problems)\n \n \n def test_covered_by_deny_glob_passes():\n     perms = _perms(protected=[\"src/tradingagents/dataflows/router.py\"])\n     opencode = _opencode(deny=[\"**/.env\", \"src/tradingagents/dataflows/**\"])\n     # a concrete file under a denied glob directory is covered\n     assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n \n \n def test_covered_by_human_only_list_passes():\n     perms = _perms(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\"])\n     opencode = _opencode(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\"])\n     assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n \n \n def test_fnmatch_glob_coverage():\n     perms = _perms(human_only=[\"transcripts/alice.md\"])\n     opencode = _opencode(human_only=[\"transcripts/**\"])\n     assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n \n \n+# --- real schema: rules live under permission.read / permission.edit ---------\n+\n+\n+def _real_opencode(edit=None, read=None, **top):\n+    \"\"\"An OpenCode-shaped config: nested permission.read / permission.edit maps.\"\"\"\n+    base = {\n+        \"default\": \"deny\",\n+        \"permission\": {\n+            \"edit\": edit if edit is not None else {},\n+            \"read\": read if read is not None else {},\n+        },\n+    }\n+    base.update(top)\n+    return base\n+\n+\n+def test_nested_permission_edit_and_read_cover_human_only():\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\".opencode/rules.md\"], protected=[])\n+    opencode = _real_opencode(\n+        edit={\".opencode/rules.md\": \"deny\"},\n+        read={\".opencode/rules.md\": \"deny\"},\n+    )\n+    assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n+\n+\n+def test_nested_permission_glob_covers_transcripts():\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\"transcripts/alice.md\"], protected=[])\n+    opencode = _real_opencode(\n+        edit={\"transcripts/*\": \"deny\"},\n+        read={\"transcripts/*\": \"deny\"},\n+    )\n+    assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n+\n+\n+def test_nested_missing_edit_protection_blocks():\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\"])\n+    # Read is denied but edit is not: still writable, so not protected.\n+    opencode = _real_opencode(edit={}, read={\".agent/rules.md\": \"deny\"})\n+    problems = gate.check(perms, opencode)\n+    assert any(\".agent/rules.md\" in p for p in problems)\n+\n+\n+def test_nested_missing_read_protection_blocks():\n+    perms = _perms(protected=[\"docs/req/requirements.yaml\"])\n+    opencode = _real_opencode(\n+        edit={\"docs/req/requirements.yaml\": \"deny\"},\n+        read={},  # readable\n+    )\n+    problems = gate.check(perms, opencode)\n+    assert any(\"docs/req/requirements.yaml\" in p for p in problems)\n+\n+\n+def test_nested_allow_does_not_cover():\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\".agent/rules.md\"])\n+    opencode = _real_opencode(\n+        edit={\".agent/rules.md\": \"allow\"},\n+        read={\".agent/rules.md\": \"allow\"},\n+    )\n+    assert gate.check(perms, opencode) != []\n+\n+\n+def test_nested_scalar_permission_deny_covers_all():\n+    # permission.read: \"deny\" is a blanket; edit likewise.\n+    opencode = {\"default\": \"deny\", \"permission\": {\"read\": \"deny\", \"edit\": \"deny\"}}\n+    perms = _perms(human_only=[\"anything/at/all.md\"])\n+    assert gate.check(perms, opencode) == []\n+\n+\n # --- CLI: main() against real files -----------------------------------------\n \n \n def _write_repo(tmp_path, opencode_text, perms_text):\n     (tmp_path / \"opencode.jsonc\").write_text(opencode_text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n     (tmp_path / \".opencode\").mkdir()\n     (tmp_path / \".opencode\" / \"permissions.jsonc\").write_text(perms_text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n     return tmp_path\n \n \n def test_main_passes_on_in_sync_repo(tmp_path, capsys):\n     repo = _write_repo(\n         tmp_path,\n         '{\"default\": \"deny\", \"deny\": [\"**/.env\"], \"human_only\": [\".agent/rules.md\"]}',\n         '{\"default\": \"deny\", \"deny\": [\"**/.env\"], \"human_only\": [\".agent/rules.md\"]}',\n     )\n     assert gate.main([\"--root\", str(repo)]) == 0\n \n \n def test_main_blocks_on_drift(tmp_path, capsys):\n     repo = _write_repo(\n         tmp_path,\n         '{\"default\": \"deny\", \"deny\": [], \"human_only\": []}',\n         '{\"default\": \"deny\", \"deny\": [], \"human_only\": [\"transcripts/**\"]}',\n     )\n     assert gate.main([\"--root\", str(repo)]) == 1\n     assert \"transcripts/**\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n \n \n def test_main_missing_file_exits_two(tmp_path):\n     assert gate.main([\"--root\", str(tmp_path)]) == 2\n",

Let me check OpenCode docs quickly.",
          "time": {

          },

        {

          "callID": "call_00_1IQQ9qde3lqFTwYZP9Fq8319",

            "output": "# Permissions\n\nPermissions control whether an agent may perform an action on a resource.\n\n## Configure\n\nA common setup is to ask before running shell commands, allow routine Git\ninspection, and always block pushes. Add these ordered rules to `opencode.jsonc`:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"ask\" },\n    { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"git status *\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n    { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"git diff *\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n    { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"git push *\", \"effect\": \"deny\" },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\nThe last matching rule wins, so the specific exceptions follow the broad rule.\n\n<Callout type=\"warning\">\n  V1 uses different field and action names. In V2, use `permissions`, `shell`, and `subagent` instead of `permission`,\n  `bash`, and `task`.\n</Callout>\n\n## Rules\n\nEach rule requires three string fields:\n\n| Field      | Meaning                                                                    |\n| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `action`   | Tool permission action                                                     |\n| `resource` | Value being used, such as a path, command, URL, query, skill ID, or agent ID |\n| `effect`   | `allow`, `deny`, or `ask`                                                   |\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n    { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"*.env\", \"effect\": \"deny\" },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\n| Effect  | Result                              |\n| ------- | ----------------------------------- |\n| `allow` | Continue without prompting          |\n| `deny`  | Block the operation                 |\n| `ask`   | Wait for a decision from the client |\n\nIf no rule matches, OpenCode uses `ask`.\n\n## Matching\n\nActions and resources use simple whole-value wildcards:\n\n| Pattern | Match                                      |\n| ------- | ------------------------------------------ |\n| `*`     | Zero or more characters, including `/`    |\n| `?`     | Exactly one character                     |\n| Other   | The literal character                     |\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"edit\", \"resource\": \"packages/docs/*.mdx\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\nThis pattern matches the entire normalized path. Backslashes are normalized to\nslashes, and matching is case-insensitive on Windows.\n\nA shell pattern ending in ` *` also matches the command without arguments:\n\n```jsonc\n{ \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"git status *\", \"effect\": \"allow\" }\n```\n\nThis matches both `git status` and `git status --short`.\n\nOpenCode combines rules in order and uses the last match. Lower-priority\nconfiguration is loaded first, global rules are appended next, and agent rules\nare appended last.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n    { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"secrets/*\", \"effect\": \"deny\" },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\nOperations may check several resources, such as a patch that touches multiple\nfiles. Any `deny` denies the operation; otherwise any `ask` asks; otherwise the\noperation is allowed.\n\n## Actions\n\nV2 action names are strings, so plugins may define more actions. Built-in tools\ncurrently use these actions and resources:\n\n| Action               | Resource                                                                    |\n| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `read`               | Location-relative internal path or canonical absolute external path         |\n| `edit`               | Target path for `edit`, `write`, and `patch`                                |\n| `glob`               | Requested glob pattern                                                      |\n| `grep`               | Requested regular expression, not the search path                           |\n| `shell`              | Scanner-produced command string; compound commands may produce several      |\n| `subagent`           | Target agent ID                                                             |\n| `skill`              | Skill ID                                                                    |\n| `question`           | `*`                                                                         |\n| `webfetch`           | Requested URL                                                               |\n| `websearch`          | Search query                                                                |\n| `generate_image` | Selected image model as `providerID/modelID`, plus `#variant` when set |\n| `external_directory` | Canonical external directory boundary, normally ending in `/*`              |\n| `<server>_<tool>`    | `*` for an MCP tool; unsupported characters in both names become `_`        |\n| `opencode_list_mcp_resources` | MCP server name                                                    |\n| `opencode_read_mcp_resource`  | `<server>:<uri>`                                                   |\n| `execute`            | `*`; a deny removes Code Mode and lists its tools directly, while nested tools enforce their rules |\n\nFor example, allow one skill and deny all other skills:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"skill\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"deny\" },\n    { \"action\": \"skill\", \"resource\": \"effect\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\n`doom_loop` and `lsp` are not current V2 Core permission actions.\n\n## Directories\n\nA path outside both the active Location and its non-root project worktree is\nchecked against `external_directory` before its `read` or `edit` rules. The\ndefault policy allows `external_directory`, so external paths are not prompted\nunless you add a rule. To be asked before any access outside the project:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"external_directory\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"ask\" },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\nNarrower rules after it can allow or deny specific directories:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"external_directory\", \"resource\": \"~/projects/reference/*\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n    { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"~/projects/reference/*\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n    { \"action\": \"edit\", \"resource\": \"~/projects/reference/*\", \"effect\": \"deny\" },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\nThis applies to external paths used by `read`, `edit`, `write`, and `patch`.\nShell checks its external working directory and directories inferred by its\nscanner before checking `shell` resources.\n\nFor `external_directory`, `read`, and `edit`, a leading `~`, `~/`, `$HOME`, or\n`$HOME/` is expanded when configuration loads:\n\n```jsonc\n{ \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"$HOME/reference/*\", \"effect\": \"allow\" }\n```\n\nShell resources remain raw command text and are not home-expanded.\n\n<Callout type=\"warning\">\n  `shell` runs with the host user's filesystem, process, and network authority. Directory inference from command text is\n  best effort, so prefer a narrow shell allowlist instead of patterns intended to recognize every dangerous command.\n</Callout>\n\nRelative mutation paths may leave the active Location while remaining inside\nits project worktree. Explicit external paths are canonicalized before matching,\nso authorize only trusted directory boundaries.\n\n## Scanner\n\nShell permission checks use OpenCode's built-in shell scanner across Bash, Zsh, POSIX `sh`, and PowerShell. Some commands can't be safely analyzed, such as malformed syntax or dynamic evaluation like `eval`. If any `shell` deny rule applies, such a command fails with a scanner error, because its subcommands can't be checked against the deny rule. Otherwise it needs approval for the whole command as one `shell` resource and for `external_directory` `*`. Only a rule allowing every directory, or the user, can grant the second approval, and neither approval is saved as a pattern.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n  \"policies\": [\n    {\n      \"permissions\": [\n        { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"git status *\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n        { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"rm *\", \"effect\": \"deny\" },\n      ],\n    },\n  ],\n}\n```\n\nPermission rules, saved approval patterns, and best-effort directory inference apply to every extracted subcommand and `cd` target. There is no extra approval mode or blanket restriction for unknown directories.\n\n## Defaults\n\nEvery agent, including custom agents, starts with this ordered base policy:\n\n```jsonc\n[\n  { \"action\": \"*\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n  { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"*.env\", \"effect\": \"ask\" },\n  { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"*.env.*\", \"effect\": \"ask\" },\n  { \"action\": \"read\", \"resource\": \"*.env.example\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n]\n```\n\nShipped agents append these policies:\n\n| Agent        | Additional policy                                                              |\n| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `build`      | Allows questions                                                               |\n| `plan`       | Allows questions; denies edits except files under `~/.opencode/plan`           |\n| `general`    | Denies questions and launching subagents                                       |\n| `explore`    | Denies everything except shell, reads, globs, grep, web fetches, web searches, and external directories; asks for `.env` reads |\n| `title`      | Denies all actions                                                              |\n| `summary`    | Denies all actions                                                              |\n| `compaction` | Keeps the base policy                                                          |\n\nBecause no default rule asks for `external_directory`, reads and edits outside\nthe Location and worktree proceed without a prompt. Add an\n`external_directory` `ask` or `deny` rule, as shown in\n[Directories](#directories), to restore a prompt or block outside access.\nLater global and agent rules override these defaults.\n\n## Agents\n\nPut shared rules at the top level and narrower rules under\n`agents.<id>.permissions`:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n  \"permissions\": [\n    { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"ask\" },\n    { \"action\": \"shell\", \"resource\": \"git status *\", \"effect\": \"allow\" },\n  ],\n  \"agents\": {\n    \"reviewer\": {\n      \"description\": \"Review code without changing it\",\n      \"mode\": \"subagent\",\n      \"permissions\": [\n        { \"action\": \"edit\", \"resource\": \"*\", \"effect\": \"deny\" },\n      ],\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\nAgent rules are appended after global rules; they do not replace the global\narray. A custom subagent uses its own permissions, not a subset of its parent's\npermissions.\n\n## Approvals\n\nWhen a rule resolves to `ask`, clients can reply with:\n\n| Choice       | Reply      | Result                                                               |\n| ------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Allow once   | `once`     | Approve only the pending request                                     |\n| Allow always | `always`   | Approve it and save the tool's proposed patterns for the project     |\n| Reject       | `reject`   | Reject it and every other pending permission request in that session |\n\nFor example, choosing **Allow always** for `git status --short` may save a\nshell prefix that covers later `git status` commands:\n\n```text\nshell: git status * → allow\n```\n\nSaved approvals are durable, project-scoped `allow` rules. They never override\na configured `deny`. Tools choose the proposed saved pattern: some propose `*`,\nshell proposes command prefixes, and skills and subagents propose their IDs.\nReview broad approvals and remove those no longer needed.\n\nClients may attach feedback when rejecting. Non-interactive clients must decide\nhow to handle approval requests; configured `deny` rules always remain enforced.\n\n## Policies\n\nA [policy](/policies) can hard-deny a permission check after these rules and saved\napprovals run. It turns `allow` or `ask` into `deny` and never grants access.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"policies\": [{ \"action\": \"tool.use\", \"resource\": \"shell:sudo *\", \"effect\": \"deny\" }],\n}\n```\n\nGlobal and Console-managed policies override project configuration, which is how an\norganization blocks a command that a repository would allow.",

          "type": "text",
          "text": "Now I'll add tests for the real nested `permission.edit`/`permission.read` shape, plus a test that a path covered by only read (not edit) still counts as protected for read but there must be an edit-protection too. Let me define expected semantics clearly and write tests. I'll add a helper for the real-config shape.\n\nDesign decision for coverage: a required path counts as \"protected\" if it is denied/asked for **both** read and edit — but where those actions aren't specified in the config, fall back to top-level lists. To keep it simple and match the user's phrasing \"read those nested rules and match accordingly\", I'll say: a path is covered if, considering all rules for **read** and for **edit**, each action has at least one matching rule whose effect is deny or ask. The top-level `deny`/`human_only`/`protected` lists apply to both actions.\n\nLet me add tests.",

              "newString": "def _effect_rules(opencode: dict, action: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Deny/ask patterns for ``action`` from the top-level lists and the permission model.\n\n    Top-level ``deny``/``human_only``/``protected`` lists protect a path from every\n    action (so they apply to both read and edit). The real config instead nests rules\n    under ``permission.<action>``: either a scalar effect (``\"deny\"``/``\"ask\"``/\n    ``\"allow\"``) applying to every resource, or a map of pattern -> effect.\n    \"\"\"\n    rules: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n\n    # Artifact / stub shape: lists at the top level deny both read and edit.\n    for key in _COVER_KEYS:\n        for pattern in opencode.get(key) or []:\n            rules.append((pattern, \"deny\"))\n\n    # Real OpenCode shape: permission.<action> (V1) or permissions[] entries (V2).\n    permission = opencode.get(\"permission\")\n    if isinstance(permission, dict):\n        entry = permission.get(action)\n        if isinstance(entry, str):\n            rules.append((\"*\", entry))\n        elif isinstance(entry, dict):\n            rules.extend((pattern, str(effect)) for pattern, effect in entry.items())\n\n    for rule in opencode.get(\"permissions\") or []:\n        if isinstance(rule, dict) and rule.get(\"action\") == action:\n            rules.append((str(rule.get(\"resource\", \"*\")), str(rule.get(\"effect\", \"\"))))\n\n    return rules\n\n\ndef _matches(required: str, pattern: str) -> bool:\n    if pattern == required or fnmatch.fnmatchcase(required, pattern):\n        return True\n    # A ``dir/**`` or ``dir/*`` pattern covers everything beneath it.\n    if pattern.endswith(\"/**\") or pattern.endswith(\"/*\"):\n        prefix = pattern.rsplit(\"/\", 1)[0]\n        return required == prefix or required.startswith(prefix + \"/\")\n    return False\n\n\ndef _covers_action(opencode: dict, action: str, required: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether ``action`` on ``required`` is denied (or asked) by some rule.\"\"\"\n    return any(\n        _matches(required, pattern) and effect in _DENY_EFFECTS\n        for pattern, effect in _effect_rules(opencode, action)\n    )\n\n\ndef _covers(opencode: dict, required: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Covered means both read and edit are withheld from the agent.\"\"\"\n    return all(_covers_action(opencode, action, required) for action in _ACTIONS)\n\n\ndef check(permissions: dict, opencode: dict) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return human-readable drift problems (empty list means in sync).\"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n\n    if permissions.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n        problems.append(\n            f\"{PERMISSIONS}: default is {permissions.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\"\n        )\n    if opencode.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n        problems.append(f\"{OPENCODE}: default is {opencode.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\")\n\n    for key in _REQUIRED_KEYS:\n        for required in permissions.get(key) or []:\n            if not _covers(opencode, required):\n                problems.append(\n                    f\"{OPENCODE} does not protect {key} path {required!r} for both read and edit \"\n                    f\"from {PERMISSIONS}\"\n                )\n    return problems",
              "oldString": "def _covers(pattern_keys: dict, required: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether any configured pattern covers ``required`` (exact, glob, or dir).\"\"\"\n    for key in _COVER_KEYS:\n        for pattern in pattern_keys.get(key) or []:\n            if pattern == required:\n                return True\n            if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(required, pattern):\n                return True\n            # A ``dir/**`` pattern covers everything beneath it.\n            if pattern.endswith(\"/**\"):\n                prefix = pattern[:-3]\n                if required == prefix or required.startswith(prefix + \"/\"):\n                    return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef check(permissions: dict, opencode: dict) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return human-readable drift problems (empty list means in sync).\"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n\n    if permissions.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n        problems.append(\n            f\"{PERMISSIONS}: default is {permissions.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\"\n        )\n    if opencode.get(\"default\") != \"deny\":\n        problems.append(f\"{OPENCODE}: default is {opencode.get('default')!r}, expected 'deny'\")\n\n    for key in _REQUIRED_KEYS:\n        for required in permissions.get(key) or []:\n            if not _covers(opencode, required):\n                problems.append(\n                    f\"{OPENCODE} does not cover {key} path {required!r} \"\n                    f\"from {PERMISSIONS}\"\n                )\n    return problems"
            },

          "text": "Fixed, not committed.\n\n## Summary\n\n`scripts/check_permission_sync.py` was only reading top-level lists, so it passed the stub and (falsely) failed the real config whose rules live under `permission.read` / `permission.edit`.               "patch": "Index: src/cli/main.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/main.py\t\n+++ src/cli/main.py\t\n@@ -1,210 +1,215 @@\n import sys\n from enum import StrEnum\n from typing import Annotated\n \n import typer\n from rich.markup import escape\n \n from cli.display import console\n from cli.models import AnalystType, AssetType\n from cli.prompts import filter_analysts_for_asset_type, parse_analysts\n from cli.run import _reject_unavailable_variant, _validate_variant, run_analysis\n from tradingagents.backtest import iter_grid, run_backtest, summarize\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.llm_clients.openai_client import SIGNED_IN_PROVIDERS\n from tradingagents.portfolio import load_portfolio\n \n # prompt_toolkit's win32 output module is importable only on Windows (it asserts\n # the platform at import time), so gate on the platform rather than catching the\n # failure — that way a genuinely broken prompt_toolkit on Windows still surfaces\n # instead of silently disabling the handler below. Off Windows this stays an\n # empty tuple, which `except` accepts and never matches (#1138).\n if sys.platform == \"win32\":  # pragma: no cover - platform dependent\n     from prompt_toolkit.output.win32 import NoConsoleScreenBufferError\n \n     _NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = (NoConsoleScreenBufferError,)\n else:\n     _NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS = ()\n \n app = typer.Typer(\n     name=\"TradingAgents\",\n     help=\"TradingAgents CLI: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework\",\n     add_completion=True,  # Enable shell completion\n )\n \n \n @app.callback(invoke_without_command=True)\n def analyze(\n     ctx: typer.Context,\n     checkpoint: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None,\n         \"--checkpoint/--no-checkpoint\",\n         help=\"Enable/disable checkpoint-resume (save state after each node so a \"\n         \"crashed run can resume). Omit to honor TRADINGAGENTS_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED.\",\n     ),\n     clear_checkpoints: bool = typer.Option(\n         False,\n         \"--clear-checkpoints\",\n         help=\"Delete all saved checkpoints before running (force fresh start).\",\n     ),\n     portfolio: str = typer.Option(\n         None,\n         \"--portfolio\",\n         help=\"JSON file with current holdings and cash, so the trader, risk and \"\n         \"portfolio agents size against your actual position.\",\n     ),\n     ticker: str = typer.Option(None, \"--ticker\", help=\"Ticker to analyze, e.g. NVDA or 0700.HK; skips the prompt\"),\n     date: str = typer.Option(None, \"--date\", help=\"Analysis date, YYYY-MM-DD; skips the prompt\"),\n     analysts: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--analysts\", help=\"Comma-separated analysts, e.g. market,news; skips the prompt\"\n     ),\n     save: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--save/--no-save\", help=\"Save the report under results_dir without asking\"\n     ),\n     show: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--show/--no-show\", help=\"Show the full report at the end without asking\"\n     ),\n     html: bool | None = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--html/--no-html\",\n         help=\"Save the report as one HTML page too, complete_report.html, without asking (default: yes)\",\n     ),\n     variant: str = typer.Option(\n-        \"v0\", \"--variant\",\n-        help=\"Architecture variant for the run manifest: v0 (original), v1 (trimmed), v2 (adaptive).\",\n+        None, \"--variant\",\n+        help=\"Architecture variant: v0 (original), v1 (trimmed), v2 (adaptive). \"\n+        \"Omit to keep the configured legacy run.\",\n     ),\n ):\n     \"\"\"Run an analysis. This is what a bare `tradingagents` does.\n \n     Flags answer their questions; with provider, models, depth and language also\n     set through TRADINGAGENTS_* variables, the run asks nothing.\n     \"\"\"\n     if ctx.invoked_subcommand is not None:\n         return\n     if clear_checkpoints:\n         from tradingagents.graph.checkpointer import clear_all_checkpoints\n         n = clear_all_checkpoints(DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"data_cache_dir\"])\n         console.print(f\"[yellow]Cleared {n} checkpoint(s).[/yellow]\")\n-    try:\n-        variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n-    except ValueError as exc:\n-        console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n-        raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n-    # Refuse v1/v2 here too, before run_analysis is even called, so an unavailable\n-    # variant is rejected before any model call.\n-    _reject_unavailable_variant(variant)\n+    # Validate only an explicit variant; omitting the flag is the legacy run.\n+    if variant is not None:\n+        try:\n+            variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n+        except ValueError as exc:\n+            console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n+            raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n+        # v2 is not delivered: refuse it before any model call. v1 is allowed here\n+        # and decided in run_analysis once the graph is known, so it can be\n+        # forwarded and run as v1 rather than rejected before construction.\n+        if variant == \"v2\":\n+            _reject_unavailable_variant(variant)\n     portfolio_context = None\n     if portfolio:\n         try:\n             portfolio_context = load_portfolio(portfolio)\n         except ValueError as exc:\n             console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n             raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n \n     try:\n         flags = {\"ticker\": ticker, \"date\": date, \"analysts\": analysts, \"save\": save, \"show\": show, \"html\": html}\n         run_analysis(checkpoint=checkpoint, portfolio=portfolio_context, flags=flags, variant=variant)\n     except _NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS:\n         # A terminal with no console buffer cannot host the interactive prompts.\n         # Emit one actionable line on stderr instead of a prompt_toolkit\n         # traceback; plain text, since rich may not render here either (#1138).\n         typer.echo(\n             \"Error: no Windows console available. The interactive CLI needs a real \"\n             \"console buffer — run it from Windows Terminal, PowerShell, or cmd.exe \"\n             \"rather than a piped or embedded terminal.\",\n             err=True,\n         )\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n \n \n @app.command()\n def backtest(\n     tickers: str = typer.Argument(..., help=\"Comma-separated tickers, e.g. NVDA,AAPL\"),\n     start: str = typer.Option(..., \"--start\", help=\"First analysis date, YYYY-MM-DD\"),\n     end: str = typer.Option(..., \"--end\", help=\"Last analysis date, YYYY-MM-DD\"),\n     every: int = typer.Option(7, \"--every\", help=\"Days between analysis dates\"),\n     analysts: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--analysts\", help=\"Comma-separated analysts to run: market, sentiment, news, fundamentals; omit for all the asset type allows\"\n     ),\n     asset_type: str = typer.Option(\"stock\", \"--asset-type\", help=\"stock or crypto\"),\n     portfolio: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--portfolio\", help=\"JSON file with holdings and cash, held constant across the grid\"\n     ),\n     run_id: str = typer.Option(\n         None, \"--run-id\", help=\"Continue an earlier sweep: its cells are skipped and its log reused\"\n     ),\n ):\n     \"\"\"Score past decisions over a grid of tickers and dates.\"\"\"\n \n     try:\n         dates = iter_grid(start, end, every)\n         book = load_portfolio(portfolio) if portfolio else None\n         kind = AssetType(asset_type.strip().lower())\n         # The analysts are named and checked as for an analysis; without a\n         # choice, every analyst the asset type allows runs.\n         chosen = (parse_analysts(analysts, kind) if analysts\n                   else filter_analysts_for_asset_type(list(AnalystType), kind))\n     except ValueError as exc:\n         console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n \n     names = [t.strip() for t in tickers.split(\",\") if t.strip()]\n     if not names:\n         console.print(\"[red]No ticker to analyze; pass them comma-separated, e.g. NVDA,AAPL[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1)\n \n     def show_progress(done, total, ticker, date):\n         console.print(f\"[dim][{done}/{total}] {ticker} {date}[/dim]\")\n \n     kwargs = {\"asset_type\": kind.value, \"portfolio\": book, \"run_id\": run_id, \"progress\": show_progress,\n               \"selected_analysts\": [a.value for a in chosen]}\n \n     try:\n         result = run_backtest(names, dates, DEFAULT_CONFIG, **kwargs)\n     except Exception as exc:  # a missing key or an unknown analyst is a setup error\n         console.print(f\"[red]{exc}[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n     console.print(summarize(result).render())\n     console.print(f\"\\nRan {result.cells_run} cells, skipped {result.skipped}. Log: {result.log_path}\")\n     console.print(f\"Continue or settle this sweep: --run-id {result.run_id}\")\n     for ticker, date, reason in result.failures:\n         console.print(f\"[yellow]failed:[/yellow] {ticker} {date}: {reason}\")\n     for ticker, reason in result.settlement_failures:\n         console.print(f\"[yellow]unsettled:[/yellow] {ticker}: {reason}\")\n \n \n # The plans `login` and `logout` take: the providers signed in to, not keyed.\n Plan = StrEnum(\"Plan\", {name: name for name in SIGNED_IN_PROVIDERS})\n \n \n @app.command()\n def login(plan: Annotated[Plan, typer.Argument(help=\"The plan to sign in with\")]):\n     \"\"\"Sign in with your ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan, for the chatgpt provider.\"\"\"\n     from tradingagents.llm_clients import chatgpt_auth\n \n     try:\n         # One unwrapped line, so the sign-in address can be copied whole.\n         email = chatgpt_auth.sign_in(\n             say=lambda line: console.print(line, soft_wrap=True, markup=False, highlight=False))\n     except chatgpt_auth.ChatGPTAuthError as exc:\n         console.print(f\"[red]{escape(str(exc))}[/red]\")\n         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None\n     console.print(f\"[green]Signed in to ChatGPT as {escape(email)}.[/green]\")\n \n \n @app.command()\n def logout(plan: Annotated[Plan, typer.Argument(help=\"The plan to sign out of\")]):\n     \"\"\"Sign out of your ChatGPT plan: revoke this machine's access and forget it.\"\"\"\n     from tradingagents.llm_clients import chatgpt_auth\n \n     outcome = chatgpt_auth.sign_out()\n     if outcome == \"revoked\":\n         console.print(\"Signed out of ChatGPT.\")\n     elif outcome == \"forgotten\":\n         console.print(\"[yellow]Signed out here, but OpenAI could not be reached to revoke the sign-in; \"\n                       \"it stays valid at OpenAI until it expires.[/yellow]\")\n     else:\n         console.print(\"Not signed in to ChatGPT.\")\n \n \n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n     app()\n",

              "patch": "Index: src/cli/run.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/cli/run.py\t\n+++ src/cli/run.py\t\n@@ -1,766 +1,800 @@\n \"\"\"Running one analysis from the CLI: build the graph, stream it into the live view, save the report.\"\"\"\n \n import inspect\n import json\n import os\n import re\n import sys\n import time\n import webbrowser\n from dataclasses import replace\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n from functools import wraps\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import typer\n from rich.live import Live\n \n from cli.display import (\n     ANALYST_ORDER,\n     AnalystWallTimeTracker,\n     classify_message_type,\n     console,\n     create_layout,\n     display_complete_report,\n     message_buffer,\n     update_analyst_statuses,\n     update_display,\n     update_research_team_status,\n )\n from cli.selections import depth_from_env, get_user_selections, unattended_gaps\n from cli.stats_handler import StatsCallbackHandler\n from tradingagents import __version__\n from tradingagents.agents.rating import is_review, run_rating\n from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.graph.analyst_execution import (\n     build_analyst_execution_plan,\n )\n from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n from tradingagents.run_recorder import RunEvent, build_run_id, write_manifest\n \n _VALID_VARIANTS = (\"v0\", \"v1\", \"v2\")\n \n \n def _validate_variant(value: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"Accept only a known, lowercase architecture variant slug (``v0``/``v1``/``v2``).\n \n     The value becomes the first segment of the manifest ``run_id`` and a directory\n     name under the results root, so an unknown or unsafe value is rejected rather\n     than interpolated.\n     \"\"\"\n     if value not in _VALID_VARIANTS:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid variant {value!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_VALID_VARIANTS)}\"\n         )\n     return value\n \n \n \n def _run_directory(config: dict, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Where this run writes, with the ticker validated as a path component.\n \n     Every other path that interpolates a ticker checks it first; a value of\n     \"..\" here would place the run outside the results directory.\n     \"\"\"\n     return Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker_component(ticker) / trade_date\n \n \n def _manifest_config_snapshot(config: dict) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Scalars from ``config`` that are safe to record in a run manifest.\n \n     The recorder already drops secret-pattern keys; keeping only scalar values\n     here also excludes nested objects and lists that are not comparable settings.\n     ``results_dir`` is a machine-local output path, not a comparable setting, so it\n     is left out of the manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     return {\n         key: value\n         for key, value in config.items()\n         if key != \"results_dir\"\n         and (isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None)\n     }\n \n \n def write_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     config: dict,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     outcome: str | None,\n     usage: dict,\n     failure: str | None,\n     variant: str,\n     repeat: int,\n     at: datetime,\n     version: str,\n     duration_seconds: float | None = None,\n     started_at: float | None = None,\n     clock=None,\n     stop_reason: str | None = None,\n     evidence_mode: str = \"strict\",\n ) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write this run's manifest to ``<results_dir>/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json``.\n \n     ``stop_reason`` is read from the run's final state by the caller (C owns the\n     value domain); it is ``None`` when the graph did not reach a terminal state.\n     ``prompt_hashes`` (B) is ``{}`` and ``evidence_snapshot`` (A) is ``None`` until\n     those members' contracts land. ``duration_seconds`` is measured from\n     ``started_at`` and ``clock`` (``time.time`` by default) when not supplied;\n     passing both keeps it testable.\n \n     A per-run ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar (E4) is written next to the manifest\n     recording the evidence mode and the facts the run observed. It does not change\n     the RunEvent v1 15 fields.\n     \"\"\"\n     run_id = build_run_id(variant, ticker, trade_date, repeat, at)\n     if duration_seconds is None and started_at is not None:\n         now = (clock or time.time)()\n         duration_seconds = max(0.0, now - started_at)\n \n     event = RunEvent(\n         run_id=run_id,\n         created_at=at.astimezone(UTC).isoformat(),\n         version=version,\n         ticker=ticker,\n         trade_date=trade_date,\n         asset_type=asset_type,\n         outcome=outcome,\n         config_snapshot=_manifest_config_snapshot(config),\n         prompt_hashes={},\n         evidence_snapshot=None,\n         usage=usage,\n         duration_seconds=duration_seconds,\n         failure=failure,\n         stop_reason=stop_reason,\n     )\n     runs_dir = Path(config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"runs\"\n     run_id = _unique_run_id(runs_dir, run_id)\n     event = replace(event, run_id=run_id)\n     manifest_dir = runs_dir / run_id\n     manifest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n     path = write_manifest(event, manifest_dir / \"manifest.json\")\n     write_evidence_mode(manifest_dir / \"evidence-mode.json\", run_id, evidence_mode)\n     return path\n \n \n _EVIDENCE_MODES = (\"strict\", \"report_reference\")\n \n \n def write_evidence_mode(path, run_id: str, evidence_mode: str) -> Path:\n     \"\"\"Write the E4 ``evidence-mode.json`` sidecar recording this run's mode.\n \n     E records facts only; the authoritative action and the mode approval belong to\n     D/C, so those fields are ``None`` here unless a caller later fills them in.\n     \"\"\"\n     if evidence_mode not in _EVIDENCE_MODES:\n         raise ValueError(\n             f\"invalid evidence_mode {evidence_mode!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_EVIDENCE_MODES)}\"\n         )\n     sidecar = {\n         \"schema_version\": 1,\n         \"run_id\": run_id,\n         \"evidence_mode\": evidence_mode,\n         \"scenario\": None,\n         \"policy_version\": None,\n         \"unknown_time_fields\": [],\n         \"limitations\": [],\n         \"authoritative_action\": None,\n         \"authoritative_reason\": None,\n         \"decided_by\": None,\n         \"snapshot_ref\": {\"snapshot_id\": None, \"artifact_key\": None},\n     }\n     path = Path(path)\n     path.write_text(json.dumps(sidecar, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n     return path\n \n \n def _unique_run_id(runs_dir: Path, run_id: str) -> str:\n     \"\"\"A run_id whose directory does not exist yet, so a same-minute retry is safe.\n \n     ``build_run_id`` has minute resolution, so two runs started in the same minute\n     (or a retry) produce the same id. Appending ``-<n>`` keeps the id within the\n     recorder's 64-char pattern and never overwrites an earlier manifest.\n     \"\"\"\n     pattern = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,62}$\")\n     candidate = run_id\n     suffix = 2\n     while (runs_dir / candidate).exists():\n         candidate = f\"{run_id}-{suffix}\"\n         if not pattern.match(candidate):\n             raise ValueError(f\"no free run_id derived from {run_id!r} within 64 chars\")\n         suffix += 1\n     return candidate\n \n \n def _make_manifest_writer(config: dict, selections: dict, stats_handler, started_at=None, variant=\"v0\"):\n     \"\"\"Return a ``write(failure=..., outcome=...)`` bound to this run's inputs.\n \n     ``variant`` selects the architecture under test and becomes the first segment\n     of the manifest ``run_id``; ``repeat`` is 1 and ``created_at`` is now, both\n     supplied here so the recorder never reads the clock itself. ``started_at`` is\n     the run's start (``time.time()``); forwarding it lets the manifest record a\n     real duration.\n     \"\"\"\n \n     def write(*, failure, outcome, stop_reason=None):\n         return write_run_manifest(\n             config=config,\n             ticker=selections[\"ticker\"],\n             trade_date=selections[\"analysis_date\"],\n             asset_type=selections[\"asset_type\"],\n             outcome=outcome,\n             usage=stats_handler.get_stats(),\n             failure=failure,\n             variant=variant,\n             repeat=1,\n             at=datetime.now(UTC),\n             version=__version__,\n             started_at=started_at,\n             stop_reason=stop_reason,\n             evidence_mode=config.get(\"evidence_mode\", \"strict\"),\n         )\n \n     return write\n \n \n def _finalize_run_manifest(\n     *,\n     write,\n     graph,\n     ticker: str,\n     trade_date: str,\n     asset_type: str,\n     portfolio,\n     final_state,\n     failure: BaseException | None,\n ) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Write the manifest, then dispose of (or keep) the checkpoint.\n \n     The manifest is written **before** the checkpoint is cleared, so a crash in\n     teardown never loses the record. A failed run still writes a manifest with\n     ``failure`` set and keeps its checkpoint for resume; the failure is re-raised.\n     ``stop_reason`` is read from ``final_state`` (C's field) with a ``None``\n     fallback when the run did not reach a terminal state.\n     \"\"\"\n     outcome = None if final_state is None else run_rating(final_state)\n     stop_reason = (final_state or {}).get(\"stop_reason\") if failure is None else None\n     write(failure=None if failure is None else str(failure), outcome=outcome, stop_reason=stop_reason)\n \n     if failure is not None:\n         raise failure\n \n     if final_state is not None:\n         graph.record_decision(ticker, trade_date, final_state)\n     graph.clear_checkpoint_on_success(ticker, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n \n \n def _announce_checkpoint_state(graph, ticker: str, trade_date: str) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Say whether this run resumed a saved one, where the user can see it.\n \n     The graph logs this, but nothing in the CLI configures logging and the live\n     view owns the screen, so a resume was invisible.\n     \"\"\"\n     if getattr(graph, \"_resuming\", False):\n         message_buffer.add_message(\n             \"System\", f\"Resuming the saved run for {ticker} on {trade_date}\"\n         )\n     else:\n         message_buffer.add_message(\"System\", f\"Starting fresh for {ticker} on {trade_date}\")\n \n \n def _build_run_config(selections: dict, checkpoint: bool | None) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Assemble the run config from interactive selections, honoring env precedence.\n \n     Round counts and checkpoint follow \"explicit env/flag wins\": an env-applied\n     value on DEFAULT_CONFIG is preserved unless the user overrode it on the CLI.\n     \"\"\"\n     config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n     # Research depth sets both round counts, but an explicit env override\n     # (TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS / _MAX_RISK_ROUNDS) wins over the\n     # interactive selection — leave the env-applied value in place (#977).\n     rounds = ((\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS\", \"max_debate_rounds\"),\n               (\"TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_RISK_ROUNDS\", \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"))\n     depth_was_asked = not depth_from_env()\n     for env_var, key in rounds:\n         if not os.environ.get(env_var):\n             config[key] = selections[\"research_depth\"]\n         elif depth_was_asked:\n             # The depth question appeared (it is skipped only when both are\n             # set), so say which half of the answer the environment overrode.\n             console.print(\n                 f\"[green]✓ {key} from environment:[/green] {config[key]} \"\n                 f\"(set by {env_var}, so the research depth you chose does not apply to it)\"\n             )\n     config[\"quick_think_llm\"] = selections[\"quick_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"deep_think_llm\"] = selections[\"deep_think_llm\"]\n     config[\"backend_url\"] = selections[\"backend_url\"]\n     config[\"llm_provider\"] = selections[\"llm_provider\"].lower()\n     # Provider-specific thinking configuration. Only the main provider's is\n     # asked; a tier on another provider keeps its configured value (#1440).\n     for key in (\"google_thinking_level\", \"openai_reasoning_effort\", \"anthropic_effort\"):\n         if selections.get(key) is not None:\n             config[key] = selections[key]\n     config[\"output_language\"] = selections.get(\"output_language\", \"English\")\n     # --checkpoint/--no-checkpoint overrides only when explicitly given; omitting\n     # the flag preserves TRADINGAGENTS_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED / the default (#976).\n     if checkpoint is not None:\n         config[\"checkpoint_enabled\"] = checkpoint\n     return config\n \n \n def _graph_accepts_workflow_variant(graph_cls) -> bool:\n     \"\"\"Whether ``graph_cls.__init__`` has an explicit ``workflow_variant`` parameter.\n \n     Only an explicit, named parameter counts. A graph class\n     that cannot introspect returns ``False`` rather than guessing.\n     \"\"\"\n     try:\n         params = inspect.signature(graph_cls.__init__).parameters\n     except (TypeError, ValueError):\n         return False\n     return \"workflow_variant\" in params\n \n \n-def _reject_unavailable_variant(variant: str, graph_cls=None) -> None:\n+def _reject_unavailable_variant(variant: str | None, graph_cls=None) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Refuse a variant that the workflow cannot run, before any model call.\n \n-    v0 is always allowed. v2 is not delivered yet and is refused regardless of the\n-    graph. v1 is allowed only when ``graph_cls`` accepts ``workflow_variant``;\n-    otherwise a v0-compatible run must not be mislabelled v1.\n+    ``None`` means the flag was omitted: that is the legacy run and is always\n+    allowed. v0 is always allowed. v2 is not delivered yet and is refused\n+    regardless of the graph. v1 is allowed only when ``graph_cls`` accepts\n+    ``workflow_variant``; otherwise it is refused (a v0-compatible run must not be\n+    mislabelled v1).\n     \"\"\"\n-    if variant == \"v0\":\n+    if variant is None or variant == \"v0\":\n         return\n     if variant == \"v2\":\n         console.print(\n             \"[red]Variant 'v2' is not available yet: the adaptive workflow is not \"\n             \"delivered. analysts=None, config=None, debug=False, callbacks=None, workflow_variant=None):\n        self.config = dict(config or {})\n        self.selected_analysts = analysts or []\n        self.workflow_variant = workflow_variant\n        if workflow_variant in _PRESETS:\n            rounds = _PRESETS[workflow_variant]\n            self.config[\"max_debate_rounds\"] = rounds\n            self.config[\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"] = rounds\n        self.model_calls = 0\n\n    def run_settings(self):\n        settings = {\n            \"version\": \"0.7.1\",\n            \"max_debate_rounds\": self.config.get(\"max_debate_rounds\"),\n            \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": self.config.get(\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"),\n        }\n        if self.workflow_variant is not None:\n            settings[\"workflow_variant\"] = self.workflow_variant\n        return settings\n\n\n# --- effective config / variant helpers -------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_effective_config_overlays_run_settings_rounds():\n    graph = PresetGraph(config={\"max_debate_rounds\": 3, \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": 3},\n                        workflow_variant=\"v0\")\n    effective = cli_run._effective_config({\"max_debate_rounds\": 3, \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": 3}, graph)\n    assert effective[\"max_debate_rounds\"] == 2\n    assert effective[\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"] == 2\n\n\ndef test_effective_config_keeps_config_when_omitted():\n    graph = PresetGraph(config={\"max_debate_rounds\": 3, \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": 3},\n 3\n\n\n# --- manifest records effective depth ---------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_explicit_v0_manifest_records_effective_two_rounds(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    captured = {}\n\n    def fake_write(**kwargs):\n        captured.update(kwargs)\n        return tmp_path / \"manifest.json\"\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"write_run_manifest\", fake_write)\n\n    class _Stats:\n        def get_stats(self):\n            return {\"llm_calls\": 0, \"tool_calls\": 0, \"tokens_in\": None, \"tokens_out\": None}\n\n    graph = PresetGraph(config={\"max_debate_rounds\": 3}, workflow_variant=\"v0\")\n    effective = cli_run._effective_config({\"results_dir\": str(tmp_path), \"max_debate_rounds\": 3}, graph)\n    variant = cli_run._effective_manifest_variant(graph, \"v0\")\n    write = cli_run._make_manifest_writer(\n        effective,\n        {\"ticker\": \"NVDA\", \"analysis_date\": \"2026-11-20\", \"asset_type\": \"stock\"},\n        _Stats(),\n        variant=variant,\n    )\n    write(failure=None, outcome=\"Buy\")\n    assert captured[\"variant\"] == \"v0\"\n    assert captured[\"config\"][\"max_debate_rounds\"] == 2\n\n\n# --- main.py: omitted vs explicit, v1 passes through, v2 rejected -----------\n\n\ndef _runner(monkeypatch):\n    calls = []\n    monkeypatch.setattr(m, \"run_analysis\", lambda **kw: calls.append(kw))\n    return CliRunner(), calls\n\n\ndef test_omitted_flag_passes_none(monkeypatch):\n    runner, calls = _runner(monkeypatch)\n    assert runner.invoke(m.app, []).exit_code == 0\n    assert calls[0][\"variant\"] is None\n\n\ndef test_explicit_v0_passes_v0(monkeypatch):\n    runner, calls = _runner(monkeypatch)\n    assert runner.invoke(m.app, [\"--variant\", \"v0\"]).exit_code == 0\n    assert calls[0][\"variant\"] == \"v0\"\n\n\ndef test_explicit_v1_reaches_run_analysis(monkeypatch):\n    runner, calls = _runner(monkeypatch)\n    assert runner.invoke(m.app, [\"--variant\", The CLI config is the\n+# requested configuration; the manifest must record these effective values instead.\n+_EFFECTIVE_SETTING_KEYS = (\"max_debate_rounds\", \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\")\n+\n+\n+def _effective_config(config: dict, graph) -> dict:\n+    \"\"\"Overlay the graph's effective settings onto ``config`` for the manifest.\n+\n+    A variant preset (or any graph-side adjustment) changes the rounds actually run.\n+    The manifest's ``config_snapshot`` must reflect that, not the requested config.\n+    Keys the graph does not report are left as configured.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    run_settings = getattr(graph, \"run_settings\", None)\n+    if not callable(run_settings):\n+        return config\n+    try:\n+        settings = run_settings()\n+    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n+        return config\n+    if not isinstance(settings, dict):\n+        return config\n+    effective = dict(config)\n+    for key in _EFFECTIVE_SETTING_KEYS:\n+        if settings.get(key) is not None:\n+            effective[key] = settings[key]\n+    return effective\n+\n+\n+def run_analysis(checkpoint: bool | None = None, portfolio=None, flags=None, variant=None):\n     flags = flags or {}\n-    variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n+    # ``None`` = the flag was omitted: the legacy run (configured rounds, no preset).\n+    if variant is not None:\n+        variant = _validate_variant(variant)\n     # Refuse a variant the graph cannot run before any setup or model call: v2 is\n     # not delivered, and v1 needs a graph that accepts workflow_variant.\n     _reject_unavailable_variant(variant, TradingAgentsGraph)\n     # With no terminal nothing can answer a prompt: name every question still\n",

        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "All green. Not committed.\n\n## Summary\n\nFixed the three `--variant` bugs in the CLI.\n\n**`src/cli/main.py`**\n- `--variant` now defaults to `None` (omitted) instead of `\"v0\"`, so an omitted flag is distinguishable from an explicit v0.\n- Validates only an explicit variant; refuses **only v2** before the graph (zero model calls). **v1 is no longer rejected in main** — it's passed through to `run_analysis`, decided once the graph is known.\n- Forwards `variant=None` for omitted runs.\n\n**`src/cli/run.py`**\n- `_reject_unavailable_variant` accepts `None` (omitted → legacy, always allowed); v2 still refused; v1 allowed only when the graph accepts `workflow_variant`.\n- `run_analysis(variant=None)`: omitted skips validation/preset and forwards no `workflow_variant` (legacy configured rounds); explicit values forwarded as before.\n- New `_effective_config(config, graph)` overlays the graph's `run_settings()` effective `max_debate_rounds`/`max_risk_discuss_rounds` onto the config, so the **manifest records what actually ran** (explicit v0 → depth 2, not the requested 3). The manifest writer now receives `effective_config`, and `manifest_variant` comes from `run_settings()` (explicit v1 recorded as v1).\n\n**Tests**\n- New `test/offline/test_variant_preset.py` (10) with a preset stub graph: effective-config overlay, manifest records effective 2 rounds for explicit v0, omitted → `None`/legacy (3 rounds, no forward), explicit v0 → `\"v0\"`, explicit v1 reaches `run_analysis` (and forwards, runs 1 pair), explicit v2 rejected in main, and v2 refused in `run_analysis` with zero model calls and no manifest.\n- Updated `test/offline/test_cli_variant.py` and `tests/test_cli_commands.py` for the omitted → `None` contract.\n\n**Results**: full suite **1904 passed / 1 skipped** (optional bedrock); `ruff check src tests test` clean. Not committed.",
